about: Machine-readable blurbs for the DOMY symbolic cosmology. The narrative canon lives in SYMBOLISM.md; these one-to-three-sentence texts are the extended info the app may surface (hovers, info panels, docs).

philosophy.white_light: White light is the sum of all colors. Sunday sits in the center because the Sun is not one color among six - the six arms are sunlight decomposed, the star is the prism, Sunday is the source.
philosophy.paint_and_light: Before Newton the world knew color as pigment: yellow, red and blue, mixed into orange, green and purple - the painter's wheel of six. Newton's prism opened the second world: red, green and blue light with cyan, magenta and yellow between them. DOMY's two Prism wheels — the Persons and One Soul — are exactly these two worlds.
philosophy.gold_and_silver: Alchemy gives one metal to each luminary: gold to the Sun, silver to the Moon. On the dial the top is solar noon and the bottom is midnight, so gold crowns the top tip and silver the bottom - the day metal above, the night metal below.
philosophy.cross_cure: Every body carries a bright and a dark face - a virtue and a vice. Across each axis of the star, one body's virtue is the cure for the opposite body's vice.
philosophy.professions: Medieval astrology drew the 'children of the planets': each planet rules the callings born under it. The seven archetypal professions of the old world land one per body, and each snaps onto its body's virtue and vice.
philosophy.theological_trio: Faith, Hope and Love are a separate set from the seven virtue/vice pairs (Love alone belongs to both, as in tradition). They span three kinds of places: Faith at the center (Sunday, toward God - the vertical), Hope on the dawn arm (west, toward what comes - the horizon), Love on Venus' arm (toward people - the human).
philosophy.religion_alternates: The owner's art holds fourteen religions in two full sets. The basic seven sit one per body: Freemasonry on Sunday (the quest for Light fits the source better than the war-day it left), Islam on Monday (the purely lunar calendar), Buddhism on Tuesday (Mara's army met and beaten without a weapon), Taoism on Wednesday (unchanged - the water-star day), Hinduism on Thursday (unchanged - Guruvara, Jupiter's own day), Christianity on Friday (Good Friday, agape, forgiveness over punishment), Judaism on Saturday (unchanged - Shabbat, Shabtai is Saturn itself). The alternate seven each take the day they fit best: Mithraism on Sunday (the Unconquered Sun, dies Solis for its holy day), Druidism on Monday (lunar reckoning, groves and tides), Zoroastrianism on Tuesday (the fire Atar, asha as the courage of truth), Shamanism on Wednesday (the walker between worlds on the messenger's day), Sikhism on Thursday (Guruvar taken literally - ten Gurus, langar generosity), Babylon on Friday (Ishtar IS Venus; Babylon invented the planetary week), Voodoo on Saturday (Baron Samedi, 'Baron Saturday', keeper of the crossroads).

blurbs.day: Sunday is the source, not one day among six: as white light contains every color, the week's center contains every day.
blurbs.profession: The Sun is the royal planet, and its child is the Ruler - whose lesson is Humility and whose sin is Pride.
blurbs.greek: Helios drives the sun chariot across the sky each day; the Greeks named this day hemera Heliou, the day of the Sun.
blurbs.norse: Sol (Sunna) is the Norse sun goddess, chased across the sky by the wolf Skoll; sunnudagr is her day.
blurbs.religion: Christianity worships on the Lord's Day; in 321 Constantine made the 'day of the Sun' the day of rest, fusing Sun and Church in history. Sunday is also the day of Faith - with Hope at dawn and Love on Venus, the three theological virtues span the dial.
blurbs.color: White-gold: the sum of all colors and the Sun's own metal.
blurbs.virtue_vice: Pride is the self at the center of everything; Humility is its only cure. The center heals itself.
blurbs.religion_alt: Rome's soldier-mysteries crowned the Unconquered Sun: seven grades of initiation under the seven planets, dies Solis for their holy day — the same Sunday this dial keeps at its white-gold center.
blurbs.egypt: Ra is the sun itself, not its god: sailing the day barque from horizon to horizon, dying into the Duat each night and reborn at every dawn. Sunday's white-gold center is his oldest throne — no pantheon fused sun, king and temple more completely.
blurbs.slavic: Dažbog is the giving sun whose grandchildren the Slavs called themselves — he pours out grain, gold and warmth from the center and keeps nothing back.
blurbs.alchemy: Gold, the sun made solid, never rusts and never tarnishes — the incorruptible metal that is the goal of the whole Great Work.
blurbs.japan: Nichiyobi is the Sun's day — 日, the very glyph that opens the name of Japan — ruled by Amaterasu and heralded by Yatagarasu, the three-legged crow who rides the solar disc.
blurbs.age_of_heroes: Two sons of Typhon and Echidna hold Sunday: the Nemean Lion, whose hide no blade could cut, and Cerberus, who keeps the door out of the underworld - Heracles' first labour and his last.
blurbs.celestial_court: Sun Wukong took the title Great Sage Equal to Heaven for himself; the Six-Eared Macaque copied him so perfectly that all of heaven failed the test, and only the Buddha could tell the two apart.
blurbs.corporate: The chief executive holds the head of the table; the board's chairman holds the body that appoints and removes the chief executive - one authority, deliberately split in two.
blurbs.wow_alliance: Two kings hold Sunday: Varian Wrynn, crowned as a boy and later sold into the fighting pits as Lo'Gosh, and Genn Greymane, who walled Gilneas off from the Alliance, lost it, and came back to serve it.
blurbs.wow_horde: Sunday is a Warchief and the successor he appointed: Thrall, born in captivity and the author of a nation, against Garrosh Hellscream, raised to the seat by Thrall's own hand and the ruin of what it was for.
blurbs.wow_evil: Sunday is two men who took a terrible instrument to win with it: Arthas Menethil, who was right about Stratholme and wrong about everything after, and Illidan Stormrage, imprisoned ten thousand years for the same bargain.
blurbs.cp_gangs: Sunday is the Fourth Corporate War's two survivors: Arasaka, which sells order and rebuilt its tower taller after a nuke, and Militech, which builds the weapons and lets a government decide what they are for.
blurbs.cp_street: Sunday is two people who ran the city from opposite sides of one bar: Johnny Silverhand, who took a nuclear device into Arasaka Tower in 2023, and Rogue, who refused that job and spent fifty years deciding who counts.
blurbs.cp_corpo: Sunday is a founder past a hundred and fifty and the son who strangled him and took the chair - and, in lockstep rotation, a president out of the arms industry and the colonel who built his own state.
blurbs.sw_jedi: Sunday is a son who refused to execute his father and the father who spent twenty years executing another man's orders - one office held twice by the same family, and the only dual where both faces are one body.
blurbs.sw_sith: Sunday is a master and the apprentice he assembled: a man voted into every office he ever held and dismantled from inside, and the nine-year-old he spent a decade preparing for the second chair.
blurbs.sw_dyad: Sunday is the pair the story itself calls a dyad - a scavenger with no name who keeps going back for people who cannot help her, and an heir who killed two masters and served both.

blurbs.day: Monday is the Moon's day in every tongue that kept the planetary week - Selene's day in Greek, Mani's in Norse, Somvar in Sanskrit.
blurbs.profession: Medieval medicine followed the Moon - bloodletting calendars ran on its phases - and the physician keeps the night watch at the sickbed: a calm hand against the patient's fear. (The Moon's traditional alternate child is the Sailor, ruler of tides.)
blurbs.greek: Selene is the Titan goddess of the Moon, crossing the night sky in a silver chariot drawn by white horses.
blurbs.norse: Mani steers the Moon through the night, hunted by the wolf Hati until the world's end.
blurbs.religion: The Buddhist calendar is lunar: Uposatha observance days follow the Moon's phases, and Vesak - the Buddha's birth, awakening and passing - falls on a full moon.
blurbs.color: Blue is the still hour before dawn: moonlight on a sleeping world.
blurbs.virtue_vice: The Moon's bright face is Serenity, its dark face Fear - the night brings both peace and dread. Courage, from the opposite arm, is Fear's cure.
blurbs.religion_alt: The druids reckoned time by the Moon - groves, tides and the lunar count of nights; the serenity of the sacred wood, and the fear of its dark.
blurbs.egypt: Khonsu, "the traveller", is the moon crossing the night sky — Thebes' young healer and reckoner of months, wrapped like the dead yet carrying the regalia of life; the serenity of the crossing, and the old fear of the dark it passes through.
blurbs.slavic: Hors is the pale light of the night, the moon-disc whose path the werewolf-prince Vseslav crossed as he ran through the dark before dawn.
blurbs.alchemy: Silver mirrors the light it is given and blackens in the air, keeping the Moon's own habit of waxing bright and waning dark.
blurbs.japan: Getsuyobi is the Moon's day, ruled by Tsukuyomi, where Japan sees not a man in the moon but tsuki no usagi, the rabbit forever pounding mochi at his mortar.
blurbs.age_of_heroes: Medusa was made, not born: Ovid's Gorgon is a mortal woman punished into the shape everyone remembers, and her blood held a poison on one side and Asclepius' resurrection cure on the other.
blurbs.celestial_court: Chang'e drank the whole elixir of immortality rather than half of it and rose to the Moon alone; the Mid-Autumn Festival still keeps her there, with the jade rabbit that grinds the medicine.
blurbs.corporate: The chief human resources officer holds the people file - hiring, grievance, dismissal and the quiet part: the one office everybody visits on their worst day at work.
blurbs.wow_alliance: Anduin was crowned a boy and made High King the day Varian did not come back from the Broken Shore - a priest-king whose weapon is healing, holding a calm his people are never allowed to see him lose.
blurbs.wow_horde: Baine Bloodhoof inherited Thunder Bluff the day his father died by a poisoned axe and refused to answer it with a war - he named the poisoner rather than the Warchief, and kept the Horde together.
blurbs.wow_evil: Kel'Thuzad was expelled from the Kirin Tor for necromancy and went north to offer himself; the Cult of the Damned then sold the end of dying to frightened people, and Lordaeron accepted the grain willingly.
blurbs.cp_gangs: Monday belongs to the two collectives that guard rather than take: a nomad family that posts a watch over its own circle every night, and a club's own workers who organised after one of them was killed.
blurbs.cp_street: Monday is the ripperdoc: a former boxer running a basement clinic in Watson who installs the chrome this whole cast fights with, tells the truth at the speed the patient can take it, and carries the bills.
blurbs.cp_corpo: Monday is Song So Mi: an FIA netrunner who reached past the Blackwall for capability nobody else has and is being dismantled by it, and whose every later decision is organised around a cure.
blurbs.sw_jedi: Obi-Wan Kenobi spent nineteen years guarding a child on a worthless planet and did not act once - Monday's Serenity is not the absence of fear here, it is an accurate fear held perfectly still.
blurbs.sw_sith: Grand Moff Tarkin is the one figure who states Monday's vice as policy and signs it - fear as an administrative instrument, issued rather than suffered, by a man who never raises his voice.
blurbs.sw_dyad: Rose Tico loses her sister in the story's first hours and spends the same night stopping a man from throwing his life away - Monday's composure assembled out of care rather than out of the absence of fear.

blurbs.day: Tuesday belongs to the red planet: Ares' day to the Greeks, Tyr's day (tysdagr) to the Norse, Mangalvar in the Vedic week.
blurbs.profession: Mars' child is the Soldier, whose two faces are the body's virtue and vice themselves: Courage in defense, Wrath unleashed.
blurbs.greek: Ares is the storm of battle itself - the Greeks honored his ferocity and feared his rage in the same breath.
blurbs.norse: Tyr, god of war AND justice, gave his right hand to bind the wolf Fenrir - courage in the service of order.
blurbs.religion: Freemasonry is sworn on oaths - and Tyr, this arm's god, gave his hand to seal one. The square and compasses build the inner temple with a soldier's discipline: Courage set to work, Wrath bound by ritual.
blurbs.color: Orange is the working afternoon: the ember of the day's fire.
blurbs.virtue_vice: Mars carries both Courage and Wrath - the same fire that defends can destroy. Serenity, from the Moon's arm, quells Wrath; Courage cures the Moon's Fear.
blurbs.religion_alt: Zoroastrianism keeps the sacred fire Atar burning, and its heart is asha - truth and justice - the courage of the flame against the lie.
blurbs.egypt: Montu is the raised arm of Egypt's armies — the falcon-headed war god of Thebes whose name was the highest praise a fighting pharaoh could earn: Courage under the king's command, Wrath the same blade turned loose.
blurbs.slavic: Svetovid is the four-faced war-god of Arkona whose sacred white horse, led over crossed spears, foretold whether the campaign would be blessed.
blurbs.alchemy: Iron is the soldier's metal and the iron in our blood — Mars really does run, red and breath by breath, in every vein.
blurbs.japan: Kayobi is Fire-day, whose planet 火星 Kasei is literally the 'fire star,' Mars — a day of the forge, the flame, and the samurai's crossed katana.
blurbs.age_of_heroes: The Minotaur is wrath with the exits closed - Athens' tribute consumed inside a labyrinth Daedalus built for the single purpose of keeping one rage away from the world.
blurbs.celestial_court: Erlang Shen is heaven's foremost warrior, the three-eyed general who fought Sun Wukong to a standstill through seventy-two transformations and finally took him by seeing through every one.
blurbs.corporate: The chief operating officer runs the machine that has to work today. Operations is the only executive function measured in hours rather than in quarters.
blurbs.wow_alliance: Muradin Bronzebeard taught Arthas Menethil to fight, and in Northrend told him to leave Frostmourne where it lay - courage spent arguing with his own best student, and the ice took him for it.
blurbs.wow_horde: Grommash Hellscream was the first orc to drink Mannoroth's blood and the one who finally killed him for it, dying in the same act - the seat's vice and its virtue inside one biography.
blurbs.wow_evil: Mannoroth did not conquer the orcs - he offered them a drink. The clans that took it doubled in strength and lost the capacity to choose, and Grommash needed his own death to undo it.
blurbs.cp_gangs: Tuesday holds force in three tempers - Maelstrom, which replaced its bodies to keep it; Barghest, which gave it a chain of command; and the Wraiths, who point it at whoever is weakest in the Badlands.
blurbs.cp_street: Tuesday holds courage in three tempers - Jackie, who spent everything on one job; Panam, who left her family over a decision and came back to rebuild it; and River, who kept working a case the department had closed.
blurbs.cp_corpo: Tuesday is the full-conversion borg who killed Johnny Silverhand in the tower in 2023 - force with the person subtracted out of it, renewed by contract for half a century.
blurbs.sw_jedi: Leia Organa was interrogated at nineteen by the man whose fleet destroyed her world and gave up nothing; thirty years later she held a command together with no state left to authorise it.
blurbs.sw_sith: General Grievous collects the weapons of the Jedi he kills and withdraws from every fight that turns against him - Tuesday's proof that ferocity and courage are different faculties.
blurbs.sw_dyad: Tuesday holds two products of one training programme: a trooper who refused an order to fire on civilians in his first hour, and the captain who commanded that programme and, with a weapon at her head, lowered her own base's shields.

blurbs.day: Wednesday is Mercury's day - Hermes' day in Greek, Woden's (Odin's) day in the north, Budhvar in Sanskrit, the water-star day in East Asia.
blurbs.profession: Hermes is the god of roads and trade, and his child is the Merchant - who weighs with Wisdom and falls to Greed.
blurbs.greek: Hermes is the messenger between worlds: god of roads, merchants, thieves and cunning speech, guide of souls into the underworld.
blurbs.norse: Odin hung nine nights on the world-tree and gave an eye at Mimir's well - all of it for wisdom. Wednesday is literally Wodnesdaeg, his day.
blurbs.religion: In the East Asian week Wednesday is the day of the water star - and water is the Tao's central image: the soft thing that overcomes the hard, the way that flows without striving.
blurbs.color: Purple is midnight: the mourning color, the day's grave and its deepest mystery.
blurbs.virtue_vice: Mercury's bright face is Wisdom, its dark face Greed - the merchant god counts both coins and stars. Generosity, from Jupiter's arm, cures Greed; Wisdom curbs Jupiter's Excess.
blurbs.religion_alt: The shaman walks between worlds on the messenger's day - Odin hanging on the tree for wisdom is itself a shamanic initiation.
blurbs.egypt: Thoth is the ibis-headed scribe of the gods — inventor of writing, reckoner of years and moons, recorder of the verdict when the heart meets Ma'at's feather; Hermes' elder mirror on the messenger's midnight arm.
blurbs.slavic: Veles is the horned cattle-god and serpent at the world-tree's roots, sworn beside Perun in the treaties and grandsire of the bard Boyan.
blurbs.alchemy: Quicksilver is the only metal liquid at room temperature, a mirror you can pour — Mercurius, the messenger who carries every metal from one state to another.
blurbs.japan: Suiyobi is Water-day, whose planet 水星 Suisei is the 'water star,' Mercury — ruled by Ryujin, the sea-dragon who commands the tides with his glowing jewels.
blurbs.age_of_heroes: The Sphinx charged a riddle as toll at the gate of Thebes: answer and pass, fail and pay. Oedipus answered 'man', and she had nothing left to sell.
blurbs.celestial_court: Guan Yu, a third-century general deified as the god of loyalty and oaths, keeps a shrine in shops and restaurants across the Chinese world - which makes him the merchant's own patron.
blurbs.corporate: The chief financial officer keeps the ledger and signs for it; the discipline that makes a company solvent is the same one that makes it stingy, and the seat holds both.
blurbs.wow_alliance: Khadgar walked into Karazhan a boy apprentice and out of it white-bearded: uncovering what Medivh really was cost him his youth in a single afternoon, and he has guarded knowledge rather than gathered it ever since.
blurbs.wow_horde: Trade Prince Gallywix sold his own people their passage off a burning Kezan and indentured them for the fare; he is never wrong about a price, and has never found one he would not take.
blurbs.wow_evil: Gul'dan traded the elements for fel, ran the orcs through the Shadow Council from behind their own chieftains, and opened the Dark Portal - every price he paid was somebody else's.
blurbs.cp_gangs: Wednesday is knowledge priced: netrunners who work the Blackwall and tell nobody what is behind it, and a veterans' militia that kept the flag and turned protection into a toll.
blurbs.cp_street: Wednesday is the fixers: Wakako, who runs Westbrook out of a parlour and once sold a client out, and Padre, who runs Heywood out of a church and keeps the collar. One commodity, two institutions.
blurbs.cp_corpo: Wednesday is the fixer who knew the city better than almost anybody in this cast, spent that knowledge on the biggest score in the setting, and then on removing the witnesses to it.
blurbs.sw_jedi: Han Solo prices everything, takes his payment and leaves - and then comes back unpaid at the one moment when coming back is worth nothing to him. Wednesday's virtue arrives exactly once.
blurbs.sw_sith: Jabba the Hutt commands no army and holds no office; he holds debt, and keeps one settled account displayed on a wall - the moment a trade stops pretending to be commerce.
blurbs.sw_dyad: Wednesday is one commodity at two prices: a keeper of a thousand years who gives away what matters at the moment it is needed, and a codebreaker who sells the same night's work to both sides.

blurbs.day: Thursday is the king planet's day: Zeus' day in Greek, Thor's day in the north, Guruvar - the guru's day - in the Vedic week.
blurbs.profession: Jupiter's children are priests, judges and teachers - Brihaspati IS the guru of the gods, and Thursday is the teacher's day: generous of hand, jovial of table.
blurbs.greek: Zeus rules sky and thunder from Olympus, king of gods and keeper of oaths and guests.
blurbs.norse: Thor, thunder itself, guards gods and men with the hammer Mjolnir; thorsdagr became Thursday.
blurbs.religion: In Hindu tradition Thursday IS Brihaspativar: Brihaspati, guru of the gods, is the planet Jupiter itself, and his day is the week's most devotional.
blurbs.color: Yellow is noon at the top of the dial - and 'jovial', joyful, literally means 'of Jupiter'.
blurbs.virtue_vice: Jupiter's bright face is Generosity - the open royal hand; its dark face is Excess, the jovial table overflowing. Wisdom, from Mercury's arm, curbs Excess; Generosity cures Greed.
blurbs.religion_alt: Sikhism takes Guruvar literally - a faith of ten Gurus whose daily practice is langar, generosity served at a common table.
blurbs.egypt: Amun is the Hidden One — king of the gods, joined with the sun as Amun-Ra, the god the Greeks themselves named Zeus Ammon; Thursday's crown arm wears his twin plumes.
blurbs.slavic: Perun is the oak-crowned thunder-god whose six-petalled storm-mark the clock's hexagram echoes, and whose rain, wrung from the serpent, is the sky's generosity.
blurbs.alchemy: Tin makes bells and bronze ring, and cries out with the faint 'tin cry' when you bend it — Jupiter's benevolent, sounding metal.
blurbs.japan: Mokuyobi is Wood-day, whose planet 木星 Mokusei is the 'wood star,' Jupiter — the living element of the sacred pines that Shinto girdles with shimenawa rope.
blurbs.age_of_heroes: The Erymanthian Boar ate whole Arcadian harvests; the fourth labour was the one where excess had to be brought back ALIVE, taken by driving it into deep mountain snow.
blurbs.celestial_court: Zhu Bajie commanded heaven's naval host before appetite got him exiled into a pig's body: Journey to the West's most generous and most gluttonous pilgrim at once.
blurbs.corporate: The chief marketing officer preaches: a brand is a message repeated until it is believed, and the department spends more on being heard than on being right.
blurbs.wow_alliance: Uther the Lightbringer was the first paladin, and his real work was the Silver Hand - the Light turned into an order with successors. He refused Arthas at Stratholme and was stripped of his command for it.
blurbs.wow_horde: Vol'jin told Garrosh to his face that a Warchief who rules by fear is finished, took a blade for it, came back to lead the rebellion, and gave the throne away with his dying breath.
blurbs.wow_evil: Kil'jaeden took Sargeras's offer on Argus while Velen fled, and has been making the same honest bargain ever since - Ner'zhul raised as the Lich King, Gul'dan given fel, a Legion assembled one signature at a time.
blurbs.cp_gangs: Thursday sells hospitality. The Tyger Claws hold Japantown's neon, and everything given away there is on a meter - the most complete inversion of a virtue on this dial.
blurbs.cp_street: Thursday is the tarot shop above the clinic. Misty has the least of anybody in this cast and is the only one who gives without invoicing - the one economy here that runs on no return.
blurbs.cp_corpo: Thursday is the handler who trained the netrunner on Monday. Tradecraft is the only asset an agent owns, and teaching it is the single act that permanently reduces his own advantage.
blurbs.sw_jedi: Qui-Gon Jinn staked a slave child's freedom on a wager he had no authority to make, then announced he would train the boy against the Council's refusal - generosity that spends the giver's standing rather than his surplus.
blurbs.sw_sith: Count Dooku left the order over a diagnosis that was largely correct, and every gift he made afterwards was an instrument - Thursday's virtue counterfeited by the cast's only teacher.
blurbs.sw_dyad: Leia at fifty-odd is argued from what she hands over - a command she built, a training she never finished, and finally her life, spent reaching a son who was most of the way gone.

blurbs.day: Friday is the day of the evening star: Aphrodite's day in Greek, Freya's day in the north, Shukravar in Sanskrit.
blurbs.profession: Venus' children in old astrology are musicians, painters and lovers - the Artist, who works from Love and burns with Jealousy.
blurbs.greek: Aphrodite, born of sea-foam, rules love, beauty and desire - the planet Venus is her lamp at dusk.
blurbs.norse: Freya, goddess of love and of the slain, rides a chariot drawn by cats and weeps tears of gold; frjadagr is her day.
blurbs.religion: Islam gathers on Friday: Jumu'ah, the congregational prayer, makes this the blessed day of the week.
blurbs.color: Red is the evening: the sunset's blood-glow, the hour when Venus rises.
blurbs.virtue_vice: Venus carries Love and its shadow Jealousy - the fear of losing what is loved. Patience, from Saturn's arm, heals Jealousy; Love dissolves Saturn's Envy.
blurbs.religion_alt: Babylon named the planets gods and gave this clock its seven-day week; Ishtar IS Venus - the evening star, love and war in one body.
blurbs.egypt: Hathor - lady of love, music, beauty and joy, the Lady of the West who receives the setting sun into her country; the Greeks called her Aphrodite, and Venus' red evening is her hour.
blurbs.slavic: Mokoš is the great spinning goddess and Moist Mother Earth, the lone goddess of Kyiv's pantheon, who lived on as St Paraskeva venerated every Friday.
blurbs.alchemy: Copper is aes cyprium, the metal of Venus' island of Cyprus, and her glyph ♀ is the very hand-mirror it was first polished into.
blurbs.japan: Kin'yobi is Metal-day, whose planet 金星 Kinsei is the 'gold star,' Venus — emblemized by Yata no Kagami, the sacred mirror that lured Amaterasu from her cave.
blurbs.age_of_heroes: The Sirens sing the one song nobody outlives - Odysseus survived it bound to his mast with his crew's ears stopped with wax, hearing everything and able to answer nothing.
blurbs.celestial_court: Zhinü the Weaver Girl meets her cowherd once a year on a bridge of magpies across the Milky Way - the Qixi festival is that single night, kept for two thousand years.
blurbs.corporate: The chief design officer defends the work - taste is the one executive function that cannot be delegated, and the one most often overruled by people who cannot do it.
blurbs.wow_alliance: Jaina Proudmoore chose peace with the Horde over her own father's fleet and watched him die for it; after Theramore's mana bomb she came within one decision of drowning Orgrimmar, and stopped.
blurbs.wow_horde: Draka was born frail among orcs who had no use for frailty, survived a rite meant to kill her, and went into exile with Durotan rather than drink the demon's blood. Thrall is what she left.
blurbs.wow_evil: Sylvanas Windrunner was Ranger-General of Silvermoon; Arthas killed her deliberately and raised her as the first banshee so she would watch her own kingdom fall while serving him.
blurbs.cp_gangs: Friday is Heywood's own: gold, Santa Muerte and the family name on the car. The Valentinos are generous inside the line and murderous across it, and the line is the edge of what they love.
blurbs.cp_street: Friday holds the two performers: Kerry, who outlived the band and could not forgive it, and Lizzy Wizzy, who staged her own death and had herself copied into chrome to finish the show.
blurbs.cp_corpo: Friday is the doll who assembled the plan the whole story runs on and tried to cut the fixer out of it - the smallest want in the cast, a life she owns, and the one the setting refuses most completely.
blurbs.sw_jedi: Padmé Amidala is where the whole catastrophe starts, and it starts in a love: a senator arguing for the republic in the chamber that votes it away, married in secret to the man who ends both.
blurbs.sw_sith: Maul organised decades around one man who had stopped thinking about him - Friday's arm with the affection removed and the intensity kept, surviving even the body it was formed in.
blurbs.sw_dyad: Han at sixty walks out onto an open bridge toward a son who has already murdered on instruction, carrying nothing - Friday's virtue in its exact sense, being within reach.

blurbs.day: Saturday is Saturn's day - Cronus' day to the Greeks, Shanivar in Sanskrit. The Norse alone gave it no god: laugardagr, washing day; the Sabbath stands there instead.
blurbs.profession: Cronus carries the harvest sickle, and Saturn's child is the Farmer - who sows and WAITS (Patience) and eyes the neighbor's field (Envy).
blurbs.greek: Cronus, Titan of time and the harvest, devoured his own children out of envy and fear of being replaced - until Zeus, hidden away, returned to overthrow him.
blurbs.norse: Loki stands on Saturday (owner canon): the bound trickster, chained beneath the serpent venom as Cronus was cast down - the north gave its rest day to the god who never rests. His envy of Baldr brought the brightest god down.
blurbs.religion: Shabbat is Judaism's seventh day of rest - and in Hebrew the planet Saturn is named Shabtai, after the Sabbath itself: the day named the planet.
blurbs.color: Green is the morning: dew, growth, the week renewing itself on the day of rest.
blurbs.virtue_vice: Saturn, keeper of time, teaches Patience; his shadow is Envy, the bitter green of wanting what another has. Love, from Venus' arm, dissolves Envy; Patience heals Jealousy.
blurbs.religion_alt: Voodoo's keeper of the crossroads is Baron Samedi - Baron Saturday by name - the patience of the grave and the envy of the living.
blurbs.egypt: Osiris is the harvest that dies and returns — lord of the underworld and of rebirth, green-skinned like sprouting grain on Saturn's green morning; the patience of the buried seed, with Set's envy the vice he answered from the grave.
blurbs.slavic: Morana is the goddess of winter and death whose straw effigy is drowned every spring equinox — death as the hinge that lets the year be born again.
blurbs.alchemy: Lead is the heaviest, slowest metal, the prima materia the Work begins from — the base matter alchemy promises to turn into gold.
blurbs.japan: Doyobi is Earth-day, whose planet 土星 Dosei is the 'earth star,' Saturn — the patient element of Mount Fuji, the rice terraces, and the weathered stone lantern.
blurbs.age_of_heroes: Cut one Hydra head and two grow back; only Iolaus' torch ended the cycle, which makes the second labour the one won by method rather than by strength.
blurbs.celestial_court: Shennong tasted a hundred herbs to sort medicine from poison and is credited with the plough and the market; the tradition says the poisons eventually killed him.
blurbs.corporate: The chief technology officer plants what nobody sees: a platform takes years, pays out for a decade, and becomes a topic of conversation only in the week it fails.
blurbs.wow_alliance: Malfurion Stormrage was the first mortal druid and slept ten thousand years in the Emerald Dream - the brother who waited, and who imprisoned the twin who would not.
blurbs.wow_horde: Cairne Bloodhoof took Thrall's hand when the orcs were strangers with a bad name, built Thunder Bluff on the wager, and died to a blade poisoned by a third party in somebody else's duel.
blurbs.wow_evil: Neltharion was the Earth-Warder, given the world's ground by the titans; the Old Gods talked him into forging the Dragon Soul, and the Cataclysm split open the world he was made to keep.
blurbs.cp_gangs: Saturday is one patience pointed two ways - the Animals build a body over years and refuse the clinic, the Scavengers cut a finished one out of somebody still using it.
blurbs.cp_street: Saturday is the braindance editor. Judy cuts somebody else's minutes until a stranger can live through them, which cannot be done at speed - patience as the refusal to call a thing finished.
blurbs.cp_corpo: Saturday is Saburo's bodyguard of decades, building a case for the murder to a standard an institution would accept, from outside that institution and with no authority at all.
blurbs.sw_jedi: Chewbacca is two centuries old, bound by a life debt to a man half his age, and famously the one survivor left undecorated - the strongest grievance in the cast and no trace of the vice.
blurbs.sw_sith: Boba Fett is a clone of his father raised as the one copy not made for the army, and his whole method is waiting - Saturday's virtue practised perfectly, for a fee.
blurbs.sw_dyad: General Hux informs on his own side for no strategic gain and says why: he wants the other man to lose. Saturday's vice named precisely by the one holding it, without noticing.

octa_extras.blurb: The west arm sits on 06h - sunrise. Cyan is the pale blue-green sky before the sun clears the horizon, and its mood is Hope: the emotion that looks forward.
The east arm sits on 18h - sunset. Red-orange is the burning evening sky, and its mood is Longing: the emotion that looks back. Hope and Longing face each other across the dial as dawn faces dusk.

cures: Humility cures Pride - the center heals itself.

articles_note: articles[theme][body] = {base, variants}: base = 3-4 left-aligned paragraphs (blank-line separated) weaving the entity with its day, color, hour mood, virtue and vice, anchored in the owner's image; variants = one short paragraph per pointer/palette combination (hexa_primary, hexa_secondary, octa_primary, octa_secondary, cross, trio). religion = the basic seven (Freemasonry Sunday, Islam Monday, Buddhism Tuesday, Taoism Wednesday, Hinduism Thursday, Christianity Friday, Judaism Saturday - the 2026-07-12 remap moved Freemasonry off Tuesday onto Sunday, Islam off Friday onto Monday, Buddhism off Monday onto Tuesday and Christianity off Sunday onto Friday); religion_alt = the alternate seven, one per body (Mithraism/Sol Invictus Sunday, Druidism Monday, Zoroastrianism Tuesday, Shamanism Wednesday, Sikhism Thursday, Babylonian religion Friday, Voodoo Saturday); entries carry a 'name' field. Display location TBD by the owner.

sun.base:
[[The Sky]] The Sun is the only body on this dial that burns with its own fire: a seething sphere of white-gold plasma, its surface boiling in granular cells of yellow and orange, ringed by a thin fringe of flame-red corona. Everything else on the wheel — every planet, and the Moon most of all — merely returns a borrowed portion of this light.

[[On the Dial]] That is why, on the hexa paint dial, the Sun takes no arm at all: it holds the center, and its color is white-gold — the sum of every color. The six arms are sunlight decomposed; the star itself is the prism; Sunday is the source. To pin the Sun to one hue would be to mistake a part for the whole.

[[The Lesson]] Its metal is gold, the day metal that crowns the dial's top tip at noon, and its calling is the Ruler — the one seat whose cure never leaves the center, for the royal planet carries the royal pair of faces: Humility as virtue, Pride as vice, the source that heals itself or nothing does. But the center is DOUBLE, always two virtues, two vices, two moods in one seat — the dial's own yin-yang. The Sun argues it plainly: its light falls on everyone alike, which is Justice, and it serves its route without a single day of rest, until the moment that service bends into mere routine and becomes Servility. Its moods are the pair the sky itself stages — Glory at full noon and Awe when the light fails — and the cure stays home: Humility answers Pride, Justice straightens Servility.

[[The Hour]] And so Sunday rules no single hour but all of them: joy, zeal, passion, sorrow, calm and renewal all radiate from the middle, the way the day's every mood is finally some angle of the same light.

variants.hexa_primary: The home position: the center of the dial, white-gold, the source from which all six arms take their color. No hour belongs to it because every hour does.
variants.hexa_secondary: In the light palette nothing moves — the center stays the center, white-gold. If anything the symbol grows more literal: this is Newton's own white beam, caught one instant before the prism splits it into red, green and blue.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the Sun holds the noon arm still, but the wheel now crowns it in royal gold (#F0C420) — the estate of the King, power at its zenith with the Crown for its object. The source of all light seated as the source of all rule: 'by me kings reign' (Proverbs 8:15), the throne hour wearing the throne's own metal.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the noon arm is Youth — life at its blazing height — and the Sun wears its sun-yellow (#FFE800). No body fits the zenith of a life better than the one that owns the zenith of the day: strength before the descent, the morning of a man read as the noon of the sky.
variants.cross: On the cross the arms point at the year's hinges, and the Sun holds the top arm at 12h, yellow for Summer, sharing it with Jupiter. The summer solstice is the Sun's own festival — the day it stands highest, the noon of the year.
variants.trio: The Trinity returns the Sun to the center, white-gold, with only three arms around it — Faith's yellow, Love's red, Hope's blue: the painter's three primaries. The prism reading at its simplest — white light decomposed not into six moods but into the three virtues, and Sunday still the source of them all.

faces.ruler:
The Ruler face is the Sun exactly as the sky shows it, with no myth standing between the disc and the eye — the physical body that names the whole day, since Sunday still carries dies Solis in root and shape. On this face there is no god riding it and no crown resting on it; the star simply is what it is, and that plainness is itself the claim to rule: nothing needs to be added to make it the source. Every other body on the dial only returns a portion of this light; the Ruler face is the one that generates what it shows instead of reflecting it.

Its virtue is Justice, argued in the plainest possible terms — this light falls on every latitude and every creature alike, playing no favorites among the arms it feeds — but Justice at the center is watched over by Pride, the fault of believing that because the light is even, it is also owed. Its mood is Glory, the sky at full noon — the hour when the source is most obviously the source, and Pride's whisper is loudest.
faces.servant:
The Servant face is the same star, not a second body but the first one with its light taken — the Sun made to serve an eclipse instead of ruling one, standing in for every myth on the dial that needed a second, dimmer face without inventing a new one.

In a total eclipse the Moon's black disc lies exactly over the Sun, leaving only a thin, blazing corona ring and, near totality's end, one last diamond-ring glint before even that goes dark.

Its virtue is Humility — the star that generates all light, admitting for these few minutes that it can be entirely covered — but the same submission tips into Servility if it is read only as absence, as a light that has stopped mattering rather than one that is briefly spent. Its mood is Awe, the sky at midnight wearing noon's own disguise, and it is the necessary far side of Glory: the same body, remembering it can be lost.

moon.base:
[[The Sky]] The Moon is silver-gray and full-faced: dark seas pool across its upper half, pale cratered highlands fill the south, and near the bottom rim one crater still throws its rays outward like a star scratched into stone. It is a world of ash and dust that shines only because the Sun is somewhere behind you.

[[On the Dial]] Its home on the hexa paint dial is the arm at 4h, deep blue, the hour before dawn — Calm. Blue is the still color, the moonlit color, the temperature of a world asleep; and 4h is the night's last watch, when darkness is at its most complete and its most peaceful at once.

[[The Lesson]] That doubleness is the Moon's whole nature. Monday's body carries Serenity as its virtue and Fear as its vice — the same unlit world, once accepted and once dreaded. Its healer hangs straight across the dial: Mars in the working afternoon, whose Courage cures Fear, while the Moon's Serenity quells Mars' Wrath in return. The Physician is its calling — the calm hand at the night sickbed against the patient's fear — and silver its metal, the night's answer to the Sun's gold, kept at the dial's bottom tip.

[[The Hour]] Calm rules 4h because that is the hour serenity is actually tested: nothing left of yesterday, nothing yet of tomorrow, only borrowed silver light. Whoever is at peace then is at peace.

variants.hexa_primary: The home arm: 4h, deep pigment blue, Calm — the Moon presiding over the hour before dawn.
variants.hexa_secondary: The light palette keeps the Moon at 4h but tunes its blue to the prism's own primary — a purer, electric blue. Calm read not as painted stillness but as the actual color of pre-dawn light.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the Moon keeps its 03h post in the deep night, but the arm now wears lamplit ink blue (#1F5FA8) — the estate of the Scholar, the Book for its object. The body already ruled by the Physician's calm finds an easy cousin here: both keep the long night watch, one reading symptoms, the other reading pages, by the same borrowed light.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the 03h arm is the Unborn, painted moonlight silver (#C8D7F0) — the age of ancestors and the not-yet-born together. Fittingly it falls to the Moon, whose light was never its own: a body that has always stood for what is not yet lit fits the hour that belongs to those not yet born.
variants.cross: The cross is the seasons palette, and the Moon takes the 6h dawn arm, green for Spring, sharing it with Saturn. The spring equinox is the year's own daybreak — a fitting post for the body that ends every night.
variants.trio: The trio keeps the Moon at its own 4h, but the arm now reads Hope — blue, shared with Mercury — and its tip is now the very center of its hue: it guards the morning third from 0h to 8h. Fitting work for the body that ends every night: hope is the Moon's calm turned to face the coming sun.

mars.base:
[[The Sky]] Mars is the rust-colored one, scarred by a canyon system long enough to stretch across a continent, a vast dark gash torn across its equator. The planet named for war actually looks wounded — its red is the red of iron oxide, of dried blood, of an old battlefield.

[[On the Dial]] Yet on the hexa paint dial its arm at 16h is orange, not red — because the arm colors belong to the hours, and 16h is the working afternoon, the mood of Zeal. Orange is the ember-color of effort: past noon's peak but far from evening, the hours when fire is not display but fuel. Mars, the planet of drive, is exactly the body to stoke them.

[[The Lesson]] Tuesday's planet carries one fire with two uses: Courage, the flame that defends, and Wrath, the same flame let loose on its own side. The Soldier is its profession because a soldier is precisely this pair walking. And its remedy hangs straight across the dial at 4h: the Moon's Serenity quells Wrath, while Mars sends Courage back along the axis to cure the Moon's Fear — the warrior and the night-watch healing each other.

[[The Hour]] Zeal rules the afternoon because that is when work is won or lost: morning's freshness is spent, evening's rest not yet earned, and only the stubborn ember carries a task to its end.

variants.hexa_primary: The home arm: 16h, ember orange, Zeal — Mars stoking the working afternoon.
variants.hexa_secondary: In the light palette Mars stays at 16h but the ember flares to pure yellow — pigment's orange has no seat in the prism wheel, so the afternoon fire burns at light's brightest hue instead. Zeal, only hotter.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Mars holds its 15h afternoon arm, now dressed in working copper (#C87533) — the estate of the Merchant, the Coin for its object. It is a demotion the fire resents and needs in equal measure: the same drive that wins battles also counts spoils, and the hour that once meant Zeal now prices what the sword has taken.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel 15h belongs to Maturity, and Mars wears it in amber (#FFB400) — past Youth's blaze, short of the Elder's rest, the hour of a life spent doing rather than dreaming. The war-planet fits this age plainly: maturity is Courage without the glory, work continued after the applause has stopped.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Mars takes the 18h dusk arm, red for Autumn, and finally wears its own color — sharing the arm with Venus, as Ares shared everything with Aphrodite. War and love on one arm, pointing at the autumn equinox, the year's long evening.
variants.trio: The Trinity moves Mars to 20h, onto Love's red arm beside Venus — each arm's tip centers its third of the day, and this pair guards the evening from 16h to 24h. Mars finally wears its own red, and Love reads through it as protection: courage keeping watch so that what is loved can sleep.

mercury.base:
[[The Sky]] Mercury is a small cratered ball of two extremes: one face scorched amber-tan, the other pale ashen gray, the whole surface pocked with craters like a well-traveled road. It suits the planet perfectly — the innermost wanderer and the fastest of all, circling the Sun in 88 days — a slow-turning world of the harshest extremes, its days scorching and its nights freezing on the very same plain.

[[On the Dial]] Its home on the hexa paint dial is the bottom arm at 0h, purple, midnight — the mood of Sorrow. Purple is the mixed color, red mourning dissolved in blue stillness, and midnight is the mind's hour: the day is dead, tomorrow unborn, and thought runs on alone. Where better for the planet of the mind than the hour when only the mind is awake?

[[The Lesson]] Wednesday's planet carries Wisdom as its virtue and Greed as its vice — the merchant's pair, for the same cleverness that understands the world can start counting it instead. Hermes was god of merchants and of roads, and his cure comes down the longest road on the dial: Jupiter's Generosity, straight above at noon, cures Greed, while Mercury's Wisdom travels back up the axis to curb Jupiter's Excess.

[[The Hour]] So Sorrow rules midnight not as despair but as depth: the hour of accounting, when the mind weighs the day honestly because no one is watching. Mercury, who guided souls across the last border, keeps that hour.

variants.hexa_primary: The home arm: the dial's bottom at 0h, mourning purple, Sorrow — Mercury keeping the midnight watch.
variants.hexa_secondary: The light palette keeps Mercury at 0h but turns its purple to magenta — the one color missing from the rainbow, existing only where red and blue light meet. A color the mind must invent: no hue could suit Mercury better.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Mercury holds its 21h evening arm, recast in stage-velvet violet (#7A2E8E) — the estate of the Artist, the Mask for its object. The trader's cunning becomes the actor's craft with barely a change of hand: the same face that priced the day's goods by lamplight now performs behind a Mask, wisdom bent toward invention instead of accounting.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel 21h is Old Age, and Mercury wears it in dusk violet (#9C6BD4) — twilight's own shade, the hour after the day's business is done. Wisdom accrues like interest: the quickest of the planets, having spent a life in trade and travel, finally sits still long enough to be called wise instead of merely clever.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Mercury returns to the bottom arm at 0h, blue for Winter, and holds it alone — the only body that shares its arm with no one. The winter solstice is the year's midnight, and Mercury stands that watch solitary, as thought does.
variants.trio: The trio lifts Mercury off midnight to 4h, onto Hope's blue arm beside the Moon, guarding the morning third from 0h to 8h. Hope is the theological shape of Wisdom's forward look: the mind that weighed the day at midnight now stands at the morning's gate, counting what comes instead of what has gone.

jupiter.base:
[[The Sky]] Jupiter is the giant in banded robes: cream and caramel stripes wrap the whole globe, whipped into curls at their borders, and low on one side turns the Great Red Spot — a single storm wider than the Earth that has been raging for centuries. Everything about the planet is surplus: the largest body, the loudest weather, a king's wardrobe of clouds.

[[On the Dial]] On the hexa paint dial the king takes the crown position: the top arm at 12h, yellow, noon — the mood of Joy. This is no metaphor smuggled in afterward: 'jovial' literally means 'of Jupiter,' and the top of this dial is where the star's vertex points at true solar noon. The day's peak belongs to the planet of abundance.

[[The Lesson]] Thursday's planet gives with an open hand — Generosity is its virtue — and keeps giving past the point of sense, for Excess is its vice: the royal table overflowing. Its calling is the Priest and Teacher, the one who distributes what he has received; and its correction hangs at the far end of the dial's spine — Mercury's Wisdom at midnight curbs Excess, while Jupiter's Generosity pours down the same axis to cure Mercury's Greed. The full hand and the counting hand, balancing each other.

[[The Hour]] Joy rules noon because noon is the day's own generosity: the most light, the most warmth, the moment the world is given more than it asked for. Jupiter simply makes that hour a person.

variants.hexa_primary: The home arm: the dial's top at 12h, noon yellow, Joy — the king planet at the crown of the star.
variants.hexa_secondary: The light palette keeps Jupiter at the 12h crown but dresses it in green — the middle color of the spectrum, which the prism wheel seats at noon. Joy read as fullness of light rather than gold.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Jupiter holds its 09h morning arm, now in alb ivory (#EDEDE0) — the estate of the Priest, the Bell for its object — and the king finds he was already dressed for the part. Generosity given from a pulpit is still generosity given, and the Bell simply rings the hour the Sun no longer needs to.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel 09h is Childhood, and Jupiter wears it in spring green (#7CE577) — the freshest hour matched to the freshest age. Nothing suits the planet of abundance like a life still all appetite and no restraint yet learned: Childhood is Excess before Excess has a name for itself.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Jupiter keeps the top arm at 12h, yellow for Summer, sharing it with the Sun. The summer solstice is the year at its most generous — the longest light, the fullest table — and the two most royal bodies preside over it together.
variants.trio: On the Trinity Jupiter keeps its crown: the 12h arm, yellow — but the yellow is Faith's now, shared with Saturn, and the arm centers the day's third - 8h to 16h, noon at its tip. Faith reads naturally through the king planet: generosity is faith practiced with the hands, giving before any return is proven.

venus.base:
[[The Sky]] Venus is not the pale pearl of the evening sky but the truth beneath it: a globe of molten orange and red, its surface veined with bright fire like embers seen through smoke. That is the real planet under the lovely clouds — a furnace hotter than Mercury — and it is exactly the passion it stands for: the most beautiful light in the sky, burning at close range.

[[On the Dial]] Its home on the hexa paint dial is the arm at 20h, deep red, the evening — the mood of Passion. The placement is astronomy before it is poetry: Venus is the evening star, the first light to open over the sunset, and 20h is when the sky itself turns blood-red. Friday's planet rules the hours when work ends and wanting begins.

[[The Lesson]] Love is its virtue and Jealousy its vice — not love's opposite but love's shadow, the fear of losing what is loved. Its cure stands straight across the dial in the green morning: Saturn's Patience heals Jealousy, while Venus' Love flows back across the axis to dissolve Saturn's Envy. The Artist is Venus' calling — old astrology read the planet's children as musicians and lovers — and art is exactly this: passion given patience enough to become form.

[[The Hour]] Passion rules the evening because evening is when the day stops demanding and starts desiring: the light turns red, the work lets go, and what remains is what one actually loves.

variants.hexa_primary: The home arm: 20h, blood red, Passion — the evening star over the evening hour.
variants.hexa_secondary: The light palette keeps Venus at 20h and gives its red the prism's full voltage — pure red, light's own primary. Passion undiluted.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Venus holds its 18h sunset arm, now recast in iron-blood crimson (#A02020) — the estate of the Soldier, the Sword for its object — and the fit is a deliberate friction: the planet of Love drawn as the planet of the blade. Yet Jealousy already IS a kind of war fought for the heart's own territory, so the Sword only names honestly what Love's vice was always capable of.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel 18h is the Elder, and Venus wears it in ember (#FF6A3C) — the banked-down fire of a harvested life. It reframes the evening star gently: passion does not vanish with age, it settles into the Elder's ember glow, Love grown patient enough to warm a room instead of burning it.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Venus holds the 18h arm, red for Autumn, sharing it with Mars — Aphrodite and Ares together, as in the oldest gossip of the gods. The autumn equinox is the year's dusk: the harvest of what was loved, and the first cold that makes one hold it tighter.
variants.trio: Venus does not move at all: the Trinity's red Love arm is her own 20h, and Love is already her virtue — the one word belonging to both the seven pairs and the theological three. Mars joins her there, and together they guard the evening from 16h to 24h: passion and courage guarding the dark third of the day.

saturn.base:
[[The Sky]] Saturn is the only body on the dial that carries its own circle: the butter-gold globe tilts inside its broad rings, band upon band of cream and caramel, the dark divisions drawn clean between them. A planet wearing a halo of orbiting dust — or, seen with this dial's eyes, a planet wearing the year itself as a ring.

[[On the Dial]] On the hexa paint dial it takes the arm at 8h, green, the morning — the mood of Renewal. It seems a paradox to give the slowest wanderer the freshest hour, but that is the point: Saturn takes nearly thirty years to close one circle, so no body knows better that mornings return. Green is dew and growth, and Saturday's morning is the week's own renewal — the day of rest, whose planet in Hebrew is named Shabtai, after the Sabbath itself.

[[The Lesson]] Patience is its virtue, learned from its own pace, and Envy its vice — the bitter green of another's harvest, the oldest failure of those who wait. The Farmer is its calling: Cronus carries the harvest sickle, and farming is patience practiced in public — sow, then wait, and do not stare too long at the neighbor's field. The cure stands across the dial in the red evening: Venus' Love dissolves Envy, while Saturn's Patience travels back to heal Venus' Jealousy — the two slow arts, waiting and loving, mending each other.

[[The Hour]] Renewal rules 8h because the morning is where patience pays out: whatever was buried in the dark comes up green. The week's day of rest owns that hour on behalf of all the others.

variants.hexa_primary: The home arm: 8h, harvest green, Renewal — the slow planet keeping the morning of the day of rest.
variants.hexa_secondary: The light palette keeps Saturn at 8h but cools its green to cyan — morning read as sky rather than field, the pale clean light after sunrise.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Saturn holds its 06h dawn arm, and here the fit needs no argument: field green (#3E8914) — the estate of the Farmer, the Plough for its object — is simply Saturn's own calling handed back to it. Cronus already carried the sickle; the Compass only gives the same hand its plough.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel 06h is Birth, and Saturn wears it in predawn mist (#8FA8C8) — the coldest, most certain hour, when night has not quite let go. It is the dial's sharpest irony made gentle: the slowest of all the wanderers, the planet of nearly thirty patient years, is set to govern the shortest and newest of the Ages.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Saturn holds the 6h arm, green for Spring, sharing it with the Moon. The spring equinox is sowing time — the farmer's own festival — patience at the exact moment it commits its seed to the ground.
variants.trio: The Trinity promotes Saturn from the morning to the crown: the 12h Faith arm, yellow, shared with Jupiter — the two slow giants on one arm, guarding the day's height from 8h to 16h. Faith reads through Saturn as patience aimed upward: trusting a harvest that takes thirty years to come round.

sun.base:
[[The Figure]] Helios is not a god who carries the sun; he is the sun, the Titan the Greeks trusted to see everything done under the open sky — witnesses swore their oaths by him because nothing escapes the one who rides above it all. He drives the quadriga, four winged horses hauling his chariot across the heaven; he does not point at his element — he wields it.

[[On the Dial]] On the six-armed dial he takes no arm at all: Sunday sits in the center, colored white-gold. This is the founding sentence of the whole design — white light is the sum of all colors, so the six arm-hues around him are nothing but his own light decomposed. The star is the prism; Helios is what goes into it.

[[The Lesson]] Helios stands at the center of everything, and the one who stands there is the one most tempted to believe he deserves to — the star that gives all light must not mistake itself for the light's owner, for his virtue is Humility and his vice is Pride, the oldest pair, and his cure crosses no axis: the center heals itself. Yet that center is DOUBLE, two virtues, two vices, two moods in one seat, and Helios lived both faces. The all-seeing eye that witnessed the theft of Persephone and testified when no other god would is Justice itself; the driver who serves the same dawn route without thanks is the servant, and Servility would be forgetting that the route is a trust, not a chore. Phaethon's day tells the rest — the chariot in a son's proud hands is Pride, the scorched sky its Awe, and Glory is the same chariot back on its arc the very next morning.

[[The Hour]] That is also why he rules no single hour. Noon's Joy is Helios overhead, evening's Passion is Helios leaving, the pre-dawn Calm is the world holding its breath for him: every mood on the wheel is the same god at a different angle.

variants.hexa_primary: The home reading: the center of the dial, white-gold, the source from which all six moods radiate. Sunday does not sit among the days — the days sit around Sunday.
variants.hexa_secondary: In the light palette nothing about him changes — still the center, still white-gold. Every arm around him translates from pigment to beam, but white is the sum in both worlds; the source is the one point where the two readings agree.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Helios steps from the center onto the noon arm dressed now in royal gold (#F0C420) — the estate of the King, the Crown for its object. The Titan who drove the sky in a golden chariot needs no metaphor to wear a crown: 'by me kings reign' (Proverbs 8:15) fits the all-seeing charioteer as naturally as it fit any throne.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the noon arm is Youth, and Helios wears sun-yellow (#FFE800) — life's blazing height matched to the god who drives the day's own height. Phaethon's brief hour behind those reins is Youth's whole warning distilled: the zenith is glorious and merciless to anyone not seasoned enough to hold it.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross his arm at 12h is Summer, colored yellow, and he shares it with Zeus. The cross arms point at the solstices and equinoxes: this is the midsummer arm, the year's longest light, where Sunday's source and Thursday's king hold the peak together.
variants.trio: On the Trinity Helios keeps the center, and the star around him thins to three arms — Faith's yellow, Love's red, Hope's blue, the painter's own primaries. The founding sentence holds at its simplest: three virtues instead of six moods, and all of them still his one white light taken apart.

faces.ruler:
Helios is the Ruler face by the oldest right there is — not a god who carries the sun but the Titan the Greeks trusted to see everything done under the open sky, sworn by because nothing escapes the one who rides above it all.

His virtue is Justice, the all-seeing eye that testified when Persephone was stolen and no other god would speak — light that plays no favorites among what it exposes — but that same all-seeing gaze tempts Pride, the driver forgetting he only witnesses the world and beginning to believe he owns it. His mood is Glory, the chariot back on its arc at sunrise after every fall, the quadriga running true — noon's own triumph, the wheels turning exactly where they should.
faces.servant:
Phaethon is the Servant face, not another god but Helios's own son, borrowed for one disastrous day — proof that the chariot's reins can be held by anyone the light trusts, and that trust is not the same as mastery.

His virtue is Humility, though he never reaches it in the story — the lesson the fall exists to teach every reader, that inheriting the light is not the same as commanding it — while Servility is what the myth actually shows: a boy pretending mastery he was only lent. His mood is Awe, the scorched sky where the sun's ordinary route should have run — and Glory's own promise is that the chariot rides again the very next morning, in steadier hands.

moon.base:
[[The Figure]] Selene is the moon as a person — not a goddess of the moon but the light itself, driving her own chariot through the night while her brother Helios sleeps. The Greeks told how she loved the shepherd Endymion and kept him in eternal sleep: the one myth where watching over someone's night is the whole story.

[[On the Dial]] Her home is the arm at dial 4h, painted deep blue — Monday's arm, the mood of Calm, the hour before dawn. The lower half of the dial is the night, and 4h is its stillest chamber, when even the sleepless finally go quiet. Blue was the phlegmatic Moon's color in the old humors, and silver is her metal: as gold crowns the star's noon tip, silver crowns its midnight one — day metal above, night metal below.

[[The Lesson]] Her virtue is Serenity and her vice is Fear, and they are the same night twice: moonlit, the world is the calmest thing there is; unlit, it is the oldest terror. That is why she is the Physician — medieval medicine timed its cures by her phases, and the healer's calm hand is exactly what is set against the patient's fear. Across the dial Ares answers: Courage cures Fear, and Serenity quells Wrath — the soldier and the physician bound to one axis.

[[The Hour]] Calm rules the hour before dawn because that is where calm is earned. Anyone can be serene at noon; the 4h watch is serenity in the dark, with no proof yet that the sun returns — the moon holding the light until it does.

variants.hexa_primary: The home reading: the 4h arm in the painter's deep blue, Monday's Calm in the hour before dawn.
variants.hexa_secondary: The same 4h arm, but the blue turns elemental: in the light wheel blue is one of the three primaries of light itself, not a mixture. Calm read through the prism is bedrock, not blend — the night as one of the world's fundamental colors.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Selene keeps her 03h deep-night post, now in lamplit ink blue (#1F5FA8) — the estate of the Scholar, the Book for its object. The goddess who watched over Endymion's endless sleep already knew how to keep a long, quiet vigil; the Scholar's Book only gives her watching a page to read by.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel her arm is the Unborn, silver moonlight (#C8D7F0) — ancestors and the not-yet-born held in one hue. Selene, whose whole light is borrowed from a brother she never quite outshines, fits an age defined by what has not yet arrived, or has already passed beyond seeing.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross she holds the 6h arm — Spring, green — and shares it with Cronus. The arm points at the spring equinox, the dawn of the year: the dial's two quiet teachers, Serenity and Patience, keeping the year's morning together.
variants.trio: The Trinity leaves Selene on her 4h arm but renames the post: the blue now means Hope, she shares the arm with Hermes, and with the pre-dawn hour at its very tip it guards the morning, 0h to 8h. The goddess who kept Endymion's night now guards the promise that night ends — calm turned to face the sun.

mars.base:
[[The Figure]] Ares is war without the parade — the Greeks gave him a planet and a weekday while keeping him at arm's length; in the Iliad, Zeus calls him the most hateful of the gods. His sacred animals are the vulture and the war-dog, which are also the battlefield's scavengers — the same fire that wins a war feeds what follows it.

[[On the Dial]] His home is the arm at dial 16h, painted orange — Tuesday's arm, the mood of Zeal, the working afternoon. Orange is fire domesticated: not the noon blaze and not the evening blood-red, but the ember that gets things done. 16h is the hour of the second wind — effort as its own mood, the soldier's hour of drill and march rather than glory.

[[The Lesson]] His virtue is Courage and his vice is Wrath — one fire, which defends or destroys depending only on where it is pointed. His cure hangs straight across the dial in Selene's blue: Serenity quells Wrath — and in return, Courage cures Fear. The soldier and the physician share an axis because they share a battlefield.

[[The Hour]] Zeal rules the working afternoon because that is where courage actually lives. Battles are rare; the long unglamorous march toward them is daily — and the ember-orange of 16h is the hour when persistence, not fury, carries the fight.

variants.hexa_primary: The home reading: the 16h arm in ember orange, Tuesday's Zeal of the working afternoon.
variants.hexa_secondary: The same 16h arm, but the prism has no pigment orange — the ember flares to full yellow, red and green light summed. Zeal read as light is louder than zeal read as paint: the working fire at battle brightness.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Ares keeps his 15h afternoon arm, recolored in working copper (#C87533) — the estate of the Merchant, the Coin for its object. It sits oddly on the god Zeus called 'most hateful' — until one remembers that war has always had its quartermasters, and even Ares' spear point has a price stamped somewhere behind it.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel 15h is Maturity, amber (#FFB400) — and it suits the war-god better than any glory-hour would. Maturity is Courage with the shouting worn off: the discipline of the march, not the charge, is exactly what an army calls its most useful age.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross he stands at 18h — Autumn, red — and shares the arm with Aphrodite. It points at the autumn equinox, the year's dusk; the lovers whom Hephaestus once caught in a single net are bound to a single arm again, war and love ruling the season of the falling leaf together.
variants.trio: On the Trinity Ares marches to 20h and stands on Love's red arm — beside Aphrodite, as always, as the net proved. Together they guard the evening from 16h to 24h. Love reads through the war god as its garrison: the same fire that rains spears in his storm stands sentry so that what the heart keeps can sleep.

mercury.base:
[[The Figure]] Hermes is the god of everything that moves between: messages, merchants, roads, thieves, and finally souls — the only Olympian who walks freely into the underworld and back. He is never a courier retired: the winged cap and winged sandals and the caduceus of twined serpents are the marks of an errand always running.

[[On the Dial]] His home is the arm at the very bottom of the dial, painted purple — Wednesday's arm, the mood of Sorrow, midnight. Why give the quickest god the darkest post? Because Hermes is the psychopomp, the guide of souls: midnight is the day's grave and its mystery, and someone must know the way through it. Purple is the mourning color, and the bottom tip he stands on carries silver, the night's metal.

[[The Lesson]] His virtue is Wisdom and his vice is Greed — the merchant's pair, for the same cleverness that understands the world can begin merely counting it. His cure stands straight overhead: Zeus at noon, whose Generosity cures Greed — while Hermes' Wisdom, in return, curbs Excess. The dial's whole vertical axis is a conversation between the open hand and the counting one.

[[The Hour]] And Sorrow suits the hour of thought. Midnight is when the mind is most itself — accounts closed, roads empty, nothing left to trade but understanding; the god of exchange keeps the one watch where wisdom is the only currency.

variants.hexa_primary: The home reading: the midnight arm at the dial's bottom, mourning purple, Wednesday's Sorrow.
variants.hexa_secondary: The same midnight post, but the purple becomes magenta — the prism's impossible color, found in no rainbow, existing only where the eye joins the two far ends of the spectrum. No hue suits the boundary-crosser better: a color that is itself a crossing.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Hermes keeps his 21h evening arm, now stage-velvet violet (#7A2E8E) — the estate of the Artist, the Mask for its object. No god wears a mask more naturally: the trickster-messenger who guided souls and stole cattle in the same myth already knew that a face is a tool, to be put on or taken off as the errand requires.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel 21h is Old Age, dusk violet (#9C6BD4) — twilight's own hue for the god who twice crosses that border, guiding the dead across it and returning himself. Wisdom is what Old Age is finally allowed to keep, and no messenger has carried more of it back and forth.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross he keeps the bottom of the dial — Winter, blue — and he shares the arm with no one. It points at the winter solstice, the year's own midnight: the guide of souls stands alone at that door, as he always has.
variants.trio: The Trinity calls Hermes up from midnight to 4h, onto Hope's blue arm beside Selene, guarding the morning from 0h to 8h. The psychopomp is handed the opposite door: not the guide down into the dark but the herald of what comes — hope being wisdom's forward road, and roads were always his.

jupiter.base:
[[The Figure]] Zeus is the storm made into law — the sky-father who ended the age of the Titans and then had to learn to govern the unruly family he freed. His oracle at Dodona spoke through the rustling leaves of a sacred oak — the thunder-god's law arriving as sound instead of decree.

[[On the Dial]] His home is the top of the dial, the 12h arm, painted yellow — Thursday's arm, the mood of Joy at noon, the day's peak. The language remembers it: jovial literally means 'of Jupiter.' The king takes the crown position, where the real sun pours its gold straight down onto his arm; and Thursday is Guruvar in the Vedic week, the day of Brihaspati, teacher of the gods — the king's arm is also the teacher's.

[[The Lesson]] His virtue is Generosity and his vice is Excess — the royal table that feeds everyone and then cannot stop. It is one hand that never closes, whether giving or reaching for a second portion. His cure stands at the opposite tip of the dial: Hermes' midnight Wisdom curbs Excess, while Zeus' Generosity, poured straight down the same axis, cures Greed.

[[The Hour]] Joy rules noon because noon hides nothing: everything stands in full light, shadows at their shortest, the world at its most given. Generosity is exactly that — the noon of the heart — and its excess is what happens when the feast refuses to admit the afternoon exists.

variants.hexa_primary: The home reading: the noon arm at the dial's top, royal yellow, Thursday's Joy at the day's peak.
variants.hexa_secondary: The same crown position, but the prism turns his yellow to green — light's own primary at the top of the wheel, and the band the human eye sees most keenly. In the light reading the king wears the color of maximum sight: nothing at noon escapes him.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Zeus keeps his noon crown-arm, now alb ivory (#EDEDE0) — the estate of the Priest, the Bell for its object. It fits better than it first seems: Zeus spoke through the rustling oak at Dodona, an oracle's voice from a king's throat, and the Bell is only that same voice given a clearer instrument.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel noon is Childhood, spring green (#7CE577) — an unlikely hue for the sky-father until his own appetite is recalled: the royal table that cannot stop feeding everyone is Excess with a child's whole heart, wanting more simply because more is good.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross he returns to the top: 12h, Summer, yellow, sharing the arm with Helios. It points at the summer solstice — the year's longest light — where Thursday's king and Sunday's source hold the peak together, as throne and sun have always shared a summit.
variants.trio: On the Trinity Zeus keeps the top: the 12h arm, yellow — but the yellow is Faith's now, and he shares it with Cronus, the father he overthrew. Together they guard the day's height from 8h to 16h. Faith reads strangely and rightly through the king: the keeper of oaths stands on the arm of what every oath is made of.

venus.base:
[[The Figure]] Aphrodite was born of sea-foam, armed with nothing, and conquered everyone anyway. Her sign is the golden apple inscribed 'to the fairest' — the prize that flattered one goddess, enraged two, and burned Troy: tenderness that carries a verdict, and a war, folded inside it.

[[On the Dial]] Her home is the arm at dial 20h, painted deep red — Friday's arm, the mood of Passion, the evening. Venus is the evening star, the first light to appear at dusk, and 20h is the hour the working day releases people to one another. Red is doubly hers: the sunset's blood and the heart's color, one pigment for the sky and for the pulse.

[[The Lesson]] Her virtue is Love and her vice is Jealousy — not love's opposite but its shadow, the fear of losing what is loved; the apple she carries is proof of how quickly 'fairest' becomes a wound. Her cure stands across the dial in Cronus' morning green: Patience heals Jealousy — and her Love, in return, dissolves Envy. She is the Artist, for old astrology read Venus' children as musicians and lovers: art is love given a form that cannot be taken away.

[[The Hour]] Passion rules the evening because passion is what the day was for. Work fills the light; what the work was in service of appears when the light goes. And Love alone also belongs to the theological trio of Faith, Hope and Love — the dial's human warmth, among people, on Friday evening.

variants.hexa_primary: The home reading: the 20h arm in deep red, Friday's Passion of the evening.
variants.hexa_secondary: The same evening arm, but the red goes pure — light's first primary at full strength. In the prism world passion is not a pigment mixed on a palette but an elemental beam: the one color that needs nothing added.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Aphrodite keeps her 18h dusk arm, now iron-blood crimson (#A02020) — the estate of the Soldier, the Sword for its object. It is no idle assignment for the goddess whose golden apple was already a verdict: 'to the fairest' started the Trojan War, and Love proved capable of arming a decade of soldiers with a single word.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel her arm is the Elder, ember (#FF6A3C) — a banked, harvested warmth. The goddess born already grown, who never ages in myth, wears it as a lesson rather than a mirror: Love's fire, however it began, is asked in the end to settle into embers that still warm a room.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross she stands at 18h — Autumn, red — sharing the arm with Ares. It points at the autumn equinox, and the pairing is the oldest gossip on Olympus: the lovers Hephaestus once trapped in a single net now share a single arm, love and war ruling the season of ripeness and fall.
variants.trio: Aphrodite does not move: the Trinity's Love arm is her own 20h in her own red, for Love alone belongs to both sets — arm virtue and theological virtue at once. Ares joins her, and the lovers guard the evening from 16h to 24h: the third of the day when work is done and only what one loves remains.

saturn.base:
[[The Figure]] Cronus is the hardest of the seven figures to argue, and it should be. The Greeks already fused Cronus the titan with Chronos, time itself — a Titan who swallowed his own children rather than be succeeded, envy of the future given a body, and was in the end deposed exactly as time deposes every ruler.

[[On the Dial]] His home is the arm at dial 8h, painted green — Saturday's arm, the mood of Renewal, the morning. The pairing looks like a paradox — the devourer on the arm of new growth — until you see the Farmer in him: Cronus carries the harvest sickle, and in Hebrew the planet is Shabtai, named for the Sabbath itself. The slowest planet keeps the day of rest, and green is dew, growth, and the week beginning again.

[[The Lesson]] His virtue is Patience and his vice is Envy — the farmer's pair: he sows and waits, and eyes the neighbor's field. Envy is the bitter green of another's harvest, renewal's own color turned sour; Cronus swallowed his children because he could not endure being succeeded — envy of the future itself. His cure stands across the dial in Aphrodite's evening red: Love dissolves Envy — and his Patience, in return, heals Jealousy.

[[The Hour]] Renewal rules the morning because renewal is patience paid out. The scythe cuts so the field can grow again; the night ends because it was waited through. On the day of rest the green arm says quietly: what you did not seize will grow back — and that is the whole cure.

variants.hexa_primary: The home reading: the 8h arm in harvest green, Saturday's Renewal of the morning.
variants.hexa_secondary: The same morning arm, but the green becomes cyan — the color of the early sky rather than the leaf. In the light reading renewal belongs to the air, not the field: the morning before anything has been planted at all.
