variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel her noon arm is Youth, and the Matriarch wears the wheel's sun-yellow (#FFE800) — a curious hue for the herd's oldest authority until her own decades are remembered: a matriarch's confidence was built young, on a first crisis survived, and Youth here names the original memory her whole later Glory was built from.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross the Matriarch stands at 12h on the Summer arm, yellow, its center pointed at the summer solstice — the year's longest light, the season a herd's memory is tested least, water everywhere. She shares the arm with the Mentor: the dial's two teaching elephants, matriarch and old tusker, holding the year's brightest spoke together.
variants.trio: On the Trinity the Matriarch keeps the center, and the court around her narrows to three arms — Faith yellow, Love red, Hope blue. It is the oldest thing memory does: it is faith practiced without proof, carried forward on nothing but the conviction that the water will be where it was before.

faces.ruler:
The Ruler here wears the name Matriarch — the Sun's own calling, and the only profession on this dial's cousin themes that fits her without translation: she leads not by force but by accumulated knowing, thirty wet and dry seasons carried in one skull.

Her virtue is Justice, argued by the column itself — a route chosen for six lives at once, with the drought-year memory to back it. Her vice is Pride, the same authority hardened past the point of doubt; her mood is Glory, the height of a long and unbroken correctness, noon for an elephant who has been right about the water for longer than anyone now living can remember being wrong.
faces.servant:
The Servant here is not a lesser twin of the Matriarch but her own history made visible: Memory, the remembered ruler, the matriarch who led before this one and taught her the map before dying of it — old ivory, worn molars, a life spent walking toward water only she recalled.

Her virtue is Humility, argued by the stillness itself — an entire living herd pausing its migration to stand over what is only bone. Her vice is Servility, the risk in any inherited authority: deferring to what the old matriarch would have done long after her actual knowledge has stopped applying. Her mood is Awe: the eclipsed sun — the black disc and gilded corona that mark every dual pair on this dial — stands for the light failed at exactly the hour a leader is lost, with Glory carried forward in the matriarch who leads now instead of the one who once did.

moon.name: Allomother
moon.base:
[[The Figure]] She is the Moon's child and Monday's figure, and the herd hands her the job without dispute — a young female not yet a mother of her own, keeping the night watch over someone else's calf, precisely the care that gives 'allomothering' its name and its oldest home in this theme's whole claim: memory is a job the whole family shares, not just the one at its head.

[[On the Dial]] Her home arm sits at dial 04h in deep blue (#002FFF), the mood called Calm — the hour before dawn. No hour suits a night-watcher better: it is the stillest, darkest stretch, when the calf is most defenseless and the watcher must be steadiest, moonlight the only argument against the dark.

[[The Lesson]] The Moon's virtue is Serenity and its vice is Fear — the same night lit or unlit, and the image holds both: a young female standing guard alone in open country, where lions hunt, must feel exactly the fear she is not permitted to show. Straight across the dial at 16h the Musth answers, and the two cure each other: Courage cures Fear, Serenity quells Wrath — the calm watcher borrows the bull's nerve when the dark turns dangerous, and the raging bull, on his better days, borrows her steadiness.

[[The Hour]] Calm rules the pre-dawn hour because that is when it is hardest and worth the most: the last watch before light, when a tired young aunt must hold her post exactly as long as the moon does.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 04h arm in deep blue (#002FFF), the Calm of the hour before dawn — the Allomother's night watch, as the base article tells it.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism wheel keeps her at 04h but sharpens the blue to #0040FF — pigment's hushed moonlight becomes light's electric one. The watch is unchanged; only the disc above the sleeping calf burns a little brighter.
variants.octa_primary: The Allomother takes the deep-night arm in lamplit ink blue (#1F5FA8) — the Walk of the Scholar, the Book its object. Allomothering is itself an apprenticeship, a young female learning the herd's whole craft of care years before she raises a calf of her own — the Scholar's patient study, performed as a night-watch instead of a page.
variants.octa_secondary: On the Ages wheel her arm turns moonlight silver (#C8D7F0) — the Unborn — and no figure on the dial sits it more plainly: she guards a calf that is not hers, practicing tomorrow's motherhood tonight, the Unborn's ancestors-and-not-yet held quite literally in her own curved trunk.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross the Allomother moves to the 06h arm — Spring, green, pointed at the vernal equinox — and shares it with the Elder. Watcher and rememberer on one spoke, and rightly: the young aunt who guards the calf tonight is the old cow who will remember the water forty years from now.
variants.trio: The Trinity keeps the Allomother at 04h but renames her watch: the blue arm now means Hope, shared with the Caller, guarding the morning from 0h to 8h. No calling earns the word more plainly — the whole night watch is hope with a body wrapped around it, holding on until the sky changes.

mars.name: Musth
mars.base:
[[The Figure]] He is Mars' child and Tuesday's figure, and the theme gives Mars its most literal body on the whole dial: musth is not a mood but a chemistry. Hormone levels spike to many times their baseline and temporin streams visibly from the temporal glands — the most dangerous animal on the savanna running on a fury he did not choose and cannot fully steer.

[[On the Dial]] His home arm sits at dial 16h in ember orange (#DC9600), the mood called Zeal — the working afternoon. The hour is right for him precisely because musth is not a single charge but weeks of sustained heat — the discipline, if it can be called that, of staying furious for a working season rather than a single dawn.

[[The Lesson]] His two faces sit in the one gland: temporin is Wrath made visible, streaming down a face that in every other season is placid; but musth is also the surest sign of a bull in his prime — the confidence to challenge, to breed, to hold ground — which is Courage's own chemistry, differently spent. Straight across the dial at 04h waits the Allomother, and the two cure each other: Serenity quells Wrath, Courage cures Fear — her steadiness is the only thing in the herd a musth bull will sometimes, briefly, still respect.

[[The Hour]] Zeal rules the afternoon because that is exactly musth's own season — not a dawn's outburst but weeks of banked, working fire, the discipline of a fury that must be carried rather than merely felt.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 16h arm in ember orange (#DC9600), the Zeal of the working afternoon — the banked fire of the base article, weeks of musth rather than one furious hour.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism keeps him at 16h but burns the ember up to pure yellow (#FFFF00) — in light, red and green fused. The temporin still streams; Newton's reading only makes the working fire glow hotter.
variants.octa_primary: The Musth bull shares his working-afternoon arm with copper (#C87533) — the Walk of the Merchant, the Coin its object, the hardest turn on the whole dial for a body running on pure hormonal war. Yet musth is also precisely what raises a bull's standing to breed and hold ground — status the herd trades in as surely as any coin, dominance itself the currency the Coin's Walk was always describing.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel his arm turns amber (#FFB400) — Maturity — and the hue names musth exactly: not a young bull's single tantrum but weeks of banked, working fury, the confidence of a bull finally old enough to challenge, breed, and hold his ground.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross the Musth stands at 18h — Autumn, red, pointed at the autumnal equinox — sharing the spoke with the Reunion. Bull and greeting-cow on the same arm, the oldest pairing on the dial reread: autumn's red is blood and rose in one color, temporin and the trunk-embrace both belonging to it.
variants.trio: On the Trinity the Musth moves to 20h, onto Love's red arm beside the Reunion, and the pair guard the evening from 16h to 24h. It explains the fury better than fear does: musth exists because reproduction matters enough to run this hot for — courage wearing a hormone instead of armor.

mercury.name: Caller
mercury.base:
[[The Figure]] She is Mercury's child and Wednesday's figure, and the theme rewrites Hermes without losing him: the messenger god's word no longer rides winged sandals, it rides the ground itself. Elephants call in infrasound too low for the human ear, a rumble that travels for kilometers through earth and bone alike, and they listen for it through their own feet.

[[On the Dial]] Her home arm sits at dial 0h — midnight, the bottom of the wheel — in Tyrian purple (#542E85), the mood called Sorrow. The hour fits the physics as much as the myth: the ground carries a rumble farthest when the world above it has gone still and cool, the same quiet that makes midnight the hour honest news travels — a call for help, a warning about poachers, word that the far waterhole finally failed.

[[The Lesson]] The listening foot and the spread ears are the whole ethics of the arm at once: Wisdom is knowing which rumble matters and which to let pass unanswered; Greed is the temptation to keep a voice this powerful for one herd only — to call the good grazing toward your own family and let word of a rival's drought go unspoken. Straight up the axis at noon the Mentor answers, and the two correct each other: Generosity cures Greed, Wisdom curbs Excess — the old tusker's open teaching answers the closed ear, the careful listener steadies the overgenerous table.

[[The Hour]] Sorrow rules midnight because the ground's own honesty rules it too: the hour the world is quiet enough to hear the truth, whatever the truth happens to be that night.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the midnight arm at 0h in Tyrian purple (#542E85), the Sorrow of a call that travels farthest when the world goes still — the base reading.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns her purple to magenta (#BD00BD) — the one hue found in no rainbow, invented by the eye where the spectrum's two ends meet. Fitting for a message human senses cannot hear at all: at midnight the Caller wears a color that, like her rumble, exists just past where ordinary perception reaches.
variants.octa_primary: The Caller shares her midnight arm with stage-velvet violet (#7A2E8E) — the Walk of the Artist, the Mask its object. Infrasound too low for any human ear is its own performance, a message composed entirely in vibration and sent through bone and earth alike to a herd she cannot see — Hermes's winged word, restaged as a rumble underfoot.
variants.octa_secondary: On the Ages wheel that hour deepens to dusk violet (#9C6BD4) — Old Age — and the Caller wears it as long practice: knowing which rumble is worth sending and which to let pass unanswered is a wisdom built only after years of listening through the ground with her own feet.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross the Caller keeps the bottom arm at 0h — Winter, blue, pointed at the winter solstice — and she alone shares it with no one. The year's midnight belongs to a single figure: the one voice that can stand at the bottom of the wheel, entirely alone, and still be heard for kilometers.
variants.trio: The Trinity lifts the Caller off midnight to 04h, onto Hope's blue arm beside the Allomother, guarding the morning from 0h to 8h. The move names what the call actually is: every rumble sent into the ground is hope with a destination, sound thrown toward a herd that may or may not still be listening.

jupiter.name: Mentor
jupiter.base:
[[The Figure]] He is Jupiter's child and Thursday's figure: Guruvar, the day of Brihaspati who IS Jupiter, the guru of the gods, and the bachelor herd's own school is the closest thing the savanna has to a classroom. An old bull disciplines a rearing adolescent by simple physical weight — a trunk laid across the shoulders until he settles — the lesson delivered as correction, not punishment.

[[On the Dial]] His home arm is the top of the dial, 12h, in bright yellow (#F8E600), the mood called Joy — and 'jovial' literally means 'of Jupiter'. The placement argues itself: an old bull's sheer bulk teaches half the lesson before he has said or done anything at all, presence as the first and oldest form of instruction.

[[The Lesson]] His virtue is Generosity — years of accumulated calm laid across a stranger's calf rather than spent defending his own status — and his vice is Excess, the same bulk that teaches so easily also apt to dominate rather than mentor, discipline curdling into simple size winning by intimidation. Straight down the axis at midnight the Caller answers, and each cures the other: Wisdom curbs Excess, and Generosity cures Greed — the far-carrying rumble below teaches proportion to the mentor's overwhelming scale.

[[The Hour]] Joy rules noon because noon is the one hour that needs no lamp: the bachelor school in full daylight, an old bull's patience on full display, asking nothing back for the lesson it gives.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the top arm at 12h in noon yellow (#F8E600), the Joy of the day's peak — the base reading, the bachelor school in full daylight.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns his noon to green (#00DC00) — the wavelength at the summit of human sight, the brightest color the eye knows. The lesson keeps its Joy; light simply measures the old bull's presence instead of painting it.
variants.octa_primary: The Mentor takes the mid-morning arm in alb ivory (#EDEDE0) — the Walk of the Priest, the Bell its object, a seat his own bulk had already half-built: an old bull's mere presence teaches half the lesson before he says or does anything, the bachelor herd's whole schoolyard run on a patience close to liturgy.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel his arm turns spring green (#7CE577) — Childhood — and the Mentor wears it not for himself but for his pupils: the young bulls pressed gently back to earth are the actual green growth his whole calm patience exists to raise.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross the Mentor stands at 12h on the Summer arm, yellow, pointed at the summer solstice — and shares it with the Matriarch. Teacher beside leader on the year's highest spoke: the herd's two memories, one for the file and one for the bachelor school, holding the brightest light together.
variants.trio: On the Trinity the Mentor keeps the top arm at 12h, yellow — but the yellow now names Faith, his own working material, and he shares the arm with the Elder as they guard the day's height from 8h to 16h. The placement reads itself: teaching a rearing bull to stand down is faith that the lesson outlasts the fury, taught over and over until it does.

venus.name: Reunion
venus.base:
[[The Figure]] She is Venus' child and Friday's figure, and the greeting ceremony is the herd's own love letter — documented in the field for as long as elephants have been watched: bonded relatives separated for weeks or months run to close the last distance, thundering and entwining trunks as if the parting had been a wound.

[[On the Dial]] Her home arm sits at dial 20h in deep red (#B60000), the mood called Passion — the evening, when Venus herself rises as the evening star. The hour suits the ceremony exactly: reunions on the savanna cluster at day's soft edges, the heat broken, the families closing ground toward each other as the light turns warm.

[[The Lesson]] The entwined trunks are her virtue and her vice in one gesture: Love, and Jealousy — the fear, real in elephant families, that a bond this strong could be crowded out by a new calf, a new ally, a rival matriarch's family merging too close. Across the dial at 08h the Elder answers, and the two heal each other: Patience heals Jealousy, and Love dissolves Envy — the old cow teaches the reuniting family to wait out a slight, and the reunion teaches the elder that what she has is still hers to celebrate.

[[The Hour]] Passion rules the evening because that is when the herd's emotional accounts come due: the day's walking and foraging done, nothing left to do at dusk but recognize who has come home.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 20h arm in deep red (#B60000), the Passion of the evening — the base reading, the trunks winding tight as the light turns warm.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism keeps her at 20h but purifies the red to its light primary (#FF0000) — the reddest red there is, unmixed. The rumble and the entwined trunks stay exactly as loud; Newton's reading only sharpens the color of the joy.
variants.octa_primary: The reuniting cows share their evening arm with iron-blood crimson (#A02020) — the Walk of the Soldier, the Sword its object, an unlikely turn for an embrace until the ceremony's own intensity is weighed: two families thundering together after weeks apart close distance with exactly the urgency of a charge, relief and reunion closing ground the way an army closes a line.
variants.octa_secondary: On the Ages wheel their arm turns ember (#FF6A3C) — the Elder, the harvest of a life — and the reunion wears it honestly: what closes in that embrace is the gathered value of a whole relationship, months of separation harvested back into one thundering, trunk-wound moment.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross the Reunion stands at 18h — Autumn, red, pointed at the autumnal equinox — sharing the spoke with the Musth. Greeting-cow beside raging bull, the oldest pairing on the dial reread through fur and temporin: autumn's red is harvest and blood and rose at once, and it takes both figures to say the whole of it.
variants.trio: The Reunion does not move: the Trinity's Love arm is her own 20h in her own red, for love is her virtue in both sets at once. The Musth joins her, and together they guard the evening from 16h to 24h — the two most physically demonstrative bodies on the dial, one embracing, one raging, both simply love with the volume turned all the way up.

saturn.name: Elder
saturn.base:
[[The Figure]] She is Saturn's child and Saturday's figure, and no figure on the whole dial states the theme's founding claim more plainly: an elephant's life is measured in six sets of molars, and when the last set wears down, she dies. The teeth are her own hourglass, and the old ones know where the water sleeps precisely because they have run out of time left to be wrong about it.

[[On the Dial]] Her home arm sits at dial 08h in field green (#007E00), the mood called Renewal — the morning. The color argues past its own irony: green belongs to growing things, and an Elder digging in a colorless drought is renewal's driest possible test, proof that patience outlasts even a landscape that has stopped rewarding it.

[[The Lesson]] Her one color holds her virtue and her vice at once, exactly as it does for every body on this arm: green is growth — Patience, decades spent carrying a memory that a wet season always eventually pays out — and green is envy's own bitter shade, the temptation of an old cow who has earned the herd's trust to resent how easily the young ones now spend it, following her without ever having doubted the water would come. Across the dial at 20h the Reunion answers, and each cures the other: Love dissolves Envy, and Patience heals Jealousy — the reuniting family reminds the elder that being trusted is still a form of being loved, and the elder teaches the reunion that anything worth having was worth this long a wait.

[[The Hour]] Renewal rules the morning because that is when a dug well is finally judged: the water either rises with first light or it does not, and either way the Elder's whole authority — the teeth worn down for it — was staked on remembering correctly.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 08h arm in field green (#007E00), the Renewal of the morning — the base reading, water rising in the sand exactly where memory said it would.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns her morning green to cyan (#00DDDD) — the color of the clear early sky rather than of the cracked field. Renewal keeps the hour; in the light world the Elder looks up at the sky she is reading for rain before she looks down at the ground she is digging.
variants.octa_primary: The Elder takes the dawn arm in field green (#3E8914) — the Walk of the Farmer, the Plough its object, the plainest match on the whole dial: she tills dry sand exactly as a Farmer tills dry ground, both trusting a memory of rain that has not yet arrived.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel her arm turns predawn mist (#8FA8C8) — Birth — and no elder on the dial earns it more sharply: the water either rises with the first light or it does not, her whole worn authority staked, at the very hour of Birth, on a memory that must still be right.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross the Elder stands at 06h — Spring, green, pointed at the vernal equinox: sowing season, water finally easy again. She shares the spoke with the Allomother — the herd's two patient callings, one tending a sleeping calf through the night, one tending the whole family's memory through the drought.
variants.trio: The Trinity promotes the Elder from the morning to the crown: the 12h Faith arm, yellow, shared with the Mentor, guarding the day's height from 8h to 16h. The pairing is the oldest sermon the herd has: digging for water you cannot see yet is faith performed with a trunk, believed in decades before it is proven right again.

sun.name: Alpha · Omega
sun.base:
[[The Figure]] The Alpha is where every real wolf pack's founding pair sits — not a tyrant crowned by force but the parent who leads because the pack's whole structure runs through him: den, hunt, and the order pups are fed. He is the Sun's creature and Sunday's figure — the one body on the dial that needed no invented crown, only the one the morning already wears.

[[On the Dial]] On the hexa dial he takes no arm at all, the same as every other reading of the center: his color is white-gold, belonging to no single hour because every hour of the pack's day answers to him eventually — the hunt he calls, the rest he permits, the den he guards. It is worth naming, here, the wolf the internet invented and ethology never did: the Sigma, a wolf supposedly equal to the Alpha but standing outside the hierarchy altogether, a ruler without a throne. No pack has ever produced one and no plate was carved for him — he belongs to modern myth-making, not to the forest, and the dial leaves him exactly where he belongs: unrepresented, a rumor the Alpha's own seat outlives.

[[The Lesson]] Real wolf biology is gentler than the old dominance stories: an alpha is usually just a parent, and the authority he carries is closer to Justice than to conquest — the fair order of the den, the hunt shared so the whole pack eats, the pups defended without exception. That is the virtue the crown of sun-rays argues for. But the very word 'alpha' was corrupted once by captive-wolf studies into a myth of constant combat for rank, and that myth is Pride's exact shape: the throne mistaken for something won and defended rather than a duty simply carried. His height is real, earned rather than borrowed — but height still tempts whoever holds it to believe the ground below owes him the view.

The center is DOUBLE, as it is on every dial theme, and here the doubling writes itself onto the clock face more plainly than anywhere else: the ring letters already spell it, M at noon and Ω at midnight, Alpha's own initial handed the sunlit seat and Omega's the dark one. The Omega answers the Alpha precisely: the pack's lowest member, feeding the pups before he feeds himself, carrying the same authority with the crown already set down. His virtue is Humility, the crown surrendered before it was ever claimed; his vice, should the servant's calm curdle, is Servility, service without the dignity real omega wolves keep even at the bottom of the order — the pups love him best precisely because he never postures. Justice straightens Servility and Humility cures Pride, the axis crossing inside this one seat exactly as it crosses on every other Sunday reading — Glory at noon when the sun crowns him full, Awe at midnight when the same sun goes dark and only its corona is left.

variants.hexa_primary: On the painter's wheel the Alpha keeps the center of the dial, white-gold, belonging to no hour: the six pigment arms are his light decomposed, every hour's mood a piece of what the pack's leader answers for. This is his home reading — the source, not a spoke, the rock outcrop rather than any one arm of the trail.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism wheel changes every arm around him but cannot change him: the center stays white-gold, because in the light world it is literally true that white is the sum of all colors. Newton's reading only proves what the rock outcrop already claimed — the crown of rays was never one hue among six.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the Alpha holds the noon arm in royal gold (#F0C420) — the estate of the King, the Crown for its object — and no seat fits him more plainly: he already wears the sun's own crown, the leader who rules not by force but because the whole pack's order runs through him. 'By me kings reign' could be his own motto, the throne hour finally wearing the throne's own metal instead of only borrowing it from the sunrise.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the noon arm is Youth, the zenith of a life, and the Alpha wears the wheel's own sun-yellow (#FFE800). No wolf in the pack fits the blazing height of Youth better than the one whose whole authority is a young pack's daily engine — strength at its peak, spent generously rather than hoarded, before any thought of the descent the Elder already knows.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross the Alpha stands at 12h on the Summer arm, yellow, its center pointed at the summer solstice — the year's longest daylight, the height any lookout could ask for. He shares the arm with Beta: leader and teacher on one spoke, the pack's first rank and its second holding the year's brightest hour together.
variants.trio: On the Trinity the Alpha keeps the center, and the pack around him narrows to three arms — Faith yellow, Love red, Hope blue, the painter's primaries. It is the oldest reading of leadership made plain: a leader holds only what radiates outward from him, and all three virtues are his white-gold light taken apart.

faces.ruler:
Alpha is the Ruler face by the oldest right there is in a pack — not a crown handed down but a crown that is simply where the den's authority happens to sit, carried by whichever parent the pack's survival currently runs through.

His virtue is Justice — the fair order of a real pack's hunt and den, argued by the pack's trust rather than its fear, authority as something practiced rather than merely held. That same height tempts Pride, real elevation mistaken for something he is owed rather than a duty he happens to carry. His mood is Glory, the sun's crown blazing whole — noon's own triumph, the pack fed, nothing yet asked of him that he has not already given.
faces.servant:
Omega is the Ruler's own other face — not a rival wolf but the pack's own lowest member, the same hierarchy read from its opposite end, proof the canon has always called this figure double rather than needing a second name for it. Real ethology gives the servant wolf real dignity: the omega often keeps the peace, defuses the pack's tension, and is loved by the pups precisely because he never postures.

The Omega's plate answers Alpha's precisely, but dark: the same crown, carried already surrendered, the kill left to the pups before he touches it himself.

His virtue is Humility, the crown never claimed and the kill never touched until the pups and the pack have eaten — but that same lowered posture is stalked by Servility, obedience with the dignity bled out of it, the omega reduced to nothing but the pack's cushion instead of its quiet keeper. His mood is Awe, the crowned sun gone dark — and Glory is simply the next plate over: the same crown, waiting for whichever wolf the den's order asks to carry it next.

moon.name: Luna
moon.base:
[[The Figure]] Luna is the cleanest link this theme makes: a she-wolf entirely alone, no pack anywhere in her reading — a deliberate emptiness, the quiet opposite of Alpha's crowned sun. She is the Moon's creature and Monday's figure.

[[On the Dial]] Her home arm sits at dial 04h in deep pigment blue (#002FFF), the mood the wheel calls Calm — the still, moonlit hour before dawn. No wolf image earns a color assignment more honestly: this is the hour real wolves actually howl in, the pre-dawn stillness when a lone voice carries farthest and costs the least to answer.

The howling lone wolf is folklore's oldest wolf cliché, and this theme does not apologize for using it — it simply corrects it. A howling wolf on a cliff is not baying at grief; she is locating her pack, or being located by it, across miles of country where scent runs out and sound does not. Solitude, for a real wolf, is a working condition, not a wound — dispersers travel alone for months finding new territory, and the howl is how alone stays in contact with together. The moon she calls to gives nothing back but light; the pack she is really calling does.

[[The Lesson]] Her virtue is Serenity — the stillness of a creature entirely sure of her own voice, needing no chorus to be heard — and her vice is Fear, the shadow side of every solitary hour: the cliff edge is real, the miles between her and the den are real, and not every howl is answered. Straight across the dial at 16h the Hunter answers, and the two cure each other exactly as the canon requires: Courage cures Fear, and Serenity quells Wrath — the calm voice on the cliff steadies the burning one at the kill, and the hunter's nerve is what lets the lone wolf's howl go out unafraid.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 04h arm in deep blue (#002FFF), the Calm of the hour before dawn — the cliff-edge howl, as the base article tells it.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism wheel keeps her at 04h but sharpens the blue to #0040FF — pigment's muted night becomes light's electric one. Same cliff, same Calm; the moon above her simply burns colder and clearer.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Luna's cliff-edge arm turns lamplit ink blue (#1F5FA8), the estate of the Scholar, the Book for its object — an unlikely seat for a howling wolf until the hour is weighed: hers is the deep-night voice that reads the wind and the miles the way a scholar reads a page, patient study rather than blind cry.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the same deep-night arm is the Unborn, ancestors and the not-yet-born together, and Luna's coat turns moonlight silver (#C8D7F0) — fitting for a howl that answers no living voice at all, only the pack that might be out there and the pack that once was, both held in the same silvered call across the dark.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Luna moves to the 06h arm — Spring, green, pointed at the vernal equinox — and shares it with the Elder. The lone howler and the old watcher on one spoke, and rightly: both keep a vigil the rest of the pack sleeps through, and both are proven right only by morning.
variants.trio: The Trinity keeps Luna at 04h but renames her watch: the blue arm now means Hope, shared with the Scout, and it guards the morning from 0h to 8h. No wolf on the dial earns the word more honestly — hope is what a howl actually is, a voice sent out believing the pack is close enough to hear it.

mars.name: Hunter
mars.base:
[[The Figure]] The Hunter is the pack's warrior at the one moment that matters — not a march or a howl but the leap itself, the pursuit closing on an elk that has turned at bay. He is Mars' creature and Tuesday's figure, the red planet's oldest calling handed to the pack member whose work is danger.

[[On the Dial]] His home arm sits at dial 16h in ember orange (#DC9600), the mood called Zeal — the working afternoon, fire banked to a heat you can actually hunt by. The placement is exact rather than romantic: this is not the dawn ambush of legend but the long grinding pursuit that real wolf hunts actually are, run down over miles before the final closing leap.

An elk turning at bay is not a helpless animal — a set of antlers and a well-placed hoof kill wolves every season, and real wolf packs choose their target with exactly that same caution: not the strongest animal in the herd, but the one whose weakness has already been read. The Hunter's courage is calculated, not reckless, which is the whole difference between a warrior and a brawler.

[[The Lesson]] His virtue is Courage — the leap taken anyway, against an animal that can kill him — and his vice is Wrath, the same drive with the calculation burned out of it, aggression for its own sake rather than the pack's next meal. Straight across the dial at 04h waits Luna, and the two heal each other: Serenity quells Wrath, and Courage cures Fear — the hunter's nerve is what lets the lone howl go out unafraid, and the cliff's calm is what keeps the leap from becoming a rampage.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 16h arm in ember orange (#DC9600), the Zeal of the working afternoon — the banked fire of the chase, the base article's own leap.
variants.hexa_secondary: In the light palette the Hunter stays at 16h but the ember flares to pure yellow — pigment's orange has no seat in the prism wheel, so the afternoon chase burns at light's brightest hue instead. Zeal, only hotter.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the Hunter's leap lands on the 15h arm in copper (#C87533), the estate of the Merchant, the Coin for its object — a strange trade for a warrior until the hunt is counted honestly: every calculated leap is itself a transaction, an elk's life weighed against the pack's fed winter, the coin here paid in meat rather than metal.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that same afternoon arm is Maturity, and the Hunter wears the wheel's own amber (#FFB400) — the color fits him better than any other body could claim it: this is no dawn cub's ambush but a grown wolf's calculated strength, courage seasoned by miles already run and elk already read correctly.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross the Hunter takes the 18h dusk arm, red for Autumn, and finally wears his own color — sharing the arm with the Mate, as the pack's warrior and its bonded pair have always shared the same protection. Chase and devotion on one arm, pointing at the autumn equinox, the year's long evening.
variants.trio: The Trinity moves the Hunter to 20h, onto Love's red arm beside the Mate — each arm's tip centers its third of the day, and this pair guards the evening from 16h to 24h. The Hunter finally wears his own red, and Love reads through him as protection: courage keeping watch so that what is loved can sleep.

mercury.name: Scout
mercury.base:
[[The Figure]] The Scout works alone and ahead, reading the ground before the pack ever sets foot on it. He is Mercury's creature and Wednesday's figure — messenger and pathfinder, the exact job description Hermes has always carried, handed here to the pack member whose legs are built for it.

[[On the Dial]] His home arm sits at the dial's bottom, midnight, 0h, in Tyrian purple (#542E85), the mood called Sorrow. It is a stranger fit than it first looks: midnight is the accounting hour, and the scout is the one who has actually walked the ground the pack will trust by morning — his information is the currency the whole night's decision runs on, weighed out alone in the dark before anyone else has to.

Real dispersing wolves and scouting pack members read country the way a merchant reads a market — wind for scent, snow for tracks, silence for danger — and the intelligence gathered on a solitary ridge is worth exactly what it is honestly reported. A scout who exaggerates the good ground or hides the bad one is not protecting the pack; he is hoarding what was never his to keep.

[[The Lesson]] His virtue is Wisdom — reading the wind and the tracks for what they actually say, not what would flatter him to report — and his vice is Greed, the temptation to keep the good find to himself a little longer than the pack needs him to. Straight up the axis at 12h Beta answers, and the two correct each other: Generosity cures Greed, and Wisdom curbs Excess — the teacher's open hand answers the scout's closed one, and the scout's careful reading of the ground keeps the teacher's table from ever promising more than the land can give.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the midnight arm at 0h in Tyrian purple (#542E85), the Sorrow of the day's ground fully walked and fully reported — the base reading.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns his purple to magenta (#BD00BD) — the one hue found in no rainbow, a color the eye invents where the spectrum's two ends meet. Fitting for the pathfinder: at midnight he wears a color that exists only in the reading he alone did, wind and track turned to knowledge no one else walked far enough to gather.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the Scout's windswept ridge turns to the 21h evening arm in stage-velvet violet (#7A2E8E), the estate of the Artist, the Mask for its object — an odd trade for a creature who works entirely alone, except that every scout's reading of the wind is itself a kind of performance staged for an audience of one pack waiting below, the mask being the scout's own unreadable face while he decides what signal to give.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the same evening arm is Old Age, and the Scout's coat turns dusk violet (#9C6BD4) — a fitting hue for the pack member whose whole worth is accumulated experience, the miles of wind and track already read, wisdom carried the way an old wolf carries scars rather than youth's raw legs.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross the Scout keeps the bottom arm at 0h — Winter, blue, pointed at the winter solstice — and he alone shares it with no one. The year's midnight belongs to a single figure: the one wolf on the dial built to walk alone in the dark and still bring back a true report.
variants.trio: The Trinity lifts the Scout off midnight to 04h, onto Hope's blue arm beside Luna, guarding the morning from 0h to 8h. The move names the pathfinder's true engine: every scouting run is hope with a direction on it — the ground read alone in sorrow at midnight becomes, by morning, the road the whole pack trusts.

jupiter.name: Beta
jupiter.base:
[[The Figure]] Beta is the pack's second seat: the correction of a teacher, not the punishment of a tyrant — discipline given without menace, authority that instructs rather than merely dominates. He is Jupiter's creature and Thursday's figure — the second-in-rank, teacher and regent, exactly the king-teacher role Brihaspati holds among the Vedic gods on this same day.

[[On the Dial]] His home arm is the top of the dial, 12h, in bright noon yellow (#F8E600), the mood called Joy — 'jovial' literally means 'of Jupiter'. The color explains the doctrine: discipline given generously, without cruelty, is itself a kind of gift — correction as instruction, not as fear.

A real Beta wolf is often the one who actually raises the litter closest, second only to the breeding pair, patient with young that test every boundary they can find. That patience under provocation is the whole art of the second rank: enough authority to correct, never so much that correction turns into cruelty.

[[The Lesson]] His virtue is Generosity — the file of yearlings taught rather than merely dominated, discipline handed down as a gift — and his vice is Excess, the second-in-command's own oldest temptation: the teacher's authority curdling into the tyrant's, correction overused until it stops teaching anything. Straight down the axis at 0h the Scout answers, and each cures the other: Wisdom curbs Excess, and Generosity cures Greed — the scout's careful reading of what the pack actually needs keeps Beta's discipline from overreaching, and Beta's open-handed teaching keeps the scout's private knowledge from staying private.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the top arm at 12h in noon yellow (#F8E600), the Joy of the day's peak — the teacher's own hour, the base reading.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns his noon to green (#00DC00) — the wavelength at the summit of human sight, the brightest color the eye knows. Beta's hour keeps its Joy; light simply measures the lesson's peak instead of painting it.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Beta's teaching arm turns alb ivory (#EDEDE0), the estate of the Priest, the Bell for its object — a natural seat: the second-in-rank who corrects a yearling without cruelty is already the pack's own clergy, ringing discipline the way a bell calls a congregation rather than driving it.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that same morning arm is Childhood, and Beta wears the wheel's spring green (#7CE577) — exact fitness rather than irony: no wolf on the dial stands closer to the pack's actual children than the one whose whole calling is raising the litter, patient with a Childhood that tests every boundary it can find.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Beta stands at 12h on the Summer arm, yellow, pointed at the summer solstice — and shares it with the Alpha himself. Teacher beside leader on the year's highest spoke: the pack's first rank and its second, holding the brightest hour together.
variants.trio: On the Trinity Beta keeps the top arm at 12h, yellow — but the yellow now names Faith, his own working material, and he shares the arm with the Elder as they guard the day's height from 8h to 16h. The placement reads itself: faith is what a teacher hands down to yearlings who cannot yet see why the lesson matters.

venus.name: Mate
venus.base:
[[The Figure]] The Mate carries the theme's one image with no hierarchy in it at all: the crossed-neck embrace, no ornament, no myth. He is Venus' creature and Friday's figure: wolves bond for life, and this theme draws that fact without the kitsch a lesser telling would reach for.

[[On the Dial]] His home arm sits at dial 20h in deep red (#B60000), the mood called Passion — the evening, Venus' own hour as the evening star. The placement fits without strain: this is the hour the day's working structure softens into its private one, and a real breeding pair's bond is the structural fact the whole pack's order is quietly built on.

Wolf monogamy is not sentiment layered on top of biology — the breeding pair's stability is the pack's actual foundation, the den the whole hierarchy protects, the reason an Alpha leads at all. A breeding pair that does nothing but stay bonded is doing the most structurally important thing in the entire pack.

[[The Lesson]] His virtue is Love — the crossed necks, the closed eyes, trust total enough to stop watching the horizon — and his vice is Jealousy, love's own shadow rather than its opposite: the mate-guarding aggression a real bonded pair can turn on any wolf, even their own, who strays too near the den. Straight across the dial at 08h the Elder answers, and the two heal each other: Patience heals Jealousy, and Love dissolves Envy — the old wolf's stillness teaches the bonded pair to trust the waiting, and their devotion teaches the old wolf that what he built is still being tended.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 20h arm in deep red (#B60000), the Passion of the evening — the base reading, the crossed-neck embrace's own hour.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism keeps him at 20h but purifies the red to its light primary (#FF0000) — the reddest red there is, unmixed. Passion in Newton's world is not a pigment but a wavelength, and the bonded pair's evening burns in it.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the Mate's crossed-neck embrace shifts to the 18h sunset arm in iron-blood crimson (#A02020), the estate of the Soldier, the Sword for its object — an edge this gentle image does not obviously wear, until the mate-guarding is remembered: a bonded pair defends its den and its partner with exactly a soldier's ferocity, the crimson naming the jealousy their love can turn to blade.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that sunset arm belongs to the Elder, the harvest of a life, and the Mate's coat deepens to ember (#FF6A3C) — fitting, since two wolves who have crossed necks year after year are themselves a harvest, the years of devotion gathered into the one bond a pack's whole structure was quietly built to protect.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross the Mate stands at 18h — Autumn, red, pointed at the autumnal equinox — sharing the spoke with the Hunter. Devotion beside courage, as in every real pack: autumn's red is harvest and hunt and hearth at once, and it takes both figures to say so.
variants.trio: The Mate does not move: the Trinity's Love arm is his own 20h in his own red, for love is his virtue in both sets at once. The Hunter joins him, and together they guard the evening from 16h to 24h — the den's devotion and the kill's courage over the same dark hours, one keeping what is loved fed, the other keeping it safe.

saturn.name: Elder
saturn.base:
[[The Figure]] The Elder sits apart from the pack's play, patience and time his whole calling now. He is Saturn's creature and Saturday's figure, the old gray wolf watching from just outside the game he can no longer join.

[[On the Dial]] His home arm sits at dial 08h in harvest green (#007E00), the mood called Renewal — the morning, the day of rest. It is a hard color for a figure this still to earn, and he earns it anyway: renewal belongs to the pack playing in the distance, not to him directly, and his stillness is what makes room for it.

Real wolf packs age their elders out of the hunt long before the hunt is done with them — an old wolf's teeth wear down, his stride slows, and the pack's survival increasingly does not include him at the kill. What remains is a kind of watching that asks nothing back — patience that reaches for nothing in return.

[[The Lesson]] His virtue is Patience — decades of it, with no urgency left to perform — and his vice is Envy, green in its bitterest key: the temptation, watching a game he can no longer play, to begrudge the pack the very youth he once had and can no longer claim. Straight across the dial at 20h the Mate answers, and each is the other's cure: Love dissolves Envy, and Patience heals Jealousy — the devotion of the bonded pair is what an old wolf's stillness was always protecting, and his patience is the proof that what they built outlasts either of them.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 08h arm in field green (#007E00), the Renewal of the morning — the pack at play he watches from the base reading.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns his morning green to cyan (#00DDDD) — the color of the clear early sky rather than of the field. Renewal keeps the hour; in the light world, the color names the sky over the game he can no longer join rather than the field itself.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the Elder's stone seat turns to the dawn arm, 06h, in field green (#3E8914), the estate of the Farmer, the Plough for its object — a fitting trade for stillness: a Farmer's whole work is patience sown into ground he may not live to harvest, precisely the discipline of an old wolf who tends a pack's future from the sidelines rather than the game.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the dawn arm is Birth, and the Elder wears predawn mist (#8FA8C8) — a pointed irony rather than a comfort: the oldest body on the dial seated at the youngest hour of a life, his own frosted muzzle a reminder that every Birth the pack celebrates is itself the beginning of the same long arc he is nearly done walking.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross the Elder stands at 06h — Spring, green, pointed at the vernal equinox: the season the pack's next litter is born. He shares the spoke with Luna — the old watcher and the lone howler together, the two patient figures who keep a vigil the rest of the pack sleeps through.
variants.trio: The Trinity promotes the Elder from the morning to the crown: the 12h Faith arm, yellow, shared with Beta, guarding the day's height from 8h to 16h. The pairing is the oldest lesson in the pack — patience is faith performed with stillness, every season endured a wager that what was built outlasts the one who built it.

sun.name: Ancient of Days · Son
sun.base:
[[The Figure]] The seat is doubled the way scripture itself doubles it: Daniel's Ancient of Days, robed white as snow with hair like pure wool, seated on a throne of fire — and John's Christ at the same supper table, on his knees with a towel at his waist, washing a disciple's feet. One throne, two testaments, and the dial keeps them as one seat because the Bible already tells the story that way: the king who is also the servant, majesty answered by its own self-lowering.

[[On the Dial]] On the hexa dial this figure holds no arm: home is the center, white-gold, the sum of every hue the six spokes carry. As the Ancient of Days he practices Justice, argued by the small book held open on his knee rather than clutched shut — but that same throne is stalked by Pride, the crown mistaking itself for the light rather than its seat. As the Son he practices Humility, the crown set down before it was ever contested — but the same self-lowering is stalked by Servility, obedience with no will behind it. The canon's own scale of self runs between two named extremes on either side of this seat, and scripture puts a third point at its exact zero: not the man who hates himself into the pit, but the one who gives himself away out of love while never once denying who he is — the same hands that could have held a scepter instead hold a basin.

[[The Hour]] That is also why this figure keeps no hour. Every mood of the day passes through the throne without settling into it: Glory at noon, when the throne blazes whole, and Awe when the light fails over a bowed head — the crown always the next plate over, waiting to be worn again.

variants.hexa_primary: On the painter's wheel this seat keeps the center of the dial, white-gold, belonging to no hour: the six pigment arms are the throne's own light taken apart, each mood — Zeal, Sorrow, Joy, Passion, Renewal, Calm — a piece of the glory the throne holds whole. This is the home reading: the fire at the center of the window, not a lancet along its rim.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism wheel changes every arm around the throne but cannot change it: the center stays white-gold, because in the light world white is, quite literally, every color at once. Newton's spectrum only proves in the laboratory what Daniel's vision already saw in fire — a light too whole to be one hue among six.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the throne steps onto the noon arm in royal gold (#F0C420), the estate of the King, the Crown for its object — Daniel's Ancient of Days needs no fresh argument for this seat, robed already in the color the wheel now names outright: 'by me kings reign' (Proverbs 8:15), the throne hour finally wearing its own metal.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the noon arm is Youth, the zenith of a life, and the same seat wears sun-yellow (#FFE800) — fitting less for the ancient robe than for the serving Christ across the same figure, an eternal life read at its blazing height rather than its ending, strength offered rather than spent before any thought of descent.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross this seat stands at 12h on the Summer arm, yellow, its center pointed at the summer solstice. It shares the arm with Solomon — throne and temple on one spoke, the Ancient of Days and the wisest of kings holding the year's longest light together.
variants.trio: On the Trinity the throne keeps the center, and the court around it narrows to three arms — Faith yellow, Love red, Hope blue. It is the oldest reading of this seat made plain: a throne that gives its light away holds nothing but what radiates outward from it, and all three virtues are the Ancient of Days' own white-gold light, taken apart.

faces.ruler:
The Ancient of Days is Sunday's own seat before the dial ever asked it to share the throne — Daniel's vision of him seated, 'his clothing was white as snow, the hair of his head like pure wool, his throne was fiery flames' (Daniel 7:9), the oldest image scripture has of authority that does not need to raise its voice.

His virtue is Justice, argued by an open book rather than a sealed one — judgment made in the light rather than behind it — but the same throne is stalked by Pride, majesty forgetting it is meant to radiate rather than to be simply admired. His mood is Glory, the throne blazing whole: noon's own triumph, nothing yet asked of him that the flame has not already given freely.
faces.servant:
The Son as Servant is the Ancient of Days' own other face, not a separate throne but the same authority read at its lowest point — John's supper-table scene, where the teacher and lord 'rose from supper... laid aside his outer garments, and taking a towel, tied it around himself' (John 13:4) before washing his own disciples' feet.

His virtue is Humility, the crown never even shown in this plate because it has already been set down before the scene begins — but that same self-lowering is stalked by Servility, obedience with no will left inside it, service that comes from fear rather than love. His mood is Awe, the light failing at exactly the hour the towel comes out — and Glory is simply the next plate over: the same throne, waiting, its fire not put out but merely banked.

moon.name: Mary
moon.base:
[[The Figure]] Mary is the Moon's own figure before the dial ever counted the phases — not by resemblance but by scripture's own naming: 'a great sign appeared in heaven: a woman clothed with the sun, with the moon under her feet, and on her head a crown of twelve stars' (Revelation 12:1). No other figure in this set has a planet named as their own attribute this directly; Monday's blue was always going to be hers.

[[On the Dial]] Her home arm sits at dial 04h in deep blue (#002FFF), the same hour the dial already calls Calm. The color needed no invention: this is the blue the Church has painted her in for a thousand years, and the dial's own pre-dawn hour turns out to be her hour too — the night not yet given over to morning, the hush before an answer is asked for. Her virtue is Serenity, spoken in one line — 'let it be to me according to your word' (Luke 1:38) — but it begins as Fear: 'she was greatly troubled at the saying' (Luke 1:29), until Gabriel's own words dissolve it, 'do not be afraid, Mary' (Luke 1:30). Straight across the dial at 16h waits David, and the two mend each other the way this axis always has: his Courage cures her Fear, her Serenity quiets his Zeal down into something aimed rather than raging.

[[The Hour]] Calm rules the hour before dawn because that is when the angel comes: not at noon's crowd or midnight's dread, but in the private, unwitnessed dark where the whole answer has to be given alone. Every other mood of the week is public; hers is the one mood earned in a room with no one else in it.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 04h arm in deep blue (#002FFF), the dial's own Calm answering the hush before Gabriel speaks — the base reading.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism sharpens her blue to #0040FF — pigment's quiet night blue becomes light's electric one. The hour and the Calm hold; the light of the hour simply burns a little brighter.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Mary's crescent arm turns lamplit ink blue (#1F5FA8), the estate of the Scholar, the Book for its object — an unexpected trade for a figure known by silence rather than study, except that her whole answer to Gabriel was itself a reading: 'let it be to me according to your word' (Luke 1:38), scripture's plainest scholar of obedience.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that deep-night arm is the Unborn, ancestors and the not-yet-born together, and Mary's mantle turns moonlight silver (#C8D7F0) — the exact hue of her own calling, the one body in the set who carried the not-yet-born quite literally, the crescent already resting beneath her feet in Revelation's own vision (Revelation 12:1).
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Mary moves to the 06h arm — Spring, green, pointed at the vernal equinox — and shares it with Joseph the Farmer. The Visitation always did read as a springtime scene, two women carrying new life meeting in a hill country in bloom.
variants.trio: The Trinity keeps Mary at 04h but renames her blue arm Hope, shared with Moses, guarding the morning from 0h to 8h. No word fits her better: her whole answer at the annunciation is hope with a body, a yes given before she can see how the promise is kept.

mars.name: David
mars.base:
[[The Story]] David is Tuesday's own figure by the oldest right there is: a shepherd boy who refuses a king's armor and brings down a giant with a sling and a stone, 'you come to me with sword and spear... but I come to you in the name of the LORD' (1 Samuel 17:45). Mars is the red planet's oldest calling for a soldier, and no soldier in scripture is less romantic about it than the boy who wins by refusing the sword's advantage.

[[On the Dial]] His home arm sits at dial 16h in ember orange (#DC9600), the mood the dial already calls Zeal — the working afternoon, fire banked to a working heat rather than a dawn charge. The placement suits him: David does not fight from a soldier's rage but a shepherd's discipline, zeal for a name rather than wrath for its own sake — Saul's own armor rejected because borrowed weight is not the same as readiness. His virtue is Courage, no swagger in the readiness; his vice, should the same fire tip over, is Wrath — the very thing this story refuses to become. Straight across the dial at 04h waits Mary, and the two mend each other: her Serenity quiets his Zeal, and his Courage cures her Fear.

[[The Hour]] Zeal rules the afternoon because that is the discipline the story actually tells: not the excitement of a dawn charge but a boy walking steadily toward a giant everyone else is too frightened to face, five stones counted out and no plan beyond the first one.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 16h arm in ember orange (#DC9600), the Zeal of the sling raised at a walking pace — the base reading.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism burns his ember up to pure yellow (#FFFF00) — red and green fused into light's own heat. The hour and the Zeal hold; the stone flies the same distance.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass David's sling-arm shifts to the 15h afternoon in copper (#C87533), the estate of the Merchant, the Coin for its object — a hard trade for the boy who refused Saul's armor rather than bargain for it, yet the fight itself is a transaction plainly stated: 'I come to you in the name of the LORD' (1 Samuel 17:45), Goliath's life weighed against Israel's freedom and paid in one stone rather than borrowed steel.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that same afternoon arm is Maturity, and David wears the wheel's amber (#FFB400) — a discipline earned rather than given: not a dawn charge but a shepherd's seasoned nerve, the steady walk of someone who has already tended flocks long enough to know exactly what a sling can do.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross David stands at 18h — Autumn, red, pointed at the autumnal equinox — sharing the spoke with Adam and Eve. The oldest pairing in the sky becomes the oldest pairing in the story too: a fight fought for love of a people, and a love that will need defending.
variants.trio: On the Trinity David moves to 20h, onto Love's red arm beside Adam and Eve, and the pair guard the evening from 16h to 24h. It is the arm that explains him best: he does not fight for a crown he wants, but for a people he loves — courage as love wearing armor, the same reason the garden ever needed a guard at all.

mercury.name: Moses
mercury.base:
[[The Figure]] Moses is Wednesday's own figure by a fittingness scripture arrived at long before this dial did: an ancient Hellenistic-Jewish writer already identified him with Hermes, the very god this day already belongs to — messenger, lawgiver, the man who talked to a burning bush at midnight and came down a mountain with the Law in stone, his face left shining from the encounter (Exodus 34:29).

[[On the Dial]] His home arm sits at dial 0h — midnight, the bottom of the wheel — in Tyrian purple (#542E85), the mood the dial already calls Sorrow: the hour he spent up the mountain long enough that the people below stopped waiting and melted their own gold into a calf (Exodus 32). His virtue is Wisdom, carried down in two tablets of stone — the same wisdom that later raised the bronze serpent Nehushtan on a staff (Numbers 21:9), an emblem so close to a caduceus that antiquity noticed the resemblance to Hermes first; the vice waiting at the foot of that same mountain is Greed — not his, but the very Greed his absence uncovered, gold made into a god you can hold rather than a law you have to keep. Straight up the axis at noon Solomon answers, and the two correct each other across the dial: his Wisdom curbs Solomon's Excess, and Solomon's Generosity cures the Greed his own mountain once uncovered.

[[The Hour]] Sorrow rules midnight because that is the hour the Law had to be carried down into: not a triumphant noon but a night already gone wrong below, tablets that would later shatter once on the ground before ever reaching the camp. Wisdom, in this story, is not spared the sight of what it corrects.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the midnight arm at 0h in Tyrian purple (#542E85), the Sorrow of a mountain and a broken camp below it — the base reading.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns his purple to magenta (#BD00BD) — the one hue found in no rainbow, a color the eye invents where the spectrum's two ends meet. Fitting for the man who came back down glowing with a light no one else could look at directly (Exodus 34:30).
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Moses' tablets shift to the 21h evening arm in stage-velvet violet (#7A2E8E), the estate of the Artist, the Mask for its object — a startling trade for the Law's own author, until the descent is remembered: he came down the mountain with his face veiled, 'the skin of his face shone' so brightly the people could not look at him unmasked (Exodus 34:29-33), the Lawgiver becoming, for once, the one figure on the mountain nobody could see plainly.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the same evening arm is Old Age, and Moses wears dusk violet (#9C6BD4) — a fitting hue for the leader who led forty years in the wilderness and still only glimpsed the promised land from a distance, wisdom accumulated across an entire lifetime he would not live to spend inside its reward.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Moses keeps the bottom arm at 0h — Winter, blue, pointed at the winter solstice — and he alone shares it with no one. The mountain's summit and the year's coldest, darkest point are both places one man has to go up entirely alone.
variants.trio: The Trinity lifts Moses off midnight to 04h, onto Hope's blue arm beside Mary, guarding the morning from 0h to 8h. It is the truer reading of the burning bush: a voice out of fire that is not consumed is hope with a name attached — 'I AM WHO I AM' — spoken to a man who had every reason to expect nothing back at all.

jupiter.name: Solomon
jupiter.base:
[[The Figure]] Solomon is Thursday's own figure the way Jupiter's other names already promise: guru of the gods, Brihaspati, teacher-king — and Solomon is uniquely both king and teacher inside one life, the wisest ruler scripture ever gives a throne to.

[[On the Dial]] His home arm is the top of the dial, 12h, in bright yellow (#F8E600), the mood the dial already calls Joy. The story argues the placement by itself: asked by God for anything at all, Solomon requests only 'an understanding heart to judge your people' (1 Kings 3:9) rather than riches or a long life — Generosity practiced before it is even his to give away. But the same king who asked for wisdom over wealth later let wealth answer back: seven hundred wives, foreign altars raised beside his own temple, the kingdom's slow rot (1 Kings 11) — Excess exactly where Generosity once stood. Straight down the axis at midnight Moses answers, and each corrects the other: Moses' Wisdom curbs Solomon's Excess, and Solomon's Generosity cures the Greed his own mountain once uncovered.

[[The Hour]] Joy rules noon because noon is the one hour a king can judge in full daylight, nothing hidden and nothing yet spent — the young Solomon of the judgment scene, before the temple's gold and the seven hundred wives, still just a king who asked for the right thing first.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the top arm at 12h in noon yellow (#F8E600), the Joy of a king who asked for wisdom before he asked for anything else — the base reading.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns his noon to green (#00DC00) — the wavelength at the summit of human sight. The judgment keeps its Joy; light simply measures the peak of the story instead of painting it.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Solomon's throne shifts to the 09h morning arm in alb ivory (#EDEDE0), the estate of the Priest, the Bell for its object — a close cousin to his own calling: the king who built the Temple and asked God for 'an understanding heart to judge' (1 Kings 3:9) before wealth or long life is already scripture's own priest-king, judgment rung out like a bell rather than decreed like a sword.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that morning arm is Childhood, and Solomon wears spring green (#7CE577) — pointed rather than flattering: the throne-scene child he judges over is the literal Childhood of the pairing, and the young king who asked for wisdom before wealth was himself closer to that same green than the bloated court of seven hundred wives he would later become.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Solomon stands at 12h on the Summer arm, yellow, pointed at the summer solstice — and shares it with the Ancient of Days. Temple and throne on the year's highest spoke, wisdom and majesty holding the same noon together.
variants.trio: On the Trinity Solomon keeps the top arm at 12h, yellow — but the yellow now names Faith, and he shares the arm with Joseph, guarding the day's height from 8h to 16h. It is the truest reading of the request he made: asking for wisdom instead of riches is itself an act of faith, a king betting his whole reign on being given what he cannot buy.

venus.name: Adam & Eve
venus.base:
[[The Figure]] Adam and Eve are Friday's own figures by the oldest right of all: created on the sixth day, the first two people, the first union — 'this at last is bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh' (Genesis 2:23), the plainest love a week has ever had to tell.

[[On the Dial]] Their home arm sits at dial 20h in deep red (#B60000), the mood the dial already calls Passion — Venus' own hour, when the evening star rises exactly as the day's labor releases into the heart. Their virtue is Love, argued before either of them has done anything at all to earn it — man alone, and God's own verdict that it was not good, answered by the one companion built for exactly that. Their vice belongs to the same arm the dial already gives Friday: Jealousy, and their story carries its own seed of it even in the garden — not envy of each other but the reach for the one thing kept apart from them, the fruit set aside precisely because it wasn't theirs to have. Straight across the dial at 08h Joseph answers, and the two heal each other the way this axis always has: his Patience heals Jealousy, and their Love dissolves the Envy his own brothers once carried.

[[The Hour]] Passion rules the evening because that is what the whole garden was built for before anything went wrong in it: not the day's labor but the day's companionship, two people given to each other before either had earned the gift, in a garden that asked for nothing back.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 20h arm in deep red (#B60000), the Passion of two people given to each other before anything else in the story — the base reading, the evening star's own hour.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism keeps them at 20h but purifies the red to its light primary (#FF0000) — the reddest red there is. Passion in Newton's world is a wavelength rather than a pigment, and the garden's first evening burns in it undiluted.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the garden's joined hands shift to the 18h sunset arm in iron-blood crimson (#A02020), the estate of the Soldier, the Sword for its object — the sharpest irony this dial owns: the first two people, created for nothing but companionship, seated now beside the very blade that would guard Eden's gate against them, 'a flaming sword ... to guard the way to the tree of life' (Genesis 3:24), love's own garden fenced the moment it was lost.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that sunset arm belongs to the Elder, the harvest of a life, and Adam and Eve deepen to ember (#FF6A3C) — fitting for the first couple in every sense: theirs is the harvest every later marriage counts itself from, 'bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh' (Genesis 2:23) the oldest devotion the whole set has to gather in.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Adam and Eve stand at 18h — Autumn, red, pointed at the autumnal equinox — sharing the spoke with David. Harvest and battle both belong to this hour, and love needing a guard is as old a story as love itself.
variants.trio: Adam and Eve do not move: the Trinity's Love arm is their own 20h in their own red, since love is their virtue in both readings at once. David joins them, and together they guard the evening from 16h to 24h — the first love and its watchman, sharing the same dark hours.

saturn.name: Joseph
saturn.base:
[[The Story]] Joseph is Saturday's own figure by an image the dial already trusted before his story arrived: sheaves of wheat, Saturn's own furniture, bowing to a single upright sheaf in a dream two brothers never forgave him for having, 'we were binding sheaves in the field, and my sheaf arose... and your sheaves gathered around it and bowed down' (Genesis 37:7).

[[On the Dial]] His home arm sits at dial 08h in field green (#007E00), the mood the dial already calls Renewal — the morning, and no calling earns a morning more honestly than a man sold into slavery who rises anyway, twice: once out of the pit, once out of the prison. His virtue is Patience narrated as a whole biography rather than one trial — years enslaved, years imprisoned, before the seven lean years he alone had the wisdom to prepare Egypt for. His vice, though, belongs to the men around him rather than to him: 'his brothers... hated him... and were even more jealous of him' (Genesis 37:5-11), Envy named directly rather than merely implied. Straight across the dial at 20h stand Adam and Eve, and each heals the other: their Love dissolves the Envy his own brothers carried, and his Patience heals the Jealousy that shadows any love worth keeping.

[[The Hour]] Renewal rules the morning because Joseph's whole life is renewal repeated: sold and rising, imprisoned and rising, forgotten and rising, until the final rising is forgiveness itself — 'you meant evil against me, but God meant it for good' (Genesis 50:20), spoken to the very brothers whose envy started the story.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 08h arm in field green (#007E00), the Renewal of a man who keeps rising — the base reading.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns his morning green to cyan (#00DDDD) — the color of the clear early sky rather than the granary field. Renewal keeps the hour; even in the light world, Joseph looks up before he looks down at what he has stored.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Joseph's sheaves shift to the dawn arm, 06h, in field green (#3E8914), the estate of the Farmer, the Plough for its object — no seat fits more naturally: his own dream already bowed a field of wheat sheaves around him (Genesis 37:7), and the years of slavery and prison before Egypt's granaries opened are exactly a farmer's patience, sowing a harvest he could not yet see.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the dawn arm is Birth, and Joseph wears predawn mist (#8FA8C8) — his whole story is repeated Birth rather than one: risen from the pit, risen from the prison, risen finally to the granary door, each rising its own small dawn before the larger one arrives.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Joseph stands at 06h — Spring, green, pointed at the vernal equinox: sowing season, and his own dream was sheaves before it was ever grain in a granary. He shares the spoke with Mary — the dreamer and the woman who 'treasured up all these things, pondering them in her heart' (Luke 2:19), two people who carry a promise years before it is fulfilled.
variants.trio: The Trinity promotes Joseph from the morning to the crown: the 12h Faith arm, yellow, shared with Solomon, guarding the day's height from 8h to 16h. The pairing reads itself — sheaves bowing in a dream believed for decades before it comes true is faith performed in patience, the same faith Solomon asked God for outright.

sun.name: Abraham · Isaac
sun.base:
[[The Story]] Abraham is Sunday's figure doubled, the Sun's own covenant-bearer: God's promise to make of him a father of many nations (Genesis 17:5) is the Ruler's crown, and Moriah is the one morning that tests whether he meant it — the knife raised over Isaac, stopped mid-stroke by the angel's word, a ram given in the boy's place (Genesis 22). His readiness to give back the very son that promise depended on is the whole of Sunday's argument in one bound son and one stayed hand.

[[On the Dial]] On the hexa dial he holds no arm at all: his home is the center, colored white-gold, the sum of every hue on the wheel. That is Abraham's whole theology in one placement — a father of a multitude is not one nation among many but the point every later nation counts itself from, just as white light is not one color among six but all of them undivided. The covenant works only if every arm can trace its way back to the altar on Moriah.

[[The Lesson]] The canon makes him DOUBLE, and Genesis 22 tells it more plainly than any other Sunday reading: Abraham raising the knife is the Ruler's own Justice — the will to give even what is dearest, asked in full — shadowed always by Pride, the father who might have mistaken the test for a debt he was owed relief from. Isaac bound and unresisting is the Servant's Humility, the son who lets himself be given rather than fighting the altar; his shadow is Servility, trust gone slack into mere passivity instead of held taut like a wire. The whole trial is a scale at balance: one figure who would give his own, one figure who lets himself be given, and the angel's hand is the fulcrum, not the ram.

[[The Hour]] That is also why the seat keeps no hour of its own. Every mood of the day passes through the altar the same way it passes through the throne elsewhere on the dial — Glory when the ram is found and the knife never falls, Awe in the long climb up the mountain before either father or son yet knows how the morning ends.

variants.hexa_primary: On the painter's wheel Abraham keeps the center of the dial, white-gold, belonging to no hour: the six pigment arms are the covenant's promise decomposed, every later nation's story radiating from the altar on Moriah. This is his home reading — the source, not a spoke.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism wheel changes every arm around him but cannot change him: the center stays white-gold, because in the light world it is literally true that white is the sum of all colors. Newton's reading only proves what the altar already claimed — a father of many nations is not one hue among six.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Abraham's raised arm shifts to the noon arm in royal gold (#F0C420), the estate of the King, the Crown for its object — a fitting crown for the man promised to be 'a father of many nations' (Genesis 17:5), the covenant itself a throne every later nation counts its founding from, the ram in the thicket the first coin ever paid against that promise.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the noon arm is Youth, the zenith of a life, and Abraham wears sun-yellow (#FFE800) — fitting less for his own age than for Isaac bound beside him, a son's whole life offered back at its own blazing height before the angel intervenes and the knife is stayed.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Abraham holds the 12h Summer arm, yellow, its center pointed at the summer solstice. He shares the arm with Noah: two covenant-bearers holding the year's longest light together, one promised a nation, the other a rainbow, neither promise costing the giver anything further to keep.
variants.trio: On the Trinity Abraham keeps the center, and the altar around him narrows to three arms — Faith yellow, Love red, Hope blue. It is Moriah's own reading made plain: a covenant holds only what radiates from it, and all three virtues are the same raised hand, stayed.

faces.ruler:
Abraham is the Ruler face by the oldest right there is in the whole set — not a crown taken but a covenant given, God's own promise that through him every nation would count its blessing (Genesis 12:3, 17:5), tested on the one morning that asked him to prove he meant it.

His virtue is Justice — the will to give even what the whole promise depended on, argued by an obedience that never once looks for a way out of the altar — but that same readiness is stalked by Pride, the father who might mistake being tested for being owed. His mood is Glory, the ram found and the knife never falling: noon's own relief, the covenant intact and the mountain already past.
faces.servant:
Isaac is the Ruler's own other face — not a separate calling but Abraham's own son, bound to the same altar, proof the canon has always read this seat as double rather than needing two different covenants to fill it.

His virtue is Humility, the son who lets himself be given rather than resisting the altar — but that same stillness is stalked by Servility, trust gone slack into mere passivity instead of held taut like a wire. His mood is Awe: trust offered before it is answered, quieter than triumph — and Glory is the same seat's other face, the same altar and the same hand, the ram already in the thicket waiting to be found.

moon.name: Jonah
moon.base:
[[The Story]] Jonah is the Moon's figure and Monday's own: three nights and three days in the belly of the earth (Jonah 1:17) is the clearest descent-and-return the whole set owns, the lunar arc read as a story instead of a phase.

[[On the Dial]] His home arm sits at dial 04h in deep blue (#002FFF), the mood called Calm — the hour before dawn, the hardest watch of the night.
