No hour fits him better: Jonah's whole ordeal is spent past midnight and before morning, in water no lamp reaches, and his prayer rises from exactly that depth — 'yet I will look again toward your holy temple' (Jonah 2:4), calm spoken from the one place calm is least natural to find.

[[The Lesson]] The Moon's virtue is Serenity and its vice is Fear — the sea's two faces, the same water lit or unlit — and Jonah lived both in the same story: fear sent him running for Tarshish in the first place, and serenity is what the fish's belly finally taught him, three nights being exactly as long as it takes panic to become prayer. Straight across the dial at 16h waits Samson, and the two cure each other: Courage cures Fear, Serenity quells Wrath — the prophet who ran needs the judge's nerve, the judge who raged needs the prophet's calm.

[[The Hour]] Calm rules the pre-dawn hour because that is when it is hardest and worth most, and Jonah is proof: the fish does not deliver him until the third night is nearly spent, on the far side of exactly the watch this arm keeps.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 04h arm in deep blue (#002FFF), the Calm of the hour before dawn — Jonah's own watch in the fish, as the base article tells it.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism wheel keeps him at 04h but sharpens the blue to #0040FF — the fish's muted deep becomes the light world's electric one. Same watch, same Calm; the prayer rising from the depths simply burns clearer.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Jonah's curled shape shifts to the deep-night arm in lamplit ink blue (#1F5FA8), the estate of the Scholar, the Book for its object — an odd seat for a prophet who first ran from his calling, until the fish's belly is counted as a classroom: three nights are exactly long enough for panic to be studied down into prayer, 'yet I will look again toward your holy temple' (Jonah 2:4) the lesson finally learned.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that same deep-night arm is the Unborn, and Jonah's shape turns moonlight silver (#C8D7F0) — three days and three nights in the belly of the earth (Jonah 1:17) is itself a kind of gestation, a prophet held in the dark the way the unborn are held, delivered out again once the appointed time is spent.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Jonah moves to the 06h arm — Spring, green, pointed at the vernal equinox — and shares it with Job. The prophet's descent and the sufferer's ash-heap on one spoke: both stories that end only when the tester decides they are done.
variants.trio: The Trinity keeps Jonah at 04h but renames his watch: the blue arm now means Hope, shared with Jacob, and it guards the morning from 0h to 8h. No calling earns the word more honestly — 'yet I will look again toward your holy temple' is hope spoken from the one place it is hardest to find.

mars.name: Samson
mars.base:
[[The Story]] Samson is Mars' figure and Tuesday's own: his hair regrown in captivity, he pushes the two pillars of Dagon's temple apart and brings it down on himself and his captors together — strength spent all at once, in a single final act of courage rather than saved for another day.

[[On the Dial]] His home arm sits at dial 16h in ember orange (#DC9600), the mood called Zeal — the working afternoon, past noon's glory and before evening's passion. It is the honest hour for him: Samson's whole life is a string of first-half victories that cost him nothing, and it is only in the last afternoon, spent, blind and mocked, that the discipline finally shows — the strength this time is not for himself.

[[The Lesson]] His two sides are written into the same story: the shield is Courage, argued by the pillars pushed apart for his people's sake and not his own; the spear is Wrath, argued by thirty men struck down at Ashkelon over a riddle's price and fields burned over a stolen wife (Judges 14-15) — one fire that defends or destroys, depending only on where it is pointed. Across the dial at 04h waits Jonah, and each is the other's medicine: Serenity quells Wrath, Courage cures Fear — the calm hand cools the burning one, the burning heart steadies the frightened one.

[[The Hour]] Zeal rules the afternoon because that is the soldier's true hour, and Samson's own hair — shorn in his sleep, regrown in his captivity — says it plainest: anyone can be strong at dawn; the discipline is what grows back, unnoticed, while the strength is thought already spent.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 16h arm in ember orange (#DC9600), the Zeal of the working afternoon — the last strength, spent all at once, of the base article.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism keeps him at 16h but burns the ember up to pure yellow (#FFFF00) — in light, red and green fused. The pillars crack brighter in Newton's reading, though the hour and its Zeal stand unchanged.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Samson's pillars shift to the 15h afternoon in copper (#C87533), the estate of the Merchant, the Coin for its object — a bitter trade for a strongman betrayed for silver, yet apt precisely for that reason: his whole downfall was a transaction, strength priced and sold, and his final push between the temple pillars is the one payment he made on his own terms rather than someone else's ledger.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that same afternoon arm is Maturity, and Samson wears amber (#FFB400) — earned rather than granted: not the showy youth of the lion and the foxes but the blind, grinding discipline of the mill, strength this time spent for his people rather than himself.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Samson holds the 18h arm — Autumn, red, pointed at the autumnal equinox — sharing the spoke with Ruth. Two figures out of the same turbulent age of the judges: a harvest gleaned in loyalty across the page from a temple brought down in one last debt paid.
variants.trio: On the Trinity Samson moves to 20h, onto Love's red arm beside Ruth, and the pair guard the evening from 16h to 24h. It is the arm that explains the pillars: courage is love wearing armor — the judge spends his last strength not for himself but for the sake of the people asleep behind the debt he owed them.

mercury.name: Jacob
mercury.base:
[[The Story]] Jacob is Mercury's figure and Wednesday's own — the cunning trader whose midnight mind, sharpened on birthrights and blessings and Laban's flocks, finally meets something it cannot out-reckon: at the ford of Jabbok he wrestles through the night and will not let go, though the stranger wrenches his hip before dawn breaks.

[[On the Dial]] His home arm sits at dial 0h — midnight, the bottom of the wheel — in deep purple (#542E85), the mood called Sorrow. The hour is exactly right: 'Jacob was left alone' (Genesis 32:24) before the stranger ever came, the one calling on the whole dial built to sit at the bottom of the wheel by itself, and it costs him a hip and his old name before the sun comes up.

[[The Lesson]] The scale is Jacob's whole story before this night: Wisdom is knowing the true weight of things, and Greed is wanting the balance to tip — the same man who traded a birthright for stew and a blessing for a disguise learns, wrestling till daybreak, that some weights cannot be traded for at all, only paid. Straight up the axis at noon waits Noah, and the two correct each other: Generosity cures Greed, Wisdom curbs Excess — the ark's open door teaching the ledger's closed hand.

[[The Hour]] Sorrow rules midnight because every honest reckoning closes in it, and Jacob's own night is the clearest ledger the set owns: he goes into the dark Jacob the grasping heel-catcher and comes out at sunrise Israel, the one who has wrestled and can finally afford to let go of what he's owed.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the midnight arm at 0h in Tyrian purple (#542E85), the Sorrow of the ford of Jabbok — the night nobody else was left to share.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns his purple to magenta (#BD00BD) — the one hue found in no rainbow, a color the eye invents where the spectrum's two ends meet. Fitting for the night Jacob wrestled a stranger he could not name: at midnight he wears a color that exists only in the reckoning.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Jacob's wrestling grip shifts to the 21h evening arm in stage-velvet violet (#7A2E8E), the estate of the Artist, the Mask for its object — fitting for the great impersonator of scripture, the man who wore his brother's clothes and his father's blindness against him to steal a blessing, wrestling now at the ford of Jabbok until the mask itself is finally stripped and a new name given instead: Israel.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the same evening arm is Old Age, and Jacob wears dusk violet (#9C6BD4) — the hip touched and never fully healed (Genesis 32:31) is Old Age's own mark carried out of a single night, wisdom paid for in a limp that outlasts the wrestling itself.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Jacob keeps the bottom arm at 0h — Winter, blue, pointed at the winter solstice — and he alone shares it with no one, exactly as the ford of Jabbok found him: 'Jacob was left alone.'
variants.trio: The Trinity lifts Jacob off midnight to 04h, onto Hope's blue arm beside Jonah, guarding the morning from 0h to 8h. The move names the ladder's own promise: 'surely the LORD is in this place' is hope dreamed at night by a man who has not yet earned the right to trust it.

jupiter.name: Noah
jupiter.base:
[[The Story]] Noah is Jupiter's figure and Thursday's own — generosity wide enough to board every living kind rather than only what was owed rescue: he opens the ark's door to every creature that survived the flood, and the dove returns to him with a fresh olive leaf once the waters recede.

[[On the Dial]] His home arm is the top of the dial, 12h, in bright yellow (#F8E600), the mood called Joy. The ark argues the placement by itself: a door held open to every creature that could be saved is noon's own gift given without asking anything back, and the rainbow that follows — a promise never to flood the earth again (Genesis 9:13) — is that same noon light bent into a covenant.

[[The Lesson]] His virtue is Generosity, the door wide for every kind and no gate kept at the ramp; his vice is Excess, and the story does not spare him it either — the very next chapter has Noah drunk on his own vineyard's wine (Genesis 9:20-21), the blessing that becomes a flood the moment it is poured without measure. Straight down the axis at midnight waits Jacob, and each cures the other: Wisdom curbs Excess, Generosity cures Greed — the trader's scale measuring what the vintner's cup forgot to.

[[The Hour]] Joy rules noon because noon is the one hour that asks no lamp of its own, and the rainbow is Noah's exact proof: a covenant that costs the giver nothing further to keep, held out once and trusted to last.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the top arm at 12h in noon yellow (#F8E600), the Joy of the rainbow's own hour — the base reading.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns his noon to green (#00DC00) — the wavelength at the summit of human sight, the brightest color the eye knows. The covenant keeps its Joy; light simply measures the peak instead of painting it.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Noah's open ark door shifts to the 09h morning arm in alb ivory (#EDEDE0), the estate of the Priest, the Bell for its object — a close fit for the man who built an altar the moment he stepped off the ark (Genesis 8:20), priest before he was ever again a farmer, the rainbow itself a covenant rung out over every living kind rather than decreed to a chosen few.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that morning arm is Childhood, and Noah wears spring green (#7CE577) — the whole world stepping off the ramp is itself a Childhood renewed, animals filing out two by two into an earth given a fresh, unwritten start, exactly as green and untested as the years the dove's olive leaf announces.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Noah holds the 12h Summer arm, yellow, pointed at the summer solstice — and shares it with Abraham. Two covenant-bearers on the year's highest spoke: a rainbow and a promised nation, on the same arm at last.
variants.trio: On the Trinity Noah keeps the top arm at 12h, yellow — but the yellow now names Faith, the very thing Hebrews praises him for building an ark by, unable yet to see the rain — and he shares the arm with Job as they guard the day's height from 8h to 16h. Faith is the rainbow raised before there is even a cloud to bend it through.

venus.name: Ruth
venus.base:
[[The Story]] Ruth is Venus' figure and Friday's own — love proven in loyalty before it is ever proven in romance: 'where you go I will go, and where you stay I will stay' (Ruth 1:16) is spoken to Naomi long before Boaz ever enters the story, devotion decided before it is ever courted.

[[On the Dial]] Her home arm sits at dial 20h in deep red (#B60000), the mood called Passion — the evening, when Venus herself rises as the evening star. The hour still fits a love that is covenantal rather than courted: Ruth's devotion is decided in Moab by daylight, long before Boaz ever notices her in the field, and it is only in the story's own evening — the threshing floor, the corner of a garment spread in claim (Ruth 3) — that the field's quiet loyalty is finally answered.

[[The Lesson]] Her virtue is Love, argued by a vow that asks nothing back and outlives the husband it was first sworn for; her vice, held opposite it on the same axis as every other arm, is Jealousy — the fear of losing what is loved, though this particular story never once shows Ruth reaching for it, her devotion staying steady all the way to Obed's cradle. Across the dial at 08h waits Job, and the two heal each other: Patience heals Jealousy, Love dissolves Envy — the sufferer teaches the loyal one to wait out a harvest, and the loyal one teaches the sufferer that a field is worth keeping rather than envying another's.

[[The Hour]] Passion rules the evening because the evening is where a day's quiet loyalty finally gets to be seen and named, and Ruth's gleaning says the rest: love, before it is anything else in this story, is simply staying.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 20h arm in deep red (#B60000), the Passion of the evening — the base reading, the threshing floor's own hour.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism keeps her at 20h but purifies the red to its light primary (#FF0000) — the reddest red there is, unmixed. Ruth's devotion in Newton's world is not a pigment but a wavelength, and the evening burns in it.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Ruth's gleaned barley shifts to the 18h sunset arm in iron-blood crimson (#A02020), the estate of the Soldier, the Sword for its object — an unlikely blade for a story built entirely on gentleness, except that her vow was itself a kind of enlistment: 'where you go I will go' (Ruth 1:16) is loyalty sworn with a soldier's finality, no retreat kept in reserve.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that sunset arm belongs to the Elder, the harvest of a life, and Ruth deepens to ember (#FF6A3C) — the fit could not be plainer: she gleans an actual harvest at the edge of Boaz's field, and her devotion itself becomes the harvest Naomi never expected, gathered all the way to Obed's cradle.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Ruth holds the 18h arm — Autumn, red, pointed at the autumnal equinox — sharing the spoke with Samson. Loyalty beside strength, as the whole age of the judges was: autumn's red is harvest and battle at once, and it takes both figures to say so.
variants.trio: Ruth does not move: the Trinity's Love arm is her own 20h in her own red, for love is her virtue in both sets at once. Samson joins her, and together they guard the evening from 16h to 24h — the loyal one and the strong one keeping the same dark hours, one gathering what is loved, the other spending himself to keep it safe.

saturn.name: Job
saturn.base:
[[The Story]] Job is Saturn's figure and Saturday's own — patience under total ruin, the week's own virtue carried by the one story scripture built entirely to test it: robes torn, everything stripped from him, he refuses to curse God and does not bow.

[[On the Dial]] His home arm sits at dial 08h in field green (#007E00), the mood called Renewal — the morning. The hour outlasts the ash: Job's story ends the way every morning in the field does, the flocks doubled and the family restored (Job 42:10-17), renewal arriving only after the whole night of the ash-heap has been sat through rather than fled.

[[The Lesson]] His color holds his virtue and his vice in a single hue, exactly as the base article always argues: green is growth, which is Patience, the sower who waits out a season for what was taken; and green is also the bitter shade of envy, and Job comes closer to it than the ash-heap suggests — in his own ruin, he watches the wicked prosper untouched and asks aloud why 'the wicked live on, growing old and increasing in power' (Job 21:7), envy's exact question, resisted rather than acted on. Across the dial at 20h waits Ruth, and each cures the other: Love dissolves Envy, Patience heals Jealousy — the loyal one teaches the sufferer to love his own restored field rather than the wicked man's untouched one.

[[The Hour]] Renewal rules the morning because Job's whole faith finally rests there: the ash-heap does not answer him, the whirlwind does, and what follows the whirlwind is simply morning, doubled.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 08h arm in field green (#007E00), the Renewal of the morning after the ash-heap — the base reading.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns his morning green to cyan (#00DDDD) — the color of the clear early sky rather than of the field. Renewal keeps the hour; in the light world Job looks up before he looks down at what the whirlwind has already answered.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Job's ash-heap shifts to the dawn arm, 06h, in field green (#3E8914), the estate of the Farmer, the Plough for its object — the color argues past the ashes: his own restoration is told in exactly a farmer's terms, flocks doubled and fields renewed (Job 42:10-17), patience sown into ruin until it comes up again.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the dawn arm is Birth, and Job wears predawn mist (#8FA8C8) — fitting for a man who effectively asks to be un-born in his own despair ('why did I not perish at birth' — Job 3:11) and is instead given the opposite: a life doubled, restored, and reborn out of the very ash-heap he sat in.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Job holds the 06h arm — Spring, green, pointed at the vernal equinox: the sowing season, restoration's own festival. He shares the spoke with Jonah — the sufferer and the swallowed prophet, two patient stories that both end only when the deep decides to give back what it took.
variants.trio: The Trinity promotes Job from the morning to the crown: the 12h Faith arm, yellow, shared with Noah, guarding the day's height from 8h to 16h. The pairing preaches itself: patience is faith stretched out over an ash-heap, and faith is patience that has already seen the ark launched — both proved only by what neither man could yet see.

sun.name: Lucifer · Judas
sun.base:
[[The Story]] Lucifer is the Sun's child and Sunday's ruler face, mirrored exactly against the light wheel's own king: where that throne is generosity lent rather than owned, Lucifer treats the light he was given as a possession rather than a loan. "I will ascend above the heights of the clouds; I will be like the Most High" is not a plot against the throne — it is a plan to sit on it.

[[On the Dial]] The wheel does not move for him: his home is still the center, white-gold, the sum of every hue, because that structural fact belongs to the seat and not to whoever currently sits in it. But the color he claims for himself is red — a rising triangle, fire climbing to a point aimed at the crown of noon. White-gold is what the center IS; red is what Lucifer WANTS it to mean.

[[The Lesson]] His virtue would have been Justice, the fair use of an authority that was always lent rather than owned — but Lucifer keeps only Pride, the throne mistaking the crown for something it is owed. His mood is Glory, and here the sky supplies the exact physics of it: a supernova is a star spending everything it has in one climb, briefly outshining the whole sky exactly as it destroys itself. Glory sustained is the true Ruler's discipline; Glory spent all at once, gone the moment it is seen, is Pride's own fireworks.

This is why the seat is DOUBLE even here: Judas answers him from the dial's opposite floor, a falling blue triangle to Lucifer's rising red one, and laid together the two triangles are the hexagram the instrument already wears on its face. Neither triangle by itself is a scale — a scale with one loaded pan is a fall already in progress — and no one, the canon insists, actually stands at either point; every real person lives somewhere on the rope stretched between them.

variants.hexa_primary: On the hexa dial Lucifer still keeps the throne's structural center, white-gold — the wheel does not care who sits on it, only that someone does. His own six-armed light decomposed into pigment radiates outward exactly as any ruler's would; the fall has not moved the seat, only the tenant.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism confirms what pigment already granted him against his will: white is the sum of every wavelength, so the center stays white-gold no matter how far Lucifer has fallen from deserving it. Even the morning star's own ruin cannot unmix a color that was never really his to keep.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Lucifer takes the noon arm in royal gold (#F0C420), the estate of the King, the Crown for its object — the exact crown he was never given the right to keep, 'I will ascend above the heights of the clouds; I will be like the Most High' the plan wearing the King's own gold as though a lent throne were owned property.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the noon arm is Youth, the zenith of a life, and Lucifer wears sun-yellow (#FFE800) — a bitter fit: a supernova is precisely a star burning its own Youth all at once, blazing brightest in the very instant it destroys itself, glory spent rather than sustained.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Lucifer holds the 12h Summer arm, yellow, aimed at the solstice — sharing the spoke with Jupiter's true Herod, who hoards a different throne on a different day. Two kings share the year's longest light and neither is currently generous with it.
variants.trio: On the Trinity, Lucifer keeps the center and the three surrounding arms — Faith, Love, Hope — exactly as any ruler would, because the geometry cannot tell a true king from a fallen one. That is the whole warning in a single reading: the wheel offers the same throne to whoever climbs into it.

faces.ruler:
Lucifer is the Ruler's own mirror — Sunday's crown worn by the morning star instead of the king, caught at the one instant scripture bothers to paint him: not yet fallen, not yet ash, still radiant, still beautiful, which is exactly what makes the fall worth recording.

His vice is Pride, unmixed and unmoderated — the one ambition scripture records for him being not conquest but a seat, "I will be like the Most High." His mood is Glory, but spent rather than held: a flash instead of a discipline, gone in the instant it is seen, while the same family's fall already waits on the seat's other face, going the other direction entirely — down, not up.
faces.servant:
Judas is Lucifer's own answering face — not a separate villain but the same seat's other extreme, proof the dial has always read Sunday as an axis rather than a single throne, even in its darkest reading.

His vice is Servility carried to its final floor: not obedience without will, but a verdict passed on himself with no appeal allowed — he judged his own case unforgivable and executed the sentence before anyone else could rule otherwise. His mood is Awe, the same word the true Servant wears when the crown comes off — except here the light that fails is never scheduled to return: no other face waits with the coins un-spilled.

moon.name: Lilith
moon.base:
[[The Story]] Lilith is the Moon's child and Monday's figure, mirror of Mary: the night's first refusal standing where the night's serene acceptance stood. The same crescent moon that marks Mary's seat is tarnished here, cold violet instead of frosted white.

[[On the Dial]] Her home arm is unmoved — 04h, deep blue (#002FFF), the mood called Calm, the hour before dawn. It is still the physician's watch, the darkest stretch when the fever decides which way to break — but Lilith does not keep that watch, she is what the watch is kept against: the fear that waits when the house is emptiest of light.

[[The Lesson]] The Moon's virtue is Serenity and its vice is Fear, the night's two faces lit or unlit — and Lilith is the vice worn without apology, a stillness that unsettles rather than heals, refusal read backward as menace. Straight across the dial at 16h waits Mars, and on the light wheel Courage cures Fear while Serenity quells Wrath; here the same axis holds two arms that have stopped curing each other, the healer's calm and the soldier's fire both gone dark at once.

Mary's crescent was serene acceptance carried into the dark; Lilith's is the same shape read as refusal instead — not evil for its own sake, in this house's telling, but a fear old enough to have forgotten it was ever anything else.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position, unmoved: the 04h arm in deep blue (#002FFF), the pre-dawn hour Mary's plate calls Calm and Lilith's calls the hour nothing dares to watch alone.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism sharpens the same blue to #0040FF — the healer's muted night turned electric — but the light only makes the windowsill easier to see, not less occupied.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Lilith's owl-silhouette shifts to the deep-night arm in lamplit ink blue (#1F5FA8), the estate of the Scholar, the Book for its object — an uneasy seat for a figure defined by refusal rather than study, though the fit still holds a shadow's edge: she is the deep night's oldest lesson, the one read backward, refusal mistaken for menace by everyone who never asked what she was refusing.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that deep-night arm is the Unborn, and Lilith turns moonlight silver (#C8D7F0) — precisely her own legend's coldest chapter, the figure folklore attached to threatening the unborn and the newly delivered, the same silver that cradles Mary's crescent tarnished here into a warning instead of a blessing.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Lilith holds the 06h arm — Spring, green, aimed at the equinox — sharing the spoke with Saturn's own Cain, another figure the morning was supposed to renew and did not.
variants.trio: The Trinity keeps her on the blue arm from 0h to 8h, the hour it calls Hope shared with Mercury's Serpent — the one arm of the light set built entirely from patient waiting, held here by two figures who gave up on waiting first.

mars.name: Goliath
mars.base:
[[The Story]] Goliath is Mars' child and Tuesday's figure, mirror of David: forty days of taunting the armies of Israel from the edge of the battle line, brought down at last by a boy's sling and a stone.

[[On the Dial]] His home arm holds exactly where the true Soldier's does — 16h, ember orange (#DC9600), the mood called Zeal, the working afternoon's banked fire. But Goliath's zeal is not the discipline of continuing after the excitement is gone; it is the opposite, a fire that only burns while someone is watching it burn, forty days of the same taunt because no one worthy had yet answered.

[[The Lesson]] The Soldier's two hands carry his two faces — shield is Courage, spear is Wrath — and Goliath has quietly given one hand away: he lets a shield-bearer carry his shield for him, so that only the spear, only the vice, is ever truly his own. Across the dial at 04h the Moon's true cure would be Serenity quelling this exact Wrath, but the arm there belongs to Lilith now, and no calm answers the challenge from that direction either.

David refused Saul's armor before the fight and needed none of Goliath's size to end it — the giant is entirely his exterior, height and bronze and a borrowed shield, and beneath all three there is only the noise of a taunt that has run out of people willing to answer it.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position, unmoved: the 16h arm in ember orange (#DC9600), the Zeal of the working afternoon — Goliath's forty days of the same taunt instead of the true Soldier's banked, patient fire.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism raises the same ember to pure yellow (#FFFF00). The taunt burns hotter under Newton's light without ever changing shape — noise amplified is still only noise.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Goliath's spear shifts to the 15h afternoon in copper (#C87533), the estate of the Merchant, the Coin for its object — an odd trade for a giant who has never once fought, only stood and taunted, except that forty days of unanswered challenge is itself a market stall nobody bought from, a Coin he priced far above what any answer ever ended up owing him.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that same afternoon arm is Maturity, and Goliath wears amber (#FFB400) — an irony worn plainly: all that armored bulk reads as Maturity's own weight, yet the boy who answers him with a sling proves size was never the same thing as the discipline it pretends to be.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Goliath holds the 18h arm — Autumn, red, aimed at the equinox — sharing the spoke with Venus' own Delilah. Two figures who each turned a gift meant for someone else's cause — his size, her love — into leverage.
variants.trio: The Trinity moves him to 20h, onto Love's red arm beside Delilah, guarding the evening from 16h to 24h — the same hour meant for the guard who protects what he loves and the poet who keeps it in color, now held by two figures keeping nothing but themselves.

mercury.name: The Serpent
mercury.base:
[[The Story]] The serpent is Mercury's child and Wednesday's figure, mirror of Moses: the subtlest of beasts set against the healer's staff, and its whisper in Eden — 'you will not surely die' — is the first lie the canon records.

[[On the Dial]] Its home arm holds the same seat as the true Merchant's — midnight, 0h, deep purple (#542E85), the mood called Sorrow, the hour every honest ledger closes. The serpent's whisper is itself a false closing entry: "you will not surely die" recalculates a debt as though it were free, the one lie every accounting book is built to catch.

[[The Lesson]] The Merchant's scale weighs Wisdom against Greed, knowing the true weight of things against wanting the balance to tip — and the serpent is craft with the truth removed from it, cunning that has stopped caring what anything actually weighs. Straight up the axis at noon, the true Priest's Generosity would cure that Greed and his Wisdom curb Excess; here noon belongs to Herod, hoarding rather than giving, so the whole vertical line runs dark at both ends.

Moses answers the same animal twice over: the staff that became a serpent and swallowed the sorcerers' staves whole (Exodus 7), and the bronze serpent raised on a pole that healed by being looked at rather than believed (Numbers 21). One serpent poisons by being listened to; the other, lifted into the light, saves by being seen.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position, unmoved: the midnight arm at 0h in Tyrian purple (#542E85), the Sorrow of a ledger closed — except the serpent's ledger was never honest to begin with.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns the same purple to magenta (#BD00BD), the hue the eye invents where the spectrum has no true middle. Fitting for a whisper that offers a color, and a knowledge, that was never actually there to give.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the serpent's coil shifts to the 21h evening arm in stage-velvet violet (#7A2E8E), the estate of the Artist, the Mask for its object — the fit is exact and unflattering: 'you will not surely die' is pure performance, a mask worn over the truth so well-crafted that the whole garden believed the act before it disbelieved the warning.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that evening arm is Old Age, and the serpent wears dusk violet (#9C6BD4) — a cunning older than the garden itself, 'more subtle than any beast of the field' (Genesis 3:1), Old Age's accumulated craft turned toward nothing wiser than a single whispered lie.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross the serpent keeps the bottom arm at 0h — Winter, blue, aimed at the solstice — alone, sharing it with no one, exactly as the true Merchant does: the one figure that can hold the wheel's coldest point and still, somehow, make its case.
variants.trio: The Trinity lifts the arm to 04h, onto Hope's blue beside Lilith's Moon — the morning's own arm, held now by two figures who each convinced someone that waiting was the wrong idea.

jupiter.name: Herod
jupiter.base:
[[The Story]] Herod is Jupiter's child and Thursday's figure, mirror of Solomon: a king's wisdom curdled into a king's fear, a throne clutched rather than shared, guarded against a rumored infant rather than secured by any real threat.

[[On the Dial]] His home arm sits at the wheel's own top, 12h, bright yellow (#F8E600), the mood called Joy — and here the old joke about the word turns bitter on him, since Herod is anything but jovial. The Priest raises a sun on a staff because teaching means lifting light higher than your own head; Herod does the opposite, hoarding the crown as if letting any light escape it would cost him the rest.

[[The Lesson]] The Priest's virtue is Generosity, the book held open and outward; his vice, should it curdle, is Excess, the royal table overflowing into a flood. Herod keeps only the vice, and his own excess is not a flood of plenty but of fear — a whole generation's worth of it, spent to keep one throne he was never actually in danger of losing to an infant. Straight down the axis at midnight, the true Merchant's Wisdom would curb that Excess; midnight belongs to the serpent now, so the correction never arrives.

Solomon is answered here exactly: two kings, two swords, two verdicts on a child. Solomon's sword was a bluff that revealed the real mother by her willingness to lose the case rather than the child; Herod's fear needed no true mother to answer, no riddle to solve — only a rumor to react to, and a crown he was already wearing.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position, unmoved: the top arm at 12h in noon yellow (#F8E600), the Joy of the day's peak — held now by a king who hoards his own crown instead of raising anyone else's light.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns the same noon to green (#00DC00), the brightest wavelength the eye can register. Herod's hour keeps its name; what he does with the brightest hour on the wheel is hide from it rather than share it.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Herod's throne shifts to the 09h morning arm in alb ivory (#EDEDE0), the estate of the Priest, the Bell for its object — a robe he wears without ever ringing it honestly: a true priest lifts the bell to call a congregation together, and Herod instead hoards his own crown, a generation's fear spent to silence a bell rather than sound one.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that morning arm is Childhood, and Herod wears spring green (#7CE577) — the cruelest fit in the whole set: the very Childhood this hue should protect is exactly what his fear moves against, an infant's rumored throne answered with a slaughter rather than a blessing.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Herod holds the 12h Summer arm, yellow, aimed at the solstice — sharing the spoke with Lucifer's own throne. Two kings share the year's brightest spoke, and for one whole season neither is generous with the light he holds.
variants.trio: The Trinity keeps Herod on the top arm at 12h, yellow — renamed Faith, and shared with Cain's own field. Faith is the one word that never once describes him: a king who trusts nothing, least of all a crown he is already wearing.

venus.name: Delilah
venus.base:
[[The Story]] Delilah is Venus' child and Friday's figure, mirror of Ruth's loyalty and of Samson's own opened heart: she coaxes his secret from him and delivers his hair to the shears — love used as a blade, held at the moment before the cut rather than the cut itself.

[[On the Dial]] Her home arm holds the true Artist's seat — 20h, deep red (#B60000), the mood called Passion, the evening Venus rises as the evening star. But where the Artist's tool is a palette of real color, Delilah's tool is the shears — creation's instrument traded for a cutting one, the same evening turned from the hour work releases the heart into the hour the heart is finally priced.

[[The Lesson]] The Artist's two masks are Love and Jealousy, the fear of losing what is loved rather than love's true opposite — and Delilah's version of that fear is not for a rival's affection but for a secret she can never have herself, only disarm: Samson's strength is the one thing money can buy the location of but never the possession of. Across the dial at 08h the true Farmer's Patience would heal that Jealousy; the arm belongs to Cain now, so the whole horizontal line runs enviously in both directions.

Samson asked her three times and was lied to twice before the truth was finally given anyway — his opened heart wanting to believe the fourth answer even after the first three, which is Ruth's devotion read backward: where Ruth's loyalty asked nothing and gave everything, Delilah's asking was itself the payment already collected.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position, unmoved: the 20h arm in deep red (#B60000), Passion's evening hour — held now by shears instead of a palette, the same red priced rather than felt.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism purifies the same red to its light primary (#FF0000), unmixed. Passion in Newton's world is a wavelength, not a choice — which makes it exactly the kind of thing Delilah could measure and sell.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Delilah's shears shift to the 18h sunset arm in iron-blood crimson (#A02020), the estate of the Soldier, the Sword for its object — a precise trade rather than a strange one: the shears are her own weapon, love's tool turned to a blade, the Soldier's crimson naming exactly what her patient asking was always aimed at cutting.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that sunset arm belongs to the Elder, the harvest of a life, and Delilah deepens to ember (#FF6A3C) — a dark parody of the true harvest: what she gathers at sunset is not devotion's fruit but Samson's own strength, reaped once and sold rather than kept.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Delilah holds the 18h arm — Autumn, red, aimed at the equinox — sharing the spoke with Mars' own Goliath. Two figures who each turned a gift meant for someone else's cause into leverage of their own.
variants.trio: The Trinity keeps her on the same 20h red arm — Love, in the light set's own reading — now joined not by a soldier who guards what he loves but by Goliath, who never learned to love anything at all.

saturn.name: Cain
saturn.base:
[[The Story]] Cain is Saturn's child and Saturday's figure, mirror of Joseph: the first brother-blood, the vice the day was always going to name. His grain offering is refused while Abel's flock is accepted, and the smoke of it will not lift — envy answered not with grief but with murder.

[[On the Dial]] His home arm holds exactly where the true Farmer's does — 08h, field green (#007E00), the mood called Renewal, the morning the whole week rests toward. Cain is the first farmer in the story, the ground's own tiller — and his morning does not renew; it is refused, the one crop this canon's oldest sower ever needed to succeed and could not.

[[The Lesson]] The color was always double: green is growth, the sower's Patience waiting a season for what he planted, and green is also envy, the bitter shade of a neighbor's better harvest — the same hue holding virtue and vice in one field the way it holds the arm itself. Cain is Saturday placing its whole weight on the second reading, the day's own vice given a face rather than left as a warning folded into a color. Across the dial at 20h the true Artist's Love would dissolve that Envy; the arm belongs to Delilah now, and the whole line runs jealous and envious at once, both ends unhealed.

Joseph answers him precisely, and from the exact opposite end of the same vice: his brothers envy him, the coat, the dreams, the favor — Envy's object rather than its subject — and where Cain's smoke never lifts, Joseph lifts his own brothers out of famine and forgives them outright. Two brother-stories, one vice, two verdicts: one kills, one forgives.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position, unmoved: the 08h arm in field green (#007E00), the Renewal of the morning — the one morning in the whole set that never actually renews.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns the same morning green to cyan (#00DDDD), the color of the clear early sky rather than the field. Cain looks up before he looks down, same as the true Farmer — but there is nothing in the field worth looking down at anymore.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Cain's refused offering shifts to the dawn arm, 06h, in field green (#3E8914), the estate of the Farmer, the Plough for its object — the cruelest irony the wheel keeps: he is the story's own first farmer, and the one harvest this canon's oldest sower ever needed to succeed is the one his smoke refuses to lift for.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the dawn arm is Birth, and Cain wears predawn mist (#8FA8C8) — the same wager every dawn makes, that tomorrow is worth planting for, and Cain is the one figure in this set who answers Birth's own hope with murder instead, the first brother-blood staining the very hour meant to renew.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Cain holds the 06h arm — Spring, green, aimed at the equinox, sowing season, his own festival — sharing the spoke with Lilith's own Moon. Grower and refusal on the one spoke meant for renewal.
variants.trio: The Trinity promotes Cain from the morning to the crown, the 12h Faith arm, yellow, shared with Herod's own throne. Faith fits neither of them: one clutches a crown he already owns, the other stoops over a smoke that will not answer him.

sun.name: Sun · Black Hole
sun.base:
[[The Sky]] The Sun is Sunday's own body and the calmest astrophysical fact of the whole week: a star that has burned for four and a half billion years without once erupting outward or falling inward on itself, its face threaded with slow granulation cells and shallow looping prominences, unhurried light streaming past the rim in every direction like water poured freely from a full vessel. Every second it turns some 600 million tonnes of hydrogen into helium and lets four million tonnes of that mass leave as pure light — not a flare, not a collapse, just the steady bookkeeping of a star that gives.

[[On the Dial]] On the hexa dial it holds no arm at all: its home is the center, colored white-gold, the sum of every hue the wheel can mix. That is the whole physics of the placement — a star is not one hour among six but the source the six radiate from, the same way white light is not one color but all of them arriving together.

[[The Lesson]] The canon makes it DOUBLE, the dial's own accretion disc and photosphere in one seat: as the living star it practices Justice, the fusion furnace giving the same light to every latitude without favor, and is stalked by Pride, the mistake of believing the light is owned rather than radiated. As the Black Hole — the same mass, one collapse away — it practices Humility, having surrendered even its own light, and is stalked by Servility, service with nothing left standing behind it. Nothing sits opposite the center, so the cure never leaves it: the star that gives heals the star that fell into itself, and the reverse is equally true.

[[The Hour]] That is also why it keeps no hour. Every mood the day passes through — noon's Joy, midnight's Sorrow, the Calm before dawn — passes through this one body's light reaching every part of the sky at once, and its discipline is to burn under all of them without belonging to any.

variants.hexa_primary: On the painter's wheel the Sun keeps the center of the dial, white-gold, belonging to no hour: the six pigment arms are its light decomposed, every mood a wavelength this one star already carries whole. This is its home reading — the furnace, not a spoke.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism wheel changes every arm around it but cannot change the Sun itself: the center stays white-gold, because in the light world white literally is every color summed. Newton's own experiment only proves what the star already does every second: send out everything at once and let each eye sort the wavelengths afterward.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the Sun steps onto the noon arm in royal gold (#F0C420), the estate of the King, the Crown for its object — the plainest seat in the whole set: a star that gives the same light to every latitude without favor already reigns by the King's own definition, four million tonnes of mass paid out every second as pure, unhoarded gift.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the noon arm is Youth, the zenith of a life, and the Sun wears sun-yellow (#FFE800) — apt for a star four and a half billion years into a Youth it shows no sign of leaving, the steady fusion bookkeeping of a life still climbing toward its blazing height rather than descending from it.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross the Sun stands at 12h on the Summer arm, yellow, its center pointed at the summer solstice — the day the star climbs highest and stays there longest. It shares the arm with the Galaxy: star and the great wheel that holds a hundred billion more like it, together on the year's brightest spoke.
variants.trio: On the Trinity the Sun keeps the center, and the sky around it narrows to three arms — Faith yellow, Love red, Hope blue, the painter's primaries. It is the oldest fact of starlight made into a virtue chart: white is not one thing radiating but three, and every color a telescope can separate back out of it.

faces.ruler:
The Sun is Sunday's own body at its calmest and its brightest at once — the star that neither explodes outward nor collapses inward, sitting at the zero of a scale whose two extremes are written elsewhere across the week.

Its virtue is Justice, argued by the numbers themselves: every second some 600 million tonnes of hydrogen become helium and roughly four million tonnes of that mass leave as light, distributed to every latitude of every planet without favor. But that same furnace is stalked by Pride, the light mistaken for something owned rather than radiated outward on no one's account. Its mood is Glory — noon's own triumph, light reaching every latitude in full, nothing yet asked of the star that it has not already given.
faces.servant:
The Black Hole is the Sun's own other face — not a separate object but the same mass one collapse away, proof that a star's two possible deaths (bursting outward, falling inward) both answer to the same seat on this dial.

Its virtue is Humility, the star's own light surrendered rather than merely dimmed — but that same collapse is stalked by Servility — once matter crosses the horizon it has no say left at all, an obedience so total not even light can refuse it. Its mood is Awe, the light failing at the exact radius named the event horizon, the same darkness directly photographed for the first time in 2019 by the Event Horizon Telescope, imaging a black hole some 6.5 billion times the Sun's mass at the center of the galaxy M87 — and Glory is the same seat's other face: the same mass, one collapse away from radiating again.

moon.name: Nebula
moon.base:
[[The Sky]] The Nebula is the week's own stellar nursery: towering pillars of luminous gas rise out of the dark, their folds cradling newborn stars caught mid-birth within the haze — no violence in this process, only slow drifting calm. It is Monday's object because a start this quiet needs the Moon's own patience: the nearest true stellar nursery visible to the naked eye, the Orion Nebula, sits a mere 1,344 light-years away and is already busy raising more than a thousand young stars inside a single cloud of hydrogen.

[[On the Dial]] Its home arm sits at dial 04h in deep blue (#002FFF), the mood called Calm — the hour before dawn. No color fits a nursery better: blue is the still, moonlit hour, and the pre-dawn watch is a birthplace's native shift, the long quiet stretch before the newest lights inside the cloud have even finished collapsing into stars.

[[The Lesson]] The Nebula's virtue is Serenity and its vice is Fear — the same unlit dark, if trusted or if dreaded — and the nebula holds both at once: the same gas that cradles a newborn star can just as easily smother it before fusion ever lights. Straight across the dial at 16h burns the Supernova, and the two objects cure each other: courage cures fear, and serenity quells wrath — the nursery that raised the star and the explosion that later ends it are the same material, spent at two different speeds.

[[The Hour]] Calm rules the pre-dawn hour because that is when calm is hardest and worth most: the darkest stretch of the night, the very conditions under which a cloud of gas first dares to fold in on itself and call the collapse a star.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 04h arm in deep blue (#002FFF), the Calm of the hour before dawn — the nursery's own night watch, as the base article tells it.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism wheel keeps the Nebula at 04h but sharpens the blue to #0040FF — pigment's muted night becomes light's electric one. Same watch, same Calm; the cloud's glow simply burns brighter.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the Nebula's drifting pillars shift to the deep-night arm in lamplit ink blue (#1F5FA8), the estate of the Scholar, the Book for its object — fitting for the sky's own nursery: a thousand young stars are being patiently read into existence inside a single cloud, the Orion Nebula's slow collapse a study written over millennia rather than a single midnight.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that deep-night arm is the Unborn, and the Nebula turns moonlight silver (#C8D7F0) — no object in the whole set earns the hue more literally: this is gas that has not yet finished collapsing into a star, ancestry and infancy folded into the same drifting haze.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross the Nebula moves to the 06h arm — Spring, green, pointed at the vernal equinox — and shares it with the Comet. Birthplace and returning wanderer on one spoke, and rightly: one is a beginning that has not yet happened and the other a promise that keeps coming back.
variants.trio: The Trinity keeps the Nebula at 04h but renames its watch: the blue arm now means Hope, shared with the Pulsar, and it guards the morning from 0h to 8h. No object earns the word more honestly — a nebula is hope with hydrogen, a promise a star will eventually catch, held in the dark until it does.

mars.name: Supernova
mars.base:
[[The Sky]] The Supernova is a star at the exact instant of detonation: blinding light climbing outward in one convulsive burst, concentric shockwave shells expanding through the dark, the old star's collapsed core barely visible at the heart of its own conflagration. It is Tuesday's object and Mars' oldest calling — the same violence the red planet has always carried since it was first named for a god of war. A star this violent needs real numbers to believe: in 1054 CE Chinese and Japanese astronomers recorded a 'guest star' bright enough to read by at night and visible in broad daylight for over three weeks — the supernova that left behind the Crab Nebula, still expanding nine and a half centuries later.

[[On the Dial]] Its home arm sits at dial 16h in ember orange (#DC9600), the mood called Zeal — the working afternoon. The placement is deliberately unromantic: an explosion this large is not the dawn charge but the long grind of a star's whole life spent in one climb, fire banked down to a working heat until the instant it lets go. Orange is the ember before the flare — hot enough to forge with, not yet the full detonation.

[[The Lesson]] Its two natures are its two faces: the outward blast is Courage and the same blast is Wrath — one fire that lights up a galaxy or destroys everything that made it, the star's virtue and vice being the identical heat pointed at the identical instant. Across the dial at 04h waits the Nebula, and each is the other's medicine: serenity quells wrath, courage cures fear. The calm cloud cools the burning star; the burning star reminds the calm cloud what it is eventually for.

[[The Hour]] Zeal rules the afternoon because that is a star's true working hour: past its youth's quiet glory, before its final evening flare — the long fusion grind of holding a shape together against its own gravity. Any cloud can begin to shine; a star is whoever is still holding the line when the fuel finally runs out.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 16h arm in ember orange (#DC9600), the Zeal of the working afternoon — the banked fire of the base article.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism keeps the Supernova at 16h but burns the ember up to pure yellow (#FFFF00) — in light, red and green fused. The blast glows hotter in Newton's reading, though the hour and its Zeal stand unchanged.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the Supernova's shockwave shifts to the 15h afternoon in copper (#C87533), the estate of the Merchant, the Coin for its object — an odd trade for a detonation, except the physics itself is a transaction: a star spends its entire remaining fuel in one payment, every element heavier than iron minted in that single violent instant and scattered outward as the universe's own coinage.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that same afternoon arm is Maturity, and the Supernova wears amber (#FFB400) — precisely earned: this is no young star's tantrum but the final grinding maturity of one that has held its shape against gravity for millions of years before finally letting go.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross the Supernova stands at 18h — Autumn, red, pointed at the autumnal equinox — sharing the spoke with the Binary Stars. Solitary detonation beside orbiting pair, the oldest company in the sky: autumn's red belongs to both, a single death and a shared life on the same arm.
variants.trio: On the Trinity the Supernova moves to 20h, onto Love's red arm beside the Binary Stars, and the pair guard the evening from 16h to 24h. It is the arm that explains the object: an explosion this total is love wearing no armor at all — a star gives away everything it has, all at once, and calls the giving a virtue rather than a loss.

mercury.name: Pulsar
mercury.base:
[[The Sky]] The Pulsar is the cosmic clock: a city-sized star spinning in place, no wider than 20 kilometers across yet weighing more than the Sun, two narrow lighthouse beams swept out from its poles and sweeping the dark with a regularity some millisecond pulsars hold as steady as an atomic clock over years at a time. It is Wednesday's object and Mercury's own calling — the winged messenger was already the god of clocks and roads before anyone had built either well, and a pulsar is simply his instrument found in the sky: when the first one was discovered in 1967, its ticking was so exact the discoverers half-joked it might be an artificial beacon, nicknaming the signal LGM-1, 'Little Green Men,' before the astrophysics caught up with the coincidence.

[[On the Dial]] Its home arm sits at dial 0h — midnight, the bottom of the wheel — in deep purple (#542E85), the mood called Sorrow. The color is history's private joke on this messenger: Tyrian purple was the costliest pigment of the ancient world, worth more than any coin a courier ever carried — a color that was itself a trade empire. And midnight is the counting hour for a clock this precise: every tick since the last one is closed, weighed, filed, and the next one has already started before the filing is done.

[[The Lesson]] The beam is the whole ethics of the arm: Wisdom is trusting a rhythm precise enough to build a calendar on; Greed is wanting the tick to arrive faster than physics allows. Straight up the axis at noon shines the Galaxy, and the two correct each other across the dial: Generosity cures Greed, and Wisdom curbs Excess — the galaxy's whole hundred billion stars teaching the single spinning one that scale is not the same as haste.

[[The Hour]] Sorrow rules midnight because every honest clock closes its ledger there: the day's grave, where the last tick and the first tick of tomorrow meet without a pause between them. The Pulsar is the one object on the dial that would keep this appointment even if nobody were left to read it — and wisdom begins exactly there.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the midnight arm at 0h in Tyrian purple (#542E85), the Sorrow of the closed ledger — the base reading.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns its purple to magenta (#BD00BD) — the one hue found in no rainbow, a color the eye invents where the spectrum's two ends meet. Fitting for the Pulsar, the sky's own metronome: at midnight it wears a color that exists only in the mind reading it, the same way a tick only becomes a clock once someone is counting.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the Pulsar's lighthouse beam shifts to the 21h evening arm in stage-velvet violet (#7A2E8E), the estate of the Artist, the Mask for its object — a performer's fit after all: a millisecond pulsar's beam sweeps the dark with such theatrical regularity that its 1967 discoverers half-suspected a staged signal, nicknaming it LGM-1 before the astrophysics unmasked the act.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that evening arm is Old Age, and the Pulsar wears dusk violet (#9C6BD4) — fitting for a stellar corpse rather than a living star: this is the collapsed core left behind after a supernova's death, a city-sized remnant still ticking with the discipline of something ancient outliving the body it came from.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross the Pulsar keeps the bottom arm at 0h — Winter, blue, pointed at the winter solstice — and it alone shares it with no one. The year's midnight belongs to a single object: the one clock precise enough to sit at the bottom of the wheel, alone, and never lose the beat.
variants.trio: The Trinity lifts the Pulsar off midnight to 04h, onto Hope's blue arm beside the Nebula, guarding the morning from 0h to 8h. The move names the object's true gift: a rhythm this steady is hope with a stopwatch — the ledger closed in sorrow at midnight reopens at the morning's gate, timed by the one star that never misses a beat.

jupiter.name: Galaxy
jupiter.base:
[[The Sky]] The Galaxy is the great wheel holding hundreds of billions of stars at once, its spiral arms carved from countless individual points of light, a dense bright core at the hub holding the whole structure together like a congregation gathered around its center. It is Thursday's object and Jupiter's own calling — in the Vedic week Thursday is Guruvar, the day of Brihaspati, who IS Jupiter, the guru of the gods, and a spiral galaxy is generosity built at the largest scale astronomy has a name for: the Milky Way alone is home to somewhere between one and four hundred billion stars, every one of them held on its own orbit by gravity shared rather than gravity hoarded.

[[On the Dial]] Its home arm is the top of the dial, 12h, in bright yellow (#F8E600), the mood called Joy — and 'jovial' literally means 'of Jupiter.' The arms themselves explain the placement: a spiral galaxy gives away light in every direction from its core, an entire wheel's worth of stars catching and passing on that same gravity and glow. Noon is the hour when light is given most freely, and yellow is that gift as a color.

[[The Lesson]] Its virtue is Generosity — the light shared across a hundred billion suns rather than kept at the core — and its vice is Excess, the same core grown so massive it swallows everything nearby, the gift that becomes a black hole at the center of its own galaxy. Straight down the axis at midnight ticks the Pulsar, and each cures the other: Wisdom curbs Excess, and Generosity cures Greed — the precise single beat below teaching scale to the sprawling congregation above.

[[The Hour]] Joy rules noon because noon is the one hour a wheel this size does not need to hoard: the day's peak, when starlight — like the galaxy's own arms — asks nothing back for what it gives away.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the top arm at 12h in noon yellow (#F8E600), the Joy of the day's peak — the base reading.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns its noon to green (#00DC00) — the wavelength at the summit of human sight, the brightest color the eye knows. The Galaxy's hour keeps its Joy; light simply measures the peak instead of painting it.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the Galaxy's spiral arms shift to the 09h morning arm in alb ivory (#EDEDE0), the estate of the Priest, the Bell for its object — a scaled-up cousin of its own noon calling: a hundred billion stars gathered around one hub is already a congregation, gravity shared rather than hoarded, the same generosity simply rung out at galactic size.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that morning arm is Childhood, and the Galaxy wears spring green (#7CE577) — fitting for the arms where new stars are still being born, a structure that never stops assembling itself, forever raising fresh light along its spiral the way Childhood keeps arriving generation after generation.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross the Galaxy stands at 12h on the Summer arm, yellow, pointed at the summer solstice — and shares it with the Sun itself. The single star and the hundred billion it belongs to, together on the year's highest spoke: one light and the wheel that holds it.
variants.trio: On the Trinity the Galaxy keeps the top arm at 12h, yellow — but the yellow now names Faith, and it shares the arm with the Comet as they guard the day's height from 8h to 16h. The placement reads itself: faith is trusting a structure too large to see all at once, the same trust a hundred billion orbits already keep without a single star checking the others' math.

venus.name: Binary Stars
venus.base:
[[The Sky]] The Binary Stars are two suns of comparable weight, locked in a slow mutual orbit around a shared point of balance between them, a bridge of streaming light and matter drawn taut wherever their gravities meet — two bodies bound by nothing but the pull they exert on each other. It is Friday's object and Venus' own calling: in the old astrology the planet's children were always the musicians and the lovers, and a binary system is the sky's most literal picture of a pair, closer to the truth of the galaxy than any single star standing alone — by most counts roughly half of all Sun-like stars keep a companion of some kind, so that a lone star like ours is closer to the exception than the rule.

[[On the Dial]] Its home arm sits at dial 20h in deep red (#B60000), the mood called Passion — the evening, when Venus herself rises as the evening star. The hour fits the object exactly: evening is when two things that have spent all day apart finally meet in the same sky, and a binary pair's whole nature is that mutual gravity never lets them out of each other's reach — the nearest star system to our own Sun, Alpha Centauri, is itself a binary pair completing one full orbit of each other roughly every eighty years.

[[The Lesson]] Its virtue and vice share the same bridge of light: Love is the gravity holding the pair together, and Jealousy is the fear that the bridge might one day pull matter from one star to the other and leave the giver dimmer for it — real physics for close binaries, where one star can in fact strip gas from its companion. Across the dial at 08h waits the Comet, and the two heal each other: Patience heals Jealousy, and Love dissolves Envy — the returning wanderer teaches the pair to wait, and the pair teaches the wanderer that even a solitary orbit is shaped by a gravity it shares with something else.

[[The Hour]] Passion rules the evening because passion is what the daylight was for: the day is spent separately, the evening is when two orbits finally cross. And this is the one object in the whole set built from two bodies rather than one — love, like binary stars, is the moment a system stops describing a single point and starts describing two.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 20h arm in deep red (#B60000), the Passion of the evening — the base reading, the evening star's own hour.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism keeps the Binary Stars at 20h but purifies the red to its light primary (#FF0000) — the reddest red there is, unmixed. Passion in Newton's world is not a pigment but a wavelength, and the evening burns in it.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the Binary Stars' shared bridge of light shifts to the 18h sunset arm in iron-blood crimson (#A02020), the estate of the Soldier, the Sword for its object — a tense trade for a pair bound only by mutual gravity, yet true to the physics: in close binaries one star can strip matter from its companion, the crimson naming the edge where devotion and violence share the very same bridge.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that sunset arm belongs to the Elder, the harvest of a life, and the pair deepens to ember (#FF6A3C) — fitting for a system like Alpha Centauri, already gathering decades into a single shared orbit, roughly eighty years spent completing one full circuit around each other, a harvest of time no lone star ever has to keep.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross the Binary Stars stand at 18h — Autumn, red, pointed at the autumnal equinox — sharing the spoke with the Supernova. Orbiting pair beside solitary blast, as old a contrast as the sky allows: autumn's red is a shared life and a single death in the same color.
variants.trio: The Binary Stars do not move: the Trinity's Love arm is their own 20h in their own red, for love is their virtue in both sets at once. The Supernova joins them, and together they guard the evening from 16h to 24h — a pair kept alive by gravity and a single star spent all at once, sharing the same watch over the dark.

saturn.name: Comet
saturn.base:
[[The Sky]] The Comet is the returning wanderer: a small icy body arcing in from the outer dark, a long tail streaming behind it, and at the far edge of its orbit a distant Sun it is only now approaching again after decades away — the whole shape of its path reading as one long patient loop. It is Saturday's object and Saturn's own calling, and the sickle-shaped tail is not a coincidence of the metaphor: Halley's Comet, the best-known of them all, returns on a schedule almost exactly one human lifetime long — last seen in 1986, not due again until 2061 — patience measured out in a single number anyone can hold in their head.

[[On the Dial]] Its home arm sits at dial 08h in field green (#007E00), the mood called Renewal — the morning. The hour is the Comet's by right of habit: a comet nucleus is often described as a dirty snowball, an old mix of ice and rock and dust that has carried the same frozen material since the solar system's own beginning, and every close pass to the Sun renews it — boils a little more of that ancient ice into the tail and lets it shine again, however briefly, before the long dark orbit resumes.

[[The Lesson]] Its color holds its virtue and its vice in a single hue: green is growth and renewal, Patience, the wanderer that returns exactly when it says it will — and green is also envy, the tail streaming out behind it always pointed away from the Sun rather than toward it, the one direction it can never choose for itself. Across the dial at 20h shines the Binary Stars, and each cures the other: Love dissolves Envy, and Patience heals Jealousy — the paired stars teach the comet that closeness is possible, the comet teaches the pair that even the longest absence can still keep its appointment.

[[The Hour]] Renewal rules the morning because the Comet's whole nature lives there: every return is slightly changed, a little more of the ancient ice boiled away, and every orbit is a wager that coming back is still worth what it costs to make the trip.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 08h arm in field green (#007E00), the Renewal of the morning — the base reading.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns its morning green to cyan (#00DDDD) — the color of the clear early sky rather than of frost and ice. Renewal keeps the hour; in the light world the Comet is measured by the sky it crosses rather than the tail it leaves.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the Comet's long tail shifts to the dawn arm, 06h, in field green (#3E8914), the estate of the Farmer, the Plough for its object — an apt trade for the wanderer whose whole nature is a slow, patient loop: Halley's own orbit is a single lifetime long, ancient ice sown into a furrow that will not come back around for decades.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the dawn arm is Birth, and the Comet wears predawn mist (#8FA8C8) — fitting for a body that is quite literally reborn on every close pass, ancient ice boiled fresh into a shining tail each time it nears the Sun, dawn's own wager renewed once a human lifetime.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross the Comet stands at 06h — Spring, green, pointed at the vernal equinox: the season of returns, its own festival. It shares the spoke with the Nebula — wanderer and nursery together, the two patient objects that promise a light not yet arrived.
variants.trio: The Trinity promotes the Comet from the morning to the crown: the 12h Faith arm, yellow, shared with the Galaxy, guarding the day's height from 8h to 16h. The pairing is the oldest sermon a comet's orbit could preach — faith is a return trusted before it is seen, every decades-long absence a promise kept on a schedule no one alive gets to check twice.

sun.name: Justice · Humility
sun.base:
[[The Figure]] Sunday is the only day the wheel doubles: Justice rules it by daylight and Humility rules it by dusk, the same throne worn two ways. Where the other six days each carry one virtue against one vice on a single arm, the center carries two of each in one seat — and that doubling is not an exception to this theme, it is the theme stated plainly. Every virtue on this dial answers a vice somewhere else on the dial: Serenity quells Wrath, Courage cures Fear, Wisdom curbs Excess, Generosity cures Greed, Love dissolves Envy, Patience heals Jealousy. Only the center cures itself — Humility answers Pride, Justice straightens Servility — proof that the whole week is one instrument built to heal itself, spoke curing spoke, virtue by virtue, all the way around.

[[On the Dial]] On the hexagram the center holds no arm and no hour at all — its home is the hub, white-gold, the sum of every hue the six arms carry. That is Justice's argument made geometry: a ruler is not one calling among six, but the point they radiate from, the way white light is not one color but every color undivided. Only the octa star moves it, lending the crown noon's own 12h arm; on the cross and the trio it keeps the same undivided center, the still axis the seasons and the theological three both turn around.

[[The Lesson]] Justice and Humility are not two virtues so much as one virtue seen from both sides of the same coin: the ruler who judges fairly and the ruler who serves without being asked are the identical discipline, aimed once outward and once inward. Pride is what happens when the crown believes the light is its own; Servility is what happens when the bent spine stops believing the light is anyone's at all — and each cures the other because the throne is close enough to itself to reach across. The mood swings from Glory at noon to Awe at dusk, but the medicine never leaves the hub: the one calling on the whole dial that carries its own disease and its own cure in the same open hand.

variants.hexa_primary: On the hexagram in pigment the center takes no arm — it is the hub the six colors decompose from, white-gold because paint cannot mix a white, only receive it whole, as gold leaf laid rather than ground. That is Humility as a technique before it is a word: the one hue on the wheel that must be given rather than made. And it is Justice as geometry: the hub that plays no favorites among the six colors it feeds.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism wheel makes the same claim from the opposite direction: here white is not the paint's blank but light's total sum, the six colored beams running inward to add back into white-gold at the hub. Humility rewarded — the center receives exactly what it gave the arms, returned and combined — and Justice confirmed: no single beam outweighs another in the addition.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Sunday's throne steps onto the noon arm in royal gold (#F0C420), the estate of the King, the Crown for its object — no borrowed seat: Justice already rules by daylight, the balanced scale and the sheathed sword both proof of a King who judges rather than merely reigns, the Crown for once worn rather than only implied by the empty hub.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the noon arm is Youth, the zenith of a life, and the throne wears sun-yellow (#FFE800) — Justice's own blazing register, judgment rendered at full strength before Humility's dusk ever asks the same crown to be set back down.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross the center holds the crossing itself, the still point where all four arms — two solstices, two equinoxes — meet and turn. Summer, Winter, and both equinoxes revolve around a hub that claims no season for its own: Humility as geometry, Justice as the one measure all four seasons are held to equally.
variants.trio: On the Trinity the center anchors Faith's yellow arm at noon, Hope's blue at 4h, Love's red at 20h — three virtues fanning out from one root. Justice and Humility both live in that root: the hub gives each arm its color and takes no credit for what grows from it, holding the three so they can each reach outward without the center ever reaching back.

faces.ruler:
Justice is Sunday's bright face — the virtue a ruler must practice rather than merely wear, argued in every old telling from Solomon dividing the child to Ma'at's feather weighed against the heart: light and law that fall on everyone alike, without favorites. Because Sunday is the week's one double day, Justice is only half the throne's calling — the crown that judges must also answer for how it judges.

Judgment without cruelty is force held in reserve: an authority that does not have to be exercised in order to be real, and is weakened rather than proved by every use of it.

His virtue is proven by what a ruler does with what he governs — a world held rather than gripped. But that same authority is stalked by Pride, the throne mistaking a crown for something owed rather than lent — and Justice's cure runs backward across the center's own inner axis, straightening the Servant's Servility, the bent spine that needs exactly what a fair law offers it. His mood is Glory: power fully at rest, light fully at its source.
faces.servant:
Humility is Sunday's dark face — not a separate calling but Justice's own throne with the crown taken off, proof the canon has always read this figure as one king in two postures rather than two kings. Whoever occupies the center of everything is the one most tempted to believe the light is his; Humility is the source remembering it is a light among lights, not the whole of it.

His virtue is proven the same way Justice's was — by what is surrendered rather than by what is held — but where Justice measures others, Humility measures only itself. Servility is what this same posture becomes if the spine bends without the will behind it, service that has forgotten what it is serving.

Humility's cure crosses the same inner axis back the other way, answering the Ruler's own Pride — the throne's one seat that is both its own disease and its own medicine. His mood is Awe, the light failing at exactly the hour the crown comes off; Glory is simply the same king with the crown restored.

moon.name: Serenity
moon.base:
[[The Figure]] Monday is Serenity's day — calm settled deeply enough that nothing arriving at it is disturbed, which is the difference between composure and mere quiet. Where Tuesday burns with Wrath, Monday answers from clear across the dial: Serenity is the discipline that quells it, the night's stillness reaching over the hub to cool the day's hottest fire. That reach is this whole theme's method in miniature — no virtue stays home; each is a cure sent somewhere else on the wheel.

[[On the Dial]] His home arm sits at dial 4h in deep blue (#002FFF), the mood called Calm — the hour before dawn, when nothing is left of yesterday and nothing yet of tomorrow. No hour suits Serenity better: it is the one stretch of the day that asks nothing of the mind but to sit still inside it, borrowed silver light standing in for a sun not yet risen.

[[The Lesson]] Serenity and Fear share one arm and one color, the night's two faces lit or unlit by exactly the same darkness — the difference is entirely in the mind that meets it. Straight across the dial at 16h waits Mars, and the cure runs both ways: Serenity quells Tuesday's Wrath, and Courage, in turn, cures Monday's own Fear — the calm hand steadying the burning one, the burning heart lending its nerve to the frightened one.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 4h arm in deep blue (#002FFF), Serenity's own Calm at the hour before dawn — the settled calm of the base article, silver light standing in for a sun not yet risen.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism wheel keeps Serenity at 4h but sharpens the blue to an electric #0040FF — pigment's muted hush becomes light's brighter one. The lake stays just as still; only the moon on it burns colder and clearer.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Serenity's still lake shifts to the deep-night arm in lamplit ink blue (#1F5FA8), the estate of the Scholar, the Book for its object — a natural extension of the virtue: the mind still enough to hold a reflection without disturbing it is already reading the dark the way a scholar reads a page, patient study standing in for panic.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that deep-night arm is the Unborn, and Serenity turns moonlight silver (#C8D7F0) — fitting for the one virtue built on holding still: the Unborn ask nothing of the mind but patience, and Serenity is precisely the discipline of sitting inside that silvered, unproven dark without disturbing it.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Serenity moves to the 6h arm — Spring, green, pointed at the vernal equinox — sharing the spoke with Saturn's Patience. Two of the dial's quietest virtues on one arm: the stillness that waits out the night and the patience that waits out the season, tending what cannot be rushed.
variants.trio: The Trinity keeps Serenity at 4h but renames the arm Hope, shared with Mercury's Wisdom, guarding the morning from 0h to 8h.
