It is the truer name for what stillness at that hour is actually doing: a calm mind before dawn is not empty, it is waiting — hope practiced quietly enough to look like rest.

mars.name: Courage
mars.base:
[[The Figure]] Tuesday is Courage's day — the nerve to hold ground rather than to flee it or to strike first. Its cure travels straight across the dial to Monday: Courage answers Fear, the soldier's steadiness reaching over the hub to still the healer's dread at the sickbed. It is the oldest of this theme's cross-cure pairs, the one every child's story already half-knows — courage and fear as two readings of the same raised pulse. Courage under discipline is a promise kept rather than a threat made: force that keeps its position instead of looking for a target.

[[On the Dial]] His home arm sits at dial 16h in ember orange (#DC9600), the mood called Zeal — the working afternoon, fire banked down to a working heat rather than a battle's opening blaze. The hour is deliberately unromantic: Courage in this canon is not the dawn charge but the discipline of still holding the line once the excitement of morning is long spent.

[[The Lesson]] Courage and Wrath are one fire pointed two ways — the shield that defends and the spear that destroys, the same heat aimed outward at what must be faced or inward at whatever the temper decides to break. Straight across the dial at 4h waits the Moon, and the cure is mutual: Courage cures Monday's Fear, and Serenity, in turn, quells Tuesday's own Wrath — the burning heart steadying the frightened one, the calm hand cooling the one that burns too hot.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 16h arm in ember orange (#DC9600), Courage's own Zeal at the working afternoon — the banked fire of the base article, hot enough to hold a line with, not yet a battle's opening blaze.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism keeps Courage at 16h but burns the ember up to pure yellow (#FFFF00) — red and green fused into light's hottest reading. The working fire glows brighter in Newton's world, though the hour and its Zeal stand exactly where the base article leaves them.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Courage's raised shield shifts to the 15h afternoon in copper (#C87533), the estate of the Merchant, the Coin for its object — an unlikely trade for a soldier's virtue, yet true to the anvil hour: holding the line once morning's excitement is spent is itself a currency, nerve paid out steadily rather than spent all at once in a single dramatic charge.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that same afternoon arm is Maturity, and Courage wears amber (#FFB400) — the exact fit: this canon's own Courage is never the dawn's raw nerve but the discipline of a soldier grown into the grind, holding the shield up long after the battle's first thrill has worn off.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Courage stands at 18h — Autumn, red, pointed at the autumnal equinox — sharing the spoke with Venus' Love. Defence beside love, the oldest pairing in the sky: autumn's red is harvest and blood at once, and it takes both virtues together to say so honestly.
variants.trio: On the Trinity Courage moves to 20h, onto Love's own red arm beside Venus, guarding the evening from 16h to 24h. It is the arm that explains the virtue at its root: courage is love in armor — the guard keeps the night watch not for the fight's sake but for the sake of what sleeps behind it.

mercury.name: Wisdom
mercury.base:
[[The Figure]] Wednesday is Wisdom's day — the mind that weighs the day honestly precisely because no one else is watching, which is the only condition under which weighing proves anything. Its cure runs straight up the dial's spine: Wisdom curbs Thursday's Excess overhead, the careful midnight reckoning teaching the noon feast when enough has already arrived.

[[On the Dial]] His home arm sits at dial 0h — midnight, the bottom of the wheel — in Tyrian purple (#542E85), the mood called Sorrow. Midnight is the accounting hour: the day is over, the market closed, and what is left is to weigh, honestly, what the day was actually worth. No color suits that reckoning better than the one dye that was once worth more than gold.

[[The Lesson]] Wisdom and Greed share the same arm because they share the same instrument — the scale. Wisdom is knowing the true weight of things; Greed is wanting the balance to tip. Straight up the axis at noon Jupiter holds the crown, and the two virtues heal in both directions: Wisdom curbs Thursday's Excess, and Generosity, in turn, cures Wednesday's own Greed — the careful scale steadying the overflowing table, the open hand teaching the closed one what it is holding.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the midnight arm at 0h in Tyrian purple (#542E85), Wisdom's own Sorrow at the closed ledger — the base article's honest reckoning, the day weighed at its grave.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns Wisdom's purple to magenta (#BD00BD) — the one hue found in no rainbow, invented by the eye where the spectrum's two ends meet. Fitting for the mind's own virtue: at midnight it wears a color that exists only in thought, not in light itself.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Wisdom's scale shifts to the 21h evening arm in stage-velvet violet (#7A2E8E), the estate of the Artist, the Mask for its object — an unlikely seat for the virtue of honest weighing, yet the owl's own night-sight is itself a kind of performance done without an audience, the mask here being the composure Wisdom keeps while the rest of the day has gone to bed.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that evening arm is Old Age, and Wisdom wears dusk violet (#9C6BD4) — the truest fit in the set: Wisdom is accumulated exactly the way Old Age is, weighed out slowly across a whole life of honest reckonings rather than arriving all at once.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Wisdom keeps the bottom arm at 0h — Winter, blue, pointed at the winter solstice — and shares it with no one. The year's midnight belongs to a single virtue: the one that can sit at the bottom of the wheel, alone, and still balance the books honestly.
variants.trio: The Trinity lifts Wisdom off midnight to 4h, onto Hope's blue arm beside Serenity, guarding the morning from 0h to 8h. The move names Wisdom's quieter engine: the mind that weighs things honestly at night is the same mind that dares to hope by morning — the ledger closed in Sorrow reopens as credit extended to the day.

jupiter.name: Generosity
jupiter.base:
[[The Figure]] Thursday is Generosity's day — the open hand pouring before any return is proven, faith practiced with the hands rather than merely professed. Its cure runs straight down the dial's spine: Generosity cures Wednesday's Greed below it, the noon table's overflow answering the midnight scale's grasping fist.

[[On the Dial]] His home arm is the top of the dial, 12h, in bright yellow (#F8E600), the mood called Joy — and 'jovial' literally means 'of Jupiter'. Noon is the one hour that needs no lamp of its own, the day's peak, when light is given most freely and asks nothing back for it — which is Generosity's whole ethic, stated as an hour rather than a sermon.

[[The Lesson]] Generosity and Excess share one arm because giving, left unchecked, becomes flooding — the same open royal hand that feeds a table can also drown it. Straight down the axis at midnight Mercury keeps the scale, and the cure runs in both directions: Generosity cures Wednesday's Greed, and Wisdom, in turn, curbs Thursday's own Excess — the open hand teaching the closed one to give, the careful scale teaching the open one when to stop.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the top arm at 12h in noon yellow (#F8E600), Generosity's own Joy at the day's peak — the base reading, the hour light is given away most freely.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns Generosity's noon to green (#00DC00) — the wavelength at the very summit of human sight, the brightest color the eye knows. The virtue keeps its Joy; light simply measures the peak it gives from instead of painting it gold.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Generosity's overflowing hand shifts to the 09h morning arm in alb ivory (#EDEDE0), the estate of the Priest, the Bell for its object — a natural kinship: the open hand that pours before any return is proven is already the Priest's own discipline, faith rung out in gifts rather than merely preached.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that morning arm is Childhood, and Generosity wears spring green (#7CE577) — fitting for the virtue that gives without keeping score, the same unguarded openness a Childhood has before the world teaches it to count what it hands away.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Generosity stands at 12h on the Summer arm, yellow, pointed at the summer solstice — sharing it with Justice, Sunday's own bright face. The open hand and the balanced scale share the year's highest spoke: giving and fairness, on the same arm at last.
variants.trio: On the Trinity Generosity keeps the top arm at 12h, yellow — but the arm now carries Faith rather than Joy, shared with Saturn's Patience, guarding the day's height from 8h to 16h. The renaming fits: faith is generosity extended toward a return that has not arrived yet, the open hand's oldest wager.

venus.name: Love
venus.base:
[[The Figure]] Friday is Love's day — passion given enough patience to become form, the one virtue that belongs both to this theme's cross-cure pairs and to the older triad of Faith, Hope and Love. Its cure crosses the dial to Saturday: Love dissolves Envy, warmth loosening the cold grip on what a neighbor's field is growing.

[[On the Dial]] His home arm sits at dial 20h in deep red (#B60000), the mood called Passion — the evening, when Venus herself rises as the evening star. The hour fits exactly: evening is when the day's work releases the heart, when the material world of daylight softens into its feeling one.

[[The Lesson]] Love's own shadow is Jealousy, not its opposite — the fear of losing what is already loved, sitting on the very same arm and colored the very same red. Straight across the dial at 8h waits Saturn, and the cure runs both directions: Love dissolves Saturday's Envy, and Patience, in turn, heals Friday's own Jealousy — the lover teaching the farmer to cherish his own field rather than covet another's, the farmer teaching the lover that what is worth having is worth waiting for.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 20h arm in deep red (#B60000), Love's own Passion at the evening — the base reading, the hour the evening star herself rises.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism keeps Love at 20h but purifies the red to its light primary (#FF0000) — the reddest red there is, unmixed. Passion in Newton's world is a wavelength rather than a pigment, and the evening burns straight in it.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Love's nested hands shift to the 18h sunset arm in iron-blood crimson (#A02020), the estate of the Soldier, the Sword for its object — the same red the virtue already wears, now sharpened: Love's own shadow is Jealousy, the fear of losing what is loved turned defensive enough to draw a blade, the Soldier simply naming what the rose's nest was always capable of becoming.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that sunset arm belongs to the Elder, the harvest of a life, and Love deepens to ember (#FF6A3C) — apt beyond metaphor: love given time enough to become form, the doves circling the rose, is precisely what a life's harvest is made of, patience turned finally into keeping.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Love stands at 18h — Autumn, red, pointed at the autumnal equinox — sharing the spoke with Mars' Courage. Rose beside shield, as in every old myth: autumn's red is harvest and blood and passion at once, and it takes both virtues to say so.
variants.trio: Love does not move for the Trinity: its own arm is already the Trinity's Love arm, the same 20h in the same red. Courage joins it, and together they guard the evening from 16h to 24h — one virtue keeping what is loved safe, the other keeping it remembered.

saturn.name: Patience
saturn.base:
[[The Figure]] Saturday is Patience's day — the farmer who sows and waits and does not stare too long at the next field, learned from a planet that takes thirty years to close one circle around the sun. Its cure crosses the dial to Friday: Patience heals Jealousy, the slow art of waiting mending the fear of losing what is loved.

[[On the Dial]] His home arm sits at dial 8h in field green (#007E00), the mood called Renewal — the morning, dew and growth, the week renewing itself on the one day set aside for rest. No hour suits waiting better: every morning the field looks slightly different, and every seed is a small wager that the waiting will work.

[[The Lesson]] Patience and Envy share the same green because growth and its shadow are the same color seen two ways — the green of the sapling coming up, and the bitter green of watching someone else's harvest come in first. Straight across the dial at 20h waits Venus, and the cure runs both ways: Patience heals Friday's Jealousy, and Love, in turn, dissolves Saturday's own Envy — the farmer teaching the lover that what is worth having is worth waiting for, the lover teaching the farmer to love his own field rather than covet another's.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 8h arm in field green (#007E00), Patience's own Renewal at the morning — the base reading, dew on a field that looks a little different every day.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns Patience's morning green to cyan (#00DDDD) — the color of the clear early sky rather than the field itself. Renewal keeps the hour; in the light world Patience looks up before it looks down.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Patience takes the dawn arm, 06h, in field green (#3E8914), the estate of the Farmer, the Plough for its object — the closest fit the whole table offers: the virtue is already sowing and waiting, and the Farmer's estate is that same discipline given a tool.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the dawn arm is Birth, and Patience wears predawn mist (#8FA8C8) — the wager fits exactly: every seed sown is itself a small Birth not yet arrived, and Patience is the discipline of trusting the mist will lift before the sapling ever breaks the ground.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Patience stands at 6h — Spring, green, pointed at the vernal equinox: sowing season, its own festival. It shares the spoke with Serenity, the Moon's own stillness — two patient virtues tending what cannot be hurried, one a season, the other a night.
variants.trio: The Trinity promotes Patience from the morning to the crown: the 12h Faith arm, yellow, shared with Generosity, guarding the day's height from 8h to 16h. It is the oldest sermon there is — sowing is faith performed with the hands, every seed a small creed buried, waited on, and believed in before it is seen.

sun.name: Pride · Servility
sun.base:
[[The Figure]] Sunday keeps no arm of its own, and the Sun's shadow is double for the same reason its virtue is: Pride is what the Ruler becomes when the crown forgets it is lent rather than owed; Servility is what the Servant becomes when the bent spine forgets what it is bowing to. Two vices, one throne — argued in the same white-gold and black-and-silver the one double seat carries in both directions.

[[The Lesson]] Christian tradition already keeps a scale for exactly this kind of loss, though it usually weighs only one side at a time. Lucifer's fall was upward — pride that would not bow; Judas's was downward — a bowing that betrayed rather than served. Set both ends on the center's own beam and the double face reads as that scale: Pride is Lucifer's end of it, the self mistaking itself for the throne's source; Servility is Judas's, the self so sure it has no claim to the seat that it will sell whoever sits in it. Both empty the throne. Neither is safe merely for falling the opposite direction from the other.

[[The Lesson]] Because nothing stands opposite the center, neither cure ever leaves it: Humility, the crown set down rather than merely spoken of, answers Pride from the same throne; Justice, the scale that will not bend for its own convenience, straightens Servility's slack spine back into the service of what is right rather than of whoever is asking. Pride is admiration turned inward instead of light sent outward; Servility is deference that has stopped being chosen. The center is the one place on the dial that must heal itself — which is exactly why losing it, in either direction, costs the most.

variants.hexa_primary: On the painter's wheel the center keeps its old shape even in shadow: white-gold, belonging to no hour, both faces sharing the one point — Pride bright when the light is looked at rather than looked through, Servility dark when the same point stops radiating and starts merely obeying. The six arms still decompose around it; the vice, like the virtue, never becomes a spoke of its own.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism wheel changes every arm around the center but cannot change what sits there: white-gold stays white-gold, because in the light world white really is every color at once — and a lie about owning all of it is exactly as total, whichever face is showing. Newton's reading only sharpens what the throne already risks.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the Sun's noon arm now wears royal gold (#F0C420) — the Walk of **the King**, judged by the Crown alone. Pride is exactly what happens when a King forgets the crown was only ever lent: seated in the same regalia that names the office, the sin discovers it never has more to answer for than the object it wears.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel noon is **Youth** — life's blazing height — and the Sun wears sun-yellow (#FFE800). Pride is Youth's own delusion stretched onto a throne: the crown convinced its noon will never dim, the same blindness by which a young man mistakes his own zenith for a permanent address.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Pride stands at 12h on the Summer arm, yellow, beside Jupiter's own Excess — the year's two overreaching sins sharing a single spoke, the doubled crown and the overflowing table both certain that abundance is a right rather than a gift. Servility has no season of its own: it lives only inside the center, never on the wheel's rim.
variants.trio: The Trinity keeps the center's shadow exactly where the center's light stays — around the same white-gold point, now the underside of Faith, Love and Hope all read from one throne. Pride is the wager that the throne owns the three virtues it merely radiates; Servility is the fear that it owns none of them, and so surrenders all three at once.

faces.ruler:
Pride is the Ruler's own face gone wrong, worn in the same white-gold as Justice because it costs nothing to counterfeit — the throne looks identical from outside whether the king remembers he serves or has forgotten it. It is Phaethon's error before it is anyone else's: the son who could drive the chariot for one day and mistook the ride for ownership of the sun.

Pride does not attend to the kingdom the light is meant to reach; it takes the light's own reflection for the thing itself. On the Judas–Lucifer scale this is the upward failure, refusal dressed as majesty: the seat lost by a self too large for it rather than too small.

Its cure never leaves the room: Humility, the same king with the crown taken off and set down. Glory, his true mood at that hour, needs no mirror at all — it radiates without checking the reflection. Pride is not cured by a smaller throne, since there is no smaller throne to give it — only by the same hands that raised the crown learning to set it down.
faces.servant:
Servility is the Servant's own grace curdled, black with silver trim like Humility but with the will bled out of it — the same bent spine, now serving the throne instead of the truth. Where Humility bends because bending is right, Servility bends because bending is safe, and safety is a much smaller reason to bend.

Nothing was stolen — it was handed over, a little at a time, by someone who stopped believing his own hands were worth keeping. On the Judas–Lucifer scale this is the downward failure: not refusal but surrender, the seat betrayed by someone convinced he had no claim to defend it.

Its cure crosses the center's own inner axis rather than reaching outward: Justice, the Ruler's scale that will not tip for anyone's comfort, is the only thing that can straighten a spine that has forgotten it is allowed to stand. Its true mood, Awe, is fear and wonder held in one honest look upward; Servility is what Awe becomes when the looking-up never lifts its own eyes again. It mistakes itself for the safest posture in the room — it is only the quietest way to lose the throne.

moon.name: Fear
moon.base:
[[The Figure]] Fear is Monday's blue turned cold, the Moon's own dark face and, by the old reckoning, older than any other sin on the list — the unlit version of exactly the same night that, faced rather than fled, is Serenity. The physician keeping the pre-dawn watch and the frightened patient in the same bed are looking at the identical darkness; only one of them has stopped believing it will end.

[[On the Dial]] It rules the same 04h arm as Serenity, deep blue (#002FFF), because Fear is not a different hour from Calm — it is Calm's own hour lost. The small hours are when the body's watch is lowest and the mind's imagining is highest, and Fear is what happens when the second outruns the first: the shadow on the wall growing a life of its own, the guttering candle read as an omen instead of just a candle running low.

[[The Lesson]] Its cure stands straight across the dial: Mars' Courage, twelve hours around the wheel at 16h, the soldier's steadied nerve reaching over the center to answer the watch that has lost its footing. Courage does not put the candle out or paint over the shadow — it simply stays until dawn proves, once again, that the shape on the wall was never more than a shape.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 04h arm in deep blue (#002FFF), Fear's own pre-dawn watch — the same hour Serenity keeps, held instead by a hand that has stopped trusting the dark.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism wheel keeps Fear at 04h but sharpens the blue to #0040FF — pigment's muted dread becomes light's colder, more electric one. The watch is the same length; the small hours simply glare instead of glow.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the deep-night arm now burns lamplit ink blue (#1F5FA8) — the Walk of **the Scholar**, the Book its object. Fear is what that same hour becomes without the lamp: the Scholar reads the dark and finds only a shadow on the page; Fear is denied even the book, and reads the identical dark as a verdict already written against it.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the deep-night arm belongs to **the Unborn**, and the Moon takes on moonlight silver (#C8D7F0) — the hour of those not yet arrived and those already gone. Fear is that same threshold turned inward: not ancestors watching or children waiting, but a mind that has started fearing both, certain the dark holds a verdict from one direction or the other.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Fear moves to the 06h arm — Spring, green, pointed at the vernal equinox — sharing the spoke with Saturn's Envy. Two patient vices on one arm: the sower's bitterness and the healer's dread, both the cost of professions that are supposed to know how to wait.
variants.trio: The Trinity keeps Fear at 04h but renames the arm's better half Hope, shared with Mercury's Greed. Fear is exactly what Hope looks like with the future subtracted — the same blue watch, kept by a hand that no longer expects the fever to break.

mars.name: Wrath
mars.base:
[[The Figure]] Wrath is Tuesday's orange loosed on its own side — Mars' fire with no hand left on the reins, the war god's own force reading as ruin instead of defence. The same heat that holds a line, unaimed, simply burns whoever is closest, friend or enemy alike. It always feels, from the inside, like strength — but Wrath spends the very reserve Courage needs to hold the line, and the wreckage left behind is the honest report of what that borrowing actually cost.

[[On the Dial]] It rules the same 16h arm as Courage, ember orange (#DC9600), because Wrath is not a different fire from the working afternoon's — it is that fire with the discipline knocked out of it. Zeal is the ember banked to forge with; Wrath is the same ember let loose the moment the day's grind stops feeling worth the grinding, mistaking exhaustion for justification.

[[The Lesson]] Its cure comes from the pre-dawn arm: Monday's Serenity, the calm that banks a furnace before it spills rather than after. Straight across the dial the physician's discipline answers the soldier's — not by extinguishing the fire, which Mars needs to keep, but by keeping a hand on it before the reins are what breaks first.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 16h arm in ember orange (#DC9600), the fire of the working afternoon spent on itself instead of on the line it was meant to hold.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism keeps Wrath at 16h but burns the ember up to pure yellow (#FFFF00) — red and green fused into the hottest reading on the wheel. The hour is unchanged; in Newton's world the loosed fire simply shows exactly how hot it really got.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the afternoon arm now trades in copper (#C87533) — the Walk of **the Merchant**, the Coin its measure. Wrath sits oddly on a scale built to weigh fair value: the same hour that should be counting cost instead closes its fist over nothing, spending fury the way an angry man spends a coin he will never get back.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the afternoon is **Maturity**, and Mars wears working amber (#FFB400) — the age that should have already learned to hold its temper. Wrath is Maturity's oldest failure: the grip that ought to have steadied by now instead closes tighter, mistaking the exhaustion of a long day's climb for a right to burn whoever is closest.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Wrath stands at 18h — Autumn, red, pointed at the autumnal equinox — sharing the spoke with Venus' Jealousy. Mars beside Venus, the oldest pairing turned to its worst use: blood and a wilting rose on the same arm, both sins that mistake grip for strength.
variants.trio: On the Trinity, Wrath moves to 20h onto Love's red arm beside Venus. It is love's own armor gone rigid — the sentry who has forgotten what he is guarding and now simply fights, the defence continuing long after there is anything left to defend.

mercury.name: Greed
mercury.base:
[[The Figure]] Greed is Wednesday's purple gone grasping — Mercury's own shadow, the merchant's clear-eyed understanding of value curdled into simple appetite for it. The same mind that can weigh anything correctly begins, in Greed, to weigh everything as a thing to be kept. It does not lock the treasure; it locks the hand, unable to open even when opening would cost nothing.

[[On the Dial]] It rules the same midnight arm as Wisdom, Tyrian purple (#542E85) — history's own joke on the sin, since that purple was itself the costliest pigment of the ancient world, a color that was a trade empire. Midnight is the accounting hour, when the market has closed and what remains is Sorrow's own task: weighing what the day was worth. Greed is what happens when that honest grief stops asking whether the day was fair and starts asking only whether it was enough — and the answer is never yes.

[[The Lesson]] Its cure falls the whole height of the dial: Jupiter's Generosity at noon, the open hand answering the closed one across the full vertical spine. The merchant is not asked to stop counting — counting well is Wisdom's own gift — only to remember that a scale is for finding the fair weight, not for making sure none of it leaves the table.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the midnight arm at 0h in Tyrian purple (#542E85), the closed-fist reading of the ledger the base article tells whole.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns Greed's purple to magenta (#BD00BD) — the one hue in no rainbow, invented by the eye where the spectrum's two ends meet. Fitting: at midnight the hoarding mind wears a color that, like its own math, exists only in the wanting.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the evening arm now drapes in stage-velvet violet (#7A2E8E) — the Walk of **the Artist**, the Mask its craft. Greed is what happens when that same quick mind stops performing for an audience and starts performing only for itself: the Mask kept on long after the curtain falls, a clever face still calculating what it can keep rather than what it can give.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the evening is **Old Age**, and Mercury wears dusk violet (#9C6BD4) — the hour for totaling what a life has actually been worth. Greed is Old Age's refusal to close the ledger honestly: the hand that should be settling its accounts instead keeps counting, unable to call any total, however large, enough.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Greed keeps the bottom arm at 0h — Winter, blue, pointed at the winter solstice — alone, sharing it with no one. Even its cure has no partner here: the one sin that can sit at the bottom of the wheel by itself and still refuse to balance the books.
variants.trio: The Trinity lifts Greed off midnight to 04h, onto Hope's blue arm beside Fear. It is hope's own arithmetic gone wrong — not faith that tomorrow provides, but the refusal to believe it will unless everything is already counted and kept.

jupiter.name: Excess
jupiter.base:
[[The Figure]] Excess is Thursday's yellow overflowing — Jupiter's own vice, generosity that never learned where the floor is. The royal table that fed everyone becomes the royal table that cannot stop being spread, past the guest's hunger and past the host's own good sense. A gift with no measure eventually cannot be received by anyone, least of all the one still trying to give it — the table fails from its own weight, not from anything attacking it.

[[On the Dial]] It rules the same noon arm as Generosity, bright yellow (#F8E600), because Excess is not a different gift from the one Jupiter gives at noon — it is that same gift with no one left minding when it should stop. Noon's own mood is Joy, which asks nothing back for its light; Excess is what happens when a mood that asks nothing back also forgets to notice it has already given everything worth giving.

[[The Lesson]] Its cure rises from the opposite pole: Mercury's Wisdom at midnight, the deep counting mind teaching the high, giving hand when enough has already been reached. Generosity does not need to shrink to be cured — it needs the merchant's honest ledger, the one discipline that can tell a king the difference between a full table and a collapsing one.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the top arm at 12h in noon yellow (#F8E600), the overflow of the base article's own collapsing table.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns Excess's noon to green (#00DC00) — the brightest wavelength the eye can hold. The hour keeps its overflow; light simply measures exactly how far past the peak the table has already gone.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the morning arm now wears alb ivory (#EDEDE0) — the Walk of **the Priest**, the Bell calling the hour. Excess is the Priest who never stops ringing it: the same open hand that blesses freely keeps giving long after the blessing has already landed, generosity that has forgotten a sermon, like a bell, is supposed to end.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the morning is **Childhood**, and Jupiter wears spring green (#7CE577) — the age that has not yet learned where enough sits. Excess is Childhood's own hunger left uncorrected: the gift asked for again and again, not from want but from a mind too young still to notice the table is already full.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Excess stands at 12h on the Summer arm, yellow, beside the Sun's own Pride — the year's two overreaching sins on one spoke, the overflowing table and the doubled crown both certain that too much is simply proof of how much there is to give.
variants.trio: On the Trinity, Excess keeps the top arm at 12h, yellow — but the arm now reads Faith, shared with Saturn's Envy. It is faith that has stopped waiting for its own harvest: a table set before the seed has even had its season, generosity spent on a promise that has not yet come due.

venus.name: Jealousy
venus.base:
[[The Figure]] Jealousy is Friday's red curdled — not love's opposite but its own shadow, the fear of losing what is already held. It begins exactly where Love does, in caring enough that the caring matters, and goes wrong only in the next step: caring so much that holding on replaces trusting. What it is trying hardest to keep is the very thing its own grip is killing — never threatened from outside, only wilting from its own tightening.

[[On the Dial]] It rules the same evening arm as Love, deep red (#B60000), because Jealousy is not a colder feeling than Love — it is the same warm one, Passion itself, with a grip added. Evening is when the day's work softens into its emotional life, the theatre lights coming up on whatever the heart actually wants; Jealousy is what happens when that same heart starts rehearsing the ways it might lose the thing it wants, until the rehearsal becomes the relationship.

[[The Lesson]] Its cure crosses from the morning arm: Saturn's Patience, insecurity outwaited rather than argued with. The two slow arts, waiting and loving, mend each other — Patience does not ask the heart to care less, only to hold the rose the way the farmer holds a season: certain enough of the harvest that it does not need to squeeze the stem to prove it is still there.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 20h arm in deep red (#B60000), the evening's own warmth turned to a grip in the base article's reading.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism keeps Jealousy at 20h but purifies the red to its light primary (#FF0000) — the reddest red there is, unmixed. The feeling loses none of its heat by being named more precisely; if anything the coil shows plainer.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the sunset arm now wears iron-blood crimson (#A02020) — the Walk of **the Soldier**, the Sword drawn to defend. Jealousy is love conscripted into that same office: the heart set on guard over what it already holds, armed against a rival that is, more often than not, only its own fear of losing the thing it is failing to trust.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the sunset arm is **the Elder** — the harvest of a whole life gathered in — and Venus wears ember (#FF6A3C). Jealousy is the Elder who cannot yet trust the harvest is in: still rehearsing every way the gathered love might be taken, unable to let the ember simply glow instead of being watched.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Jealousy stands at 18h — Autumn, red, pointed at the autumnal equinox — sharing the spoke with Mars' Wrath. Venus beside Mars at their worst: the rose gripped and the fist raised are the same failure of the same old pairing, love and war both mistaking force for care.
variants.trio: Jealousy does not move on the Trinity: Love's arm is its own 20h in its own red, the sin that never has to travel to find its virtue — only to remember it. The Soldier's Wrath keeps the same spoke, guarding the same dark hours with the same fire aimed the wrong way.

saturn.name: Envy
saturn.base:
[[The Figure]] Envy is Saturday's green soured — Saturn's own bitter shadow, and by the old reckoning the oldest failure of anyone who has learned to wait. It starts as Patience's own eye, the one that can see how another's field is doing, and goes wrong in the next breath: watching becomes wanting, and wanting becomes resentment that the watching was ever necessary at all. The neighbor's field was never guarded against him; the fence is only as tall as his own attention keeps making it.

[[On the Dial]] It rules the same morning arm as Patience, field green (#007E00), because Envy is not a different color from growth — it is Renewal's own hue looked at sideways, over a fence, at a stalk that is not one's own. The farmer's whole faith is that waiting works; Envy is what happens when the same farmer starts measuring his wait against someone else's harvest instead of his own soil.

[[The Lesson]] Its cure reaches from the evening: Venus' Love, warmth dissolving the cold arithmetic of what someone else has. Love does not lower the neighbor's fence or raise the farmer's harvest — it simply gives the farmer something to tend that is worth more, to him, than what is on the other side of it.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 08h arm in field green (#007E00), the morning's own growth soured into the fence-line stare of the base article.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns Envy's morning green to cyan (#00DDDD) — the color of the clear early sky rather than the field. In the light world the sin still looks outward before it looks down, up over the fence before down at its own row.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the dawn arm keeps field green (#3E8914) — the Walk of **the Farmer**, the Plough turning his own soil. Envy is the Farmer who has stopped looking at his own furrow: patience curdled into a fence-line stare at a neighbor's greener stalks, the plough still in hand but pointed, in spirit, at ground that was never his to work.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the dawn arm is **Birth**, and Saturn wears predawn mist (#8FA8C8) — the hour before anything has proven itself. Envy is Birth measured against a birth not its own: resentment already forming before the first light has even cleared, certain someone else's dawn arrived with a better field attached.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Envy stands at 06h — Spring, green, pointed at the vernal equinox — sharing the spoke with the Moon's Fear. Two patient professions' failures on one arm: the grower's grudge and the healer's dread, both the cost of professions that are supposed to know how to wait and, this once, didn't.
variants.trio: The Trinity promotes Envy from the morning to the crown: the 12h Faith arm, yellow, shared with Jupiter's Excess. It is faith that has stopped believing its own seed is enough — envy dressed as ambition, wanting the height of someone else's table instead of trusting the height of its own field.

sun.name: Glory · Awe
sun.base:
[[The Figure]] Sunday alone is doubled, and this theme's whole system rests on that seam: the wheel's center holds not one mood but two, Glory bright and Awe dark, the same throne wearing two lights. Glory casts no shadow at all, because at that height it is the light rather than something merely lit by it; Awe's own shadow stretches long, the mark of one who is watched by the light rather than being it. Every other day of the week gets one mood and one hour. Sunday gets a mood that has no hour, doubled into a mood that has no hour either — only a direction to look.

[[On the Dial]] Both faces share the same address on the dial: the center, which belongs to no arm and therefore to no clock-hour at all. Glory is not noon, though it wears noon's own gold — it is what every hour looks like at its most complete, not one hour but the sum of all of them seen at their best. Awe keeps the same seat but wears it from underneath, in black with a thin silver trim rather than a color of its own, because a servant does not get to redecorate the throne he serves beneath.

This is the axis every other opposite pair on the dial has to build across twelve hours of arm — Calm answering Zeal, Sorrow answering Joy, Passion answering Renewal, each mood facing its opposite from the far side of the wheel. Glory and Awe cannot do that; nothing stands opposite the center, so their opposition has nowhere to travel to. It collapses into one seat read from two heights: Glory is being seen, Awe is seeing. Psychology's own wheel agrees down to the compound — fear plus surprise is exactly Plutchik's own recipe for awe, the feeling of standing under something larger than yourself — and the dial keeps the same rule: whoever holds the center is watched from below, and whoever watches from below keeps the center honest.

[[The Hour]] That is also why the pair has no hour to rule the way Calm rules four o'clock or Joy rules noon. Every mood the week passes through — noon's Joy, midnight's Sorrow, the Renewal of Saturday morning — is a version of the same light the center already holds in full, and Glory's discipline is to hold under all of them without spending itself on any one. Awe is the mood that remembers to look up while it happens.

variants.hexa_primary: On the painter's wheel Glory keeps the center of the dial, white-gold, belonging to no hour: the six pigment arms are its own light taken apart, every rim mood a fraction of what the center holds whole. This is the pair's home reading — the source, not a spoke — with Awe waiting, unseen, at the same address.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism wheel changes every arm around it but cannot touch the center: Glory stays white-gold, because in the light world it is literally true that white is the sum of every color. Newton's reading only proves what the throne already claimed of itself.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the noon arm crowns itself in royal gold (#F0C420) — the Walk of **the King**, the Crown its whole office. Glory is the King seen at that exact crown, majesty owned rather than merely worn; Awe is the same throne watched from below, too bright to meet head-on.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel noon is **Youth** — the blazing zenith of a life — and the Sun wears sun-yellow (#FFE800). Glory is Youth at its own peak, unspent and certain of itself; Awe is the same zenith glimpsed from beneath, the feeling of standing under a height not yet one's own to claim.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Glory stands at 12h on the Summer arm, yellow, its center pointed at the summer solstice — the sun's own festival — sharing the spoke with Joy itself. Two golds on one arm: the mood with no hour and the mood that owns noon, holding the year's longest light together.
variants.trio: On the Trinity, Glory keeps the center, and the court beneath it narrows to three arms: Faith's yellow carrying Joy and Renewal, Love's red carrying Zeal and Passion, Hope's blue carrying Sorrow and Calm. Six rim hours folded into three spokes under one unmoved white-gold sum — the oldest argument the center ever made, read here in moods instead of virtues.

faces.ruler:
Glory is Sunday's bright face, the one mood on the wheel that is not tied to any hour because it does not need to wait for one — it is noon's own gold read at its most complete: light that casts no shadow at all, because at that height it is not lit by the light but is the light, open to itself rather than resisting itself.

Glory's opposite is Awe, and the two need each other more than any of the six paired hours do, because they cannot even face each other across the dial — the center has no far side. Glory is being seen; Awe is seeing. It is also, without needing an hour of its own, secretly present at every one of the day's other peaks: it is what noon's Joy is reaching for, what midnight's Sorrow has temporarily lost, the light the whole week is measured against.
faces.servant:
Awe is Sunday's dark face, kept at the same center as Glory but read from the opposite height — fear and wonder in a single feeling, and a shadow, unlike Glory's own, that stretches long: the mark of one who is watched by the light rather than being it.

Its opposite is Glory, and psychology already keeps the recipe for the distance between them: fear plus surprise compound, in Plutchik's own wheel, into exactly this feeling — the sense of standing under something larger than yourself. Glory is being seen, Awe is seeing, and the dial's own logic is that a center watched from below stays honest; take away the watcher from below and the ruler's light would have nothing left to answer to.

moon.name: Calm
moon.base:
[[The Figure]] Calm rides Monday's blue, the temperature of a world still asleep — no ripple, no wingbeat, nothing that would count as an event.

[[On the Dial]] Its home arm sits at dial 4h in deep blue (#002FFF), the stillest hour of the whole night. The placement is not gentle — it is the hardest test the mood has: four in the morning is where yesterday is fully spent and tomorrow has not yet arrived, and the water only holds its stillness because nothing has come along yet to ask it to move.

Its opposite is Zeal, twelve hours around the dial on Tuesday's orange at 16h — the one other mood measured by how a body holds itself, a heron's stillness against a blacksmith's motion. Each is the picture of the other's absence: Zeal is effort with nowhere left to hide it, Calm is effort that has, for one hour, nowhere left to go.

[[The Hour]] Calm rules the pre-dawn hour because that is where stillness is worth the most and costs the most: the darkest, longest stretch of the night, when it would be easiest to panic and the heron does not. The dial's map of feeling puts this hour first for a reason — every day's other six moods get to move; this one's whole argument is that, for one hour, nothing has to.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 4h arm in deep blue (#002FFF), Calm at the hour before dawn — the heron's stillness, as the base reading holds it.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism wheel keeps Calm at 4h but sharpens the blue to #0040FF — pigment's hushed night becomes light's more electric one. The hour and the stillness both hold; only the water's color changes under it.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the deep-night arm now reads by lamplit ink blue (#1F5FA8) — the Walk of **the Scholar**, the Book held open in the stillest hour. Calm is exactly the Scholar's own condition: a mind awake while the rest of the night sleeps, untroubled because it has found something steady to hold its attention rather than its fear.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the deep-night arm belongs to **the Unborn**, and the Moon wears moonlight silver (#C8D7F0) — the hour of those not yet arrived and those already gone. Calm is the stillness that hour asks of anyone caught between two lives not their own: the heron's steadiness borrowed by a mind simply waiting, unhurried, for whichever life comes next.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Calm moves to the 6h arm — Spring, green, pointed at the vernal equinox — sharing the spoke with Renewal. Two patient moods on one arm: the stillness that waits and the growth that is the waiting's reward, paired at the hour when night finally lets go.
variants.trio: The Trinity keeps Calm at 4h but renames the arm: blue becomes Hope, shared with Sorrow, who moves up from midnight to join it, guarding the morning from 0h to 8h. No pairing reads truer — the stillest hour and the darkest hour turn out to want the same thing from the dawn.

mars.name: Zeal
mars.base:
[[The Figure]] Zeal rides Tuesday's orange, the ember of the working afternoon rather than noon's blaze or evening's open flame — forge-work and foot-work sharing one fire, the same discipline whether the exertion is a hammer's or a stride's.

[[On the Dial]] Its home arm sits at dial 16h in ember orange (#DC9600) — past noon's freshness, before evening lets the day go. The placement is deliberately unglamorous: this is not the dawn charge or the victory lap, it is the hour when the excitement has already worn off and the work is still not finished.

Its opposite is Calm, twelve hours around the dial on Monday's blue at 4h — a heron's stillness against a hammer's motion, and each mood is what the other one is not doing. Where Calm is a body holding itself perfectly still, Zeal is a body that has found a rhythm it can sustain past the point where enthusiasm alone would have quit.

[[The Hour]] Zeal rules the afternoon because that is when the mood is actually earned: anyone can feel it at dawn, when the day is still a promise; the harder trick is still feeling it at four, past noon's glory and short of evening's passion, with nothing left but the discipline of continuing.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 16h arm in ember orange (#DC9600), Zeal at the height of the working afternoon — the banked fire of the base reading.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism keeps Zeal at 16h but burns the ember up to pure yellow (#FFFF00) — red and green fused in light where they only sat side by side in pigment. The hour and its Zeal hold; the fire simply reads hotter.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the afternoon arm now trades in copper (#C87533) — the Walk of **the Merchant**, the Coin weighed fairly. Zeal is the same discipline turned to labor rather than ledger: the steady, unglamorous push of an afternoon that keeps working because the work, like a fair trade, is worth finishing properly rather than abandoning halfway.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the afternoon is **Maturity**, and Mars wears working amber (#FFB400) — the age that has traded youth's blaze for something that lasts longer. Zeal fits that age exactly: not the first excitement of a young effort but the steadier burn of someone who has learned how to keep working past the hour enthusiasm alone would have quit.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Zeal moves to the 18h arm — Autumn, red, pointed at the autumnal equinox — sharing the spoke with Passion. The oldest pairing in the sky, read in moods instead of gods: autumn's red belongs to the ember and the flame both, effort and desire meeting on one arm.
variants.trio: The Trinity moves Zeal from 16h to 20h, onto Love's red arm beside Passion, which does not move — and together the two guard the evening from 16h to 24h. The pairing explains itself: effort sustained long enough starts to look like love; Zeal is simply Passion before it admits what it is working for.

mercury.name: Sorrow
mercury.base:
[[The Figure]] Sorrow rides Wednesday's purple, red mourning dissolved into blue stillness rather than despair outright — grief thinned to a single fallen drop rather than a flood.

[[On the Dial]] Its home arm sits at dial 0h — midnight, the bottom of the wheel — in deep Tyrian purple (#542E85), history's own quiet joke on the mood: the costliest pigment the ancient world ever made, worn at the one hour when nothing is being bought or sold. Midnight is the accounting hour of feeling the same way it is the accounting hour of trade — the day is over, and what is left is to weigh what it cost.

Its opposite is Joy, twelve hours around the dial on Thursday's yellow at noon — the day's two extremes of light, one at its brightest and one gone entirely. Where Joy scatters outward, arms thrown wide, Sorrow gathers inward, one bowed figure and one falling drop; each mood is what the other spends all its light avoiding.

[[The Hour]] Sorrow rules midnight because every honest day closes there: the grave of the day's light, where whatever the day was worth is finally told apart from what it merely looked like. It is not despair — it is depth, the mind's own hour, thought running on alone after the world outside it has gone quiet.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the midnight arm at 0h in Tyrian purple (#542E85), Sorrow at the hour of the closed ledger — the base reading.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns the purple to magenta (#BD00BD) — the one hue found in no rainbow, a color the eye invents only where the spectrum's two ends meet. A fitting hour for Sorrow to wear a color that exists only in the mind that is doing the mourning.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the evening arm now drapes in stage-velvet violet (#7A2E8E) — the Walk of **the Artist**, the Mask its instrument. Sorrow is the Mask taken off after the performance ends: the evening's own quiet reckoning, feeling weighed rather than performed, the same violet that dressed the stage now dressing the private grief left when the audience has gone.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the evening is **Old Age**, and Mercury wears dusk violet (#9C6BD4) — the hour for weighing what a whole life has amounted to. Sorrow belongs there honestly: not despair but depth, the accounting a long life owes itself once the day's noise has finally gone quiet enough to hear the total.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Sorrow keeps the bottom arm at 0h — Winter, blue, pointed at the winter solstice — and shares it with no other mood at all. The year's own midnight belongs to exactly one figure: the mood that can sit at the bottom of the wheel, alone, and still keep its composure.
variants.trio: The Trinity lifts Sorrow off midnight to 4h, onto Hope's blue arm beside Calm, guarding the morning from 0h to 8h. The move names the mood's real secret: the ledger that closes in sorrow at midnight reopens in hope by morning, because grief that does not expect an answer is only despair wearing a nicer coat.

jupiter.name: Joy
jupiter.base:
[[The Figure]] Joy rides Thursday's yellow, the day's own generosity given a shape — light not aimed at anything in particular, simply too much to keep in one place.

[[On the Dial]] Its home arm is the top of the dial, 12h, in bright yellow (#F8E600) — "jovial" means, literally, of Jupiter — and noon is the one hour of the day that needs no lamp: the peak, when light is given away more freely than at any other point on the wheel.

Its opposite is Sorrow, twelve hours around the dial on Wednesday's purple at midnight — noon's brightest reading answered by the one hour with none at all. Where Sorrow gathers a single figure inward around one falling drop, Joy throws its own figure's arms open and lets the light scatter outward without keeping any of it back.

[[The Hour]] Joy rules noon for the same reason the sun does: it is the hour that asks nothing back for its own light. Every other mood on the wheel is earned by an hour's particular hardship — Calm's stillness, Zeal's grind, Sorrow's weight — but noon simply gives, and Joy is what receiving that gift, undeserved and unrepayable, feels like.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the top arm at 12h in noon yellow (#F8E600), Joy at the day's own peak — the base reading.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns noon to green (#00DC00) — the wavelength at the very summit of human sight, the brightest color the eye can register. Joy keeps its hour; the light world simply measures the peak instead of painting it.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the morning arm now wears alb ivory (#EDEDE0) — the Walk of **the Priest**, the Bell ringing the hour freely for anyone within earshot. Joy is that same open-handed ringing given a mood instead of an office: light given away because morning asks nothing back for it, the bell's plain gladness needing no congregation to justify itself.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the morning is **Childhood**, and Jupiter wears spring green (#7CE577) — the age that has not yet learned to measure its own delight. Joy is Childhood's native condition: laughter thrown wide before anyone has taught it to be careful with its own light, the gift of a life not yet old enough to hold anything back.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Joy stands at 12h on the Summer arm, yellow, pointed at the summer solstice, sharing the spoke with Glory itself. Two golds on the year's highest arm: the mood that owns noon and the mood that has no hour, holding the longest light of the year together.
variants.trio: On the Trinity, Joy keeps the top arm at 12h, yellow — but the yellow now names Faith, and Joy shares the arm with Renewal, who moves up to join it from the morning, guarding the day's height from 8h to 16h. The reading explains itself: Joy is what faith looks like once it has already been rewarded.

venus.name: Passion
venus.base:
[[The Figure]] Passion rides Friday's red, the sky itself turned the color of the mood as the evening star opens over the sunset. Its whole tension is the reach, not the meeting — the wanting matters more than the arrival.

[[On the Dial]] Its home arm sits at dial 20h in deep red (#B60000), the evening — the exact hour Venus herself rises as the evening star. The hour fits the mood precisely: evening is when the day's work lets go of the heart it was holding all along, when the material world of the daylight hours softens into its own feeling.

Its opposite is Renewal, twelve hours around the dial on Saturday's green at 8h — one mood reaching toward a partner across a burning sky, the other reaching down into soil that has not yet produced anything to reach back. Passion wants what is already in front of it; Renewal waits for what has not arrived yet.

[[The Hour]] Passion rules the evening because passion is what the daylight hours were always for: the day earns, and the evening is where all of that earning finally gets to be felt rather than spent. The reach not quite arriving is the whole argument — the mood is not the arrival, it is the entire distance still being crossed.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 20h arm in deep red (#B60000), Passion at the evening star's own hour — the base reading.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism keeps Passion at 20h but purifies the red to its light primary (#FF0000) — the reddest red there is, with nothing mixed into it. In Newton's world Passion is not a pigment but a wavelength, and the evening simply burns in it.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the sunset arm now wears iron-blood crimson (#A02020) — the Walk of **the Soldier**, the Sword raised in earnest. Passion borrows the same readiness for a gentler war: the evening's whole reaching toward another person fought with exactly the Soldier's nerve, a heart that advances on what it wants with a blade's own certainty, if not its violence.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the sunset arm is **the Elder** — a life's harvest gathered in — and Venus wears ember (#FF6A3C). Passion at that age is memory more than reach: the same want recalled rather than pursued, the fire banked into a warmer, quieter glow that remembers wanting more clearly than it still wants.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Passion stands at 18h — Autumn, red, pointed at the autumnal equinox — sharing the spoke with Zeal. Autumn's red belongs to both moods at once, effort and desire meeting on the year's own turning point.
variants.trio: Passion does not move: the Trinity's Love arm is its own 20h in its own red, since love is this mood's whole material in both readings at once. Zeal joins it there, and together the two guard the evening from 16h to 24h — one mood keeping what is wanted safe, the other keeping the wanting itself alive.

saturn.name: Renewal
saturn.base:
[[The Figure]] Renewal rides Saturday's green, dew and growth on turned soil rather than any grander gesture — nothing dramatic, just a thing that was buried, coming up anyway.

[[On the Dial]] Its home arm sits at dial 8h in field green (#007E00), the morning. The paradox is the whole point: the slowest planet in the sky is given the freshest hour of the day, because no mood on the wheel understands better than this one that mornings keep coming back regardless of how long the wait before them felt.

Its opposite is Passion, twelve hours around the dial on Friday's red at 20h — one mood reaching toward a partner it can already see, the other trusting toward a harvest it cannot see yet. Where Passion is the feeling of wanting, Renewal is the feeling of having waited long enough that wanting has turned into something steadier.

[[The Hour]] Renewal rules the morning because that is where the mood's whole faith actually lives: every morning the field looks slightly different than it did the day before, and every seed sown into it is a small bet that the waiting will have been worth it — a bet this mood keeps making, on schedule, every single week.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 8h arm in field green (#007E00), Renewal at the morning — the base reading.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns the morning green to cyan (#00DDDD) — the color of the clear early sky rather than the field itself. Renewal keeps its hour; in the light world it simply looks up before it looks down.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the dawn arm keeps field green (#3E8914) — the Walk of **the Farmer**, the Plough already turning new ground. Renewal is the Farmer's whole creed made into a mood: the field looking slightly different every morning, and the plough returning to it anyway, certain that what was buried is already on its way back up.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the dawn arm is **Birth**, and Saturn wears predawn mist (#8FA8C8) — the hour before anything has had the chance to prove itself yet. Renewal and Birth are nearly the same wager: a field sown on faith and a life begun on none, both betting that the mist will lift into something worth the waiting.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Renewal stands at 6h — Spring, green, pointed at the vernal equinox: sowing season, its own festival — sharing the spoke with Calm. Two patient moods together at the hour night finally lets go: the growth that waits and the stillness that waited for it.
variants.trio: The Trinity promotes Renewal from the morning to the crown: the 12h Faith arm, yellow, shared with Joy, guarding the day's height from 8h to 16h. The oldest sermon there is, read as mood instead of virtue: growth performed patiently enough starts to look exactly like joy that arrived on time.

sun.base:
[[The Figure]] Zeus is the storm made into law — the sky-father who ended the age of the Titans and then had to learn to govern the unruly family he freed. The thunderbolt is his weapon because the storm was always his first form of law, and the eagle is his bird because no creature outranks it among the ones that fly; behind both stands the oak at Dodona, his oldest oracle, where the god was said to speak through the rustle of its own leaves. The Planetary roster hung this plate on Thursday; the Pantheon reads rank — the king of the gods takes the throne of the week.

[[On the Dial]] On the six-armed dial he takes no arm at all: Sunday sits in the center, colored white-gold. This is the founding sentence of the whole design — white light is the sum of all colors, so the six arm-hues around him are one kingdom decomposed: the star is the prism, and the throne is what goes into it. Olympus drawn as optics — six provinces radiating from one seat, each day one color of the king's light.

[[The Lesson]] His virtue is Justice, the guest-law he enforces precisely because he is bound by it himself, and his vice is Pride, the myths its catalog: a hundred disguises, the king believing the rules could bend around him where the oath could not. His cure crosses no axis; the center heals itself. Yet the center is DOUBLE, two virtues, two vices, two moods in one seat, argued here by blood: the throne above wears Justice, Pride and Glory, while the throne below — his brother Hades, this Sunday's shadow face — wears Humility, Servility and Awe. Three brothers drew lots for the world; the dial refuses to forget the sky and the underworld came out of the same urn.

[[The Hour]] That is also why he rules no single hour. Glory is his weather: noon's Joy is the court in session, evening's Passion the feast after it, pre-dawn Calm a kingdom asleep under one law — every mood on the wheel is the throne's weather at a different angle.

variants.hexa_primary: The home reading: the center of the dial, white-gold, the source from which all six moods radiate. The king who spent the Planetary roster on Thursday's crown now takes the hub itself — Sunday does not sit among the days; the days sit around Sunday, the way the Olympians sit around one throne.
variants.hexa_secondary: In the light palette nothing about him changes — still the center, still white-gold. Every arm around him translates from pigment to beam, but white is the sum in both worlds; the throne is the one point where the two readings agree — fitting for the keeper of oaths, whose word is supposed to bind in every world it is spoken in.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the noon arm crowns itself in royal gold (#F0C420) — the Walk of **the King**, the Crown its very office — and no seat on the wheel fits its occupant more plainly than this one fits Zeus. The king of Olympus needs no argument for the King's estate; the Crown he already wears on every other reading is simply, here, the wheel's own object as well as his own.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel noon is **Youth** — life at its blazing height — and Zeus wears sun-yellow (#FFE800), the same brightness he threw off as a boy hidden from his father's own hunger. Youth suits the god who overthrew a whole generation of Titans before he ever sat still enough to become the aging Sky-Father the later myths remember.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross his arm at 12h is Summer, colored yellow, and he shares it with Apollo. The cross arms point at the solstices and equinoxes: this is the midsummer arm, the year's longest light, where the throne and the son who answers on its behalf hold the peak of the year together — the same summit they have always shared, read now from the father's side.
variants.trio: On the Trinity Zeus keeps the center, and the star around him thins to three arms — Faith's yellow, Love's red, Hope's blue, the painter's own primaries. The founding sentence holds at its simplest for the keeper of oaths: three virtues instead of six moods — three things a king swears to uphold — and all of them still one white light taken apart.

faces.ruler:
Zeus is the Ruler face of the Sunday throne by the oldest right a king can claim — not a borrowed sun but the sky-father who ended the age of the Titans and then had to learn to govern the unruly family he freed, the throne every other Olympian throne answers to.

His virtue is Justice, the law of guest and host he enforces on every mortal precisely because he is bound by it himself — the king who cannot break the oath without breaking the throne under him — but that same authority tempts Pride, and the myths are a catalog of it: a hundred disguises taken because the king believed the rules could bend around him even where the oath could not. His mood is Glory, the storm parting to gold light, the throne at its fullest hour — noon with a crown on.
faces.servant:
Hades is the Servant face, not a lesser god but Zeus's own brother, drawing the throne no one else wanted when the three of them split the world by lot — proof that the dial's shadow face is not evil, only the same royal blood facing the other direction.

His virtue is Humility — of the three brothers, only Hades never left his kingdom to scheme for a better one, ruling the worse-esteemed lot as faithfully as Zeus rules the visible sky — but that same constancy risks Servility, mistaken by outsiders for mere guarding rather than reigning. His mood is Awe, an empty throne room's hush, dark majesty rather than terror — Glory's own far side, the same crown worn where no one claps.

moon.base:
[[The Figure]] Poseidon is the sea as a person — not a god who rules water from somewhere dry but the water itself given a throne, one of three brothers who drew lots for the world and kept the two-thirds that move. His trident is both sceptre and weapon in one, because the sea he claims keeps both tempers as a single office: glass calm at dawn, a grave by dusk, never two gods but one. The Greeks called him Earth-Shaker as often as Sea-Lord — the same restlessness under both titles.

[[On the Dial]] His home on the hexa paint dial is the arm at 4h, deep blue, the hour before dawn — Calm. The lower half of the dial is the night, and 4h is its stillest chamber; but Poseidon's claim to that hour is not borrowed the way it was for Selene, it is physical: the Moon literally drags his tides, twice a day, whether he consents or not. Blue is the sea's own color before any myth is added to it, and silver is his metal, crowning the dial's midnight tip the way gold crowns its noon.

[[The Lesson]] His virtue is Serenity and his vice is Fear, and no figure on the dial earns that pair more literally: the same water is glass at dawn and a grave by dusk. He is the Physician all the same — the cult title Poseidon Asphaleios, "the Securer," was invoked exactly as a healer is invoked, to steady what shakes, whether a ship's deck or the ground itself. Across the dial Artemis answers: Courage cures Fear, and Serenity quells Wrath — the huntress and the sea-lord bound to one axis.

[[The Hour]] Calm rules the hour before dawn because that is where the sea is tested honestly: no wind yet to prove it gentle, no storm yet to prove it cruel — only the water, and whatever is trusted to cross it.

variants.hexa_primary: The home reading: the 4h arm, painter's deep blue, Monday's Calm in the hour before dawn — the sea-lord keeping the stillest watch of the night, the one hour even his own tides seem briefly to hold their breath before turning again, patient the way only something that has never once missed a turning can afford to be.
variants.hexa_secondary: The same 4h arm, but the blue turns electric — in the light wheel, blue is one of the three primaries of light itself, not a mixture poured from other colors. Calm read through the prism is bedrock, not blend: the sea's own stillness taken down to the one wavelength that makes it blue at all.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the deep-night arm now reads by lamplit ink blue (#1F5FA8) — the Walk of **the Scholar**, the Book its instrument — an odd seat for a sea-god until the trident is set down: Poseidon Earth-Shaker studies the deep the way a scholar studies a text he can never fully close, tides worked out by patient calculation long before any storm proves the sum correct.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the deep-night arm belongs to **the Unborn**, and Poseidon wears moonlight silver (#C8D7F0) — the hour of ancestors and of those not yet come. The sea already keeps both: every wrecked hull returned to it and every ship not yet launched across it, the god of the water simply presiding over the one arm built from what has not yet happened as much as what already has.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross he holds the 6h arm — Spring, green — and shares it with Demeter. The arm points at the spring equinox, the year's own dawn: the sea-lord who steadies what shakes and the grain-mother whose daughter has just come back up share the year's morning between them.
variants.trio: The Trinity leaves Poseidon on his 4h arm but renames the post: the blue now means Hope, shared with Athena, and with the pre-dawn hour at its very tip it guards the morning third, 0h to 8h. The Securer who steadies the shaking ground now guards the hour that promises the shaking will stop — calm turned to face what comes.

mars.base:
[[The Figure]] Artemis is the hunt without the parade the way her brother rules the light without the throne — a virgin huntress the other Olympians learned early not to provoke. Her office is the stalk before the kill rather than the trophy after it, and no hunter under her law is ever fully safe from becoming the hunted: Actaeon learned that by becoming the stag himself, and Niobe learned it a different way, losing every child she had boasted of to Artemis's arrows and Apollo's together.

[[On the Dial]] Her home is the arm at 16h, orange, the working afternoon — Tuesday's Zeal. Orange is fire domesticated, and the hunt is exactly that: not the single dramatic kill but the hours of the stalk before it, the patient tracking that makes the strike look effortless when it finally comes. 16h is the soldier's drill-and-march hour, and the hunt is a soldier's craft in every particular but the uniform.

[[The Lesson]] Her virtue is Courage and her vice is Wrath, and the bow that feeds a village is the same bow that answers an insult with annihilation — Actaeon's hounds and Niobe's children are Tuesday's fire pointed the wrong way. Her cure hangs straight across the dial in Poseidon's blue: Serenity quells Wrath, while her own Courage, in return, cures his Fear — the huntress and the sea-lord healing each other along one axis.

[[The Hour]] Zeal rules the working afternoon because the hunt is rarely won in the first hour: it is won by whoever is still moving quietly when the light starts to fail.

variants.hexa_primary: The home reading: the 16h arm, ember orange, Tuesday's Zeal of the working afternoon — the huntress keeping the hour of the patient stalk rather than the hour of the kill, when the bow is drawn but nothing has been loosed yet — patience with an edge, which is what the ember always was underneath the blaze.
variants.hexa_secondary: The same 16h arm, but the prism has no pigment orange to offer — the ember flares to full yellow, red and green light summed to their brightest. Zeal read as light rather than paint is louder and harder to look away from: the stalk lit up as if the forest itself were watching.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the afternoon arm now trades in copper (#C87533) — the Walk of **the Merchant**, the Coin its measure of worth — a stranger seat for a huntress than the Soldier's used to be, yet no goddess reads a fair value more exactly: Artemis takes only what a village needs and no more, the hunt itself a kind of honest accounting between what the forest can give and what is owed back to it.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the afternoon is **Maturity**, and Artemis wears working amber (#FFB400) — patience over blaze, the steady stalk that makes the strike look effortless only because the discipline came first. No huntress on the dial earns that age more plainly: the bow drawn full is not a young hand's excitement but an old hand's certainty.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross she stands at 18h — Autumn, red — and shares the arm with Hera. It points at the autumn equinox, the year's dusk: the huntress who answers every insult in full and the queen who answers every rival the same way hold the season of the falling leaf together.
variants.trio: On the Trinity Artemis moves to 20h and stands on Love's red arm beside Hera. Together they guard the evening from 16h to 24h. Love reads through the huntress as its watch kept armed: the same bow that punished Actaeon stands sentry now so that what the queen keeps can sleep undisturbed.

mercury.base:
[[The Figure]] Athena is the mind that plans rather than merely reacts — not a goddess who happens to be clever but Wisdom's own person, sprung fully armed from Zeus's skull the day a headache became a birth. Her owl sees precisely where daylight fails, which is why the bird stands for her strategy rather than merely accompanying it, and her olive branch is the gift that won Athens over Poseidon's own salt spring — judged the better offering by the very city that carries her name.

[[On the Dial]] Her home is the arm at the dial's bottom, purple, midnight — Wednesday's Sorrow. Why hand the goddess of clear daylight strategy the darkest hour? Because the owl sees precisely where daylight fails, and purple on this dial is already ruled the night of the MIND — wisdom won in the dark, not the realm of darkness itself, which lives elsewhere on the wheel. Midnight is where a council actually decides something, after the arguing is done.

[[The Lesson]] Her virtue is Wisdom by the seat's own name, and her vice is Greed — the same counsel that plans a city's defense can start hoarding the plan as a possession rather than a gift to the polis. Her cure stands straight overhead: Apollo at noon, whose Generosity cures Greed, while her Wisdom, in return, curbs his Excess.

[[The Hour]] Sorrow suits midnight because that is the hour real counsel is paid for: not the speech given in daylight for applause, but the plan reasoned out alone, after everyone who wanted credit has gone to bed.

variants.hexa_primary: The home reading: the midnight arm at the dial's bottom, mourning purple, Wednesday's Sorrow — the owl's hour, when the goddess of daylight strategy does her actual thinking, far from the applause any plan collects once it works, where no one is yet convinced she is right.
variants.hexa_secondary: The same midnight post, but the purple becomes magenta — the prism's impossible color, found in no rainbow, existing only where the eye joins the two far ends of the spectrum. No hue suits the strategist better: a mind that sees the whole board by joining what looks unconnected.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the evening arm now drapes in stage-velvet violet (#7A2E8E) — the Walk of **the Artist**, the Mask its craft — and Athena wears it as strategy rather than performance: the owl's calm sees exactly where the Mask conceals and where it reveals, counsel composed as carefully as any tragedy and delivered, like the best of them, after the audience has already gone quiet.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the evening is **Old Age**, and Athena wears dusk violet (#9C6BD4) — a fitting hour for the goddess whose whole gift is counsel weighed rather than impulse spent. Old Age is Wisdom's own season, and no figure on the dial has done more with a night's patient thinking than the one who was never young in the ordinary sense, born already armed.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross she keeps the bottom of the dial — Winter, blue — and shares the arm with no one. It points at the winter solstice, the year's own midnight: the goddess who plans alone stands that watch alone, exactly as her own owl always has, through every winter the calendar has kept.
variants.trio: The Trinity calls Athena up from midnight to 4h, onto Hope's blue arm beside Poseidon, guarding the morning from 0h to 8h. The strategist is handed the opposite door: not the counsel reasoned out in the dark but the plan already drawn for what comes — hope being wisdom's forward march.

jupiter.base:
[[The Figure]] Apollo is light made into prophecy — Zeus's favorite son, given Delphi as his own oracle and made to answer, through the Pythia's smoke, questions his father would rather leave unspoken. The tripod is his oracle's own instrument and the laurel his crown by the same right; the lyre offered outward argues the gift given freely, and the quiver he keeps within reach argues the same generosity has a harder edge that has already been used once, on the Greek camp's own plague-arrows.

[[On the Dial]] His home is the top of the dial, the 12h arm, yellow — Thursday's Joy at the day's peak. He inherits the crown position honestly: Phoebus, "the radiant one," was already half a sun-title before the later poets finished the conflation, and Delphi made him the Priest and Teacher outright — the one Olympian whose whole office was answering, freely, whatever was asked of him.

[[The Lesson]] His virtue is Generosity and his vice is Excess — prophecy and music given without a price is the open hand, and the same hand loosed the plague-arrows on the Greek camp and skinned Marsyas alive for daring to compete. His cure stands at the dial's other post: Athena's midnight Wisdom curbs Excess, while his Generosity, poured down the same axis, cures her Greed.
