[[The Hour]] Joy rules noon because noon is generosity performed by the sky itself, and Apollo — oracle, healer, musician, archer — is simply that noon given a face and asked to keep giving past the hour it should have stopped.

variants.hexa_primary: The home reading: the noon arm at the dial's top, radiant yellow, Thursday's Joy at the day's peak — the oracle's own hour, when the tripod's smoke is easiest to read and the god has the least reason to withhold an answer, the whole day arranged so nothing stays ambiguous.
variants.hexa_secondary: The same crown position, but the prism turns his yellow to green — light's own primary at the top of the wheel, the band the human eye sees most keenly. In the light reading the oracle wears the color of maximum sight: nothing asked of him at noon escapes his notice.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the morning arm now wears alb ivory (#EDEDE0) — the Walk of **the Priest**, the Bell calling whoever will listen — Apollo's own office in everything but name: Delphi already made him the Priest outright, oracle and healer both, the one Olympian whose entire calling was answering, freely, whatever question was brought to his door.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the morning is **Childhood**, and Apollo wears spring green (#7CE577) — an hour that suits the god of music and prophecy more gently than noon's crown ever did: the fresh, untested brightness of a gift still being discovered rather than already proven, the lyre picked up before the day has asked anything hard of it yet.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross he returns to the top: 12h, Summer, yellow, sharing the arm with Zeus. It points at the summer solstice, the year's longest light, where the throne and the son who answers on its behalf hold the peak of the year together, as they have always shared a summit.
variants.trio: On the Trinity Apollo keeps the top: the 12h arm, yellow — but the yellow is Faith's now, shared with Demeter, and the arm centers the day's third, 8h to 16h, noon at its tip. Faith reads naturally through the oracle: prophecy is faith given a working method, an answer trusted before the outcome is proven.

venus.base:
[[The Figure]] Hera is marriage raised to the rank of an institution — queen before she was ever called wife, sister to Zeus before his consort, and the one Olympian whose whole portfolio is the vow itself rather than what the vow permits. Her cuckoo is the marriage-oath's own emblem, for it was as a wounded, shivering cuckoo that Zeus first won the pity that became her hand; her peacock argues the same vow's other half, a hundred eyes that read as devotion from the front and as watchfulness from the side — love that never once stops keeping guard.

[[On the Dial]] Her home is the arm at 20h, deep red, the evening — Friday's Passion. The placement holds even for an institution: the marriage that survives is the one renewed every evening when the work is done, not merely sworn once at the altar. Red is doubly hers by then — the sunset's color and the hearth-fire's.

[[The Lesson]] Her virtue is Love as vow rather than impulse, and her vice is Jealousy — not love's opposite but its shadow, and no myth on the dial illustrates a vice more thoroughly than hers: Io, Leto, Semele, Heracles, a whole catalog of rivals answered one by one. Her cure stands across the dial in green morning: Demeter's Patience heals Jealousy, while her own Love, in return, dissolves Envy. She is the Artist by the seat's own rule, and the wedding hymn is her medium: a vow is a composed thing, built to be kept in the same way a poem is built to be remembered.

[[The Hour]] Passion rules the evening because that is when the day's business ends and the marriage — the thing actually chosen, not merely inherited — is what remains.

variants.hexa_primary: The home reading: the 20h arm, deep red, Friday's Passion of the evening — the queen's own hour, when the day's business ends and the vow renewed at the hearth outlasts whatever the daylight demanded of it, kept quietly, with no audience left to perform it for.
variants.hexa_secondary: The same evening arm, but the red goes pure — light's first primary at full strength. In the prism world the marriage vow is not a pigment mixed and softened on a palette but an elemental beam: the one color that needs nothing added to be believed on sight.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the sunset arm now wears iron-blood crimson (#A02020) — the Walk of **the Soldier**, the Sword drawn in defense — and no goddess on the dial has defended a vow more relentlessly: Hera's marriage is a fortress held against Zeus's own wandering, Io and Leto and Semele each a campaign fought to keep one oath standing.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the sunset arm is **the Elder** — a life's harvest gathered in — and Hera wears ember (#FF6A3C). The queen of Olympus wears it as an institution's own long memory: marriage is not sworn once and forgotten but renewed at every evening's close, the ember of a vow that has already survived more seasons than most gods bother to count.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross she stands at 18h — Autumn, red — sharing the arm with Artemis. It points at the autumn equinox: the queen who answers every rival and the huntress who answers every insult share a single arm, two different disciplines for the same refusal to be crossed.
variants.trio: Hera does not move: the Trinity's Love arm is her own 20h in her own red, for Love alone belongs to both the seven-arm set and the theological three. Artemis joins her there, and together they guard the evening from 16h to 24h — the vow and the watch that keeps it safe standing one arm apart.

saturn.base:
[[The Figure]] Demeter is the harvest as a mother's patience — grain and grief in the same body, for no other Olympian's private sorrow ever became a season. Her torch is the one she carried searching the world without rest, and her wheat sheaf is the harvest that only resumes once the search ends: winter and spring are the same field before and after her daughter comes back, not two different fields at all. She taught Triptolemus the art of sowing and sent him out to spread it, which makes her agriculture's first teacher as much as its goddess.

[[On the Dial]] Her home is the arm at 8h, green, the morning — Saturday's Renewal. Unlike the titan who once claimed this same arm, there is no paradox to explain here: the grain goddess needs no forcing onto the color of new growth. Green is dew and shoot, and Saturday is the day of rest whose planet, in Hebrew, is named for the Sabbath itself.

[[The Lesson]] Her virtue is Patience, learned across the exact nine days she searched before Zeus intervened, and her vice is Envy — not one myth but a mood: the grief that begrudges every other field its daughter, every other mother her spring, while hers stays below. Her cure stands across the dial in Hera's red evening: Love dissolves Envy, while her own Patience, in return, heals Jealousy.

[[The Hour]] Renewal rules the morning because Persephone's return is the myth Renewal was named after: a third of every year spent in true grief, followed by the exact rebirth green promises. No figure on the dial pays the hour off more literally.

variants.hexa_primary: The home reading: the 8h arm, harvest green, Saturday's Renewal of the morning — the grain-mother keeping the hour when whatever was buried through her nine days of searching finally shows itself above the soil, green proof the waiting was never wasted.
variants.hexa_secondary: The same morning arm, but the green cools to cyan — morning read as sky rather than field, the pale clean light before the first shoot has broken ground at all. In the light reading renewal belongs to the air a moment before it belongs to the wheat itself.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the dawn arm keeps field green (#3E8914) — the Walk of **the Farmer**, the Plough turning new soil — and no goddess needs less persuading into that estate than the one who taught Triptolemus to sow in the first place. Demeter is agriculture's own first teacher, the Farmer's whole craft traced back to a single grieving mother's hand.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the dawn arm is **Birth**, and Demeter wears predawn mist (#8FA8C8) — the exact hour her own myth keeps repeating. Persephone's yearly return is Birth argued as fact rather than metaphor: a third of the year spent in true loss, answered every spring by a green that has never once failed to arrive.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross she keeps 6h — Spring, green — and shares the arm with Poseidon. It points at the spring equinox, the exact season Persephone comes back: the sea-lord who steadies what shakes and the mother whose whole year finally steadies share the year's dawn.
variants.trio: The Trinity lifts Demeter to the crown: the 12h Faith arm, yellow, shared with Apollo — the grieving mother and the god who answers every question about what is coming, guarding the day's height from 8h to 16h. Faith reads through her as the hardest patience of all: to trust a daughter's return every single year, and mean it again each time.

moon.base:
[[The Figure]] Isis is Great of Magic, heka's own mistress and the most venerated goddess Egypt ever raised — sister and wife to Osiris, mother of Horus, and the one deity whose cult outlived the pharaohs themselves, carried by soldiers and merchants until her temples stood as far as the Thames and the Tiber. Her name, Aset, means throne, and she wears that meaning on her own brow: the hieroglyph she carries is the seat of kingship itself, for it is Isis who makes a king by seating one on it. Her tyet knot, crossed with the ankh, is her own protective emblem — the craft that gathers a broken thing back into wholeness.

[[On the Dial]] On the dial she keeps Monday, riding the deep blue arm at 4h — Calm, the hour before dawn, the stillest watch of the night. No goddess earns that blue more honestly: it is the color of the wing-vigil she kept over the infant Horus hidden among the marsh reeds of Chemmis, and Egypt named her tears in the Nile flood itself — the yearly rise called Isis weeping for Osiris, silver water falling from a silver sky. Silver, the Moon's own metal at the dial's bottom tip, is hers by that same right.

[[The Lesson]] Her two faces are exactly the arm's pair of Serenity and Fear. She worked her spells in perfect calm even while hunted through the marshes with a newborn god at her breast, and cured him of a scorpion's sting by naming every poison it could carry — magic as the Serenity that answers Fear rather than denies it. The Physician's arm fits no goddess better: she reassembled a murdered husband and raised a hunted son on nothing but craft and nerve. Her cure stands straight across the dial at 16h: Horus, the falcon she raised in secret, whose Courage cures the Moon's Fear — while Isis's Serenity, in return, is the steady hand that cools her son's Wrath once the throne is finally his.

variants.hexa_primary: The home post: the 04h arm in deep pigment blue (#002FFF), Calm, the hour before dawn. Isis keeps the last watch before sunrise — her own wing-vigil is the myth this hour repeats each night — and the paint reads like Egypt's own night pigment: the ground lapis the texts gave the gods for hair.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism wheel keeps her at 04h and sharpens the blue to #0040FF — the pure primary, Calm read as light instead of paint. It suits her doubly: the moon carries only borrowed light across the dark, and Isis's own magic works the same way — heka drawn from the gods' true names and given back as healing, borrowed power returned as light.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the deep-night arm now reads by lamplit ink blue (#1F5FA8) — the Walk of **the Scholar**, the Book its craft — and Isis fills that seat by trade as much as by night: heka's own mistress, who reassembled a murdered husband and named a scorpion's poison correctly by knowing its text exactly, magic itself a kind of scholarship worked by lamplight when no one else is still awake to help.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the deep-night arm belongs to **the Unborn**, and Isis wears moonlight silver (#C8D7F0) — the hour of ancestors and of those not yet born, and few goddesses on the dial have stood at that threshold more literally: she gathered a dead god back into wholeness with one hand and raised a hidden infant king with the other, keeping watch over both ends of the same silver hour.
variants.cross: The cross is the seasons palette: her arm at dial 6h points at the spring equinox, colored spring green, and she shares it with Osiris. Wife and husband on one spoke is Egypt's own resurrection told twice — Isis gathered him, and the sown Osiris-beds sprout every spring exactly where her mourning ends: the healer handing the season its returning life.
variants.trio: The Trinity keeps Isis at her 04h post but renames the watch: the blue arm (#002FFF) now stands for Hope, and she shares it with Thoth — the record-keeper beside the mother who out-magicked him for the sun's own secret name. The arm guards the morning third from 0h to 8h, and no one holds better title to it: Isis proved, gathering a murdered god piece by piece, that even the ended can be hoped whole again.

mars.base:
[[The Figure]] Horus is the falcon in the sky itself — his right eye the sun, his left eye the moon, and his outstretched wings the heavens from horizon to horizon. Every living pharaoh claimed to BE him: the king's first and oldest title, older than "Pharaoh," is simply his Horus name. Osiris's murdered son, raised in secret by Isis among the marsh reeds, he grew to fight Set for eighty years over the throne of Egypt — a war the temple at Edfu still tells in stone, ending the only way Egyptian justice allows: the rightful heir seated, the usurper cast down. His own eye, the Wedjat, was torn out by Set and healed whole again — the wound survived is exactly the claim his kingship rests on.

[[On the Dial]] He stands on Tuesday because Horus is Egypt's own word for a war fought with a right on its side: dies Martis, Mars' burning hour, given not to force alone but to force with a cause. The hexa arm at 16h burns orange — Zeal, the mood of the working afternoon — and no god campaigns closer to that tempo: eighty years of contest, tribunal after tribunal before the Ennead, a claim pressed without ever once abandoning it. The Soldier is this arm's profession, and Horus is the soldier who never stopped filing the case even while he fought it.

[[The Lesson]] Mars carries Courage and Wrath, one fire with two uses, and no myth on the dial draws the line as cleanly as this one: Horus's Courage is a son's claim pressed for eighty years without breaking, while his Wrath is the same fire loosed the day he finally corners Set and will not let the other gods intervene. His remedy stands straight across the dial at 4h: Isis, the mother who raised the falcon in hiding, whose Serenity quells his Wrath — while Horus sends Courage back along the axis to cure the Moon's Fear, the son repaying the mother who hid him from a murderer until he was strong enough to face one.

variants.hexa_primary: The home arm: 16h, ember orange, Zeal — Horus's campaign hour, the working afternoon when a claim is pressed and pressed again; the falcon rides the day's stubborn fire.
variants.hexa_secondary: In the light palette Horus keeps 16h but the ember flares to pure yellow — pigment's orange has no seat in the prism wheel, so the afternoon burns at light's brightest hue. For this god the flare is doctrine: his right eye IS the sun, and the war-arm blazing solar yellow is simply Horus looking back at himself.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the afternoon arm now trades in copper (#C87533) — the Walk of **the Merchant**, the Coin weighed fairly — an unlikely seat for the falcon of war until the myth is read whole: Horus's eighty-year claim against Set was pressed tribunal after tribunal before the Ennead, a case argued and re-argued like an honest ledger rather than simply seized by force.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the afternoon is **Maturity**, and Horus wears working amber (#FFB400) — patience earned rather than given, fitting the god whose war for the throne was won by outlasting an usurper, not by a single young strike. The Wedjat eye, torn out and healed whole again, is Maturity's own scar: proof carried rather than merely claimed.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Horus takes the 18h dusk arm, red for Autumn, pointing at the autumn equinox — and shares it with Bastet, the cat who guards what the falcon has already won. Egypt likes the pairing: the avenger beside the protector at the hour the sun goes west — the throne finally won standing next to the hearth that now gets to keep it.
variants.trio: The Trinity moves Horus to 20h, onto Love's red arm beside Bastet — each arm's tip centers its third of the day, and this pair guards the evening from 16h to 24h. Horus finally wears his own red, and Love reads through him as protection: the falcon on the wall so that the throne he won can be kept — courage standing guard over what is now safe to love.

jupiter.base:
[[The Figure]] Anubis is Egypt's oldest funeral rite made into a god — jackal-headed because jackals were the animal Egyptians actually watched prowling the desert cemeteries, and the wisest answer to that danger was to put the jackal in charge of the tomb instead of fighting it. He is the god who invented embalming on the very first corpse: when Set scattered Osiris, it was Anubis who wrapped the gathered pieces and performed the rites that made a dead king rise as a god, and every mummy wrapped in Egypt afterward was wrapped in his name. His black, in every rendering, is the black of fertile Nile silt and of resin-dark preserved flesh, never the black of death itself — a rite built to defeat death, not to dress it.

[[On the Dial]] His arm is the crown itself: the top vertex at 12h, yellow, noon — the mood of Joy, at the very tip the star points at true solar noon. It looks like the wrong hour for a god of the dead until the ledger is read whole: the Hall of Two Truths is where Thursday's Generosity is finally totaled, every gift given and withheld weighed against one feather, and no priest anywhere audits more fairly. Anubis's gold is the same noon-gold the crown wears, because judgment done in full daylight, hiding nothing, is its own kind of generosity.

[[The Lesson]] Thursday's virtue is Generosity and its vice is Excess, and Anubis reads both off the same scale. Generosity is the heart light enough to rise — a life spent giving leaves little weight behind — while Excess is the heart so swollen with what it hoarded that Ammit waits open-jawed at the scale's foot to eat it. The cure hangs across the dial at midnight: Thoth's Wisdom curbs Anubis's Excess by writing the verdict down exactly as the scale tips, while Anubis's Generosity pours down the same axis to cure Thoth's Greed — the two officers of the Hall of Two Truths, the weigher and the scribe, still balancing each other on the dial the way they did at every judgment in the Duat.

variants.hexa_primary: The home arm is the crown of the star: the dial's top at 12h, noon yellow, the mood of Joy — and Anubis's scale was drawn for that seat, held exactly where the top vertex points, at true solar noon. The rite-master in gold, weighing every heart in the one light nothing can hide from.
variants.hexa_secondary: The light palette keeps Anubis at the 12h crown but dresses the arm in green — the middle color of the spectrum, which the prism wheel seats at noon. A fitting robe for the rite-master: green was Egypt's own color of rebirth, painted onto Osiris's skin the day Anubis finished wrapping him — Joy read as the exact shade the dead wear when the rite has worked.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the morning arm now wears alb ivory (#EDEDE0) — the Walk of **the Priest**, the Bell calling the hour before any scale is raised — and Anubis wears it as the rite-master he has always been: the embalmer's workshop opens at exactly this hour, calm and unhurried, long before the Hall of Two Truths ever needs its golden scale.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the morning is **Childhood**, and Anubis wears spring green (#7CE577) — the one age his office never judges, since no heart is weighed and no mummy wrapped before a life has even had the chance to accumulate anything worth balancing. Childhood is the rite-master's true rest: the ledger not yet opened, the scale not yet needed.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Anubis keeps the top arm at 12h, yellow for Summer, sharing it with Ra — the sun that watches every hour Anubis works the ones it cannot see. The summer solstice is the year at its most generous — the longest light, and the rite-master's whole craft is proving that even what goes into the dark is not lost by it.
variants.trio: On the Trinity Anubis keeps his crown: the 12h arm, yellow — but the yellow is Faith's now, shared with Osiris, the very god whose body he first wrapped. The arm centers the day's third from 8h to 16h with noon at its tip. Faith is the rite-master's native virtue in the end: every rite he performs is a bet that the wrapped and weighed will rise again — belief in the unseen, practiced with his own hands.

venus.base:
[[The Figure]] Bastet began as a lioness and Egypt loved her enough to gentle her. In the earliest texts she stands beside Sekhmet as one more form the war-eyed Eye of Ra could take — but by the New Kingdom the claws sheathed themselves and the goddess of Bubastis became the cat the household actually kept: patroness of music, fertility, joy, and the home's protection from disease and evil, presiding over a yearly festival at her city that Herodotus swore poured out more wine than the whole rest of Egypt's year combined. Her sistrum is the same rattle Hathor shakes, for the two goddesses share the temple's music.

[[On the Dial]] She belongs to Friday because Friday belongs to whatever love feels like once the danger has gone out of it. Her arm is 20h, deep red, the mood of Passion — the hour work ends and a household actually gets to enjoy itself, music starting the way it started every year at Bubastis. The lioness Egypt tamed into a housecat is exactly the myth this hour needs: passion that has learned to purr instead of pounce, without ever quite forgetting how.

[[The Lesson]] Love is her virtue and Jealousy her vice, and no animal on the dial argues the vice more honestly: a cat's affection is total and its territory is absolute, the same purring warmth turning instantly to claws if a kitten or a favorite lap is threatened. Bastet's temple guarded granaries and homes precisely by that possessiveness — she kept vermin and evil out because she considered the whole household hers to defend. Her cure stands across the dial at 8h: Osiris, the grain god whose harvest her own temple cats literally protected, whose Patience heals Jealousy — while Bastet's Love, in return, dissolves Envy, guarding the buried seed the way she once guarded the granary above it.

variants.hexa_primary: The home arm: 20h, blood red, Passion — Bastet on the arm of the evening a household finally gets to enjoy, the sistrum shaking the way it shook every year at Bubastis.
variants.hexa_secondary: The light palette keeps Bastet at 20h and turns her red to the prism's full voltage — pure red, light's own primary. Passion undiluted: the goddess whose one festival reportedly drank more wine than the rest of Egypt's year gets the strongest red light itself can mix.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the sunset arm now wears iron-blood crimson (#A02020) — the Walk of **the Soldier**, the Sword raised in defense — and the lioness Egypt gentled into a housecat still remembers the posture: Bastet's temple guarded granaries and homes by the same fierce territorial instinct a soldier guards a border, claws sheathed but never quite forgotten.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the sunset arm is **the Elder** — a life's harvest gathered in — and Bastet wears ember (#FF6A3C), the color of a hearth kept warm long after the wine of Bubastis's own festival has stopped pouring. The Elder's ember suits a goddess whose whole later myth is warmth banked down from a lioness's original fire, purring rather than pouncing, but still glowing.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Bastet holds the 18h arm, red for Autumn, sharing it with Horus — protector and avenger on one arm, the household cat and the falcon who finally cleared it of danger. The autumn equinox is the year's dusk, the harvest brought in and guarded — exactly the granary Bastet's own temple cats were kept to defend.
variants.trio: Bastet does not move at all: the Trinity's red Love arm is her own 20h, and Love is already her whole estate — the one virtue standing in both the seven pairs and the theological three. Horus joins her there, and together they guard the evening from 16h to 24h: music on one side of the door and a falcon on the other, passion and courage keeping the dark third of the day safe enough to enjoy.

sun.base:
[[The Figure]] Where the Planetary Odin walks, the Pantheon Odin sits: the Allfather enthroned upon Hlidskjalf, the seat that sees into all nine worlds. Every mark of the wanderer becomes, on this throne, a mark of the ruler instead: the traded eye that once begged knowledge door to door now presides over it, Gungnir stands for a law rather than a road, Huginn and Muninn report to the throne rather than to a shoulder, and Geri and Freki are fed from his own table, so the god who once knocked at other tables need never beg at one again. The same purchases, held differently.

[[On the Dial]] His seat is the center, white-gold, Sunday — the throne every arm answers to. He once answered only for Wednesday's midnight, the wanderer's own purple arm; the Pantheon promotes him to the hub they all turn on, since no other northern god sat atop so many myths before the throne was offered: an eye traded for wisdom, nine nights hanged for runes, knowledge gathered under one hood now crowned.

[[The Lesson]] And the center is DOUBLE, as always: two virtues, two vices, two moods in one seat. As Allfather he practices Justice, a wanderer-king's own, earned testing mortal halls in disguise before judging one from a throne — but that claim is stalked by Pride, the hunger that hanged him on the tree, now certain no secret is worth leaving unbought. As the Wanderer he practices Humility, the beggar turned from doors by hosts who never knew him — but Servility is that disguise gone wrong, knowledge gathered by a king who never answers for how the beggar got in. Glory is Valhalla's light, warriors under a hall bought by sacrifice already made; Awe is the tree itself: nine nights hanging, pierced by his own spear, given to himself.

[[The Hour]] So his mood, like Sól's before him, is not one of the six but their spring — except where she lit every hour equally, he has already bargained for what each one privately knows. Ragnarok is the one bill even the Allfather cannot cancel, and his throne does not slow the wolf already loose.

variants.hexa_primary: The home reading: the center of the dial, white-gold, the throne every arm already answers to. Sunday does not ride the wheel of hours — it is the hub the Allfather claimed the day he stopped merely wandering it.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism reading repaints every arm, but not him: white stays white in both worlds, the one color pigment and beam never argue about. Odin alone stands unchanged at the center while the six seats he once merely visited change color around him.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the noon arm crowns itself in royal gold (#F0C420) — the Walk of **the King**, his own hard-bought office — and Odin wears it honestly for once: Hlidskjalf already seats him above all nine worlds, an eye and nine nights on the tree paid in advance for exactly this Crown.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel noon is **Youth** — life's blazing zenith — and Odin wears sun-yellow (#FFE800), an odd hour for a god famous for what age and sacrifice cost him. Yet Youth fits the wanderer who traded an eye before he ever wore a crown: knowledge bought early enough that its whole life was spent, unspent, on ruling well.
variants.cross: His arm at dial 12h points at the summer solstice, colored summer yellow, shared with Tyr. The throne that sees every world and the hand that was given to guarantee one oath hold the season of longest light together — sight and sacrifice, the sky's two costliest gifts on one arm.
variants.trio: The Trinity is the theological palette: Odin returns to the hub with three arms only — Faith's yellow, Love's red, Hope's blue — all decomposed from his white-gold center, exactly as they once were decomposed from Sól's. Every secret he ever bought still radiates outward from the same throne.

faces.ruler:
Odin the Allfather is the Ruler face — the wanderer-king enthroned rather than walking, the same god who bought every secret at a price now sitting where all those secrets finally pay their due.

His virtue is Justice, the wanderer-king's own — the god who walked every road in disguise before he ever judged a hall from a throne, so his verdicts carry a beggar's memory inside a king's authority; but that same claim to have seen everything is stalked by Pride, the same hunger that hanged him nine nights on the tree for wisdom now certain no secret in any of the nine worlds is worth leaving unbought. His mood is Glory, Valhalla's own hall-light: warriors chosen, half the slain, feasting under a roof built from a sacrifice already paid before the first of them arrived.
faces.servant:
Odin the Wanderer is the Servant face — not a separate god but the same Allfather with the crown set aside, the beggar-guise he wore across every hall long before Hlidskjalf ever needed defending, the same body as the Ruler's stripped of every ornament that argued rule.

His virtue is Humility, the god who let himself be turned away at doors, insulted, and tested by hosts who never once suspected who stood dripping on their threshold; but that same disguise curdles into Servility whenever the wandering becomes an excuse — knowledge gathered by a king who never once has to answer for how the beggar got in. His mood is Awe, the specific dread of the tree itself: nine nights hanging, no food, no water, pierced by his own spear and given to himself, wisdom bought at the one price that could have simply killed him instead.

moon.base:
[[The Figure]] Hel is death itself given a body split down the middle: one half a fair young queen in unmarked flesh, the other a rotted corpse to the bone, both halves equally hers and equally final. Her hall Eljudnir and its hound Garm at the gate serve the population no saga bothers to name — everyone who was never going to fall in battle — and her ledger of the dead's names is the record where no one from that population is left off.

[[On the Dial]] Her home is the 04h arm in deep blue, Monday's arm, the hour before dawn, mood Calm. Where Máni merely crossed this hour nightly, hunted, Hel simply belongs to it: the pre-dawn stillness is the closest the living world comes to her own kingdom, half-lit, half-dark, neither one nor the other. The arm's profession is the Physician, and it lands on her with a colder honesty than it ever did on him — she is the ledger every physician's chart eventually closes into, the diagnosis that does not miss.

[[The Lesson]] Blue carries her pair exactly as it carried Máni's: Serenity is the virtue, purer here than anywhere on the dial — the half-dead queen is the stillest thing in the whole cosmology, calm because she is already past whatever could disturb her. Fear is the vice, and it is not hers to feel but to BE: Monday's dark face made a throne rather than a wolf's chase. Across the dial at 16h, in the Pantheon's own reseating, Thor answers: his Courage cures her Fear, and her Serenity quells his Wrath in turn — the same axis Máni and Tyr once kept, worked now by a queen who never fights for her calm and a god who never stops fighting for his.

[[The Hour]] So Calm rules the hour before dawn because it most resembles her — the world briefly neither night nor morning, exactly Hel's own body split down the middle, and the dial gives its stillest watch to the one queen for whom stillness was never an achievement, only a fact.

variants.hexa_primary: The home position: the 04h arm, deep pigment blue (#002FFF), the Calm of the hour before dawn — Monday resting one arm below the sunrise line, exactly where a half-dead queen keeps her stillest watch.
variants.hexa_secondary: Same arm, same hour, but the pigment gives way to the prism's pure blue (#0040FF) — Calm read as light. Of all the arms this one changes least between the two worlds; death, unlike the moon, was never a matter of physics to begin with.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the deep-night arm now reads by lamplit ink blue (#1F5FA8) — the Walk of **the Scholar**, the Book its instrument — and no queen keeps a more exact ledger: Hel's own record of the dead, open untouched across her lap, is the Scholar's Book made literal, a text that never once needs correcting.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the deep-night arm belongs to **the Unborn**, and Hel wears moonlight silver (#C8D7F0) — the hour of ancestors and of what has not yet come, and her half-and-half body already argues the same threshold in flesh: one side young and unmarked, the other already past whatever end waits for it.
variants.cross: Her arm at dial 6h points at the spring equinox, colored spring green, shared with Freyr. The half-dead queen and the harvest lord hold the sunrise arm together — Hel keeps only the coldest half of the year, and lends the warmer half freely to whoever is alive enough to use it.
variants.trio: The Trinity keeps Hel at her 04h post but renames the watch: the blue arm (#002FFF) now stands for Hope, shared with Loki, guarding the morning from 0h to 8h. A strange grace for the queen of the dead — yet earned: she has already proven that even the stillest night ends in a reckoning, and every reckoning, eventually, opens a door.

mars.base:
[[The Figure]] Thor's whole nature is labor rather than majesty: thunder is not something Thor has, it is something he does. Mjolnir is his hammer because it must be swung and not merely held, and the girdle of might is the strength that lets him swing it — a god defined entirely by the verb rather than the throne.

[[On the Dial]] His seat in the Pantheon is the 16h arm in ember orange, Tuesday — not his own Thursday but the mars seat Tyr held in the Planetary set, reseated now for the fight rather than the feast. The arm's profession is the Soldier, and this Thor needs no argument for it: Mjolnir mid-swing is a weapon in the instant of use, not resting between a wedding's blessings, and no god on the dial hits harder or gets hit by more.

[[The Lesson]] Orange carries the Soldier's own pair, and Thor supplies both without straining for either: Courage is the virtue, Midgard's guardian meeting every giant and every serpent without flinching; Wrath is the vice, and no god's temper is better documented — the rages that split mountains, that nearly capsized the boat hauling Jormungandr up from the deep. His cure stands across the dial at 04h, in Hel: her Serenity quells his Wrath, and his own Courage cures her Fear in turn — the soldier and the still queen healing each other along one axis.

[[The Hour]] Zeal, the working afternoon's own fire, suits him even better here than Joy once did at noon: not the table but the swing, banked heat instead of full blaze — the same hammer, the same god, simply working a harder shift than the one his own day used to give him.

variants.hexa_primary: The home position: the 16h arm, ember orange (#DC9600), the Zeal of the working afternoon — Tuesday's fire banked into steady heat, the hammer never far from the forge that makes it ring.
variants.hexa_secondary: Same 16h arm, but the prism burns the ember to bright yellow (#FFFF00): zeal read as raw light instead of glowing coal — lightning's own color standing in for iron's.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the afternoon arm now trades in copper (#C87533) — the Walk of **the Merchant**, the Coin its fair weight — a strange seat for a hammer mid-swing, yet Thor's whole war against Jormungandr is itself a kind of ledger: giants and serpents kept in balance against Midgard, a debt collected with Mjolnir instead of a scale.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the afternoon is **Maturity**, and Thor wears working amber (#FFB400) — the age of a guardian who has done this fight enough times that the swing no longer needs the rage of a first battle. Maturity is banked heat, and no god on the dial works a harder or steadier shift than the one still swinging at Ragnarok's own approach.
variants.cross: His arm at dial 18h points at the autumn equinox, colored autumn red, shared with Frigg. The hammer that guards Midgard and the devotion that guards one household hold the red season together — two different scales of the same promise, kept.
variants.trio: On the Trinity Thor shifts to 20h and stands under Love's deep red (#B60000), sharing the arm with Frigg — the hammer and the household guarding the evening from 16h to 24h. Love reads through Thor as plain defense: he never asks who deserves the shelter, only that the roof holds.

mercury.base:
[[The Figure]] Loki is the only smiling god on the dial — the trickster whose every object here is either his invention or his sentence: the net is the tool the gods rebuilt from his own ashes to catch him as a salmon, the serpent that drips venom onto his bound face is his own punishment, and the wolf is Fenrir, his own son, bound in turn by the very gods Loki keeps outwitting.

[[On the Dial]] His seat in the Pantheon is the 0h arm at the very bottom of the dial, mourning purple, Wednesday — not his own Saturday but the mercury seat Odin held in the Planetary set, reseated now for cunning rather than wisdom bought at a price. The arm's profession is the Merchant, and it suits a trickster at least as well as it ever suited a wanderer: every object in his own plate is already a transaction, a debt, a trade gone sideways.

[[The Lesson]] Purple carries the mind's own pair, reread as mischief rather than sacrifice: Wisdom is the virtue, cunning sharpened until it works — every trap the other gods eventually escape only because Loki built the lock as carefully as the door; Greed is the vice, and unlike Odin's hunger for knowledge, his is a hunger for advantage, an angle worked for no reason but its own sake. His cure stands across the dial at 12h, in Tyr: Tyr's Generosity cures Loki's Greed, and Loki's own Wisdom curbs Tyr's Excess — the merchant and the priest correcting each other from opposite hours.

[[The Hour]] Sorrow, midnight's own color, lands on him strangely and then does not: every plan Loki spins ends exactly the way the myths already know it will, at Ragnarok, on the losing side of his own making — a trickster clever enough to see the ending and unable to stop building toward it anyway.

variants.hexa_primary: The home position: the 0h arm at the very bottom of the dial, mourning purple (#542E85), the Sorrow of midnight — Wednesday at the day's nadir, exactly the hour a trickster's schemes are hardest to see coming.
variants.hexa_secondary: Same midnight arm, but the prism electrifies the purple into magenta (#BD00BD): sorrow with a neon edge, the midnight mystery read as strange light rather than mourning cloth — mischief caught mid-flicker instead of hidden.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the evening arm now drapes in stage-velvet violet (#7A2E8E) — the Walk of **the Artist**, the Mask its craft — and no god on the dial wears a mask more literally: Loki is the only smiling face in the whole gallery, every trap and trade he builds a small performance staged for an audience he is usually also fooling.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the evening is **Old Age**, and Loki wears dusk violet (#9C6BD4) — the hour for totaling a life honestly, which is exactly the reckoning the trickster keeps outrunning. He can see every ending the myths already promise him, Ragnarok included, and keeps building toward it anyway, clever enough to read the ledger and unable to close it in his own favor.
variants.cross: He keeps the 0h arm, pointed at the winter solstice and colored winter blue — and alone. Every other body shares its seasonal arm; Loki has no partner here either, which suits the one god this dial never fully trusted to share anything.
variants.trio: The Trinity raises Loki from midnight to the 4h arm of Hope, blue (#002FFF), shared with Hel — an odd pairing until it isn't: the schemer and the queen of the dead both already know exactly how the story ends, and keep working anyway. Hope is what a wandering mind does with an ending it cannot cancel.

jupiter.base:
[[The Figure]] Tyr's missing hand is the whole story: when the gods bound Fenrir with a ribbon they swore was harmless, only Tyr would lay his hand in the wolf's mouth as pledge, knowing the pledge was false and the hand was forfeit. He carries the loss unhidden rather than concealed, because the point of the sacrifice was always that it be seen and believed.

[[On the Dial]] His seat in the Pantheon is the 12h arm crowning the dial, noon yellow, Thursday — not his own Tuesday but the jupiter seat Thor held in the Planetary set, reseated now for the oath rather than the storm. The arm's profession is the Priest and Teacher, and the given hand argues it better than any hammer could: a sacrifice made once, in public, so that every oath sworn after it would be believed on his word alone.

[[The Lesson]] Yellow carries the priesthood's own pair, reread through sacrifice rather than feast: Generosity is the virtue, and no god on the dial gave more plainly — a hand, traded outright, no bargain attached, so that Fenrir could be bound at all; Excess is the vice read against the grain, not a table that overflows but a justice severe enough to take a hand and still call the trade fair. His cure stands across the dial at 0h, in Loki: Loki's Wisdom curbs Tyr's Excess, and Tyr's own Generosity cures Loki's Greed — the priest and the trickster correcting each other from opposite hours.

[[The Hour]] Joy, noon's own crown, rests oddly on a god missing a hand — until the myth finishes itself: Fenrir bound is the whole world kept safe one more full turn, and joy is exactly what a promise, kept at cost, buys for everyone else.

variants.hexa_primary: The home position: the 12h arm crowning the dial, noon yellow (#F8E600), the Joy of the day's peak — Thursday at the top of the world, the hand once given still the world's proof that the pledge holds.
variants.hexa_secondary: Same crowning arm, but the prism turns noon green (#00DC00) — the middle band of the spectrum for the middle of the day. Joy read as light: the oath-keeper's peak hour in the color of full leaf.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the morning arm now wears alb ivory (#EDEDE0) — the Walk of **the Priest**, the Bell calling on the strength of a vow alone — and Tyr fills it by sacrifice rather than sermon: a hand given outright so that every oath sworn after it would be believed on his word, the one relic honesty needs no further preaching to prove.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the morning is **Childhood**, and Tyr wears spring green (#7CE577) — an unlikely hour for a god defined by one costly, adult choice, yet Childhood is exactly what his sacrifice protects: Fenrir bound is a whole world's next generation kept safe one more turn, a hand traded so that youth, elsewhere, gets to stay young a while longer.
variants.cross: His arm at dial 12h points at the summer solstice, colored summer yellow, shared with Odin. The hand that was given to guarantee one oath and the throne that sees every world hold the season of longest light together — sacrifice and sight, the sky's two costliest gifts on one arm.
variants.trio: On the Trinity Tyr keeps the crown at 12h in Faith's yellow (#F8E600), sharing the arm with Freyr, as the two guard the day's height from 8h to 16h. Faith reads plainest through Tyr of all the gods on this dial: a hand given once is a promise that never needs repeating.

venus.base:
[[The Figure]] Frigg's devotion is carried in objects with no edge: a ring of household keys, a distaff spinning cloud-thread rather than any weapon. Her one gap is the mistletoe, the single plant she never thought to ask an oath from, and her seat at Hlidskjalf already gave her the same reach her husband is famous for — sight into everything, power to change nothing of what it showed her.

[[On the Dial]] Her home is the 20h arm in deep red, Friday, the evening hour. Venus' arm is the Artist's, and hers is authored in a different key from Freya's evening star — not the passion that rises with the star but the devotion that stayed up every night before it, extracting a promise from fire, water, iron, sickness, every beast and tree, that none would ever harm her son.

[[The Lesson]] Red carries her pair, reread: Love is the virtue, and it is devotion rather than desire — securing an entire world's goodwill on behalf of one child, oath by individual oath. Jealousy is the vice, transmuted: not fear of a rival but a mother's fierce, all-consuming protection, jealous not of another lover but of every harm that might still reach him. She missed only the mistletoe, too young to swear, and Loki's arrow found that exact gap. Her cure stands across the dial at 08h, in Freyr, the field's own patience: his Patience heals a protection stretched past its breaking point, and her proven Love would dissolve his Envy of a harvest that always risks failing once.

[[The Hour]] Passion, in her case, is grief wearing the evening's own color: not the hour the day's wanting begins but the hour a mother discovers exactly how much she was willing to ask of the whole world — and how the one thing she forgot to ask was the only thing that mattered.

variants.hexa_primary: The home position: the 20h arm, deep pigment red (#B60000), the evening hour — Friday glowing where the evening star rises, though the fire she keeps is a hearth's, not a lover's.
variants.hexa_secondary: Same evening arm, but the prism saturates the red to full light (#FF0000): devotion as a beam instead of an ember — the evening at maximum intensity, every oath she ever asked for burning at once.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the sunset arm now wears iron-blood crimson (#A02020) — the Walk of **the Soldier**, the Sword raised in defense — and Frigg fought that exact campaign without ever lifting one: an oath extracted from fire, water, iron and every beast and tree, a mother's whole war waged in promises instead of blades, undone by the one recruit she forgot to muster.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the sunset arm is **the Elder** — a life's harvest finally gathered in — and Frigg wears ember (#FF6A3C), the color of grief banked rather than raging. Her harvest is measured in oaths kept by an entire world on her son's behalf, and the one gap in it, the mistletoe too young to swear, is the single stalk her Elder's ember still cannot stop tending.
variants.cross: Her arm at dial 18h points at the autumn equinox, colored autumn red, shared with Thor. The queen who guards a household and the god who guards a whole world hold the red season together — devotion and defense on one arm, each protecting what the other cannot reach alone.
variants.trio: Frigg stands still: the Trinity's Love arm is her own 20h in her own red (#B60000), for Love alone belongs to both sets. Thor joins her, and together they guard the evening from 16h to 24h — the household's devotion and Midgard's own hammer guarding the dark third, love with a shield behind it as well as a heart.

saturn.base:
[[The Figure]] Freyr's whole inventory argues abundance rather than war: Gullinbursti, his golden-bristled boar, is wealth that shines rather than threatens, and his antler — held in place of the sword he traded away for love — stands for a weapon surrendered outright, not merely set aside. His folded ship Skidbladnir carries the same argument in miniature: abundance that travels light and still holds more than it seems to. Where Loki's saturn seat is built from a trickster's inventions and sentences, Freyr's needs no cunning at all — only a harvest that keeps its own promises.

[[On the Dial]] His home is the 08h arm in green, Saturday, the morning hour, mood Renewal, profession the Farmer. Loki held this seat only by the owner's own paradox — Cronus' empty chair, a bound trickster standing in for a bound Titan on a day the north never gave a god. Freyr needs no such argument: no figure in any pantheon on this dial looks more naturally at home behind the plow, and the arm that once belonged to him by irony now belongs to him by simple fact.

[[The Lesson]] Green still carries a pair, gentler than Loki's: Patience is the virtue, the taught truth of every planted seed, proven each spring whether or not last year's harvest failed. Envy is the vice, read out of the same gold rather than any one act of his — the shine of Gullinbursti beside a neighbor's thinner field, abundance that makes its own envy simply by existing, the one bad year that turns every good one bitter in the retelling. His cure stands across the dial at 20h, in Frigg: her devoted Love dissolves the sourness abundance breeds, and his field-taught Patience heals a protection she has stretched past what any single oath can hold.

[[The Hour]] Renewal ruled Loki's morning only because he forced the paradox to work; it needs no forcing for Freyr, who is simply the green season keeping its promise — the same grain that closes the dial's arm every autumn was already sworn to return the moment his hand first opened it.

variants.hexa_primary: The home position: the 08h arm, morning green (#007E00), the Renewal of the young day — Saturday, the week's rest and restart, and for once a seat that needed no argument to belong to its god.
variants.hexa_secondary: Same morning arm, but the prism turns the green to cyan (#00DDDD) — renewal read as water-light, the same rain that ripens Freyr's own grain rather than any trick that once caught another god as a fish.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the dawn arm keeps field green (#3E8914) — the Walk of **the Farmer**, the Plough turning ripened ground — and no god on the dial needs less argument for the seat: Freyr's whole claim to it is the harvest itself, a sword traded away for love and a sheaf of wheat kept in its place.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the dawn arm is **Birth**, and Freyr wears predawn mist (#8FA8C8) — the hour before a season has proven anything yet. Birth suits the god whose whole calling is what grows after the sunrise: the same grain that closes his arm every autumn was already sworn to return the moment his hand first opened it.
variants.cross: His arm at dial 6h points at the spring equinox, colored spring green, shared with Hel. The harvest lord and the half-dead queen hold the sunrise arm together — the season that undoes winter, held by the one god who makes it grow and the one queen who never has to wait for it.
variants.trio: The Trinity gives Freyr the plainest promotion on the dial: the 12h Faith arm, yellow (#F8E600), beside Tyr, guarding the day's height from 8h to 16h. Faith on the harvest lord needs no argument at all — the seed sworn to become grain and the hand sworn to an oath are the same trust, kept two different ways.

sun.base:
[[The Figure]] Perun is the thunder-god, the axe-bearer, the chief of the old Slavic sky — and in this roster he is seated where his rank has always pointed: the throne itself. His tree is the oak, his weapon the axe and the hurled thunderstone, and his sign is the six-petalled thunder-mark — the gromovnik rosette the Slavs carved into their roof-beams to turn the lightning away. When the Rus' princes swore their treaties they swore 'by Perun' first and every other god after: the sky-court's law came before the goods it protected. His great myth is the storm itself: the serpent Veles steals the cattle and dams the waters, and Perun hunts him across the sky and strikes him with the bolt — the combat this Sunday now carries whole, storm above and water below.

[[On the Dial]] His day is Sunday — nedelja, the 'no-work' day, the day the week rests before it begins again. Perun does not take an arm at all: he holds the CENTER of the dial, white-gold, the still hub the six colored arms radiate from — and those six arms ARE his six-petalled gromovnik, the thunder-mark drawn at full size with the thunderer himself seated at its heart.

[[The Lesson]] The center is DOUBLE — two virtues, two vices, two moods in one seat — and this roster fills it with the combat myth itself. Perun's face is Justice, the sky-court's oath-keeping law, shadowed by Pride, the storm's own arrogance; his mood is Glory, the bolt's white flash. And beneath him the same Sunday wears Veles — the Humility of the yielded throne below, its curdled Servility, and the Awe of deep water. The two old enemies are not king and rival here but crown and root of one day: the storm above is only half the Sunday; the water it falls into is the other half.

variants.hexa_primary: In the paint palette the center is the one color no brush can reach: pigments mix by subtraction, and no blending of pigments ever yields white. So Perun's white-gold hub is the unmixable center — the six arms of his own gromovnik carry the colors out, yet no mixing of them climbs back to the crown. The sky-court hands the law down; nothing painted below can hand it back.
variants.hexa_secondary: In the light palette the logic reverses: the six colored beams of the arms, summed at the hub, add up to exactly white. Here Perun's white-gold center is a radiance that is the sum of all six — the thunder-mark proven by arithmetic, every petal's color returning to make the light whole, the sky-court's verdict assembled from every voice beneath it.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the noon arm crowns itself in royal gold (#F0C420) — the Walk of **the King**, the Crown his own by ancient rank — and Perun wears it as the sky-court's own law: the Rus' princes swore treaties 'by Perun' first, the thunderer's Crown backing every oath sworn beneath it before any other god's name was added.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel noon is **Youth** — life's blazing height — and Perun wears sun-yellow (#FFE800), the bolt's own brightness read as an age rather than a weapon. Youth suits the god still hunting Veles across the sky every retelling: a combat fought at full strength, never once softened into an older god's patience.
variants.cross: The seasons cross keeps a true crossing — four arms meeting at one point — and Perun keeps that meeting-place, the hub where the year's four quarters intersect. The thunderer holds the still center around which spring, summer, autumn and winter wheel — the sky-court seated where every season must pass its judgment on the way to the next.
variants.trio: In the trio — Faith, Hope, Love — the sun keeps the center, and from it the yellow Faith arm rises straight up the 12h vertical (Faith at top, Hope at 4h, Love at 20h). Perun is the white-gold source, and Faith is the first thing that climbs out of him toward noon: the oath sworn 'by Perun' made into the upward-pointing virtue, the vertical his bolt travels turned the other way.

faces.ruler:
Perun is the Ruler face of Sunday — the supreme thunderer enthroned, axe-bearer and chief of the old Slavic sky, his oak the world's most sacred tree and his six-petalled thunder-mark, the gromovnik, the very rosette the clock's own hexagram pointer echoes at the crown of the dial.

The storm that has always surrounded the thunder-god is, at this seat, the sky-court's own throne-image: not weather passing through but the canopy proper to a seated king.

His virtue is Justice — the sky-court's law, the oath every Rus' prince once swore 'by Perun' before a word of it was written down, the thunderbolt that falls on the oath-breaker and no one else. His shadow is Pride, the storm's own arrogance, the god who can mistake the crash of his own weather for judgment rightly passed. His mood is Glory — the high white flash at the bolt's own strike, the sky-court at its most blinding.
faces.servant:
Veles is the Servant face of Sunday — not a lesser king but the throne BELOW, the horned serpent-lord of waters, herds and the dead whom the old combat myth sets against Perun on this very same day: storm above, water and root beneath, the two faces one Sunday has always worn.

Veles needs no likeness of his own for this seat: the throne below he has always held simply needs reading at the bottom of the same day Perun crowns at the top.

His virtue is Humility — the serpent who yields the sky and asks only for the roots and the waters, losing the storm's duel in every retelling and never once contesting the crown again. Its shadow is Servility, humility curdled into bare submission, the throne below mistaken for no throne at all. His mood is Awe — not Glory's blaze but the hush at the bottom of the world, the deep water Perun's own rain becomes once it has finally fallen all the way down.

moon.base:
[[The Figure]] Mokoš is the great goddess — the only goddess Prince Vladimir set among the idols of his Kyiv pantheon, standing alone among the gods. She is the spinner: the flax and the wool, the distaff and the thread, and by extension the thread of fate itself, measured out and cut. And she is Moist Mother Earth, Mati Syra Zemlya — her very name holds the wet: mok-, moisture itself. That name is why this roster seats her here: the blue seat is the water seat, and Mokoš is the one Slavic deity whose name IS water — the damp ground, the well, the rain soaked in and held.

[[On the Dial]] Her day is Monday — ponedeljak, the day 'after nedelja,' the first step out of rest and still half in the dark. Mokoš takes the 4h arm, low on the left of the dial, in deep blue — the hour before dawn, when the household sleeps and someone is nevertheless awake, keeping it. Her mood is Calm: not the held breath of an empty night but the settled quiet of a watched one — the Physician's hour, the mother sitting up with whoever needs sitting up with. The same image serves the spinner elsewhere on this wheel and the nurse here without changing a line: the veil that covers a bride's hair covers a woman keeping vigil, and the hands that draw the thread are the hands that draw a blanket close.

[[The Lesson]] Her axis is Serenity against Fear. The dark is where fear breeds — every shape a threat, every sound a wolf — and Mokoš answers it the way water answers fire: with the deep, damp steadiness of the ground itself, the wet mother whose stillness soaks the panic out. Her cure lies across the dial in the mars arm: the Courage of Svetovid is what ends the night her Serenity holds. Care keeps the dark bearable; courage makes it end.

variants.hexa_primary: In the paint palette Mokoš holds the 4h arm in a deep blue (#002FFF) — the pigment of the pre-dawn hour, night thinned but not yet broken. It is the mixing-blue of the darkest part of the wheel, and hers by name: the color of damp earth before first light, the wet mother's own hour, when the dew settles and the ground drinks.
variants.hexa_secondary: In the light palette the same 4h arm burns as pure primary blue (#0040FF) — one of the three beams the white hub decomposes into. Mokoš is no longer a mixed pigment but a fundamental ray: the blue that light itself is built from, water's own frequency standing clean in the prism wheel, the moist mother reduced to her element.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the deep-night arm now reads by lamplit ink blue (#1F5FA8) — the Walk of **the Scholar**, the Book its instrument — and Mokoš keeps that watch the way she keeps every thread: patiently, by hand, the same care that spins flax also holding a sick-house steady through the hour the household most needs a text it can trust.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the deep-night arm belongs to **the Unborn**, and Mokoš wears moonlight silver (#C8D7F0) — the hour of ancestors and of those not yet come, fitting for the goddess whose own name means the wet ground that holds every seed before it rises. Moist Mother Earth already keeps both ends of that silver threshold, buried and unborn, in the same damp soil.
variants.cross: The seasons cross moves Mokoš to the 6h arm, colored spring green and aimed straight at the vernal equinox — and here she shares the arm with Morana, the saturn body. The pairing is the rite itself: the vernal equinox is the day Morana's straw effigy is drowned, and the water that receives it is Mokoš's. The wet mother and the winter-death stand on one spring arm — the drowning and the water that does it.
variants.trio: In the trio Mokoš keeps the 4h arm, but it is now the Hope arm, colored Hope blue (#002FFF) — and she shares it with Svarog, the mercury body. The last dark hour becomes the hour of Hope: the mother who tends the night and the smith who rests from it stand together, the care that outlasts the dark as the promise that the sun will rise.

mercury.base:
[[The Figure]] Svarog is the heavenly smith — the sky-fire forge-god the old Hypatian Chronicle glosses onto the Greek Hephaestus, father of Dažbog the giving sun, so every ray his son pours out began as a spark in his father's forge. His name carries the old root svar-, the sky's own brightness, and the chroniclers credit him with dropping the first tongs from the heavens and binding one husband to one wife under a single forged law — order struck out of raw ore the way a blade is struck out of raw iron. Where Perun rules by the bolt and Veles by the flood, Svarog rules by the hammer: the sky is his workshop, and every fixed star is a spark he never let go out.

[[On the Dial]] His day is Wednesday — sreda, 'the middle,' the hinge of the week, as it has always been for whoever holds this seat. Svarog takes the very BOTTOM of the dial, the 0h/24h arm at midnight, in mourning purple — not a grave this time but a cooling forge, coals banked to embers while the smith rests between one day's work and the next. His mood is Sorrow: the hour the hammer falls silent and the day's sparks settle into the sky as fixed, cold stars, waiting to be struck alight again at dawn.

[[The Lesson]] His axis is Wisdom against Greed. The smith-god is Wisdom itself — order struck out of raw ore, the craft that turns chaos into law and tool — but the same forge that shapes the world can close its doors, and that is Greed: the craft hoarded, the fire kept for one hand only. His cure is across the dial in the jupiter arm: Dažbog's Generosity, the open horn his father's forge first hammered into being, melts the smith's Greed back down. Svarog makes the sun-disc; only his son's giving completes the gift.

variants.hexa_primary: In the paint palette Svarog holds the 0h arm in mourning purple (#542E85) — a mixed, bruised color, red and blue ground together into the hue of a forge gone cold. It is the pigment of the smith's own midnight, the deepest, most blended dark on the wheel, the color of the banked coals Svarog tends until dawn relights them.
variants.hexa_secondary: In the light palette his purple resolves to magenta (#BD00BD) — the strange color the prism itself cannot make, that only appears where the spectrum's two ends are bent around to touch. Fitting for the god who welds two things into one: Svarog wears the hue born only where two ends are forced together, the smith's own trick played back to him by light itself.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the evening arm now drapes in stage-velvet violet (#7A2E8E) — the Walk of **the Artist**, the Mask its craft — an unlikely seat for a smith until the forge is read as a stage: Svarog hammers each fixed star into the sky one at a time, a maker's performance played out in sparks instead of paint, every constellation a finished piece he never signs.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the evening is **Old Age**, and Svarog wears dusk violet (#9C6BD4) — the hour a long day's work finally banks its coals. Old Age suits the sky-smith exactly: not exhaustion but earned rest, the hammer set down only because the work of an entire heaven has, for once, been finished for the day.
variants.cross: The seasons cross keeps Svarog on the 0h arm, aimed at the winter solstice and colored winter blue — and alone. Every other body shares its seasonal arm; the smith shares none. The forge holds the year's longest night by itself, the hammer resting at the bottom of the year and of the dial alike — the one night even the sky-smith lets his own fire go all the way down.
variants.trio: In the trio Svarog climbs to the 4h Hope arm, colored Hope blue (#002FFF), and shares it with Mokoš, the moon body. The smith rises from his midnight forge to stand on the arm of Hope beside the calm night-mother — the ordering Wisdom leaning toward dawn, a night's worth of banked sparks finally catching light at the promise of morning.

jupiter.base:
[[The Figure]] Dažbog is the giving sun — his very name binds dati, to give, to bog, god: the god who gives. He is the son of Svarog the sky-smith, and he rides the daylight across the heavens in a chariot, dealing out warmth and grain and fortune to whoever stands beneath him. The Tale of Igor's Campaign calls the Slavs themselves Dažbog's grandchildren, vnutsi Dazhbozhi — a whole people descended from an ancestor who asks nothing and pours out everything. In this roster his seat is written by his own name: Dažd-bog, the giver, on Generosity's day.

[[On the Dial]] His day is Thursday — četvrtak, 'the fourth' — and he takes the TOP of the dial, the 12h arm, the crown of the star, in noon yellow. His mood is Joy: the high, ringing gladness of the sky at its brightest — and no figure earns noon more honestly, because noon is the hour the sun gives hardest, the horn tipped all the way over, the whole day's warmth handed down at once.

[[The Lesson]] His axis is Generosity against Excess. The giving is his name and his nature — the day dealt out like bread, the horn that empties itself over every field alike — but a sun that gives without measure scorches what it means to ripen, and that is Excess, the gift that gives too hard. His cure is across the dial in the mercury arm: the Wisdom of Svarog — his own father, the smith who knows exactly when the metal is done. The son pours; the father knows when to stop pouring. Generosity fills the horn; wisdom decides its tilt.

variants.hexa_primary: In the paint palette Dažbog crowns the 12h arm in noon yellow — the pure high pigment of midday, the brightest color the wheel puts at the top. The crown-petal glows the yellow of the sky at noon, Joy given the boldest hue on the dial, straight up where the giving is heaviest and the light pours hardest.
variants.hexa_secondary: In the light palette the top arm resolves to green — because green sits at the exact middle of the visible spectrum, and the middle of the spectrum belongs at the middle of the crown. Dažbog's noon becomes green here: the giving sun wearing the balance-point of all light, the center wavelength raised to the zenith — the gift weighed exactly even.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the morning arm now wears alb ivory (#EDEDE0) — the Walk of **the Priest**, the Bell ringing freely for whoever stands beneath it — and Dažbog needs no ordination for the office: his own name means the god who gives, a horn of plenty tipped over an entire people who call themselves, in the old song, his grandchildren.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the morning is **Childhood**, and Dažbog wears spring green (#7CE577) — the giving sun's warmth still rising rather than yet at its noon crest. Childhood suits the god whose whole myth is generosity offered before it is ever asked for, the horn already pouring while the day itself is still young.
variants.cross: The seasons cross keeps Dažbog at the 12h arm, colored yellow and aimed at the summer solstice — and he shares it with Perun, the sun body. The giving sun and the thunderer stand together at the top of the year: high summer is the season of both the ripening light and the ripening storm, the horn and the rain crowning the dial as one.
variants.trio: In the trio Dažbog keeps the crown at 12h, now the Faith arm in Faith yellow, shared with Morana, the saturn body — and he guards the day third of the dial from 8h to 16h. The giver at the top of the vertical holds the arm of Faith over the bright working hours: the trust that the horn will pour again tomorrow, which is the only faith a working day truly runs on.

venus.base:
[[The Figure]] Lada is the folk-songs' own goddess of love and the spring wedding — never carved among the idols Prince Vladimir set on his hill above Kyiv, but sung into being a thousand times over in the refrain that still opens half the wedding and ritual songs of the Slavic world: oj, Lado, lado moje. Serbian girls still carry her name every spring in the lazarice and kraljice processions, wreathed and singing door to door before Easter for a good harvest and a good match. Honesty owes her one caveat the other gods don't need: serious Slavicists still argue whether Lada was ever a worshipped deity, or whether chroniclers built a goddess out of a refrain that once meant no more than 'dear' — the songs kept singing her regardless, and a thousand years of wedding choirs outvote a footnote.

[[On the Dial]] Her day is Friday — petak, 'the fifth' — and folk memory keeps a warmer name behind it too, the day the wedding songs claim as their own and still count lucky for a match. On the dial she takes the 20h arm, deep in the evening, in blood red, and her mood is Passion — the warm fire of the kolo circling at dusk, the same red heat the venus arm has always carried, now sung rather than spun.

[[The Lesson]] Her axis is Love against Jealousy. Lada is Love by name and by custom — the wreath offered, the ribbon tied, an entire village singing a couple into the kolo — but the songs keep one dark verse for the shadow: Jealousy, the beloved who will not let the dance end. Her cure is across the dial in the saturn arm: the Patience of Morana, the frozen ground that waits out a whole winter without grasping, steadies the Jealousy. A love that can wait for spring need not hold the wreath so tight.

variants.hexa_primary: In the paint palette Lada holds the 20h arm in blood red — the deep mixed crimson of the evening, of the wedding ribbon, the ripe rowan berry, and the blush the kolo dance raises. It is the warmest pigment on the lower dial, the color of Passion given body, the evening turned the red of the love-song.
variants.hexa_secondary: In the light palette her arm resolves to pure red — one of the three primary beams the white hub breaks into. Lada's evening becomes a fundamental ray: not the mixed crimson of the pigment but the clean elemental red that light itself is built from, Passion stripped down to the note the folk-song was singing all along.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the sunset arm now wears iron-blood crimson (#A02020) — the Walk of **the Soldier**, the Sword raised in earnest — a strange dress for a wedding goddess, yet the wreath she offers is fought for just as fiercely: a village's whole chorus mustered every spring to defend one match against a hard winter and a harder harvest, oj Lado sung like a battle-cry for love.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the sunset arm is **the Elder** — a life's harvest finally gathered in — and Lada wears ember (#FF6A3C), the kolo's fire banked into memory. The Elder suits a goddess sung rather than carved: a thousand years of wedding choirs keeping her ember lit long after any single festival's flames have gone out.
variants.cross: The seasons cross sets Lada on the 18h dusk arm, colored red and aimed at the autumn equinox — shared with Svetovid, the mars body. Autumn was the season the wedding feasts were sung, once the grain stood threshed and the bare fields held room for a kolo — the same red dusk shared by the sickle and the sword that kept the harvest safe to dance over.
variants.trio: In the trio Lada keeps the 20h arm — and here the red Love arm is truly hers, the virtue that is her whole nature turned into a direction. She shares it with Svetovid, the mars body: the love-goddess's Love and the war-god's guard on the same evening arm, the wedding song and the sword that keeps the dancers safe to sing it.

rows: The trio's summit belongs to The One — God read as the union of the two below him, in the noon yellow of Joy. He loves himself AND questions himself, holding Pride and Weakness in a single person, and because he carries both he corrects his own deeds and can be neither manipulated nor steered. His own verse names him: "I am the Alpha and the Omega... who is, and who was, and who is to come" (Revelation 1:8) — and on this dial Omega already keeps the 24h seat while Sigma is the union of the two, so the geometry says what the scripture says. E PLURIBUS UNUM: out of many, one; "I AM THAT I AM" (Exodus 3:14), the name that needs no other.

As the Judge he is the one who knows all and sees all, and therefore the only one fit to weigh the case. He holds the PRESENT — the sole ideal seat, for the past never happened and the future never comes — and from it he answers the Prosecutor's zeal and the Advocate's mercy without becoming either. NOVUS ORDO SECLORUM is his permanent prophecy: Virgil's "the great order of the ages is born anew" (Eclogue IV), a new One always coming to lead mankind toward a better day.

The red evening arm of Passion belongs to The Devil — Pride, love turned back upon itself, and in these articles the face of enjoyment and hedonism. His is the Boss syndrome, the appetite that would have everyone please him; the tempter of Matthew 4 who offers the bread, the glory and all the kingdoms of the world at once. His creed is "let us eat and drink; for tomorrow we die" (1 Corinthians 15:32, after Isaiah 22:13) — the future devoured now, in one sitting.

As the Prosecutor he is the Accuser, KATEGOROS (Revelation 12:10), the adversary who walks the earth in Job and accuses at Joshua's right hand in Zechariah 3. He wants to punish and enjoys punishing, and he strikes FORWARD — the one who seeks to ruin a future the way the red arm forever imagines and wants MORE. His Wrath is real, and only the cross-dial mercy answers it.

Jesus holds the blue pre-dawn arm of Calm, and his quality is WEAKNESS — love turned wholly toward others, and in these articles the face of renunciation. His is the Servant syndrome, the one who pleases everyone at his own cost: "let him deny himself, and take up his cross" (Matthew 16:24), "not my will, but thine, be done" (Luke 22:42). Where the Devil keeps everything, he keeps nothing back.

As the Advocate he is literally the PARAKLETOS (1 John 2:1), the one who always steps in to defend the other. He works in the PAST — the advocate pleads for deeds already done, and the blue arm is the gaze that stays behind; his shadow is Judas's, to drown in old mistakes, and Hope is the medicine he must not refuse ("forgetting those things which are behind" — Philippians 3:13).

The Court's centre is the Eye of Providence: the union of the three arms, and this dial's reading of objectivity itself. A court needs a fourth thing its three offices cannot supply — a standard that none of them owns — and clear, untinted light is that standard, which is why the centre is the only uncoloured element of the whole wheel. Every arm bends the light toward its office; the centre is what the light is before any office touches it. ANNUIT COEPTIS, Providence favours the undertaking, is the motto that steadies the court, and against the Family's centre it reads as the exact complement: the court's union is the watching, the household's is the warming. "The eyes of the Lord are in every place, beholding the evil and the good" (Proverbs 15:3).

The apex belongs to The Child, in spring green — new, growing, unformed, the seat the two below STRIVE FOR. In the paint trio the top is the one who JUDGES; in the light trio the top is the one who is SERVED — the same triangle read once as the hierarchy of power and once as the hierarchy of care. Small and in need of safety, the Child's given love flows to the Father, the pillar of the house: the smallest sleeps soundest behind the Shield.

As the Dawn he is the new morning, rebirth without the past — the day born clean, needing no more thought of what is finished. He learns what love looks like by watching it happen above him, for "the most important thing a father can do for his children is to love their mother" (Theodore Hesburgh). The home runs against the clock: love in a family flows backward in care and forward in growth, and the Dawn is where it returns.

The Mother holds the light-red arm — Venus's own red, love embodied, on the day already given to the woman. Her given love pours to the Child, where the flame is newest and most fragile, as nature itself commands; she is the queen of the hearth, its high seat and its leadership. The circuit needs her to be carried in turn, for the one who holds everyone cannot hold herself.

As the Heart she holds the office that carries the whole house, and the Family triangle exists to solve the problem that office creates. The circuit's law is that each member gives what they are to the one who needs exactly that, and the Heart's difficulty is structural rather than personal: the one who holds everyone cannot hold herself. That is why the Shield bends toward her rather than toward the Child — warming her warms the house through her, so the household's welfare is routed through the person who distributes it. Her gift up the circuit is leadership, the hearth's own small crown. "Her children arise up, and call her blessed" (Proverbs 31:28).

The Father holds the light-blue arm of trust and Calm — Hope's arm in the paint trio, the guardian's color. His given love flows to the Mother, not the Child: the Heart carries everyone, so someone must carry the Heart. The strongest bends toward the one who holds everyone else, and in doing so teaches the Child by example what love is.

As the Shield he is security and protection, the pillar the small turn to. He covers the Heart because warming her warms the house, and he is what comes between the Child and the dark, so the Dawn can sleep. This is the family circuit's meaning: safety flows backward to its source, care flows forward to its future — "a threefold cord is not quickly broken" (Ecclesiastes 4:12).

The centre is the Hearth — the family's union, mirroring the court's Eye: the court's union is the Eye that WATCHES, the family's is the fire that WARMS. Three members, one flame; each gives what they are to the one who needs exactly that, and the love CIRCULATES rather than pooling, so no one is left dry and no one hoards. Theology has a word for this circling dance of love — PERICHORESIS — and the Hearth is its household form, the triangle that is really a circle.
