The Submissive Enabler is the same corner continued past its measure: the bond kept so completely that the keeper has nothing left to keep it with. The fall is not disloyalty but the disappearance of the person doing the loving, which is why it looks like virtue from outside. Ophelia is seated by one act — she agrees to return Hamlet's gifts on her father's instruction, letting herself be used as an instrument in another man's test, and afterwards there is no self to which she can return. Eva Braun's is the descent into the bunker: a devotion that had long since stopped asking what it was devoted to. Peter Pettigrew's is the severed hand: ordered to give what the ritual required, he cuts off his own right hand for a master who had just been carried in like an infant — the self spent instantly and completely on whoever is strongest, with nothing of the man left to ask whether the bond deserves it. Humility without a floor is not humility; it is absence. "The fear of man bringeth a snare" (Proverbs 29:25).

The Sacrificial Protector holds Vigor, Loyalty and Humility together: the bond defended by ACTION, with the defender refusing to step into the place he defends. One axis turns from the Quiet Devotee — Activation — and that single turn is the whole difference between keeping faith and fighting for it. Moses is seated by his answer after the golden calf: offered a nation of his own descendants in place of the one that had just betrayed him, he asks instead to be blotted out of the book rather than let them be destroyed. Harriet Tubman's deed is the returning — not the first escape but the journeys BACK into the country that would have hanged her, each one a decision to re-enter a danger already survived. Harry Potter's is walking into the forest unarmed, going to a death he believes final so that it ends for everyone else. Orange gives the seat its motion; green keeps the protector out of the frame. "Yet now, if thou wilt forgive their sin—; and if not, blot me, I pray thee, out of thy book" (Exodus 32:32).

The Fanatical Martyr is protection that has fallen in love with its own cost. The deed still looks like sacrifice, but the thing protected has become secondary to the act of paying. Samson's seat is the last act at Gaza: he pulls the temple down on himself and three thousand others — a rescue with no one being rescued. Yukio Mishima's is the seizure of the Ichigaya garrison: a speech no soldier wanted, delivered from a balcony, ending in a ritual death staged as an argument. Kylo Ren's is the killing on the bridge, an act performed precisely because it costs him everything, in the belief that the price itself will make him whole. The fall is legible by one test: remove the audience and the deed loses its reason. "Though I give my body to be burned, and have not charity, it profiteth me nothing" (1 Corinthians 13:3).

The Charismatic Champion is Vigor, Loyalty and Dignity at one corner: the one who stands in front, keeps faith with his own, and knows his own worth while doing it. Self-Regard turns positive here — this is the first vertex that permits its holder to be seen — and red is its colour for that reason. Beowulf is seated by the choice to meet Grendel unarmed, laying aside sword and mail because the creature bears none: fairness extended to a monster, past any point where it could be required. Winston Churchill's deed is the decision of late May 1940, taken against a cabinet that wanted terms explored — he refused to open negotiations while the army was still on the beaches, and staked a nation on a judgment he could not prove. Wonder Woman's is crossing No Man's Land alone and upright, walking into fire that had pinned an army for a year. "Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid" (Joshua 1:9).

The Tribal Warlord is the champion whose worth has swallowed the bond that gave it meaning. He still leads and is still followed; what has gone is any measure outside his own honour. Agamemnon's seat is the taking of Briseis: with the army already dying of plague and his own prize surrendered, he takes his best man's woman instead — not for her, but so that no one may see him give up anything without taking something back. Mussolini's is the March on Rome: power taken by demonstration rather than by argument, the crowd's roar accepted as the verdict. Khal Drogo's is the vow sworn in the horde — a promise of conquest offered as tribute to his own name, his followers' devotion turned into fuel for it. The fall of this vertex is always the same: the tribe stops being what the champion serves and becomes what proves him. "Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall" (Proverbs 16:18).

The Steady Guardian holds Composure, Loyalty and Dignity: worth carried without motion, a post kept because it is the post. Activation turns down from the Champion — this guardian's whole strength is that he does not move — and duty in the plainest sense of the word occupies this corner. Hector is seated by the decision to stand outside the Scaean gate: he knows what Achilles will do, his parents call him in from the wall, and he stays because going in is the one thing he cannot do. Elizabeth II is seated by the broadcast from Cape Town on her twenty-first birthday, 21 April 1947: a vow made in advance, in public, that her whole life would be devoted to a service she had not yet begun — the post accepted before she had any idea what it would cost. Aragorn's is the night outside the walls: crowned nowhere and by nobody, he keeps the camp on the Pelennor rather than enter the city, because the city is not yet his to enter. Rose is red thinned by moonlight, and this is what the thinning means: dignity that waits. "Let us not be weary in well doing" (Galatians 6:9).

The Complacent Nepotist is the guardian who has confused the post with its comforts. He is still loyal, still dignified, still unmoved — but the stillness has stopped being a watch and become a chair. Lear's seat is the map: he divides a kingdom by which daughter praises him best, government conducted entirely as a test of affection. Louis XV is seated by the disgrace of Maurepas in April 1749 — the minister who had run the navy for a quarter of a century dismissed over a verse about a royal mistress, the state's business settled as a household grievance. (The famous *"après moi, le déluge"* is apocryphal and is not what seats him.) Denethor's is the refusal to light the beacons: a steward who will not call for aid because calling would admit the house he keeps is no longer enough. Composure without vigilance is not composure; it is sleep with the eyes open. "Woe to them that are at ease in Zion" (Amos 6:1).

The Wise Statesman is Composure, Integrity and Dignity: judgment that rests on principle rather than on bonds, held steady and held with self-respect. The Judgment axis turns here for the first time — the covenant gives way to the rule — and moon-purple takes the seat, midnight's own colour, the hue of a law that does not care who is asking. Joseph is seated by the moment in Egypt when he holds absolute power over the brothers who sold him and uses it to feed them: the principle outlasts the injury, and he says so plainly. George Washington's deed is the resignation of his commission at Annapolis on 23 December 1783 — handing an army back to a congress that could not have taken it from him, nine months after his own officers at Newburgh had offered him the alternative to his face. Its entire content is a limit voluntarily accepted. Dumbledore's is declining the Ministry three times, having learned in one summer exactly what he would become with power. The seat is not cleverness; it is the willingness to be bound. "He hath shewed thee, O man, what is good" (Micah 6:8).

The Cold Elitist is principle that has stopped believing anyone else can be trusted with it. The judgment is still sound and the composure still real; what has gone is the assumption that the governed are of the same kind as the governor. The Grand Inquisitor is seated by his own speech — he explains, calmly and at length, that freedom must be taken back from people for their own good, and means every word. Metternich's is the Carlsbad Decrees: a continent's demand for constitutions answered with censorship and surveillance, order preserved by preventing the question. Saruman's is the argument at Orthanc — alliance with the stronger power proposed in the language of realism, wisdom converted into calculation. Integrity without fellowship curdles into administration. "Ye have taken away the key of knowledge" (Luke 11:52).

The Visionary Founder is Vigor, Integrity and Dignity: principle carried at speed by someone who knows he is the one carrying it. It is the most dangerous positive corner on the cube, because every quality that makes a founder is also what a tyrant needs — only the direction of the founding tells them apart. Aeneas is seated by the departure from Carthage: leaving a love and a kingdom already offered him because the thing he owes is not yet built, a choice the poem treats as costly rather than heroic. Atatürk's deed is 3 March 1924: the caliphate abolished by law in a single day, thirteen centuries of an office ended by a man who could simply have occupied it. Leia Organa's is founding a resistance from nothing after the republic she had already rebuilt collapsed a second time, beginning again with no state left to draw on. Orange gives the seat its speed, purple its law. "Where there is no vision, the people perish" (Proverbs 29:18).

The Messianic Tyrant is the founder who has concluded that he IS the founding. The vision survives; what dies is any authority above it. Pharaoh is seated by the chariots at the sea: having let them go, he turns out after them with six hundred chariots into water that has already opened for somebody else — the evidence total, and the conclusion drawn from it that he is the exception to it. Napoleon's is the coronation at Notre-Dame: he lifts the crown from the altar himself and sets it on his own head — a gesture arranged with Pius VII beforehand and performed anyway, in front of everyone, because being SEEN to take it was the whole content. Paul Atreides is seated by the choice at the end of the desert road — he sees the jihad his own name will unleash, counts the dead in advance, and accepts the throne anyway. This is the corner Lucifer's pole feeds: his fall made governmental. "I will ascend into heaven, I will exalt my throne above the stars of God" (Isaiah 14:13).

The Principled Reformer is Vigor, Integrity and Humility: a rule pressed hard by someone who does not intend to sit on the throne he is clearing. Self-Regard turns down from the Founder — one axis — and that turn is the whole difference between reform and conquest. Antigone is seated by the burial: she covers her brother's body knowing the decree and the penalty, claiming no office and offering no defence but the older law. Martin Luther King Jr.'s deed is the Letter from Birmingham Jail, written in the margins of a newspaper to eight clergymen who had called his campaign unwise — an argument made from inside the punishment and addressed to allies rather than enemies. Luke Skywalker's is throwing the lightsaber away in front of the Emperor, refusing a victory that would have made him the thing he came to end. Green holds the seat because the reformer's proof is that he does not stay. "Let judgment run down as waters" (Amos 5:24).

The Puritanical Zealot is the reformer who has fallen in love with the cleansing. He still wants no throne — that is what makes him hard to see — but the rule has become an appetite, and the standard rises to meet whoever is left. Frollo is seated by the ultimatum at Notre-Dame: a man who has spent his life on discipline offering a woman her life in exchange for herself, experiencing his own desire as her crime. Savonarola's is the Bonfire of the Vanities — a city persuaded to burn its own mirrors, paintings and books, purification staged as a public act. Stannis Baratheon's is the burning on the march: the last correct decision in a chain of correct decisions, each one following from the last. Humility that measures others is not humility. "Why beholdest thou the mote that is in thy brother's eye?" (Matthew 7:3).

The Contemplative Sage is Composure, Integrity and Humility: the corner that thinks before it moves, judges by the rule, and does not enter its own account. It is the cube's opposite pole to the Charismatic Champion — all three axes reversed — and the two make the clearest pair on the wheel: one is believed because he is seen, the other because he waited. Job is seated by his answer at the ash-heap: offered the one move that would end the argument — curse God and be done — he refuses both that and the false comfort of his friends' theology, and keeps asking the question honestly. Tolstoy's deed is the renunciation of the copyrights, signing away the income of his own books because he could not hold the argument and the royalties at once. Gandalf's is the finding of Isildur's scroll in the Minas Tirith archives — one document, read by nobody for an age, which turns a suspicion he had refused to act on into the thing everything after it depended on. "The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom" (Proverbs 9:10).

The Paralyzed Purist is the sage who has made the waiting permanent. The reasoning stays excellent — that is the trap — and every further hour of it is defensible on its own terms. Hamlet is seated by the chapel: the king is at prayer, the sword is drawn, and he sheathes it on a refinement about the state of the man's soul, a scruple that costs four more lives. Nicholas II's is the marginal note: told by his own ministers that the country wanted a government answerable to it, he wrote across the request that the men making it were possessed by *"senseless dreams"* — the question closed with a phrase, and never reopened until it reopened itself. Mace Windu's is the standing law of the Council: a code that could not name what was already sitting inside its own chamber, correct in every particular and blind in the one that mattered. Integrity without the willingness to act is only preference. "To him that knoweth to do good, and doeth it not, to him it is sin" (James 4:17).

moon.name: Medusa
moon.base:
[[The Figure]] Medusa is Monday's figure because the Gorgon is the seat's own virtue inverted: the Moon's arm is Serenity, and hers is the one face in Greek myth before which serenity is not available. Ovid is explicit that she was not born monstrous — the Metamorphoses makes her a mortal woman punished into the shape everyone remembers — so the terror on this arm is imposed rather than innate, which is exactly how Fear works and exactly why it is the Moon's vice rather than Mars'.

[[On the Dial]] Her home is the 04h arm in deep blue (#002FFF), the hour before dawn the canon names Calm: the emptiest interval of the night, when nothing has happened yet and everything still might. Petrifaction is that interval made permanent — not a wound but an arrest, the victim stopped in the instant before he could decide anything. Blue's mood and blue's monster describe the same stillness from opposite sides, one chosen and one inflicted.

[[The Lesson]] The bundle's virtue is Serenity and its vice is Fear, and the tradition hands her both. Her blood was drawn into two vials for Asclepius: from one side a poison, from the other a cure that raised the dead — one body, two pharmacies, the plainest statement this bestiary makes that a terror and a medicine can be the same substance read from different sides. Across the dial at 16h the Minotaur answers her, and the cure runs both ways: Courage dissolves Fear, and Serenity quiets Wrath. Rage is fear that finally moved; petrifaction is rage that never did.

[[The Hour]] *"She was once most beautiful, and the jealous hope of many suitors"* (Ovid, Metamorphoses IV). The line matters to the seat, because a monster who was made can in principle be unmade, and Monday's whole discipline is the refusal to treat a fear as a permanent fact about the world.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 04h arm in deep blue (#002FFF), the Calm of the hour before dawn — the base reading, stillness held as an arrest rather than as peace.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism keeps her at 04h and sharpens the blue to #0040FF — pigment's muted night becomes light's electric one. The hour and its Calm are unchanged; the gaze simply carries further in a colder light.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Medusa takes the deep-night arm in lamplit ink blue (#1F5FA8), the estate of the Scholar, the Book for its object — an unlikely trade until the Gorgon's real mechanism is weighed: she is the one figure in the set whose danger is transmitted entirely by LOOKING, knowledge that destroys whoever acquires it, the oldest warning any library carries.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that deep-night arm is the Unborn, and Medusa turns moonlight silver (#C8D7F0) — earned twice over: her death is Pegasus' birth, so the one seat on this wheel reserved for the not-yet-living is held by the only figure of the week whose ending is somebody else's beginning.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Medusa moves to the 06h arm — Spring, green, aimed at the vernal equinox — and shares it with the Hydra. Two serpent-crowned figures on the season of regrowth, and the pairing is exact: one grows heads back faster than they can be cut, the other grows nothing back at all.
variants.trio: The Trinity keeps her at 04h but renames the watch: the blue arm now means Hope, shared with the Sphinx, guarding the morning from 0h to 8h. The assignment is deliberately hard — hope is what Perseus carried and what her victims lost, and the same arm has to hold both.

mars.name: Minotaur
mars.base:
[[The Figure]] The Minotaur is Tuesday's figure because he is Wrath with the exits closed. Every other rage in the Greek record is spent on something — Achilles on Hector, Ares on a battlefield — while Asterion's is spent on nothing at all: Athens sent tribute into the labyrinth on a schedule, and Daedalus built the maze for the single purpose of keeping one anger from reaching the world. Orange is the seat of Courage and Wrath together, and the labyrinth is the argument for why one fire needs two names.

[[On the Dial]] His home is the 16h arm in ember orange (#DC9600), the Zeal of the working afternoon — the hour the canon gives to banked, continuing fire rather than to a first flare. A maze is precisely banked fire: rage that has been given a shape and a boundary instead of an end. The tribute cycle is that hour's own rhythm, an anger maintained rather than resolved.

[[The Lesson]] The bundle's virtue is Courage and its vice is Wrath, and the myth splits them between two bodies rather than one: the bull-headed half of the story carries the Wrath, and Theseus — who walked in with a thread and no advantage of strength — carries the Courage. The Minotaur is what this seat becomes when its virtue is subtracted. Across the dial at 04h Medusa's Serenity is the named cure, and it is real in both directions: the calm that would have quieted him is the same calm his own terror makes impossible for anyone else.

[[The Hour]] Aristotle's test fits the seat better than any bestiary line: *"Anybody can become angry — that is easy; but to be angry with the right person, and to the right degree, and at the right time, and for the right purpose, and in the right way — that is not within everybody's power"* (Nicomachean Ethics II). Asterion fails every clause of it, and a labyrinth is what a city builds when a rage cannot be corrected, only contained.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 16h arm in ember orange (#DC9600), the Zeal of the working afternoon — the base reading, a fire kept rather than spent.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism keeps him at 16h and burns the ember up to pure yellow (#FFFF00) — red and green fused. Light gives the same rage a hotter hue without giving it a door; the hour and its Zeal are unchanged.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the Minotaur takes the 15h afternoon in copper (#C87533), the estate of the Merchant, the Coin for its object — brutal but exact: Athens paid him in children on a fixed schedule, the only figure of this bestiary whose whole existence is a price agreed between two cities and honoured on time.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that same afternoon arm is Maturity, and he wears amber (#FFB400) — the irony is the point. A body that reached full strength and never once reached the world measures its maturity in mass alone, while every faculty that makes maturity worth having stayed walled up with it.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross the Minotaur takes the 18h arm — Autumn, red, aimed at the equinox — sharing the spoke with the Sirens. Bull and song, the two lures of the set: one keeps what is sent to it, the other calls in what would otherwise have sailed past.
variants.trio: The Trinity moves him to 20h, onto Love's red arm beside the Sirens, guarding the evening from 16h to 24h. The seat is an accusation rather than a promotion: Pasiphae's own ruinous love made him, and the arm names the thing he was born out of and can never practise.

mercury.name: Sphinx
mercury.base:
[[The Figure]] The Sphinx is Wednesday's figure because she runs the seat's bundle as a business. Mercury's arm is Wisdom and Greed at once — the Merchant's own pair — and the Sphinx is the only creature in Greek myth who charges for knowledge and collects in lives. The riddle at the gate of Thebes is a toll: answer and pass, fail and pay. That is a trade, priced by someone who knows exactly what the crossing is worth to the traveller.

[[On the Dial]] Her home is the midnight arm at 0h in Tyrian purple (#542E85), the mood the canon calls Sorrow — the day's ledger closed and read. The riddle is a closed ledger in one sentence: four legs, two legs, three legs, a whole life summed and handed back to whoever is walking it. Oedipus wins by naming the account rather than by cleverness about beasts, and the answer costs him more than the failure would have cost anybody else.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Wisdom and the vice is Greed, and the Sphinx is the exact hinge between them: her knowledge is genuine, her pricing is not. The moment the toll is paid honestly she has nothing left to sell and destroys herself — the clearest proof in this bestiary that Greed is not an appetite for goods but an appetite for the leverage knowledge gives over people who lack it. Across the dial at 12h the Erymanthian Boar's Generosity is the named cure: wisdom that gives itself away cannot be charged for, and so cannot be lost.

[[The Hour]] *"For in much wisdom is much grief: and he that increaseth knowledge increaseth sorrow"* (Ecclesiastes 1:18) — Wednesday's own mood written long before this dial assigned it, and the Sphinx's whole career is the commercial version of it.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the midnight arm at 0h in Tyrian purple (#542E85), the Sorrow of the closed ledger — the base reading, a toll collected and counted.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns her purple to magenta (#BD00BD) — the one hue found in no rainbow, a color the eye invents where the spectrum's two ends meet. Fitting for a riddle: the answer was never in the words, only in the mind that closed the gap between them.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the Sphinx shifts to the 21h evening arm in stage-velvet violet (#7A2E8E), the estate of the Artist, the Mask for its object — a truer seat than the Merchant's own, since her riddle is a performance with a fixed script replayed for every traveller, and the mask is the composure kept by someone who already knows the answer.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that evening arm is Old Age, and she wears dusk violet (#9C6BD4) — precisely earned, because her riddle IS a life measured in ages: the crawling, the walking and the staff, three stages of one creature that only someone at the third could state so calmly.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross the Sphinx keeps the bottom arm at 0h — Winter, blue, aimed at the winter solstice — and she alone shares it with no one. The year's midnight belongs to a single figure, and the set has only one that works entirely by speech: the rest of this bestiary kills by contact.
variants.trio: The Trinity lifts her off midnight to 04h, onto Hope's blue arm beside Medusa, guarding the morning from 0h to 8h. The move names what a riddle actually offers: every traveller who reaches the gate is being given a chance, and a chance priced this cruelly is still, structurally, hope.

jupiter.name: Erymanthian Boar
jupiter.base:
[[The Figure]] The Erymanthian Boar is Thursday's figure because Excess is the vice of a seat whose virtue is Generosity, and the Boar is the one creature in the labours that consumes a gift. Jupiter's arm is abundance — the harvest, the full table, the priest who feeds his village — and the Boar is that same abundance eating itself: whole terraces of Arcadian vine and grain taken in a season by an appetite with no notion of a season.

[[On the Dial]] Its home is the top arm at 12h in noon yellow (#F8E600), the Joy of the day's peak, and the placement is not ironic. Excess only exists where there is plenty; nobody overeats a famine. Noon is the hour with the most to give, and therefore the only hour on the wheel where this vice can even be committed — the seat's own generosity is the precondition of the sin that spoils it.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Generosity and the vice is Excess, and the fourth labour separates them with unusual precision. Heracles was ordered to bring the Boar back ALIVE, and did it by driving it into deep mountain snow, where the same bulk that made it unstoppable became the thing that trapped it. Excess is not defeated by force; it is defeated by the exhaustion of its own conditions. Across the dial at 0h the Sphinx's Wisdom is the named cure — measure, applied before the field is gone rather than after.

[[The Hour]] *"Hast thou found honey? eat so much as is sufficient for thee, lest thou be filled therewith, and vomit it"* (Proverbs 25:16). Thursday's Joy is the fullest hour this dial has, and the Boar is its standing reminder that the difference between a feast and a ruin is a quantity rather than a kind.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the top arm at 12h in noon yellow (#F8E600), the Joy of the day's peak — the base reading, plenty at the hour that has the most of it.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns its noon to green (#00DC00) — the wavelength at the summit of human sight. Fitting for the one figure of the set whose whole quarrel is with growing things: light measures the field the Boar spends.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the Boar shifts to the 09h morning arm in alb ivory (#EDEDE0), the estate of the Priest, the Bell for its object — the sharpest trade in the set, since a priest's work is exactly the distribution the Boar refuses: one harvest, either shared out or taken in a single mouth.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that morning arm is Childhood, and the Boar wears spring green (#7CE577) — apt rather than cruel. An appetite that has never once been told no is a child's appetite in a body large enough to act on it.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross the Boar holds the 12h Summer arm, yellow, aimed at the solstice — sharing the spoke with the Nemean Lion. Two beasts of the same labour cycle on the year's brightest hour, one taken alive and one taken bare-handed, the set's twin proofs that strength alone settles nothing.
variants.trio: On the Trinity the Boar keeps the top arm at 12h, yellow, where the color now names Faith, shared with the Hydra as they guard the day's height from 8h to 16h. The pairing is honest about the vice: faith and appetite both trust that there will be more tomorrow, and only one of them is right about why.

venus.name: Sirens
venus.base:
[[The Figure]] The Sirens are Friday's figures because the seat's vice is Jealousy and its virtue is Love, and the Sirens are the only creatures in Homer who are wanted without ever wanting. Venus' arm is the Artist's — beauty made and beauty desired — and the Siren song is art separated from every purpose except capture. What it offers is not pleasure but knowledge: in the Odyssey they promise Odysseus everything that happened at Troy, tuned exactly to the one appetite he cannot refuse.

[[On the Dial]] Their home is the 20h arm in deep red (#B60000), the Passion of the evening. The hour is theirs by construction: Passion is the mood of wanting something enough to move toward it, and the Sirens do nothing but supply the wanting. They never pursue, never board, never strike — the whole mechanism is voluntary approach, which is what makes this the red arm's own danger rather than Mars'.

[[The Lesson]] Love and Jealousy share a hue because they share a motion, and the Sirens hold only the second half. A jealous love wants the other near and does not care in what condition; the wrecks in the shallows are that preference carried to its end. Odysseus is the counter-argument the same book supplies: bound to the mast with his crew's ears stopped with wax, he takes in the whole song and arrives anyway — proof that the cure is not deafness but structure. Across the dial at 08h the Hydra's Patience answers them exactly: what cannot be resisted in a moment can be outlasted across one.

[[The Hour]] *"Never yet has any man rowed past this isle in his black ship until he has heard the sweet voice from our lips"* (Odyssey XII) — a boast, and true, and beside the point. Friday's discipline is not to be unmoved by what is beautiful; it is to have decided in advance, while still calm, what one intends to do about it.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 20h arm in deep red (#B60000), the Passion of the evening — the base reading, desire supplied rather than felt.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism keeps them at 20h and purifies the red to its light primary (#FF0000) — the reddest red there is, unmixed. In Newton's world Passion is a wavelength rather than a pigment, and a song that admits no mixture is the right tenant for it.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the Sirens shift to the 18h sunset arm in iron-blood crimson (#A02020), the estate of the Soldier, the Sword for its object — a seat they earn without ever lifting a weapon. The count of dead on their shore is the highest in the set, and every one of it was volunteered.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that sunset arm belongs to the Elder, the harvest of a life, and the pair deepens to ember (#FF6A3C) — the fit is what they actually sell. Their bargain is memory: the whole of Troy offered back to the men who fought it, a harvest of years traded for the years remaining.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross the Sirens hold the 18h arm — Autumn, red, aimed at the autumnal equinox — sharing the spoke with the Minotaur. Lure and maze together: one draws the traveller in, the other makes sure he cannot leave.
variants.trio: The Sirens do not move: the Trinity's Love arm is their own 20h in their own red. The Minotaur joins them, and the two guard the evening from 16h to 24h — the arm of Love held by this set's two proofs that being wanted and being loved are different facts about a person.

saturn.name: Hydra
saturn.base:
[[The Figure]] The Hydra is Saturday's figure because it inverts the seat's own economy. Saturn's arm is the harvest — cut, and what was cut is gathered — and the Hydra is the one body in this bestiary where cutting produces more of what was cut. Two heads for every one taken is not a monster's flourish; it is agriculture running backwards, and it is why the second labour could not be finished by the method that finished the first.

[[On the Dial]] Its home is the 08h arm in field green (#007E00), the Renewal of the morning. Renewal is the seat's promise and the Hydra is its parody: regeneration with no direction in it, growth that answers every intervention with more of itself. The same green holds the arm's virtue and its vice, and this figure is why the canon insists they are one hue — Patience and Envy are both a refusal to let a thing be finished.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Patience and the vice is Envy, and Heracles wins only when he stops competing with the creature's own tempo. Iolaus' torch seals each neck as it is opened, so the wound cannot be answered: method applied at the pace of the problem rather than the pace of the anger. That is the whole content of Patience on this dial, and it is why the labour is remembered as the one that needed a second pair of hands. Across the dial at 20h the Sirens' Love is the named cure — what is envied is what somebody decided to want without first asking whether it was ever available.

[[The Hour]] *"To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven: a time to plant, and a time to pluck up that which is planted"* (Ecclesiastes 3:1-2). The Hydra is what a field becomes when the second half of that sentence is never allowed to arrive.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 08h arm in field green (#007E00), the Renewal of the morning — the base reading, regrowth with nothing to govern it.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns its morning green to cyan (#00DDDD) — the color of the clear early sky rather than of the marsh. Renewal keeps the hour; light names the air above the swamp instead of the water in it.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the Hydra shifts to the dawn arm, 06h, in field green (#3E8914), the estate of the Farmer, the Plough for its object — the estate whose entire discipline it lacks. A farmer cuts in order to finish; the Hydra is the field that has never once agreed to be harvested.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the dawn arm is Birth, and it wears predawn mist (#8FA8C8) — earned literally rather than by metaphor, since this is the one body on the wheel that gives birth at the site of its own wounds, twice over each time.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross the Hydra moves to 06h — Spring, green, aimed at the vernal equinox — sharing the spoke with Medusa. Two serpent figures on the season of return, and the contrast is the lesson: one cannot stop growing back, the other could not grow back at all.
variants.trio: The Trinity promotes the Hydra from the morning to the crown: the 12h Faith arm, yellow, shared with the Boar, guarding the day's height from 8h to 16h. The reading is uncomfortable and correct — persistence is faith with no object, and the only difference between the two is whether anything is owed at the end.

sun.name: Nemean Lion · Cerberus
sun.base:
[[The Figure]] Sunday's seat is held by two sons of Typhon and Echidna, which makes this the only dual in the book whose two faces are literally brothers. The Nemean Lion holds the bright face and Cerberus the dark one, and both are Heracles' work — the first labour and the last. The argument here is therefore about one house rather than about two opposed powers: the throne and its shadow drawn from a single bloodline, exactly as the canon says a dual should be.

[[On the Dial]] The center holds no arm and no hour. White-gold is the sum of every hue the wheel can mix, and the six monsters around it are that light taken apart — Fear, Wrath, Greed, Excess, Jealousy, Envy, one to each spoke. The Lion is what the source looks like when nothing has yet been subtracted from it: an invulnerability that needs no weapon at all.

[[The Lesson]] The bundle gives the ruler face Justice against Pride and the servant face Humility against Servility. The Lion's pelt could not be cut by iron, and Heracles took it bare-handed and then wore it — the labour that proves a crown is something worn rather than something owned. Cerberus is the same house's other office: three heads on one door, admitting everything and releasing nothing, and the only labour Heracles completed by asking leave and returning what he had borrowed. Nothing sits opposite the center, so the two cure each other and nobody else — the guard heals the king, and the king heals the guard.

[[The Hour]] Their parents hold this theme's own title, and that is the theme's argument in a line: a week of monsters descending from one pair is a week claiming that terror has a genealogy rather than a cause. *"Except the LORD keep the city, the watchman waketh but in vain"* (Psalm 127:1) — the Sunday seat holds both offices at once, the one that is kept and the one that keeps.

variants.hexa_primary: On the painter's wheel the Lion keeps the center of the dial, white-gold, belonging to no hour: the six monster arms are its light decomposed, one vice to each spoke. This is the home reading — the source, not a spoke, invulnerability rather than any single terror.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism changes every arm around him and cannot change the center: white remains the sum of all wavelengths. It is the same fact from the other side — a hide no blade divides is the physical version of a light no prism can take apart into anything it was not already carrying.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the Lion steps onto the noon arm in royal gold (#F0C420), the estate of the King, the Crown for its object — the plainest seat in the set. A hide no iron could cut, taken bare-handed and thereafter worn, is a crown by the King's own definition: authority proven before it is claimed.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the noon arm is Youth, the zenith of a life, and the pair wears sun-yellow (#FFE800) — apt for a first labour. The Lion opens the twelve and Cerberus closes them, so one seat holds a whole career's beginning and its end under a single hue.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross the Sunday pair holds 12h on the Summer arm, yellow, aimed at the summer solstice — shared with the Erymanthian Boar. Two of Heracles' twelve on the year's brightest spoke: the labour he could not cut and the labour he could not kill.
variants.trio: On the Trinity the seat keeps the center and the bestiary around it narrows to three arms — Faith yellow, Love red, Hope blue. The geometry is indifferent to who holds it, which is the warning the dual exists to make: the same center seats the lion that was worn as a crown and the hound that was borrowed and given back.

faces.ruler:
The Nemean Lion is Sunday's bright face, and the argument for the seat is the first of the twelve labours: a hide that no iron, bronze or stone could cut, taken by hand and thereafter worn.

Its virtue is Justice — an authority proven before it is claimed, and one that afterwards protects whoever wears it rather than whoever granted it. The pelt is the whole point: it changed owners, and the invulnerability came with it, so the power was never a property of the beast. But the same seat is stalked by Pride, which is the exact error of believing the hide is the man. Its mood is Glory, noon's own triumph — the first labour finished, and a crown taken from the one creature that had no use for it.
faces.servant:
Cerberus is Sunday's dark face and the Lion's own brother — Typhon and Echidna's other son, the two of them making this the only dual in the book bound by blood rather than by opposition.

His virtue is Humility, and the twelfth labour is the argument: Heracles could take this one neither by force nor by trick, only by asking Hades' leave, using no weapon, and returning what he had borrowed. A guard who can be borrowed and comes back is the definition of an office held rather than owned. The vice that stalks it is Servility — three heads on a door, admitting everyone and releasing no one, an obedience so total it has stopped being a choice. His mood is Awe, the feeling of standing at a threshold larger than oneself: the underworld gate is the one door on this dial that everybody eventually reaches, and Glory is the same seat's other face.

moon.name: Chang'e
moon.base:
[[The Figure]] Chang'e is Monday's figure because the seat's vice is Fear and hers is the only immortality myth decided by it. The elixir was one dose for two people or a whole dose for one; the versions differ on whether she drank it to keep it from a thief, from her husband's enemy, or from her husband — and all of them agree that she drank it alone and could not come back down. Fear is what turns a reversible situation permanent, and no figure in this cast demonstrates it more exactly.

[[On the Dial]] Her home is the 04h arm in deep blue (#002FFF), the hour before dawn the canon names Calm. She holds the Moon's seat by the plainest correspondence in the whole cast — she lives there — but the mood earns it independently: hers is the one Chinese myth whose entire content is stillness after a single irreversible act, a quiet that is not peace.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Serenity and the vice is Fear, and the Mid-Autumn Festival is China's own verdict on which of the two she ended with. A whole country looks up at the fullest moon of the year and eats a round cake, and the festival is about reunion — the one thing the woman being honoured does not have. The jade rabbit grinds the same elixir forever, medicine prepared for nobody. Across the dial at 16h Erlang Shen's Courage is the named cure: the fear that flees is answered by the discipline that stays.

[[The Hour]] Li Bai wrote the mood down eleven centuries ago and nobody has improved on it: *"I raise my cup and invite the bright moon; with my shadow we are three."* Monday's Calm is the mood of a company that is not quite company, and Chang'e is its patron.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 04h arm in deep blue (#002FFF), the Calm of the hour before dawn — the base reading, the stillness that follows a decision which cannot be taken back.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism keeps her at 04h and sharpens the blue to #0040FF — pigment's muted night becomes light's electric one. The Moon she lives on has no atmosphere to soften anything, and the harder blue is the honest one.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Chang'e takes the deep-night arm in lamplit ink blue (#1F5FA8), the estate of the Scholar, the Book for its object — earned by the rabbit rather than by her: an elixir ground by measure for centuries with no patient left to take it is study that has outlived its own purpose.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that deep-night arm is the Unborn, and she turns moonlight silver (#C8D7F0) — the exact hue of her exile. Immortality taken alone is a life with no next generation in it, ancestry and posterity closed on the same night.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Chang'e moves to the 06h arm — Spring, green, aimed at the vernal equinox — sharing it with Shennong. Elixir and herb on one spoke: the medicine that took a single person out of the world beside the medicine tasted a hundred times to keep everyone else in it.
variants.trio: The Trinity keeps her at 04h but renames the watch: the blue arm now means Hope, shared with Guan Yu, guarding the morning from 0h to 8h. The naming is not sentimental — the Mid-Autumn Festival is held under her Moon and is entirely about reunion, so the hope on this arm belongs to the people looking up rather than to the figure looked at.

mars.name: Erlang Shen
mars.base:
[[The Figure]] Erlang Shen is Tuesday's figure because he is this cast's own proof that Courage and Wrath are separable. Heaven sent an entire army against Sun Wukong and lost; it sent Erlang Shen, and the duel that followed is the most famous contest of transformations in Chinese literature — sparrow against hawk, fish against cormorant, a temple against a general who noticed that the flagpole was in the wrong place. He wins by attention rather than by fury, which is exactly the distinction the orange arm exists to make.

[[On the Dial]] His home is the 16h arm in ember orange (#DC9600), the Zeal of the working afternoon — the canon's hour for a fire that is maintained rather than flared. A duel of seventy-two transformations is maintenance: no single blow decides it, and the winner is whoever is still reading the other correctly at the end.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Courage and the vice is Wrath, and the third eye is the argument for the first. He does not fight harder than heaven's other generals; he sees what they cannot, which is why he alone can hold a shapeshifter to account. Wrath is the same fire spent on whatever is already visible. Across the dial at 04h Chang'e's Serenity is the named cure, and it cures both ways — the general who sees clearly is the calmest body on this wheel, and flight is the one move he never makes.

[[The Hour]] Sun Tzu wrote the seat's own doctrine: *"If you know the enemy and know yourself, you need not fear the result of a hundred battles"* (The Art of War III). Erlang Shen is that sentence given a face, and the third eye is what the sentence costs.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 16h arm in ember orange (#DC9600), the Zeal of the working afternoon — the base reading, a fire held steady across seventy-two exchanges.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism keeps him at 16h and burns the ember up to pure yellow (#FFFF00) — red and green fused. Apt for the one fighter on this wheel who wins by seeing: light's brightest arm for the general with an extra eye.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Erlang Shen shifts to the 15h afternoon in copper (#C87533), the estate of the Merchant, the Coin for its object — stranger than it looks until his own cult is traced: it grows up around the Dujiangyan waterworks, an irrigation system that has been dividing one river fairly among farmers for over two thousand years, which is a ledger long before it is a battle.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that afternoon arm is Maturity, and he wears amber (#FFB400) — precisely earned, because heaven sent its youth first and lost. Maturity here is not age but the refusal to be surprised, the one quality the Monkey King could not counterfeit.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Erlang Shen holds the 18h arm — Autumn, red, aimed at the equinox — sharing the spoke with Zhinü. The cast's soldier beside its lover, and the pairing says what autumn always says: everything that is kept has to be kept by somebody.
variants.trio: The Trinity moves him to 20h, onto Love's red arm beside Zhinü, guarding the evening from 16h to 24h. The seat is honest rather than flattering: a widespread telling has him split a mountain to free his own imprisoned mother and then go on serving the heaven that imprisoned her, and love practised as duty toward an authority that wronged you is the hardest reading this arm has.

mercury.name: Guan Yu
mercury.base:
[[The Figure]] Guan Yu is Wednesday's figure because he is the only deity in the world whose shrine is standard equipment in a shop. A third-century general of the Three Kingdoms, canonized first by the state and then by the market, he is venerated today by merchants and police alike — both praying to the same virtue, which is loyalty made enforceable by oath. Mercury's arm belongs to trade, and trade rests on precisely that: a promise that costs something to break.

[[On the Dial]] His home is the midnight arm at 0h in Tyrian purple (#542E85), the mood the canon calls Sorrow — the day's ledger closed and read. The whole Guan Yu tradition is a ledger. He surrenders to Cao Cao on stated terms, accepts honours he has already announced he will return, leaves the moment he learns where his sworn brother is, and later settles the account by letting Cao Cao pass at Huarong. Every entry is closed.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Wisdom and the vice is Greed, and the merchant seat needs both named because the same shrewdness serves either. Guan Yu is the cast's answer: a man who counted with total precision and never once counted in his own favour. One strand of the legend even makes him the inventor of the daily account, and Caishen, the actual god of wealth, is the guest in his house rather than the other way round. Across the dial at 12h Zhu Bajie's Generosity is the named cure and the opposite error: the ledger without appetite beside the appetite without a ledger.

[[The Hour]] Confucius, whose Annals Guan Yu is said to have read by candle for the rest of his life: *"The superior man understands what is right; the inferior man understands what will sell"* (Analects IV). Wednesday holds both men, and a shrine in a shop is a daily wager on the first.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the midnight arm at 0h in Tyrian purple (#542E85), the Sorrow of the closed ledger — the base reading, and the one figure of the cast who closes his by hand.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns his purple to magenta (#BD00BD) — the one hue found in no rainbow, invented by the eye where the spectrum's two ends meet. A god made by acclamation rather than by birth wears a color made the same way: real, universally seen, and present in no original.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Guan Yu shifts to the 21h evening arm in stage-velvet violet (#7A2E8E), the estate of the Artist, the Mask for its object — earned by the Romance of the Three Kingdoms rather than by the histories. The red face and the long beard are a stage convention of Chinese opera, and far more people know the performance than know the general.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that evening arm is Old Age, and he wears dusk violet (#9C6BD4) — a fair hue for a figure whose rank kept rising after death. Emperors promoted him for a thousand years, from duke to king to god, which is the only career on this wheel that continues past its own end.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Guan Yu keeps the bottom arm at 0h — Winter, blue, aimed at the winter solstice — and he alone shares it with no one. Fitting for the cast's oath-keeper: the year's midnight has no company, and a promise is only tested where nobody is watching.
variants.trio: The Trinity lifts him off midnight to 04h, onto Hope's blue arm beside Chang'e, guarding the morning from 0h to 8h. The move states what a shrine in a shop actually is — not a prediction about profit but a hope about conduct, renewed every morning the doors open.

jupiter.name: Zhu Bajie
jupiter.base:
[[The Figure]] Zhu Bajie is Thursday's figure because Excess is the vice of the seat whose virtue is Generosity, and he is the one pilgrim in Journey to the West who has both without the discipline to keep them apart. He was Marshal Tianpeng, commander of heaven's naval host, exiled into a pig's body for a drunken advance on the moon goddess — a fall caused by appetite, into a body that then became appetite. The yellow arm is the fullest hour on the dial, and it needs a figure who shows what plenty does to somebody with no measure.

[[On the Dial]] His home is the top arm at 12h in noon yellow (#F8E600), the Joy of the day's peak, and he earns it honestly rather than by irony. He is the warmest and funniest member of the pilgrimage, the one who complains, eats, sleeps, and keeps going anyway. Joy is a mood on this wheel rather than a virtue, and Zhu Bajie is the only figure in the cast who has it constantly.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Generosity and the vice is Excess, and the novel is unusually fair about the distance between them. He is repeatedly ready to abandon the journey and divide the luggage, and he never actually goes; at the end he is given a title — Altar Cleanser — that is a joke and a genuine promotion at once, the office of consuming what is left over on every altar in the world. Across the dial at 0h Guan Yu's Wisdom is the named cure: appetite corrected by an account, and an account warmed by appetite.

[[The Hour]] The Analects again, on the exact difference the seat turns on: *"The superior man may indeed have to endure want, but the inferior man, when he is in want, gives way to unbridled license"* (Analects XV). Zhu Bajie gives way constantly and arrives anyway, which is why this cast keeps him at the brightest hour instead of punishing him with a darker one.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the top arm at 12h in noon yellow (#F8E600), the Joy of the day's peak — the base reading, plenty held by the one figure who never pretends not to want it.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns his noon to green (#00DC00) — the wavelength at the summit of human sight. The brightest color the eye knows for the pilgrim who is most alive at the table: light measures the appetite that pigment only colors.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Zhu Bajie shifts to the 09h morning arm in alb ivory (#EDEDE0), the estate of the Priest, the Bell for its object — absurd until his final title is read. Altar Cleanser is the office of consuming what is offered at every altar in the world, which is a clerical appointment however it was meant.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that morning arm is Childhood, and he wears spring green (#7CE577) — the plainest fit in the cast. His faults are a child's faults exactly: hunger, laziness, complaint, and an affection nobody in the party has ever doubted.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Zhu Bajie holds the 12h Summer arm, yellow, aimed at the solstice — sharing the spoke with Sun Wukong. Marshal and Sage on the year's brightest hour: both were thrown out of heaven for appetite, and only one of them ever admitted that it was appetite.
variants.trio: On the Trinity he keeps the top arm at 12h, yellow, where the color now names Faith, shared with Shennong as they guard the day's height from 8h to 16h. The pairing is exact about what faith is on a long road: the farmer who tests every leaf and the pig who complains every mile both finish the journey, and neither of them ever left it.

venus.name: Zhinü
venus.base:
[[The Figure]] Zhinü is Friday's figure because the red arm holds Love and Jealousy in one hue, and the Weaver Girl's story is the only Chinese myth where the two are the same act performed by different parties. She loves a cowherd; the Queen Mother of Heaven draws a river across the sky to keep them apart. The separation is not a punishment for what she did but for whom she chose — jealousy exercised by heaven, and love paid for by her.

[[On the Dial]] Her home is the 20h arm in deep red (#B60000), the Passion of the evening, and the hour is hers by observation as much as by symbolism. The stars the story is built on — Vega on her side of the Milky Way and Altair on his — are summer evening stars, and Qixi falls on the seventh night of the seventh lunar month, when they are highest. This is the one seat in the cast whose hour can be checked against the sky.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Love and the vice is Jealousy, and the festival is two thousand years of a verdict on which is stronger. One night a year magpies bridge the river; the rest of the year is the weaving. What the tradition praises is not the meeting but the interval — a devotion measured in the three hundred and sixty-four days nobody watches. Across the dial at 08h Shennong's Patience is the named cure, and here the two virtues are barely distinguishable: love at this distance IS patience, and the arm knows it.

[[The Hour]] Qin Guan's Qixi lyric closes the argument better than any commentary: *"If the two hearts are joined for ever and ever, why must they stay together night and day?"* Friday's discipline is exactly that question, asked without bitterness.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 20h arm in deep red (#B60000), the Passion of the evening — the base reading, and the one seat in the cast whose hour is a real observation of a real sky.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism keeps her at 20h and purifies the red to its light primary (#FF0000) — the reddest red there is, unmixed. Fitting for a story told in stars: Vega and Altair are not pigments on a wheel but two of the brightest wavelengths the summer sky sends.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Zhinü shifts to the 18h sunset arm in iron-blood crimson (#A02020), the estate of the Soldier, the Sword for its object — a hard trade for a weaver, and the right one. The river was drawn across the sky with a hairpin, and the only defence available to her afterwards was to keep working every single day of the separation.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that sunset arm belongs to the Elder, the harvest of a life, and she deepens to ember (#FF6A3C) — earned by arithmetic. A marriage kept across two millennia of one night a year is the longest harvest on the wheel, gathered a day at a time and counted only once.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Zhinü holds the 18h arm — Autumn, red, aimed at the autumnal equinox — sharing the spoke with Erlang Shen. Weaver and general on one arm: the two figures of the cast whose whole worth is measured in how long they hold a position.
variants.trio: Zhinü does not move: the Trinity's Love arm is her own 20h in her own red, for love is her virtue in both sets at once. Erlang Shen joins her, and together they guard the evening from 16h to 24h — the one who keeps a promise and the one who keeps a gate.

saturn.name: Shennong
saturn.base:
[[The Figure]] Shennong is Saturday's figure because the green arm is the harvest, and he is the person the Chinese tradition credits with making a harvest possible. The Divine Farmer gave the plough and the market, and then did what nobody else in this cast ever does: he tested. The tradition says he tasted a hundred herbs to sort medicine from poison, and that the poisons eventually killed him — the seventy-ninth, in the usual telling, on a day the antidote did not arrive in time.

[[On the Dial]] His home is the 08h arm in field green (#007E00), the Renewal of the morning. Renewal is the mood of work whose result is not visible on the day it is done, and no figure on this wheel embodies that more literally: a herb tested today protects a stranger a century from now. The seat's hour is the one the canon gives to beginnings that somebody else will finish.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Patience and the vice is Envy, and Shennong is this cast's proof that patience is a method rather than a temperament. One leaf at a time, one effect recorded at a time, until a pharmacopoeia exists — the Shennong Bencao Jing, compiled centuries later, still carries his name over three hundred and sixty-five entries. Envy is the same green refusing the wait and wanting the finished field. Across the dial at 20h Zhinü's Love answers him, and the exchange is even: the weaver proves that waiting can be devotion, the farmer proves that devotion can be a procedure.

[[The Hour]] *"They that sow in tears shall reap in joy"* (Psalm 126:5). Shennong sowed in poison, which is the harder version of the same sentence, and the tradition's own verdict is that he knew what each leaf might cost before he took it.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 08h arm in field green (#007E00), the Renewal of the morning — the base reading, work whose result belongs to somebody not yet born.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns his morning green to cyan (#00DDDD) — the color of the clear early sky rather than of the field. Renewal keeps the hour; light names the weather a farmer reads before it names the crop.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Shennong takes the dawn arm, 06h, in field green (#3E8914), the estate of the Farmer, the Plough for its object — the only seat in this cast that needs no argument at all. He is the Divine Farmer; the estate is named after his trade and the object is his own invention.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the dawn arm is Birth, and he wears predawn mist (#8FA8C8) — earned by consequence rather than by age. Agriculture is where a settled human life begins, so the oldest figure of the cast holds the wheel's youngest hour by being the reason anyone is there to hold it.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Shennong moves to 06h — Spring, green, aimed at the vernal equinox — sharing the spoke with Chang'e. Two medicines on the season of return: the elixir that removed one person from the world, and the pharmacopoeia that kept everyone else in it.
variants.trio: The Trinity promotes Shennong from the morning to the crown: the 12h Faith arm, yellow, shared with Zhu Bajie, guarding the day's height from 8h to 16h. The reading is literal — a man who swallows an unknown leaf to find out what it does is performing faith with his own body, and the tradition says it eventually took it.

sun.name: Sun Wukong · the Six-Eared Macaque
sun.base:
[[The Figure]] Sunday's seat is held by a title nobody granted. Sun Wukong wrote Great Sage Equal to Heaven on his own banner, and heaven — having failed to remove him — entered it in the register. That is Pride in its exact technical form: not vanity but a self-issued authority, a crown taken rather than conferred. The dark face is his perfect counterfeit, the Six-Eared Macaque, who claims the same title with the same body, the same weapon and the same memories, and is wrong for no reason anyone in heaven could name.

[[On the Dial]] The center holds no arm and no hour. White-gold is the sum of every hue the wheel can mix, and the six days around it are that light taken apart. The Monkey King belongs there by the only credential the seat recognizes: he is the figure the whole cast is defined against — heaven's armies, Erlang Shen, the pilgrimage itself. A source is whatever the rest of the wheel radiates from.

[[The Lesson]] The ruler face carries Justice against Pride and the servant face Humility against Servility, and the episode that decides between them is this cast's own sealed argument. The Six-Eared Macaque is indistinguishable: the Jade Emperor's mirror fails, Guanyin's incantation fails, and the underworld's register of every living soul fails, until the Buddha names him. What separates a true sage from a perfect imitation is therefore not any observable property. It is only whether the thing was earned. Nothing sits opposite the center, so the two cure each other and nobody else — the false Sage is what the true one becomes the moment the title is all that is left of him.

[[The Hour]] Laozi gives the sharpest reading of the seat available: *"He who conquers others has force; he who conquers himself is strong"* (Daodejing 33). The whole of Journey to the West is the second half of that sentence taking five hundred years and one golden headband to arrive.

variants.hexa_primary: On the painter's wheel the Sage keeps the center of the dial, white-gold, belonging to no hour: the six arms are his light decomposed. This is the home reading — the figure the rest of the cast is arranged against rather than one day among them.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism changes every arm around him and cannot change the center: white is the sum of every wavelength. The reading is his own oldest trick turned back on him — seventy-two transformations, and the one shape he could never take was somebody else's centre.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Sun Wukong steps onto the noon arm in royal gold (#F0C420), the estate of the King, the Crown for its object — the only figure in the book who took that object literally. The seat is granted here on the same terms heaven finally granted the title: not because it was deserved, but because nothing else stopped him.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the noon arm is Youth, the zenith of a life, and the pair wears sun-yellow (#FFE800) — precisely earned. Everything that made the Monkey King famous happens before the journey begins, and the pilgrimage is the long correction of a youth that would not end.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross the Sunday pair holds 12h on the Summer arm, yellow, aimed at the summer solstice — shared with Zhu Bajie. Two exiles from heaven on the year's brightest spoke, thrown out for the same reason and given their titles back at the same ceremony.
variants.trio: On the Trinity the seat keeps the center and the cast around it narrows to three arms — Faith yellow, Love red, Hope blue. The geometry cannot tell the Sage from his copy, which is the dual's whole warning: the same center seats the one who earned the title and the one who only holds it.

faces.ruler:
Sun Wukong is Sunday's bright face, and the case for the seat is that he is the only figure in this cast who took the throne instead of receiving it. Stone-born, self-taught, and refused a place at the Peach Banquet, he answered by writing Great Sage Equal to Heaven on a banner of his own — and heaven, after losing an army, wrote it into the register too.

His virtue is Justice, argued from the end of the story rather than the beginning: five hundred years under a mountain and ten thousand miles of escort duty, and the title he is finally given — Victorious Fighting Buddha — is conferred by somebody else. A crown earned twice, once by force and once by service, is this seat's own definition of authority. But the same seat is stalked by Pride, and he is its clearest case in the book: the banner came first, and everything after it was the correction. His mood is Glory — noon's own triumph, a fame that arrived before the deeds that justify it.
faces.servant:
The Six-Eared Macaque is Sunday's dark face and the most exact shadow any throne in this book has. He is not an opposite. He is a copy: the same fur, the same golden fillet, the same iron-banded staff, the same voice and the same memories, claiming the same title with the same conviction.

His virtue would be Humility and he has none of it, which leaves the vice bare — Servility, an existence with no content of its own beyond the shape it is imitating. The episode is the cast's own sealed argument: the Jade Emperor's mirror could not separate them, Guanyin's incantation could not, and the underworld's register of every living soul could not, because by every property available to inspection the two were identical. Only the Buddha named him, and what he named was not a difference in the copy but the absence of a history. His mood is Awe — the vertigo of a court discovering that its highest instruments cannot tell an earned title from a taken one, and Glory is the same seat's other face.

moon.name: CHRO
moon.base:
[[The Office]] The chief human resources officer holds Monday because the blue arm's vice is Fear, and no other office in a company deals in it professionally. Every other executive is measured on an output; this one is measured on what happens to people when the outputs go wrong. Redundancy, grievance, investigation, the difficult conversation — the calendar of this role is a list of the worst days other people are having.

[[On the Dial]] The seat is the 04h arm in deep blue (#002FFF), the hour before dawn the canon names Calm: the interval when nothing has happened yet and everything still might. That is precisely the state a company keeps its workforce in — notice periods, restructurings announced but not executed, the quiet around a decision already taken elsewhere. The office that administers the interval belongs to the hour that IS the interval.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Serenity and the vice is Fear, and this role is the corporate proof that both are administered from one desk. The same function that protects an employee from an abusive manager also drafts the letter that ends his job, and it does both in the same calm voice, because calm is the instrument. Serenity here is not peace of mind; it is composure supplied to a room that has none. Across the dial at 16h the operating office's Courage is the named cure — the fear that paralyses is answered by the discipline that decides.

[[The Hour]] The role's own hazard is worth naming: an office whose product is composure will eventually be tempted to produce composure instead of remedy. *"A soft answer turneth away wrath"* (Proverbs 15:1) is true, and it is also the exact sentence a company hides behind when the wrath was earned.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 04h arm in deep blue (#002FFF), the Calm of the hour before dawn — the base reading, composure supplied to a room that has none of its own.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism keeps the office at 04h and sharpens the blue to #0040FF — pigment's muted night becomes light's electric one. The colder blue is the more honest one, because the calm this role produces is manufactured to specification rather than felt.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the seat takes the deep-night arm in lamplit ink blue (#1F5FA8), the estate of the Scholar, the Book for its object — a natural trade, since this is the company's only true archivist: every warning, every review and every settlement is written down here and nowhere else.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that deep-night arm is the Unborn, and the office turns moonlight silver (#C8D7F0) — earned by function. Hiring is the corporate version of the not-yet-born: an organisation chart drawn for people who have not been chosen, budgeted for a year that has not started.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross the seat moves to the 06h arm — Spring, green, aimed at the vernal equinox — sharing the spoke with the technology office. Recruitment and infrastructure on the season of planting: the two functions whose work is judged years after it is done.
variants.trio: The Trinity keeps the office at 04h but renames the watch: the blue arm now means Hope, shared with the finance seat, guarding the morning from 0h to 8h. The naming is exact — every hire is a wager on a person, and the whole of this function is the management of wagers nobody can settle in advance.

mars.name: COO
mars.base:
[[The Office]] The chief operating officer holds Tuesday because operations is the only executive function measured in hours. Strategy is judged over years and a brand over decades; this office is judged by whether the thing that had to ship this morning shipped. Orange carries Courage and Wrath in one hue, and this is the seat where a company learns that a single drive produces both, depending only on whether the target is the problem or the person nearest to it.

[[On the Dial]] The seat is the 16h arm in ember orange (#DC9600), the Zeal of the working afternoon — the canon's hour for a fire that is maintained rather than flared. Operations has no other mode. The work is continuous, the metric refreshes, and the discipline required is the ability to still be burning at the end of a shift in which nothing was resolved, only handled.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Courage and the vice is Wrath, and the distinction here is procedural rather than temperamental. Courage in this office is escalating a failure upward, on the record, before it is convenient; Wrath is escalating it downward, to whoever is available. Both feel identical from inside — urgency, volume, speed — which is exactly why the seat needs two names. Across the dial at 04h the people office's Serenity is the named cure, and the exchange runs both ways: composure without decision is paralysis, and decision without composure is damage.

[[The Hour]] Aristotle set the standard the seat is graded against: *"Anybody can become angry — that is easy; but to be angry with the right person, and to the right degree, and at the right time, and for the right purpose, and in the right way — that is not within everybody's power"* (Nicomachean Ethics II). An operating officer is asked to pass that test several times a day, in public.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 16h arm in ember orange (#DC9600), the Zeal of the working afternoon — the base reading, urgency that has to survive a whole shift.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism keeps the office at 16h and burns the ember up to pure yellow (#FFFF00) — red and green fused. A live metrics wall is precisely that fusion: alarm and clearance rendered in the same light, refreshing on the same interval.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the seat shifts to the 15h afternoon in copper (#C87533), the estate of the Merchant, the Coin for its object — a fair trade rather than a demotion. Operations is where a company's promises are actually paid: every delivery date sold by somebody else is settled here, in units and hours.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that afternoon arm is Maturity, and the office wears amber (#FFB400) — precisely earned. This is the one executive seat that cannot be held on potential: it is judged entirely on what has already been delivered, which is the working definition of a mature record.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross the seat takes the 18h arm — Autumn, red, aimed at the equinox — sharing the spoke with the design office. Throughput beside taste on the harvest arm, and the argument between them is the oldest one any company has: shipped, against shipped well.
variants.trio: The Trinity moves the office to 20h, onto Love's red arm beside the design seat, guarding the evening from 16h to 24h. The seat is less strange than it looks — the people who stay for the incident at three in the morning are not doing it for the metric, and every operating officer knows exactly what they are doing it for.

mercury.name: CFO
mercury.base:
[[The Office]] The chief financial officer holds Wednesday because the purple arm carries Wisdom and Greed in a single bundle, and finance is the only office where the two are one skill pointed in two directions. The discipline that keeps a company solvent — counting honestly, refusing what cannot be afforded, closing the books on time — is indistinguishable in method from the discipline that starves a good project and hoards a reserve nobody will ever be allowed to spend.

[[On the Dial]] The seat is the midnight arm at 0h in Tyrian purple (#542E85), the mood the canon calls Sorrow: the day's ledger closed and read. A company's accounts are literally that — a period closed, restated and signed for. Nothing else in a business has so exact a claim on the hour, and nothing else is so unwelcome when it arrives.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Wisdom and the vice is Greed, and the seat's honest difficulty is that finance is rewarded for the vice in the short term and for the virtue only in the long one. A cost cut that flatters a quarter is visible immediately; a reserve that survives a downturn is visible once a decade. Across the dial at 12h the marketing office's Generosity is the named cure and the opposite error — the message with no budget discipline beside the discipline with no message.

[[The Hour]] The oldest audit standard in the literature is still the best: *"A false balance is abomination to the LORD: but a just weight is his delight"* (Proverbs 11:1). Every accounting scandal on record is a company that decided the balance was a presentation rather than a measurement.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the midnight arm at 0h in Tyrian purple (#542E85), the Sorrow of the closed ledger — the base reading, and the one office that closes it literally.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns the purple to magenta (#BD00BD) — the one hue found in no rainbow, a color the eye invents where the spectrum's two ends meet. Apt for a discipline whose central objects, goodwill and provision and fair value, are real, universally reported, and present in no warehouse.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the seat shifts to the 21h evening arm in stage-velvet violet (#7A2E8E), the estate of the Artist, the Mask for its object — sharper than it sounds. A quarterly result is a performance with a fixed script and a rehearsed voice, and the whole craft of the office is deciding what a true number is allowed to look like.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that evening arm is Old Age, and the office wears dusk violet (#9C6BD4) — the right hue for the only executive function that thinks in decades by obligation rather than by temperament: depreciation, pension, provision, each of them a promise made to a company's own later life.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross the seat keeps the bottom arm at 0h — Winter, blue, aimed at the winter solstice — and it alone shares it with no one. Fitting for the office that signs: the year's midnight has no company, and an audit letter carries exactly one name.
variants.trio: The Trinity lifts the office off midnight to 04h, onto Hope's blue arm beside the people seat, guarding the morning from 0h to 8h. The move names what a budget actually is — not a record but a forecast, a whole year of hope written down in units precise enough to be wrong about.

jupiter.name: CMO
jupiter.base:
[[The Office]] The chief marketing officer holds Thursday because the yellow arm's virtue is Generosity and its vice is Excess, and marketing is the only corporate function whose whole product is given away. Attention, explanation, welcome — the message is free at the point of delivery and paid for out of the largest discretionary budget in the company. It is also the function most easily converted into pure volume, which is the same generosity with the measure removed.

[[On the Dial]] The seat is the top arm at 12h in noon yellow (#F8E600), the Joy of the day's peak. Marketing owns the loudest hour by construction: it is the office that speaks when a company has the most to say and the largest audience to say it to. Joy is a mood on this wheel rather than a virtue, and this is the only seat in the corporation whose job description includes producing it.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Generosity and the vice is Excess, and this is where a business learns that a message repeated past its evidence becomes the thing it was invented to replace. Marketing at its best is a priesthood in the plain sense — a discipline for saying the same true thing to a new congregation every year without letting it go stale. At its worst it is the identical liturgy with nothing left underneath it. Across the dial at 0h the finance office's Wisdom is the named cure: a budget is the only real limit on a claim.

[[The Hour]] *"Let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil"* (Matthew 5:37). It is an impossible standard for an advertising department, and exactly the right one to be measured against.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the top arm at 12h in noon yellow (#F8E600), the Joy of the day's peak — the base reading, the loudest hour held by the office that supplies the noise.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns the noon to green (#00DC00) — the wavelength at the summit of human sight, the brightest color the eye knows. A department whose entire craft is being noticed belongs at the exact peak of what an eye can register.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the office shifts to the 09h morning arm in alb ivory (#EDEDE0), the estate of the Priest, the Bell for its object — the least metaphorical trade in the set. A brand is a creed with a budget: repetition, ritual, a congregation counted weekly, and a promise nobody can independently verify.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that morning arm is Childhood, and the seat wears spring green (#7CE577) — apt rather than dismissive. Marketing is the function that has to keep meeting the world for the first time, over and over, and an audience that already knows the story is of no use to it at all.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross the office holds the 12h Summer arm, yellow, aimed at the solstice — sharing the spoke with the chief executive. Message and mandate on the year's brightest hour: the two seats a company puts on a stage, and the two whose failures are public by default.
