variants.trio: On the Trinity the seat keeps the top arm at 12h, yellow, where the color now names Faith, shared with the technology office as they guard the day's height from 8h to 16h. The pairing is exact: one asks a market to believe a promise, the other asks a board to fund a platform nobody can see yet, and both spend today on a conviction about later.

venus.name: CDO
venus.base:
[[The Office]] The chief design officer holds Friday because the red arm carries Love and Jealousy in one hue, and design is the only executive function whose authority rests on a preference. Every other office can produce a number to justify a decision. This one produces taste, defends it in rooms full of people who cannot do the work, and is overruled more often than any other seat at the table.

[[On the Dial]] The seat is the 20h arm in deep red (#B60000), the Passion of the evening. Passion is the mood of wanting something enough to move toward it, and design is the one corporate function that fails immediately without it: an indifferent operator still ships, an indifferent accountant still counts, and an indifferent designer produces work that is technically complete and worth nothing.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Love and the vice is Jealousy, and the office holds both by one mechanism. Care for the work is what makes the function worth having; possessiveness about the work is the failure mode every design leader knows by name — the review taken as an attack, the compromise taken as a betrayal, the credit counted. Across the dial at 08h the technology office's Patience is the named cure: what cannot be won in one review can be won across a roadmap.

[[The Hour]] Plato set the argument down long before there were companies to have it: *"The beauty of style and harmony and grace and good rhythm depend on simplicity"* (Republic III). Design's whole standing in a business is the claim that this is a fact about the work rather than an opinion about it.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 20h arm in deep red (#B60000), the Passion of the evening — the base reading, the one office that produces nothing at all without it.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism keeps the seat at 20h and purifies the red to its light primary (#FF0000) — the reddest red there is, unmixed. Fitting for a discipline that argues in colour: in the light world red is a measured wavelength, and this office's whole claim is that taste is measurable too.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the office shifts to the 18h sunset arm in iron-blood crimson (#A02020), the estate of the Soldier, the Sword for its object — earned in every design review. This is the only seat at the table whose work is edited by people who could not produce it, and defending it is a weekly engagement.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that sunset arm belongs to the Elder, the harvest of a life, and the seat deepens to ember (#FF6A3C) — the right hue for the one corporate function with a portfolio. Judgement here is accumulated rather than trained, and it is the only executive credential that can be looked at directly.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross the office holds the 18h arm — Autumn, red, aimed at the autumnal equinox — sharing the spoke with the operating seat. Taste beside throughput on the harvest arm, which is where a company actually decides what it is: what shipped, or what was worth shipping.
variants.trio: The design office does not move: the Trinity's Love arm is its own 20h in its own red, for love is its virtue in both sets at once. The operating seat joins it, and the two guard the evening from 16h to 24h — the function that cares how a thing is made and the function that makes sure it is made at all.

saturn.name: CTO
saturn.base:
[[The Office]] The chief technology officer holds Saturday because the green arm is the harvest, and this is the only executive seat whose work is planted in one year and cut in another. A platform decision made now determines what a company can build in five years and what it will be unable to build for ten. Nothing else at the table has that shape; everything else is graded on the quarter it happened in.

[[On the Dial]] The seat is the 08h arm in field green (#007E00), the Renewal of the morning — the canon's hour for work whose result is not visible on the day it is done. Infrastructure is invisible by design and by success. It becomes a topic of conversation on exactly one kind of day, and by then the decision under discussion was taken years earlier by somebody who may no longer be in the building.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Patience and the vice is Envy, and this is where a company discovers the two are one appetite pointed at different clocks. Patience is refusing the shortcut that would look excellent this quarter; Envy is watching a competitor take that shortcut and shipping it anyway. The green arm's own cure sits at 20h with the design office, and the exchange is even: taste keeps patience from becoming inertia, and patience keeps taste from becoming a single unshippable draft.

[[The Hour]] The proverb usually quoted against this office belongs to it instead: *"One generation passeth away, and another generation cometh: but the earth abideth for ever"* (Ecclesiastes 1:4). A platform outlives the executives who argued about it, which is both the whole value of the seat and the reason it is so easy to underfund.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 08h arm in field green (#007E00), the Renewal of the morning — the base reading, work planted now and cut by somebody else.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns the morning green to cyan (#00DDDD) — the color of the clear early sky rather than of the field. Renewal keeps the hour; light names the conditions a build runs under rather than the build itself.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the office takes the dawn arm, 06h, in field green (#3E8914), the estate of the Farmer, the Plough for its object — the plainest trade in the set. A platform is a field: prepared once, worked continuously, and productive only for as long as somebody keeps tending ground nobody looks at.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the dawn arm is Birth, and the seat wears predawn mist (#8FA8C8) — earned by dependency. Every product a company will launch in the next five years is already constrained by a choice this office makes before any of them exist.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross the office moves to 06h — Spring, green, aimed at the vernal equinox — sharing the spoke with the people seat. Infrastructure and recruitment on the season of planting: the two functions whose returns arrive long after the budget that paid for them was closed.
variants.trio: The Trinity promotes the technology office from the morning to the crown: the 12h Faith arm, yellow, shared with the marketing seat, guarding the day's height from 8h to 16h. The reading is literal — every architecture decision is a bet on a future nobody has seen, defended in a room that wants a date.

sun.name: CEO · Chairman of the Board
sun.base:
[[The Office]] Sunday's seat is the corporation's own dual, and it is the cleanest one in this book because company law wrote it down first. The chief executive runs the company; the chairman of the board runs the body that appoints and removes the chief executive. Two offices, one authority, and a deliberate separation — most modern governance codes recommend the roles be held by different people, precisely because a throne with no shadow answers to nobody.

[[On the Dial]] The center holds no arm and no hour. White-gold is the sum of every hue the wheel can mix, and the six offices around it are that light taken apart: people, operations, finance, message, design, infrastructure. The executive seat is not one of the six because it is not a function — it is the point at which all six are reconciled, which is also the only real content of the job.

[[The Lesson]] The ruler face carries Justice against Pride and the servant face Humility against Servility. The chief executive's Justice is the allocation itself: every budget is a judgement about which of the six arms deserves what, made on incomplete information and defended in public. The Pride that stalks it is the belief that the authority is personal rather than delegated, and the corporate record is a long catalogue of that exact error. The chairman's Humility is structural — an office whose whole power is exercised through other people — and its own failure is Servility, a board that ratifies rather than governs. Nothing sits opposite the center, so the two cure each other and nobody else.

[[The Hour]] *"Where no counsel is, the people fall: but in the multitude of counsellors there is safety"* (Proverbs 11:14). That sentence is, almost word for word, the argument for having a board at all.

variants.hexa_primary: On the painter's wheel the executive seat keeps the center of the dial, white-gold, belonging to no hour: the six offices around it are its light decomposed. This is the home reading — not a seventh function but the point where the other six are reconciled.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism changes every arm around it and cannot change the center: white is the sum of every wavelength. The reading is the seat's own standing complaint — an executive is accountable for every colour in the company and personally responsible for none of them.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the seat steps onto the noon arm in royal gold (#F0C420), the estate of the King, the Crown for its object — the least disguised trade in the whole book. The corporation borrowed the vocabulary directly: a chief executive is a monarch with a fixed term and a board that can end it.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the noon arm is Youth, the zenith of a life, and the pair wears sun-yellow (#FFE800) — apt for an office measured entirely at its peak. Nobody is appointed for what they will be at the end of the term, and the average tenure is short enough that the descent is usually somebody else's problem.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross the Sunday pair holds 12h on the Summer arm, yellow, aimed at the summer solstice — shared with the marketing office. Mandate and message on the year's brightest spoke: the two seats a company puts in front of an audience, and the two whose mistakes are never private.
variants.trio: On the Trinity the seat keeps the center and the company around it narrows to three arms — Faith yellow, Love red, Hope blue. The geometry does not distinguish an executive from a caretaker, which is this dual's own warning: the same chair holds the one who decides and the one who only signs.

faces.ruler:
The chief executive is Sunday's bright face — the office at the head of the table, and the only seat in the corporation whose product is the allocation of every other seat's resources.

Its virtue is Justice, argued from the mechanism rather than from character: a budget is a judgement, made annually, about which of the six functions deserves what, on incomplete information, in front of everyone it affects. An executive who allocates fairly under those conditions is practising the seat's virtue whether or not it feels like one. The vice that stalks it is Pride, and the corporate record is largely a catalogue of one error repeated — an authority delegated by a board and lent by shareholders, treated as a personal possession. Its mood is Glory, noon's own triumph: the office that receives the credit for work done by every arm on this wheel.
faces.servant:
The chairman of the board is Sunday's dark face, and the separation is not a metaphor. Company law and most governance codes recommend that the chair and the chief executive be different people, for a reason this dial states in its own vocabulary: a throne with no shadow answers to nobody.

The office's virtue is Humility, and it is structural rather than personal. A chairman commands nothing directly, runs no function, and exercises the whole of the role's power through a body that must be persuaded — the appointment and removal of the chief executive, and almost nothing else anyone outside the room would notice. The vice that stalks it is Servility: a board that ratifies rather than governs, present for the signature and absent for the decision, which is the failure mode underneath nearly every governance scandal on record. Its mood is Awe — the position of watching a company from a seat that cannot touch its daily working, and Glory is the same seat's other face.

moon.name: Anduin
moon.base:
[[The Figure]] Anduin Wrynn is Monday's figure because he is this cast's argument that serenity is a discipline rather than a temperament. He was crowned a boy, made High King the day his father did not come back from the Broken Shore, and the office he chose for himself was priest: the Alliance's war leader is the one member of its command who fights by mending rather than by cutting. A calm inherited would prove nothing about the seat. A calm maintained by a king with that much reason to abandon it is the whole evidence Monday asks for.

[[On the Dial]] His home is the 04h arm in deep blue (#002FFF), the hour the canon names Calm — the emptiest interval of the night, when nothing has happened yet and everything still might. That is exactly the hour a young king governs in: every decision taken before the day's news arrives, on nothing but the standing state of the world and the nerve to wait for the rest of it.

[[The Lesson]] The bundle's virtue is Serenity and its vice is Fear, and Anduin is seated by holding the first against an unlimited supply of the second — a war on two fronts, a throne taken too early, and a kingdom that would read any tremor in him as a verdict. Across the dial at 16h Muradin's Courage is the named cure, and it runs both ways: courage answers a fear that has already arrived, serenity refuses to spend the hours before it.

[[The Hour]] *"Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you"* (John 14:27). The distinction is the seat's own. The peace the world gives is the absence of a threat; the peace Monday asks for is the one that has to be produced while the threat is still there.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 04h arm in deep blue (#002FFF), the Calm of the hour before dawn — the base reading, a composure produced rather than inherited.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism keeps him at 04h and sharpens the blue to #0040FF — pigment's muted night becomes light's electric one. The hour and its Calm do not move; the same composure simply reads colder, which is what a court sees of a king who never lets the strain reach his voice.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Anduin takes the deep-night arm in lamplit ink blue (#1F5FA8), the estate of the Scholar, the Book for its object — earned rather than borrowed. He was taught by Velen and argued with by Moira Thaurissan long before any general got to him, and the Light he wields is a doctrine he studied, not a birthright he was handed.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that deep-night arm is the Unborn, and he turns moonlight silver (#C8D7F0) — the one seat the wheel reserves for the not-yet-living, held by the youngest king this Alliance has crowned. His whole reign is an argument on behalf of a peace nobody now alive has met.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Anduin moves to the 06h arm — Spring, green, aimed at the vernal equinox — and shares it with Malfurion. Healer and druid on the season of return: one mends bodies, the other mends the ground they are standing on.
variants.trio: The Trinity keeps him at 04h and renames the watch: the blue arm now means Hope, shared with Khadgar, guarding the morning from 0h to 8h. The assignment is exact — a king who will not concede a war is practising hope as policy rather than as feeling.

mars.name: Muradin Bronzebeard
mars.base:
[[The Figure]] Muradin Bronzebeard is Tuesday's figure because he is wrath already schooled into instruction. Brother to Ironforge's king and no king himself, he spent his life as a master-at-arms among humans, and his fame is entirely pedagogical: he is remembered as the man who taught Arthas Menethil to fight. That is the hardest possible test of Tuesday's claim — that courage is taught and wrath is not inherited — and it is why the seat belongs to him rather than to any of the Alliance's louder soldiers.

[[On the Dial]] His home is the 16h arm in ember orange (#DC9600), the Zeal of the working afternoon — the hour the canon gives to banked, continuing fire rather than to a first flare. A weapons master is banked fire by definition: the whole craft is heat kept at a working temperature for decades, spent on drill rather than on grievance.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Courage and the vice is Wrath, and Muradin's decisive act was courage spent on a friend instead of an enemy. In Northrend he told Arthas to leave Frostmourne where it lay, argued against a prince who had already decided, and was cut down by the shattering ice for it. Refusing your own best student, out loud, with nothing to gain, is the seat's own definition of the virtue. Across the dial at 04h Anduin's Serenity is the named cure: the steadiness that would have made the argument unnecessary.

[[The Hour]] *"He that is slow to anger is better than the mighty; and he that ruleth his spirit than he that taketh a city"* (Proverbs 16:32). Tuesday's whole discipline is that sentence's comparative: the seat does not ask for less fire, it asks for the fire to answer to somebody.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 16h arm in ember orange (#DC9600), the Zeal of the working afternoon — the base reading, heat kept at a working temperature rather than spent.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism keeps him at 16h and burns the ember up to pure yellow (#FFFF00) — red and green fused. Light gives the same discipline a hotter hue without giving it an object; the hour and its Zeal are unchanged, and a forge burns brightest doing nothing but staying hot.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Muradin takes the 15h afternoon in copper (#C87533), the estate of the Merchant, the Coin for its object — a stranger seat than the Soldier's, and truer. A master-at-arms trades in the one commodity that cannot be bought back: he is paid in the years of other people's lives, and his entire professional judgement is what a lesson is worth against what it costs to learn late.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that afternoon arm is Maturity, and he wears amber (#FFB400) — the plainest fit in the set. Maturity on this wheel is the age at which a man's strength stops being about himself, and a dwarf who spends his prime teaching human children to hold an axe has already made that trade.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Muradin takes the 18h arm — Autumn, red, aimed at the equinox — sharing the spoke with Jaina. Teacher and student of the same lost prince, seated together on the season of reckoning: both of them warned Arthas, and neither was heard.
variants.trio: The Trinity moves him to 20h, onto Love's red arm beside Jaina, guarding the evening from 16h to 24h. The seat reads harder than it looks: what a teacher does for twenty years with no return on it has no other name, and Northrend is where he paid for the word.

mercury.name: Khadgar
mercury.base:
[[The Figure]] Khadgar is Wednesday's figure because his fame is the price of knowledge, charged against his own body. Apprenticed to Medivh at Karazhan, he uncovered what his master really was, and the Guardian's magic took his youth in an instant — a boy who walked out of that tower white-bearded and old. Mercury's arm holds Wisdom and Greed together, and no member of this cast makes the pairing cheaper to explain: everything he knows was bought, and the bill was presented immediately.

[[On the Dial]] His home is the midnight arm at 0h in Tyrian purple (#542E85), the mood the canon calls Sorrow — the day's ledger closed and read. It is the archmage's own hour twice over: the account of what learning cost, and the long watch of a man who then spent centuries sealing the Dark Portal, holding Outland, and rebuilding the Kirin Tor rather than seeking anything further for himself.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Wisdom and the vice is Greed, and Khadgar is seated on the hinge between them. Greed on this arm is not an appetite for goods; it is the appetite for knowing more than one is owed, which is exactly the sin Medivh's tower was built out of and exactly the one Khadgar declined to repeat. Across the dial at 12h Uther's Generosity is the named cure: knowledge given away cannot be hoarded, and therefore cannot be lost the way Medivh lost his.

[[The Hour]] *"All men by nature desire to know"* (Aristotle, Metaphysics I). The sentence is descriptive, not permissive, and Wednesday's seat is the difference: a desire everybody has is precisely the one that most needs a governor.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the midnight arm at 0h in Tyrian purple (#542E85), the Sorrow of the closed ledger — the base reading, an account of what learning cost.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns his purple to magenta (#BD00BD) — the one hue found in no rainbow, a color the eye invents where the spectrum's two ends meet. Apt for an archmage: the answer he found at Karazhan was in no book there, only in the gap between two things he had been told separately.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Khadgar shifts to the 21h evening arm in stage-velvet violet (#7A2E8E), the estate of the Artist, the Mask for its object — a truer seat than the Merchant's own. He spent his apprenticeship being lied to by a master wearing his own kindly face, and every year afterwards he had to keep a composure his body no longer matched.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that evening arm is Old Age, and he wears dusk violet (#9C6BD4) — the only figure of this cast who holds it as a fact rather than a stage. He was made old in one afternoon and has been old for every year since, which is a different thing from having aged.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Khadgar keeps the bottom arm at 0h — Winter, blue, aimed at the winter solstice — and he alone shares it with no one. The year's midnight belongs to a single figure, and this cast has only one whose decisive act was performed alone in a dark room.
variants.trio: The Trinity lifts him off midnight to 04h, onto Hope's blue arm beside Anduin, guarding the morning from 0h to 8h. The move is argued by what he actually did with the Portal: sealing a door is a bet that the thing behind it can still be kept out, which is hope written as engineering.

jupiter.name: Uther the Lightbringer
jupiter.base:
[[The Figure]] Uther the Lightbringer is Thursday's figure because he did not keep the Light — he founded an order to give it away. The first paladin, anointed at the head of the Silver Hand, he turned what could have been a personal gift into a curriculum with successors, and the Alliance's whole idea of holy war descends from that decision. Jupiter's arm is abundance and the priest who distributes it; a man whose fame is that he taught the second, third and fortieth paladin holds it by right.

[[On the Dial]] His home is the top arm at 12h in noon yellow (#F8E600), the Joy of the day's peak. The placement is literal rather than poetic: the Light on this arm is not a metaphor for plenty, it is the thing given, and noon is the hour with the most of it to hand out.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Generosity and the vice is Excess, and Uther holds both without contradiction. The same absolute standard that made him give without measure made him unable to bend: at Stratholme he refused his own prince's order and was stripped of his command for it, and every later Silver Hand quarrel traces back to a teacher who would not concede a degree. Excess here is not appetite — it is a virtue practised past the point where judgement could still correct it. Across the dial at 0h Khadgar's Wisdom is the named cure: measure, applied before the order is given rather than after.

[[The Hour]] *"Freely ye have received, freely give"* (Matthew 10:8). Thursday's whole doctrine is the symmetry of that sentence, and the Silver Hand is the one institution in this cast built to enforce it on people who will outlive its founder.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the top arm at 12h in noon yellow (#F8E600), the Joy of the day's peak — the base reading, plenty at the hour that has the most of it.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns his noon to green (#00DC00) — the wavelength at the summit of human sight. Fitting for a founder rather than a champion: what he made grows, and an order is measured by whether it is still producing after the teacher is gone.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Uther holds the 09h morning arm in alb ivory (#EDEDE0), the estate of the Priest, the Bell for its object — the one seat in this cast that needs no argument at all. He is the estate: the office of distributing a thing nobody privately owns, and the bell is a summons rather than a possession.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that morning arm is Childhood, and he wears spring green (#7CE577) — read as a founder's age rather than a man's. Every paladin who came afterwards is a child of that anointing, and an order in its first generation has all of childhood's traits: certainty, appetite, and no memory of ever having been wrong.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Uther holds 12h on the Summer arm, yellow, aimed at the solstice — sharing the spoke with Varian and Genn. The founder of the Silver Hand beside the throne he never sat on: the year's brightest hour held by an office and a crown that answer to each other.
variants.trio: On the Trinity Uther keeps the top arm at 12h, yellow, where the color now means Faith, shared with Malfurion as they guard the day's height from 8h to 16h. He is the least strained tenant this arm has: the Light is the one power in the cast that does not work at all unless it is believed in first.

venus.name: Jaina
venus.base:
[[The Figure]] Jaina Proudmoore is Friday's figure because she is the cast's clearest case of love and its vice sharing one hue. She loved Arthas and would not follow him. She chose peace with Thrall's Horde over her own father's fleet, and watched Daelin Proudmoore die for the choice. She rebuilt at Theramore and made it the one place on Kalimdor where the two sides could speak. Every act of the seat is love treated as a decision with a cost attached, which is the only version of it Venus's arm will accept.

[[On the Dial]] Her home is the 20h arm in deep red (#B60000), the Passion of the evening — the mood of wanting something enough to move toward it. Theramore was that motion made into a city, and its destruction by a mana bomb is the hour's other half: passion is also what is left over when the thing wanted is taken away in an afternoon.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Love and the vice is Jealousy, and the myth splits them across one life rather than across two figures. After Theramore she came within a decision of drowning Orgrimmar, and she stopped — the only member of this cast to take the arm's vice all the way to the edge of an act and then set it down. Across the dial at 08h Malfurion's Patience is the named cure, and it is the exact medicine: what cannot be forgiven in a season can sometimes be outlasted across one.

[[The Hour]] *"Love is strong as death; jealousy is cruel as the grave: the coals thereof are coals of fire"* (Song of Solomon 8:6). The verse puts Friday's virtue and Friday's vice in a single sentence, and gives them the same temperature.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 20h arm in deep red (#B60000), the Passion of the evening — the base reading, wanting treated as a decision.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism keeps her at 20h and purifies the red to its light primary (#FF0000) — the reddest red there is, unmixed. In the light world Passion is a wavelength rather than a pigment, which suits a mage: what she does is never mixed, only aimed.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Jaina shifts to the 18h sunset arm in iron-blood crimson (#A02020), the estate of the Soldier, the Sword for its object — a seat she has never wanted and has twice been forced to hold. She is the cast's only member whose weapon is also her grief, which is what makes the sword the honest object for her rather than the mirror.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that sunset arm belongs to the Elder, the harvest of a life, and she deepens to ember (#FF6A3C). The fit is chronological as well as symbolic: she is younger than half this cast and has already buried a teacher, a father, a city and the man she meant to marry.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Jaina takes the 18h arm — Autumn, red, aimed at the autumnal equinox — sharing the spoke with Muradin. Two people who told Arthas the truth to his face and lost him anyway, seated together on the season that counts what a year actually produced.
variants.trio: Jaina does not move: the Trinity's Love arm is her own 20h in her own red. Muradin joins her, and the two guard the evening from 16h to 24h — the arm held by this cast's two proofs that loving someone and being able to save them are different facts.

saturn.name: Malfurion
saturn.base:
[[The Figure]] Malfurion Stormrage is Saturday's figure because he is the only member of this cast whose principal contribution is having waited. The first mortal druid, taught by Cenarius, he spent ten thousand years asleep in the Emerald Dream while the world he had saved forgot how it had been saved. Saturn's arm is the harvest and its long preparation; a discipline whose unit of time is the millennium belongs to no other seat.

[[On the Dial]] His home is the 08h arm in field green (#007E00), the Renewal of the morning. Druidism is renewal held as a profession rather than a hope: the Dream is a working copy of the world kept in reserve, and tending it is the least dramatic and most Saturnine labour in the Alliance.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Patience and the vice is Envy, and this seat's vice has a name inside his own family. Illidan is his twin, and everything Illidan did — the Well, the demon's gift, the second Well beneath Hyjal — was the same appetite this arm holds, taken without waiting. Malfurion is the brother who did not, and who then imprisoned the one who did. Across the dial at 20h Jaina's Love is the named cure: envy is a want with the other person left in it, and only love has ever removed that.

[[The Hour]] *"Be patient therefore, brethren... behold, the husbandman waiteth for the precious fruit of the earth, and hath long patience for it"* (James 5:7). The verse names the seat's profession and its virtue with one word, and the ten thousand years are only a difference of scale.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 08h arm in field green (#007E00), the Renewal of the morning — the base reading, renewal practised as a profession.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns his morning green to cyan (#00DDDD) — the color of the clear early sky rather than of the forest floor. Renewal keeps the hour; light names the Dream above the wood instead of the roots inside it.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Malfurion takes the dawn arm, 06h, in field green (#3E8914), the estate of the Farmer, the Plough for its object — the one estate whose whole method he actually practises. A farmer's authority comes from having been present for every season of the same ground, and nobody in this cast has been present for more of them.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the dawn arm is Birth, and he wears predawn mist (#8FA8C8) — earned rather than assigned. Druidism itself is born in him: he is the first, taught directly by a demigod, and every druid since is a descendant of one apprenticeship.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Malfurion moves to 06h — Spring, green, aimed at the vernal equinox — sharing the spoke with Anduin. The season of return held by the cast's two healers, one of bodies and one of everything a body is standing on.
variants.trio: The Trinity promotes him from the morning to the crown: the 12h Faith arm, yellow, shared with Uther, guarding the day's height from 8h to 16h. The reading is uncomfortable and correct — ten thousand years asleep is either faith or abdication, and only the outcome decides which.

sun.name: Varian Wrynn · Genn Greymane
sun.base:
[[The Figure]] Sunday's seat is held by two kings, and the argument is about what a crown is for rather than about good against evil. Varian Wrynn holds the bright face: a boy king, then a gladiator slave under an assumed name, then High King of an alliance that had to be argued into existing. Genn Greymane holds the dark one: a king who walled his nation off from that same alliance, lost it, and came back to serve the thing he had refused. Neither is a villain; they are the throne read from inside and from outside.

[[On the Dial]] The center holds no arm and no hour. White-gold is the sum of every hue the wheel can mix, and the six figures around it are that light taken apart — Serenity, Courage, Wisdom, Generosity, Love, Patience, one to each spoke. Varian is what the source looks like when nothing has yet been subtracted from it: an authority that was earned in a pit before it was ever conferred in a hall.

[[The Lesson]] The bundle gives the ruler face Justice against Pride and the servant face Humility against Servility. Varian's justice is the kind learned from underneath, which is also the source of his temper — a man who has been owned does not concede easily, and the Alliance's worst councils are the ones where that refusal is the loudest thing at the table. Genn's humility is the harder kind: he was right about the Forsaken and wrong about the wall, and he had to hold both facts at once for the rest of his life. Nothing sits opposite the center, so the two cure each other and nobody else.

[[The Hour]] *"Except the LORD keep the city, the watchman waketh but in vain"* (Psalm 127:1). The Sunday seat holds both offices at once — the crown that is worn and the wall that is kept — and this cast is the one that learned the hard way that a wall alone is not a policy.

variants.hexa_primary: On the painter's wheel Varian keeps the center of the dial, white-gold, belonging to no hour: the six arms around him are that light decomposed, one virtue to each spoke. This is the home reading — the source, not a spoke, an authority that precedes the offices it hands out.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism changes every arm around him and cannot change the center: white remains the sum of all wavelengths. It is the same fact from the other side — a High King is not a seventh member of the council, he is the thing the other six are readings of.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the pair steps onto the noon arm in royal gold (#F0C420), the estate of the King, the Crown for its object — the plainest seat in the set, and the only one this cast fills twice. One of them was crowned and then enslaved and then crowned again; the other was crowned, lost the country under the crown, and kept the title anyway.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the noon arm is Youth, the zenith of a life, and the pair wears sun-yellow (#FFE800) — apt for a throne this cast never lets get old. Varian dies at the height of his command and Genn outlives the country he was king of, so the seat holds a career's summit and its aftermath under one hue.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross the Sunday pair holds 12h on the Summer arm, yellow, aimed at the summer solstice — shared with Uther. The crown beside the order it authorised: the year's brightest spoke held by the two institutions this cast is actually made of.
variants.trio: On the Trinity the seat keeps the center and the cast around it narrows to three arms — Faith yellow, Love red, Hope blue. The geometry is indifferent to who holds it, which is the warning the dual exists to make: the same center seats the king who died covering a retreat and the king who built a wall and let a continent burn behind it.

faces.ruler:
Varian Wrynn is Sunday's bright face, and the argument for the seat is a biography no other Alliance figure can match: crowned as a child, abducted and sold, and made to fight for years in the pits under the name Lo'Gosh before anybody in Stormwind knew he was alive.

His virtue is Justice — an authority tested from underneath before it was ever exercised from above, and one that afterwards protected whoever was lowest in the room. Onyxia's magic once split him into two men, the diplomat and the fighter, and the reunion is the seat's own thesis: neither half was a king alone. The vice that stalks it is Pride, the refusal to concede that comes free with having been owned. His mood is Glory, noon's own triumph — the High King who spent his last order holding a line so that the rest of the army could get off the Broken Shore.
faces.servant:
Genn Greymane is Sunday's dark face — a king in his own right, seated here as the Servant because his whole later life is the office of serving a crown he once refused.

His virtue is Humility, and the argument is Gilneas: he built a wall against the world, kept his nation out of the Alliance, and then lost the country behind the wall to a curse and an invasion at once. Coming back to a table he had walked away from, with nothing left to offer but himself, is humility as a fact rather than a manner. The vice that stalks it is Servility — a man who has lost his own kingdom can become the crown's instrument instead of its counsel, and his pursuit of Sylvanas is where that line gets crossed. His mood is Awe: the worgen curse means he carries a second self he did not choose and cannot dismiss, and Glory is the same seat's other face.

moon.name: Baine
moon.base:
[[The Figure]] Baine Bloodhoof is Monday's figure because he inherited Thunder Bluff on the day his father was killed in a duel and did not answer it with a war. Cairne died by a poisoned axe and the tauren nation had every reason to burn Orgrimmar for it; Baine took back his own capital from Magatha Grimtotem, named the poisoner rather than the Warchief, and kept the Horde together. Serenity on this arm is not a temperament — it is a policy adopted under maximum provocation.

[[On the Dial]] His home is the 04h arm in deep blue (#002FFF), the hour the canon names Calm — the emptiest interval of the night. It is the hour of a chieftain who governs by stillness: Thunder Bluff's authority in this cast comes from being the one place where nobody raises their voice, and the whole later history of the Horde turns on it having stayed that way.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Serenity and the vice is Fear, and Baine's career is a running argument about which of them a quiet man is actually practising. He sheltered Jaina Proudmoore, his father's old enemy's ally, when the Horde would have killed her; he returned Derek Proudmoore's body to his family and was condemned to death by Sylvanas for it. Across the dial at 16h Grommash's Courage is the named cure, and it runs both ways: courage makes a stillness credible, and stillness is what keeps a courage from becoming a rampage.

[[The Hour]] *"But the meek shall inherit the earth; and shall delight themselves in the abundance of peace"* (Psalm 37:11). The verb is the seat's own: Baine did inherit, at the worst possible moment, and the abundance of peace is precisely what he chose to spend the inheritance on.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 04h arm in deep blue (#002FFF), the Calm of the hour before dawn — the base reading, stillness adopted as a method of government.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism keeps him at 04h and sharpens the blue to #0040FF — pigment's muted night becomes light's electric one. The hour and its Calm are unchanged; only the temperature of the quiet changes, from warm to deliberate.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Baine takes the deep-night arm in lamplit ink blue (#1F5FA8), the estate of the Scholar, the Book for its object — a fair trade for the one chieftain in this cast who argues rather than fights. His decisive interventions are all arguments made in rooms full of people who had already decided.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that deep-night arm is the Unborn, and he turns moonlight silver (#C8D7F0) — earned by what he keeps rather than by what he has done. The Horde Baine defends is a thing that does not exist yet and has never existed: the one Cairne was promised when he shook Thrall's hand.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Baine moves to the 06h arm — Spring, green, aimed at the vernal equinox — and shares it with Cairne. Father and son on the season of return, and the pairing is the cast's whole tauren argument: the same office held twice, deliberately the same way.
variants.trio: The Trinity keeps him at 04h and renames the watch: the blue arm now means Hope, shared with Gallywix, guarding the morning from 0h to 8h. The pairing is deliberately unflattering to both — one believes the Horde can be better than it is, and the other has priced that belief.

mars.name: Grommash Hellscream
mars.base:
[[The Figure]] Grommash Hellscream is Tuesday's figure because he is the only member of this cast who committed the seat's vice on behalf of an entire people and then paid the seat's virtue to undo it. He was the first orc to drink Mannoroth's blood at Hellfire, and the clans followed him into it; generations later he was the one who killed the pit lord and died doing it, ending the demon's hold on the orcs. Wrath and Courage are not two figures here, they are two halves of one biography.

[[On the Dial]] His home is the 16h arm in ember orange (#DC9600), the Zeal of the working afternoon — the hour the canon gives to continuing fire rather than to a first flare. The Warsong is the clan that never stood down, and the arm names exactly that: a heat that does not go out between battles and therefore has to be aimed at something or it aims itself.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Courage and the vice is Wrath, and the cure in this case had to be administered by the same hand that caused the disease. Nothing about the drink was forced on him — he took it as a way to keep fighting — and nothing about the killing was survivable, and he did that too. Across the dial at 04h Baine's Serenity is the named cure: a stillness that would have made the first bargain unnecessary is exactly what the Warsong never had.

[[The Hour]] *"It is not because things are difficult that we do not dare; it is because we do not dare that things are difficult"* (Seneca, Letters to Lucilius). The sentence is Tuesday's whole grammar, and Grommash's life is the case where the daring came first, went wrong, and had to be spent a second time to correct it.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 16h arm in ember orange (#DC9600), the Zeal of the working afternoon — the base reading, a fire that never goes out between battles.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism keeps him at 16h and burns the ember up to pure yellow (#FFFF00) — red and green fused. Light gives the same rage a hotter hue without giving it an object, which is the exact condition the blood pact was offered to solve.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Grommash takes the 15h afternoon in copper (#C87533), the estate of the Merchant, the Coin for its object — brutal and exact. The defining act of his life was a purchase: strength bought at a price he was told and accepted, and the second half of the story is the refund being fought for.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that afternoon arm is Maturity, and he wears amber (#FFB400). The irony is the point: he reaches full strength in the same decade he becomes least his own, and maturity only arrives on the day he chooses an ending that benefits nobody now alive except the clans.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Grommash takes the 18h arm — Autumn, red, aimed at the equinox — sharing the spoke with Draka. Two Frostwolf-era figures on the season of reckoning: one refused the blood and was murdered for it with her mate, the other drank it and spent the rest of the story paying.
variants.trio: The Trinity moves him to 20h, onto Love's red arm beside Draka, guarding the evening from 16h to 24h. The seat is an accusation and an acquittal at once: what he did at Ashenvale was done for people who would not know for years that it had been done.

mercury.name: Gallywix
mercury.base:
[[The Figure]] Trade Prince Gallywix is Wednesday's figure because he is the only member of the Horde who joined it as a business decision. Mercury's arm holds Wisdom and Greed together — the Merchant's own pair — and Gallywix is the case that proves they are one faculty rather than two: he is never wrong about a price, and he has never once found a price he would not accept. When Kezan burned he sold his own people their passage off the island and indentured them for the fare.

[[On the Dial]] His home is the midnight arm at 0h in Tyrian purple (#542E85), the mood the canon calls Sorrow — the day's ledger closed and read. It is the goblin hour by construction. A ledger is the only instrument in this cast that tells the truth about a war, and Gallywix is the one member who reads it every night without flinching and without concluding anything.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Wisdom and the vice is Greed, and the Trade Prince is the hinge. His judgement is genuine and his pricing is not: what he sells is never the goods, it is the leverage that comes from being the only party who knows what the goods are worth. The Horde kept him because a war needs a quartermaster, and expelled him when the accounting finally caught up. Across the dial at 12h Vol'jin's Generosity is the named cure: what is given away cannot be priced, and therefore cannot be leveraged.

[[The Hour]] *"For the love of money is the root of all evil: which while some coveted after, they have erred from the faith"* (1 Timothy 6:10). Wednesday's discipline is the clause everybody forgets — the verse does not condemn the money, it condemns the affection, which is the only part a goblin would even recognise as his own.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the midnight arm at 0h in Tyrian purple (#542E85), the Sorrow of the closed ledger — the base reading, an account read nightly and never once acted on.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns his purple to magenta (#BD00BD) — the one hue found in no rainbow, a color the eye invents where the spectrum's two ends meet. Fitting for a trade prince: the value he sells exists nowhere in the goods, only in the gap between what two parties know.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Gallywix shifts to the 21h evening arm in stage-velvet violet (#7A2E8E), the estate of the Artist, the Mask for its object — an unlikely trade for a trade prince until his actual method is weighed. Nothing he sells is the goods; what he sells is a performance of scarcity, priced for an audience that cannot see the inventory.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that evening arm is Old Age, and he wears dusk violet (#9C6BD4) — read as an accusation rather than a compliment. He is fully formed, entirely competent, and has never grown past the single appetite he started with, which is what a long life looks like when nothing else in a person develops.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Gallywix keeps the bottom arm at 0h — Winter, blue, aimed at the winter solstice — and he alone shares it with no one. The year's midnight belongs to a single figure, and this cast has only one whose work is done entirely in private with a book of figures.
variants.trio: The Trinity lifts him off midnight to 04h, onto Hope's blue arm beside Baine, guarding the morning from 0h to 8h. The seat is the harshest reading in the cast and the most honest: credit is hope with a rate attached, and Gallywix has never lent to anyone he did not believe would pay.

jupiter.name: Vol'jin
jupiter.base:
[[The Figure]] Vol'jin is Thursday's figure because he gave the Horde back to itself and then gave away the throne as well. The Darkspear chieftain whose people were homeless until Thrall took them in, he repaid it by telling Garrosh to his face that a Warchief who rules by fear is finished — and took a blade for the sentence. He came back, raised the Darkspear Rebellion, deposed Garrosh, was made Warchief by acclamation, and named a successor with his last words rather than an heir.

[[On the Dial]] His home is the top arm at 12h in noon yellow (#F8E600), the Joy of the day's peak. Jupiter's arm is the priest who distributes rather than the king who collects, and Vol'jin holds it as a shadow hunter: the loa's power is borrowed by definition, never owned, and a man who spends a borrowed abundance on other people's survival is the arm's plainest tenant.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Generosity and the vice is Excess, and Thursday is the one seat where the vice is the virtue's own overshoot rather than its opposite. He gave the rebellion everything and gave the office away the moment it was his; naming Sylvanas his successor is generosity practised past the point where judgement could still correct it, and the Horde paid for that gift for years. Across the dial at 0h Gallywix's Wisdom is the named cure: a price asked in advance is what a gift needs and what this one did not get.

[[The Hour]] *"It is more blessed to give than to receive"* (Acts 20:35). Thursday's seat holds the sentence and its cost in the same life — the blessing is real, and so is the fact that a gift made without measure is still a decision somebody else has to live inside.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the top arm at 12h in noon yellow (#F8E600), the Joy of the day's peak — the base reading, an abundance borrowed and handed straight on.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns his noon to green (#00DC00) — the wavelength at the summit of human sight. Apt for a shadow hunter: what the loa lend is measured by what grows out of it afterwards, and the Darkspear are the only thing he ever kept.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Vol'jin holds the 09h morning arm in alb ivory (#EDEDE0), the estate of the Priest, the Bell for its object — the trade needs no argument. He is a priest by office as well as by nature, and the bell is a summons rather than a possession, which is exactly what a rebellion called in a Warchief's own capital amounts to.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that morning arm is Childhood, and he wears spring green (#7CE577) — read as the Horde's age rather than his own. The nation he hands to Sylvanas is barely a generation old and has already been ruled by three different arguments about what it is for.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Vol'jin holds 12h on the Summer arm, yellow, aimed at the solstice — sharing the spoke with Thrall and Garrosh. The year's brightest hour held by all three Warchiefs this cast produced, which is also the whole history of the Horde on one spoke.
variants.trio: On the Trinity Vol'jin keeps the top arm at 12h, yellow, where the color now means Faith, shared with Cairne as they guard the day's height from 8h to 16h. The pairing is exact: both of them backed the Horde's better argument before there was any evidence for it, and one of them was killed for the wager.

venus.name: Draka
venus.base:
[[The Figure]] Draka is Friday's figure because hers is the cast's one love argued entirely as a decision. Born frail in a people that had no use for frailty, she took a rite meant to kill her and came back from it; she then chose Durotan, and the choice cost her the clan's whole future twice — first into exile when the Frostwolves refused the demon's blood, and then into an ambush that killed them both. What she leaves behind is Thrall, which is to say the Horde this cast is actually about.

[[On the Dial]] Her home is the 20h arm in deep red (#B60000), the Passion of the evening — the mood of wanting something enough to move toward it. Exile is that motion in its most expensive form: the Frostwolves walked away from the entire orc project on the strength of a judgement about what their children would be, and Friday is the hour where a want becomes an act.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Love and the vice is Jealousy, and the arm holds both because they share a motion. A love that guards can curdle into a love that will not share, and the Frostwolf refusal is exactly one degree away from the clannishness the orcs are otherwise ruined by. Draka's answer is that she guarded a principle rather than a possession. Across the dial at 08h Cairne's Patience is the named cure: what cannot be protected in one generation can sometimes be handed to the next.

[[The Hour]] *"Many waters cannot quench love, neither can the floods drown it"* (Song of Solomon 8:7). The verse is Friday's own boast, and this seat is where the cast tests it: the two of them were killed, the clan was scattered, the child was raised by the enemy — and the thing survived anyway.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 20h arm in deep red (#B60000), the Passion of the evening — the base reading, love as a decision with a printed cost.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism keeps her at 20h and purifies the red to its light primary (#FF0000) — the reddest red there is, unmixed. Fitting for the one figure of this cast whose choice was never diluted by a second consideration.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Draka shifts to the 18h sunset arm in iron-blood crimson (#A02020), the estate of the Soldier, the Sword for its object — earned on the plainest facts available. She was an exile who fought as an exile, with no army, no hold and no prospect of relief, which is the estate at its least ceremonial.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that sunset arm belongs to the Elder, the harvest of a life, and she deepens to ember (#FF6A3C). She does not live to be old, which is why the seat is hers: the harvest of her life is a person rather than a span, and it was gathered by somebody else.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Draka takes the 18h arm — Autumn, red, aimed at the autumnal equinox — sharing the spoke with Grommash. The two answers to the same offer, seated together on the season that counts what a year produced: one clan refused the blood, one drank it, and both paid.
variants.trio: Draka does not move: the Trinity's Love arm is her own 20h in her own red. Grommash joins her, and the two guard the evening from 16h to 24h — the arm held by the cast's two proofs that the orcs' worst decision and their best one were made by people who loved the same thing.

saturn.name: Cairne
saturn.base:
[[The Figure]] Cairne Bloodhoof is Saturday's figure because his whole contribution is a wager settled slowly. He took Thrall's hand when the orcs were strangers with a bad reputation and the tauren had no reason on earth to trust them; from that handshake came Thunder Bluff, the alliance that saved both peoples at Hyjal, and the moral case the new Horde has ever since been trying to live up to. Saturn's arm is the harvest, and a harvest is the one thing that cannot be produced quickly.

[[On the Dial]] His home is the 08h arm in field green (#007E00), the Renewal of the morning. The tauren are this cast's agricultural argument in every sense: the plains, the herd, the long view, and a chieftain whose authority comes from having outlasted the question rather than from having answered it loudly.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Patience and the vice is Envy, and Cairne's death is the seat's own cautionary half. He challenged Garrosh to a rite of single combat and lost to a poisoned blade — patience destroyed by an impatience that was not even his opponent's but Magatha's, a third party's envy inserted into somebody else's duel. Across the dial at 20h Draka's Love is the named cure: envy is a want with another person still inside it, and only love has ever removed that.

[[The Hour]] *"In your patience possess ye your souls"* (Luke 21:19). Saturday's seat reads the verb literally — patience on this arm is not endurance but ownership, and Cairne is the one member of the cast who is never at any point somebody else's instrument.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 08h arm in field green (#007E00), the Renewal of the morning — the base reading, a wager settled across a generation.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns his morning green to cyan (#00DDDD) — the color of the clear early sky rather than of the plain. Renewal keeps the hour; light names the long horizon the herd is walking toward instead of the grass it is walking on.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Cairne takes the dawn arm, 06h, in field green (#3E8914), the estate of the Farmer, the Plough for its object — the one estate whose entire method is his. A farmer's authority is having been present for every season of the same ground, and Thunder Bluff is a settlement built by somebody who intended to be buried there.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the dawn arm is Birth, and he wears predawn mist (#8FA8C8) — earned literally. Everything this cast calls the Horde was born out of the handshake he offered, and he is the only figure here whose decisive act happened before the nation existed.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Cairne moves to 06h — Spring, green, aimed at the vernal equinox — sharing the spoke with Baine. Father and son on the season of return: the same office, the same method, and the second one inheriting on the worst possible day.
variants.trio: The Trinity promotes him from the morning to the crown: the 12h Faith arm, yellow, shared with Vol'jin, guarding the day's height from 8h to 16h. The reading is exact — his handshake with Thrall was made on no evidence whatsoever, which is the definition the arm carries.

sun.name: Thrall · Garrosh
sun.base:
[[The Figure]] Sunday's seat is held by a Warchief and the successor he chose, which makes this the one dual in the cast that a single man is responsible for. Thrall holds the bright face: born in captivity, raised as a gladiator by the man who owned him, and the author of an entire nation afterwards. Garrosh holds the dark one: Grommash's son, found on a distant world, elevated by Thrall's own hand, and the ruin of everything the elevation was meant to secure.

[[On the Dial]] The center holds no arm and no hour. White-gold is the sum of every hue the wheel can mix, and the six figures around it are that light taken apart — Serenity, Courage, Wisdom, Generosity, Love, Patience, one to each spoke. Thrall is what the source looks like before anything is subtracted: a shaman rather than a general, whose authority is the only one in the cast that was never inherited from anybody.

[[The Lesson]] The bundle gives the ruler face Justice against Pride and the servant face Humility against Servility. Thrall's justice is that he built rather than conquered, and his pride is the belief that he could name who came next — the one act of his life he could not undo by returning to fix it. Garrosh's servility is the obedience of a man who spent his whole youth serving a name: he ruled in the shape of his father's legend and made an entire nation serve it with him. Nothing sits opposite the center, so the two cure each other and nobody else.

[[The Hour]] *"Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall therein"* (Proverbs 26:27). The Sunday seat holds both offices at once, and this cast is the one where the throne's shadow was appointed to it in writing by the throne itself.

variants.hexa_primary: On the painter's wheel Thrall keeps the center of the dial, white-gold, belonging to no hour: the six arms around him are that light decomposed, one virtue to each spoke. This is the home reading — the source, not a spoke, an authority that had no predecessor to inherit from.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism changes every arm around him and cannot change the center: white remains the sum of all wavelengths. The same fact from the other side — a Warchief who is also a shaman is not a seventh member of the council, he is the thing the other six are readings of.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the pair steps onto the noon arm in royal gold (#F0C420), the estate of the King, the Crown for its object — and this cast's version of the seat is the sharpest in the book. One of them was a slave who became a king and then resigned; the other was handed a crown he had not asked for and could not put down.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the noon arm is Youth, the zenith of a life, and the pair wears sun-yellow (#FFE800). It is the exact word for both: Thrall frees his people while still a young man, and Garrosh is given a nation before he has ever governed anything, so the seat holds a summit reached early twice over.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross the Sunday pair holds 12h on the Summer arm, yellow, aimed at the summer solstice — shared with Vol'jin. All three Warchiefs on the year's brightest spoke: the one who built it, the one who broke it, and the one who took it back.
variants.trio: On the Trinity the seat keeps the center and the cast around it narrows to three arms — Faith yellow, Love red, Hope blue. The geometry is indifferent to who holds it, which is the warning the dual exists to make: the same center seats the Warchief who gave the orcs a country and the Warchief who spent it.

faces.ruler:
Thrall is Sunday's bright face, and the argument for the seat is that no other figure in this cast made anything from nothing. He was born the year his parents were murdered, raised in a cage by the man who found him, and taught to fight for an audience before he was taught anything else.

His virtue is Justice — an authority tested from underneath before it was ever exercised from above, and one that afterwards protected whoever was lowest. What he built was a country with borders, a capital and an argument, rather than the raiding confederation the Horde had been. The vice that stalks the seat is Pride, and his is specific and expensive: the conviction that he could see far enough to appoint the future. His mood is Glory — the day the orcs stopped being somebody's army and became somebody's nation.
faces.servant:
Garrosh Hellscream is Sunday's dark face, and the reason he belongs on this seat rather than in the Evil cast is that Thrall put him there. He was found on a distant world, ashamed of a father he had been told was a traitor, and raised to the Warchief's seat by the man whose whole legacy he then dismantled.

His virtue is Humility in the same way a shadow is a shape: it is the thing he is defined by lacking, and the seat holds him precisely because a throne without it is what this arm exists to describe. The vice is Servility, and his version is the unexpected one — not the servility of a subject but of a son. He served a name for his whole life, ruled in the outline of Grommash's legend, and required a nation to serve it with him. His mood is Awe: the Horde under Garrosh was genuinely terrifying, which is the effect he mistook for respect, and Glory is the same seat's other face.

moon.name: Kel'Thuzad
moon.base:
[[The Figure]] Kel'Thuzad is Monday's figure because the Scourge's plague is fear turned into an industry. An archmage of the Kirin Tor, expelled from the Council of Six for pursuing necromancy, he went north and offered himself to the Lich King rather than be argued with any further. What he then built was not an army but a recruitment method: the Cult of the Damned sold eternal life to frightened people, and the plague reached Lordaeron through grain the villages accepted willingly.

[[On the Dial]] His home is the 04h arm in deep blue (#002FFF), the hour the canon names Calm — the emptiest interval of the night, when nothing has happened yet and everything still might. Undeath is that interval made permanent. A lich is not at peace; a lich has simply had every faculty removed that could produce anything else, which is the seat's virtue counterfeited exactly.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Serenity and the vice is Fear, and this arm's occupant runs the second as a business against the first. What the cult offered was the end of dying, which is the only fear it is impossible to argue somebody out of, and the price was the capacity to feel anything about it afterwards. Across the dial at 16h Mannoroth's arm names Courage as the cure, and the pairing is honest: courage is fear with a decision attached, and the Scourge's whole method is removing the decision.

[[The Hour]] *"The last enemy that shall be destroyed is death"* (1 Corinthians 15:26). Monday's seat is where this cast reads that sentence backwards: Kel'Thuzad did defeat death, on the only terms available, and the result is the argument for why the promise was never his to make.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 04h arm in deep blue (#002FFF), the Calm of the hour before dawn — the base reading, stillness as the absence of anything left to disturb.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism keeps him at 04h and sharpens the blue to #0040FF — pigment's muted night becomes light's electric one. The hour and its Calm are unchanged; the cold simply stops pretending to be restfulness.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Kel'Thuzad takes the deep-night arm in lamplit ink blue (#1F5FA8), the estate of the Scholar, the Book for its object — the seat he actually held before he lost it. He was expelled from a council of scholars for reading the wrong thing, and every horror he built afterwards was research he was refused permission to publish.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that deep-night arm is the Unborn, and he turns moonlight silver (#C8D7F0) — the wheel's one seat for the not-yet-living, held by the figure who put a whole kingdom into that category. The Scourge is not the dead; it is people kept permanently short of being alive.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Kel'Thuzad moves to the 06h arm — Spring, green, aimed at the vernal equinox — and shares it with Deathwing. The season of regrowth held by this cast's two specialists in the counterfeit of it: one raises what should have stayed down, the other cracks open the ground it was lying in.
variants.trio: The Trinity keeps him at 04h and renames the watch: the blue arm now means Hope, shared with Gul'dan, guarding the morning from 0h to 8h. The assignment is deliberately hard — what the cult sold was hope, correctly identified and honestly delivered, and that is the whole horror of it.

mars.name: Mannoroth
mars.base:
[[The Figure]] Mannoroth is Tuesday's figure because he is the transaction in which courage was traded for wrath. The pit lord did not conquer the orcs; he offered them a drink, and the clans that accepted it doubled in strength and stopped being able to choose anything afterwards. Every atrocity of the First and Second Wars descends from a bargain that looked, at the moment of signing, like the most decisive thing a warrior could do.

[[On the Dial]] His home is the 16h arm in ember orange (#DC9600), the Zeal of the working afternoon — the hour the canon gives to banked, continuing fire. Demonic wrath is the arm's own vice at industrial scale: not an outburst but a supply, maintained indefinitely and issued to whoever will take delivery.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Courage and the vice is Wrath, and this seat is the cast's proof that the two are not degrees of one thing. What the blood gave was fury without limit; what it removed was the capacity to be afraid, and with it the capacity to be brave, since courage is defined against a fear that has to still be present. Grommash killed him and died of it, which is the same lesson from the other side. Across the dial at 04h Kel'Thuzad's arm names Serenity as the cure: the stillness in which an offer can be declined.

[[The Hour]] *"Wrath is cruel, and anger is outrageous; but who is able to stand before envy?"* (Proverbs 27:4). The verse ranks the vices, and Tuesday's seat is where this cast learns the ranking is about durability rather than damage: wrath burns out, and what Mannoroth sold was a wrath that could not.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 16h arm in ember orange (#DC9600), the Zeal of the working afternoon — the base reading, fury supplied rather than felt.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism keeps him at 16h and burns the ember up to pure yellow (#FFFF00) — red and green fused. Light gives the same rage a hotter hue without giving it an end, which is precisely the product on offer.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Mannoroth takes the 15h afternoon in copper (#C87533), the estate of the Merchant, the Coin for its object — the truest trade in this cast and the ugliest. He is not a warrior at all in the story that matters; he is a vendor, and the terms were disclosed, accepted and honoured on both sides.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that afternoon arm is Maturity, and he wears amber (#FFB400) — apt for a being whose entire function is finished on the day of the sale. Nothing about him develops afterwards; he is a completed instrument waiting for the next buyer, which is maturity with nothing left to mature into.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Mannoroth takes the 18h arm — Autumn, red, aimed at the equinox — sharing the spoke with Sylvanas. Two figures whose defining moment is somebody else's conversion, seated on the season that counts what a year actually produced.
variants.trio: The Trinity moves him to 20h, onto Love's red arm beside Sylvanas, guarding the evening from 16h to 24h. The seat is an accusation rather than a promotion: what the blood pact imitated was devotion, and the clans that drank it believed they were giving themselves to something.

mercury.name: Gul'dan
mercury.base:
[[The Figure]] Gul'dan is Wednesday's figure because he is the clearest case in the book of knowledge purchased with other people. A shaman who could no longer hear the elements, he took Kil'jaeden's offer instead, founded the Shadow Council to run the orcs from behind their own chieftains, brokered the blood pact, and opened the Dark Portal. Mercury's arm holds Wisdom and Greed together, and no figure in this cast makes the pairing cheaper to demonstrate: everything he knew was correct, and every price he paid was somebody else's.

[[On the Dial]] His home is the midnight arm at 0h in Tyrian purple (#542E85), the mood the canon calls Sorrow — the day's ledger closed and read. It is the warlock's own hour. Fel magic is an accounting system before it is a power: every effect is drawn from a store that belongs to someone, and Gul'dan is the one member of this cast who always knew exactly whose.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Wisdom and the vice is Greed, and the distinction the seat insists on is that Greed is not an appetite for goods but for leverage. He never wanted a throne — he wanted to be the only party in the room who understood the terms, which is why he governed through chieftains rather than instead of them. Across the dial at 12h Kil'jaeden's arm names Generosity as the cure, and the irony is deliberate: his own master out-gave him and thereby owned him.

[[The Hour]] *"For what shall it profit a man, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul?"* (Mark 8:36). Wednesday's seat is where the question stops being rhetorical: Gul'dan answered it out loud, in favour of the world, and was the only one at the table who had done the arithmetic first.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the midnight arm at 0h in Tyrian purple (#542E85), the Sorrow of the closed ledger — the base reading, power drawn from an account that belongs to someone.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns his purple to magenta (#BD00BD) — the one hue found in no rainbow, a color the eye invents where the spectrum's two ends meet. Fitting for a warlock: fel is not a found power but a manufactured one, assembled in the gap between two things that were never meant to touch.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Gul'dan shifts to the 21h evening arm in stage-velvet violet (#7A2E8E), the estate of the Artist, the Mask for its object — the exact instrument of his career. The Shadow Council was a mask worn by an entire government, and the orcs spent a generation obeying chieftains who were repeating lines.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that evening arm is Old Age, and he wears dusk violet (#9C6BD4) — earned by method rather than by years. He is the only figure in this cast who never once expected to be the strongest thing in the room and arranged his whole life around not needing to be.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Gul'dan keeps the bottom arm at 0h — Winter, blue, aimed at the winter solstice — and he alone shares it with no one. The year's midnight belongs to a single figure, and this cast has only one whose real work was done in a room nobody knew existed.
variants.trio: The Trinity lifts him off midnight to 04h, onto Hope's blue arm beside Kel'Thuzad, guarding the morning from 0h to 8h. The reading is the harshest available and the most accurate: what he sold the clans was a future, and they had already run out of other offers.

jupiter.name: Kil'jaeden the Deceiver
jupiter.base:
[[The Figure]] Kil'jaeden is Thursday's figure because every gift he makes is real and every one of them has a hook already set. He and Archimonde accepted Sargeras's offer on Argus while Velen refused it and fled; what the eredar were promised was power, and they received it exactly as described. His entire subsequent career is the same transaction repeated at every scale — Ner'zhul raised into the Lich King, Gul'dan given fel, the Legion assembled one honoured bargain at a time.

[[On the Dial]] His home is the top arm at 12h in noon yellow (#F8E600), the Joy of the day's peak, and the placement is not ironic. Jupiter's arm is abundance and the office that distributes it, and Kil'jaeden distributes more than anybody else in this cast. The seat's danger has never been scarcity; it is that the hour with the most to give is also the only hour where a gift can be used as an instrument.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Generosity and the vice is Excess, and this is the seat where the cast argues that Excess is not over-eating but over-promising. Nothing he offers is a lie; the defect is that there is always more of it than the recipient can assess, and the surplus is where the obligation hides. Across the dial at 0h Gul'dan's arm names Wisdom as the cure — measure, applied before the gift is accepted rather than after, which is the one step his own best pupil skipped.

[[The Hour]] *"Beware of false prophets, which come to you in sheep's clothing, but inwardly they are ravening wolves"* (Matthew 7:15). Thursday's seat sharpens the warning: the difficulty was never that the offer looked false. It looked, and was, entirely genuine.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the top arm at 12h in noon yellow (#F8E600), the Joy of the day's peak — the base reading, abundance issued as an instrument.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns his noon to green (#00DC00) — the wavelength at the summit of human sight. Apt for the Legion's recruiter: what he plants grows, reliably and forever, and none of it was ever intended to be his to harvest.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Kil'jaeden holds the 09h morning arm in alb ivory (#EDEDE0), the estate of the Priest, the Bell for its object — the most uncomfortable trade in the whole book, and the exact one. He performs a priest's function without exception: he arrives where hope has failed, offers a doctrine, and asks for everything.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that morning arm is Childhood, and he wears spring green (#7CE577) — read as the condition he requires rather than the age he is. Every bargain he has ever closed depended on the other party being new to the terms, and the Legion recruits nowhere else.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Kil'jaeden holds 12h on the Summer arm, yellow, aimed at the solstice — sharing the spoke with Arthas and Illidan. The year's brightest hour held by the maker and by two of his best-known products, which is the cast's own family tree on a single spoke.
variants.trio: On the Trinity he keeps the top arm at 12h, yellow, where the color now means Faith, shared with Deathwing as they guard the day's height from 8h to 16h. The pairing is exact and merciless: both are figures whose whole power came from somebody agreeing to believe them first.

venus.name: Sylvanas
venus.base:
[[The Figure]] Sylvanas Windrunner is Friday's figure because her defining motive is not hatred of the living but the loss of having been one. Ranger-General of Silvermoon, she fought Arthas's advance down the Dead Scar and lost; he killed her deliberately and raised her as the first banshee specifically so that she would have to watch her own kingdom fall while serving the thing that took it. Everything afterwards — the Forsaken, the plague works, the war — is a life reconstructed around an absence.

[[On the Dial]] Her home is the 20h arm in deep red (#B60000), the Passion of the evening — the mood of wanting something enough to move toward it. The Banshee Queen is never once inert; every act of hers is a movement toward something she has already been told she cannot have, which is the arm's own definition rather than its exception.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Love and the vice is Jealousy, and this seat holds only the second — but it holds it in the exact shape of the first. Jealousy is love pointed at a thing that belongs to somebody else, and what belongs to somebody else here is being alive. Across the dial at 08h Deathwing's arm names Patience as the cure, and in this cast the cure is refused by both parties: neither the banshee nor the Aspect can tolerate the idea that a wrong might be outlasted rather than answered.

[[The Hour]] *"Hope deferred maketh the heart sick: but when the desire cometh, it is a tree of life"* (Proverbs 13:12). Friday's seat is where the second clause is unavailable, and the whole argument of the arm is what a person does with the first clause once that is established.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 20h arm in deep red (#B60000), the Passion of the evening — the base reading, a life rebuilt around what it no longer has.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism keeps her at 20h and purifies the red to its light primary (#FF0000) — the reddest red there is, unmixed. Fitting for a figure whose motive has never once been diluted by a second consideration in the whole story.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Sylvanas shifts to the 18h sunset arm in iron-blood crimson (#A02020), the estate of the Soldier, the Sword for its object — the estate she actually held. She was a general before she was anything else, and she has never once stopped commanding, which is why the Forsaken function at all.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that sunset arm belongs to the Elder, the harvest of a life, and she deepens to ember (#FF6A3C). The fit is bitter and exact: she is the only figure of this cast whose harvest was taken by somebody else on a date she can name.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Sylvanas takes the 18h arm — Autumn, red, aimed at the autumnal equinox — sharing the spoke with Mannoroth. Two figures who exist as somebody's conversion: one performed it wholesale on a people, and one had it performed on her by name.
variants.trio: Sylvanas does not move: the Trinity's Love arm is her own 20h in her own red.
