Mannoroth joins her, and the two guard the evening from 16h to 24h — the arm held by this cast's two proofs that the machinery of devotion works exactly as well when it is installed against a person's will.

saturn.name: Deathwing
saturn.base:
[[The Figure]] Deathwing is Saturday's figure because the Earth-Warder is this seat's own office corrupted. Neltharion was given dominion over the world's soil and stone by the titans themselves — the Aspect whose entire charge was the ground everything else grows in. The Old Gods whispered him into forging the Dragon Soul, he turned it on the other Aspects at the Well of Eternity, and the Cataclysm eventually split open the world he had been made to keep.

[[On the Dial]] His home is the 08h arm in field green (#007E00), the Renewal of the morning, and the placement is the cast's sharpest single argument. Renewal is the seat's promise and the Earth-Warder was its custodian; the arm is not being ironic, it is naming what was lost. There is no other seat on this wheel that a Dragon Aspect of the earth could occupy.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Patience and the vice is Envy, and green holds both because they are two answers to the same wait. Patience is a custodian's discipline — the ground repays only whoever leaves it alone long enough. Envy is what that same custodian becomes when the waiting stops being tolerable, and the Old Gods' entire method was to make it intolerable, one whisper at a time, for centuries. Across the dial at 20h Sylvanas's arm names Love as the cure: envy is a want with somebody else still inside it.

[[The Hour]] *"For where envying and strife is, there is confusion and every evil work"* (James 3:16). Saturday's seat reads the first noun as a cause rather than a symptom, which is exactly what the Cataclysm was: not an attack but a confusion, the world's own keeper rearranging it past the point of use.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 08h arm in field green (#007E00), the Renewal of the morning — the base reading, the custodian's own hour held by the custodian who broke it.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns his morning green to cyan (#00DDDD) — the color of the clear early sky rather than of the field. Renewal keeps the hour; light names the air above the ground instead of the ground, which is the one part of the world he was never given.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Deathwing takes the dawn arm, 06h, in field green (#3E8914), the estate of the Farmer, the Plough for its object — the estate he was literally appointed to. A plough opens the ground in order to plant, and the Cataclysm is the same instrument used by somebody who had stopped intending to sow anything.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the dawn arm is Birth, and he wears predawn mist (#8FA8C8) — earned by office rather than by age. He is one of the five who were present when the world was ordered, and everything on this dial that grows was, at one time, in his charge.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Deathwing moves to 06h — Spring, green, aimed at the vernal equinox — sharing the spoke with Kel'Thuzad. The season of return held by the cast's two counterfeiters of it: one raises the dead, the other reopens the ground.
variants.trio: The Trinity promotes him from the morning to the crown: the 12h Faith arm, yellow, shared with Kil'jaeden, guarding the day's height from 8h to 16h. The reading is uncomfortable and correct — an Aspect is an office held on trust, and this is the one figure in the book who was trusted by the titans themselves.

sun.name: Arthas · Illidan
sun.base:
[[The Figure]] Sunday's seat is held by two figures who took a terrible instrument in order to win with it, which makes this the one dual in the book whose faces committed the same error twice. Arthas Menethil holds the bright face: a crown prince who purged his own city because the grain was already plagued, then went north for a blade that would let him finish what he had started. Illidan Stormrage holds the dark one: a night elf who accepted Sargeras's own gift in order to hunt demons, and was imprisoned for ten thousand years by his own brother for it.

[[On the Dial]] The center holds no arm and no hour. White-gold is the sum of every hue the wheel can mix, and the six figures around it are that light taken apart. Arthas is what the source looks like when everything has been subtracted from it and the shape is still there: the Lich King rules, holds a throne, commands absolutely, and has nothing whatever left to rule for.

[[The Lesson]] The bundle gives the ruler face Justice against Pride and the servant face Humility against Servility. Arthas at Stratholme is a justice argument and not a madness one — he was not wrong about the grain, and he was wrong about everything that followed from being right. His pride is the specific conviction that no one else could carry it. Illidan's servility is the reverse error: he took every weapon anybody offered — Sargeras's gift, Kil'jaeden's orders, a summons he could not refuse — and called the sequence his own will. Nothing sits opposite the center, so the two cure each other and nobody else.

[[The Hour]] *"There is a way which seemeth right unto a man, but the end thereof are the ways of death"* (Proverbs 14:12). The Sunday seat holds both offices at once, and this cast is the one where both faces were, at the moment of choosing, entirely convinced they were the only person willing to do what was necessary.

variants.hexa_primary: On the painter's wheel Arthas keeps the center of the dial, white-gold, belonging to no hour: the six arms around him are that light decomposed, one virtue to each spoke. This is the home reading — the source rather than a spoke, and the coldest center this instrument has.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism changes every arm around him and cannot change the center: white remains the sum of all wavelengths. The same fact from the other side — the Frozen Throne is not a seventh power in this cast, it is the thing the other six are readings of.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the pair steps onto the noon arm in royal gold (#F0C420), the estate of the King, the Crown for its object — and this cast holds the seat with two figures who were never crowned by anybody. One took a throne by sitting in it, the other declared himself a lord of a realm he had conquered on his own account.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the noon arm is Youth, the zenith of a life, and the pair wears sun-yellow (#FFE800). It is precise rather than flattering: both of them made the decisive choice young, with a whole career still in front of them, and neither ever reached a second decision of comparable size.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross the Sunday pair holds 12h on the Summer arm, yellow, aimed at the summer solstice — shared with Kil'jaeden. The maker beside his two best-known products, on the year's brightest spoke: neither of them was ever anything he did not first supply.
variants.trio: On the Trinity the seat keeps the center and the cast around it narrows to three arms — Faith yellow, Love red, Hope blue. The geometry is indifferent to who holds it, which is the warning the dual exists to make: the same center seats a prince who wanted to save his people and a hunter who wanted to save his world.

faces.ruler:
Arthas Menethil is Sunday's bright face, and the seat is his because he began as the argument for it. Crown prince of Lordaeron, trained by Uther, taught the axe by Muradin, he was the Alliance's best case for what an inherited throne could produce.

His virtue is Justice, and it is genuinely present at Stratholme: the grain was plagued, the city was already lost, and no other person in the room was willing to say so. What the seat then demonstrates is that Justice with nothing above it becomes the vice that stalks it. Pride here is exact — not vanity, but the conviction that he alone could be trusted with the decision, which is what carried him to Frostmourne and eventually to the Frozen Throne, where he killed his own father and merged with the being that had been steering him. His mood is Glory: an absolute command, held at the top of the world, over a kingdom with nothing alive in it.
faces.servant:
Illidan Stormrage is Sunday's dark face, and the case for him here is that he made the same trade as the Ruler and was punished for it by his own family rather than crowned for it.

His virtue is Humility in the form the seat actually recognises — the acceptance of being useful rather than admired. He fought the Legion for ten thousand years with no office, no army of his own worth the name, and the settled hatred of everybody he was fighting for. The vice that stalks it is Servility, and it is the sharper charge: he accepted a weapon from Sargeras, orders from Kil'jaeden, and a summons from the Lich King, and each time he called the arrangement his own choice. An obedience that insists on being called freedom is the arm's own definition. His mood is Awe — the demon hunter who became indistinguishable from the thing hunted — and Glory is the same seat's other face.

moon.name: Aldecaldos · Mox
moon.base:
[[The Figure]] Monday's seat is held by the two collectives in Night City that exist to keep people safe rather than to take ground from anybody. The Aldecaldos are a nomad family: a clan that works the Badlands, circles its vehicles at night and treats the ring as the whole of its politics. The Mox were founded in 2076 by the workers of Lizzie's Bar after the woman who ran it was killed by a client, for the single purpose of making sure it did not happen to the next one. Serenity on this arm is never a temperament; it is a peace somebody is standing guard over.

[[On the Dial]] Their home is the 04h arm in deep blue (#002FFF), the hour the canon names Calm — the emptiest interval of the night, and the one that has to be held for anyone to sleep through it. Both members are night institutions: a convoy that posts a watch, and a bar that keeps its own door.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Serenity and the vice is Fear, and this seat is the argument that the two are one material differently spent. The Aldecaldos' calm is a working calm, produced every night by people who assume a raid is possible; the Mox exist because somebody's fear was correct and nobody answered it in time. Across the dial at 16h Tuesday's Courage is the named cure, and it runs both ways: without courage this quiet is only a hiding place, and without the quiet the courage has nothing left to protect.

[[The Hour]] *"I will both lay me down in peace, and sleep: for thou, LORD, only makest me dwell in safety"* (Psalm 4:8). The verse names the seat exactly — the peace belongs to the sleeper, and the safety is somebody else's night shift.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 04h arm in deep blue (#002FFF), the Calm of the hour before dawn — the base reading, a quiet that somebody is posted to keep.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism keeps the seat at 04h and sharpens the blue to #0040FF — pigment's muted night becomes light's electric one. The hour and its Calm do not move; only the temperature changes, from a campfire's warmth to a doorway's neon.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the seat takes the deep-night arm in lamplit ink blue (#1F5FA8), the estate of the Scholar, the Book for its object — stranger than it looks and exact. Both members keep a record nobody else keeps: a family carrying its own genealogy across a desert with no archive in it, and a club that remembers the name of every worker the city wrote off.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that deep-night arm is the Unborn, and the seat turns moonlight silver (#C8D7F0). It is the honest hue for two collectives whose whole product is a future person — the child who will be raised inside the convoy, and the worker who will walk out of a shift because somebody made sure she could.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross the seat moves to the 06h arm — Spring, green, aimed at the vernal equinox — and shares it with Saturday. Protection beside discipline on the season of return: one keeps a circle intact and the other keeps a body intact, and both are slow work with nothing to show for a year of it.
variants.trio: The Trinity keeps the seat at 04h and renames the watch: the blue arm now means Hope, guarding the morning from 0h to 8h beside Wednesday's netrunners. The pairing is deliberately unflattering to both — one hopes a family can outlast the corporations, the other hopes a wall can be talked through, and neither has evidence.

mars.name: Maelstrom · Barghest · Wraiths
mars.base:
[[The Figure]] Tuesday holds force in three registers, and the point of the rotation is that they are not one thing. Maelstrom began as the Metal Warriors, was almost wiped out in an ambush, and rebuilt itself by replacing as much of the body as the body would tolerate — force that has stopped negotiating with its own limits. Barghest is Colonel Kurt Hansen's militia in Dogtown, built out of ex-Militech soldiers and run as a chain of command. The Wraiths are nomads who went raider: force that hunts instead of fighting. One is heat, one is discipline, one is appetite.

[[On the Dial]] Their home is the 16h arm in ember orange (#DC9600), the Zeal of the working afternoon — the hour at which a fire is being used rather than admired. This is the only arm whose virtue and vice are the same energy at two temperatures, and the seat fills it three times over to make the point.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Courage and the vice is Wrath. Maelstrom is the arm with the governor removed; Barghest is the arm with a rank structure bolted on, which is not the same thing as a conscience; the Wraiths are what is left when the fire is aimed at whoever is weakest in reach. Across the dial at 04h Monday's Serenity is the named cure, and the Wraiths are the proof — they are the Badlands' own answer to the Aldecaldos, the same desert and the same convoys, with no watch kept for anybody but themselves.

[[The Hour]] *"He that is slow to anger is better than the mighty; and he that ruleth his spirit than he that taketh a city"* (Proverbs 16:32). Three factions share this arm, and not one of them clears the second clause.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 16h arm in ember orange (#DC9600), the Zeal of the working afternoon — the base reading, three different ways of keeping one fire lit.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism keeps the seat at 16h and burns the ember up to pure yellow (#FFFF00) — red and green fused. Light gives the heat a brighter hue without giving it an object, which is this seat's whole problem stated as a wavelength.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the seat takes the 15h afternoon in copper (#C87533), the estate of the Merchant, the Coin for its object — the reading that stings. All three sell force: Maelstrom trades it for chrome, Barghest sells it to a colonel in exchange for a country, and the Wraiths sell what they cut off the people they take it from.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that afternoon arm is Maturity, and the seat wears amber (#FFB400) — an age none of the three reaches. Maturity on this wheel is the point at which strength stops being about the person holding it, and the rotation is three consecutive failures to arrive there.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross the seat takes the 18h arm — Autumn, red, aimed at the equinox — sharing the spoke with Friday. The season of reckoning holds the city's two most territorial instincts: one counts ground and one counts the people standing on it.
variants.trio: The Trinity moves the seat to 20h, onto Love's red arm beside the Valentinos, guarding the evening from 16h to 24h. The reading is harsh and correct — each of the three is somebody's loyalty before it is anybody's threat, and Maelstrom in particular got its members back by giving up their bodies for them.

mercury.name: Voodoo Boys · 6th Street
mercury.base:
[[The Figure]] Wednesday is knowledge held as property. The Voodoo Boys are Pacifica's netrunners, the only crew in the city that deliberately works at the Blackwall, and their entire standing rests on knowing what is behind it and telling nobody. 6th Street was founded by veterans of the Unification War to defend a district the state had abandoned, and it kept the flag while the defence drifted into a protection racket — an expertise in force converted into a toll booth. Both hold something the city needs, and both price it.

[[On the Dial]] Their home is the midnight arm at 0h in Tyrian purple (#542E85), the Sorrow of the closed ledger. Purple is the dye that cost more than the cloth it coloured, and both members are in the business of the surcharge: one on information, one on safety.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Wisdom and the vice is Greed, and this is where the canon's web pulls tightest — wisdom is the only virtue that can be stockpiled, which is exactly what makes greed its shadow. Across the dial at 12h Thursday's Generosity is the named cure. Everything the Voodoo Boys offer an outsider is the same trade in different words, and 6th Street's offer is the older one: we already protect you, and now you find out what that costs.

[[The Hour]] *"For in much wisdom is much grief: and he that increaseth knowledge increaseth sorrow"* (Ecclesiastes 1:18). Wednesday's mood is Sorrow, and this seat is the reason — the people who went furthest past the wall came back with something they will not repeat.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the midnight arm at 0h in Tyrian purple (#542E85), the Sorrow of the closed ledger — the base reading, knowledge kept as an asset.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns the purple to magenta (#BD00BD) — the one hue found in no rainbow, invented by the eye where the spectrum's two ends are made to meet. Apt for a seat whose expertise is a wall with something living on the other side.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the seat shifts to the 21h evening arm in stage-velvet violet (#7A2E8E), the estate of the Artist, the Mask for its object. Both members trade on a face: one wears a religion it did not inherit as the cover for a research programme, the other wears a war it fought fifty years ago as the cover for a fee.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that evening arm is Old Age, and the seat wears dusk violet (#9C6BD4). 6th Street holds it literally — a veterans' association that never dissolved and now has nothing left to be a veteran of; the Voodoo Boys hold it in the older sense, as the last crew still practising what netrunning was before the DataKrash.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross the seat keeps the bottom arm at 0h — Winter, blue, aimed at the winter solstice — and it alone shares that spoke with nobody. The year's midnight belongs to a single seat, and knowledge held back is the one vice on this dial that can be practised entirely alone.
variants.trio: The Trinity lifts the seat off midnight to 04h, onto Hope's blue arm beside Monday's protectors, guarding the morning from 0h to 8h. The move is argued by what the Voodoo Boys actually attempt: speaking to whatever lives past the Blackwall is a bet that it can be dealt with, which is hope written as engineering.

jupiter.name: Tyger Claws
jupiter.base:
[[The Figure]] Thursday is generosity turned into a business model. The Tyger Claws hold Japantown and the Kabuki strip, and what they sell is the appearance of being given something: the club that never closes, the braindance that is better than the hour anybody actually had, the room upstairs. Nothing in the arrangement is free and everything in it is presented as hospitality, which makes it the most complete inversion of a virtue on this dial and the reason the seat is theirs.

[[On the Dial]] Their home is the top arm at 12h in noon yellow (#F8E600), the Joy of the day's peak. Thursday's plenty is the entire premise of a vice district: the hour when there is more than enough, sold by the hour, to people paying for the feeling that there is.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Generosity and the vice is Excess. The Claws are the seat's cautionary half almost without remainder — pleasure supplied at industrial scale, with the supplier's margin taken out of the people supplying it. Across the dial at 0h Wednesday's Wisdom is the named cure, and it is the exact one, because the whole trade depends on the customer not counting. Clouds is the plainest case: a house where the staff are the product and the hospitality is a chip in somebody's head.

[[The Hour]] *"He that loveth pleasure shall be a poor man"* (Proverbs 21:17). The proverb is aimed at the customer; the Claws have built a district on being the other party to it.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the top arm at 12h in noon yellow (#F8E600), the Joy of the day's peak — the base reading, plenty at the hour that has the most of it.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns the noon to green (#00DC00) — the wavelength at the summit of human sight. The reading is unflattering and exact: what this seat runs is the most visible thing in the city, and the visibility is the product.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the seat holds the 09h morning arm in alb ivory (#EDEDE0), the estate of the Priest, the Bell for its object — the one placement here meant to sting. A priest's authority is the distribution of something nobody privately owns, and a neon strip that runs all night is a bell rung over an offering plate.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that morning arm is Childhood, and the seat wears spring green (#7CE577). The fit belongs to the customer rather than to the gang: everything sold on this arm is sold on the promise of an appetite with no consequence attached, which is a condition only children are entitled to.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross the seat holds 12h on the Summer arm, yellow, aimed at the solstice — sharing the spoke with Sunday. The year's brightest hour held by the district and by the corporation whose money quietly stands behind it: one balance sheet, two very different frontages.
variants.trio: On the Trinity the seat keeps the top arm at 12h, yellow, where the colour now means Faith, shared with Saturday as they guard the day's height from 8h to 16h. It is the arm this seat has least right to and holds anyway — an economy that runs entirely on the customer believing the night will be worth what it costs.

venus.name: Valentinos
venus.base:
[[The Figure]] Friday is loyalty with a border drawn around it. The Valentinos are Heywood's own and the largest gang in the city, and the only one whose iconography is religious rather than industrial: gold, Santa Muerte, the family name carried on the car. What they defend is not territory in the abstract but the specific streets that raised their members, and the ferocity is proportional to the closeness. Love on this arm is never sentiment; it is the willingness to do something about it.

[[On the Dial]] Their home is the 20h arm in deep red (#B60000), the Passion of the evening. Friday's red is the hour when the work is over and what remains is who a person is going home to — which is the entire political programme of a barrio gang, stated as a colour.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Love and the vice is Jealousy, and this is the clearest case on the dial that they are one motion at two distances. The Valentinos are generous inside the line and murderous across it, and the line is exactly the edge of what they love. Across the dial at 08h Saturday's Patience is the named cure: jealousy is a want with another person still inside it, and the only thing that has ever dissolved one is the ability to wait.

[[The Hour]] *"Set me as a seal upon thine heart... for love is strong as death; jealousy is cruel as the grave"* (Song of Solomon 8:6). The verse puts both of this arm's names in one line, in that order, and does not pretend they can be separated.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 20h arm in deep red (#B60000), the Passion of the evening — the base reading, loyalty practised as a decision rather than felt as a mood.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism keeps the seat at 20h and purifies the red to its light primary (#FF0000) — the reddest red there is, unmixed. In the light world Passion is a wavelength rather than a pigment, and this seat's version of it is never diluted and never aimed at more than one thing at a time.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the seat shifts to the 18h sunset arm in iron-blood crimson (#A02020), the estate of the Soldier, the Sword for its object. It is the honest placement rather than the flattering one: everything this gang has protected it has protected by force, and its own members are the currency it spends doing so.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that sunset arm belongs to the Elder, the harvest of a life, and the seat deepens to ember (#FF6A3C). The reading is generational, which is also the gang's own claim about itself — Heywood is the one district in this cast where the same families have held the same streets long enough for a harvest to be countable.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross the seat takes the 18h arm — Autumn, red, aimed at the autumnal equinox — sharing the spoke with Tuesday. Two territorial instincts on the season of reckoning, and only one of them is inheritable.
variants.trio: The seat does not move: the Trinity's Love arm is its own 20h in its own red. Tuesday joins it, and the two guard the evening from 16h to 24h — the arm held by this cast's two proofs that loving a place and being lethal to everyone outside it are the same fact under two names.

saturn.name: Animals · Scavengers
saturn.base:
[[The Figure]] Saturday is the long, patient work done to a body, and the two members of this seat are that discipline pointed in opposite directions. The Animals refuse most cyberware on principle and build strength chemically and physically instead — years of it, for a result that cannot be bought at a clinic. The Scavengers have the identical patience and none of the ownership: they cut implants out of living people and sell them. One grows what it has; the other takes what somebody else grew.

[[On the Dial]] Their home is the 08h arm in field green (#007E00), the Renewal of the morning — the hour of slow, repeated, unglamorous work. Every other faction in this cast is defined by what it holds; this seat is defined by what it accumulates, which is the only thing on the arm that time can actually do.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Patience and the vice is Envy, and the pairing is the cleanest illustration of that pair anywhere in the cast. Envy is not wanting a thing; it is wanting the thing because somebody else has it, and the Scavengers are that appetite with a scalpel in it. Across the dial at 20h Friday's Love is the named cure, and the argument is structural: the Scavs are the one collective here with no inside — nobody they would not sell, and therefore nothing worth waiting for.

[[The Hour]] *"But let patience have her perfect work, that ye may be perfect and entire, wanting nothing"* (James 1:4). The last two words are the seat's whole test, and it fails them by exactly one member.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 08h arm in field green (#007E00), the Renewal of the morning — the base reading, a result that only accumulates.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns the morning green to cyan (#00DDDD) — the colour of the clear early sky rather than of the ground under it. Renewal keeps the hour; light names what the work is for instead of the work, which is precisely where this seat's two members part company.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the seat takes the dawn arm, 06h, in field green (#3E8914), the estate of the Farmer, the Plough for its object — an estate one member practises and the other parodies. A farmer's authority comes from having been present for every season of the same ground; a harvest taken out of somebody else's body is the same verb with the ownership removed.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the dawn arm is Birth, and the seat wears predawn mist (#8FA8C8). Both members deal in the body as raw material: one spends years making one, the other sells the parts of one that was already finished.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross the seat moves to 06h — Spring, green, aimed at the vernal equinox — sharing the spoke with Monday. The season of return held by this cast's two forms of slow work: keeping a circle whole, and keeping a body whole.
variants.trio: The Trinity promotes the seat from the morning to the crown: the 12h Faith arm, yellow, shared with Thursday, guarding the day's height from 8h to 16h. The reading is exact and uncomfortable — years of training against no guarantee is faith with nothing but a body staked on it, and the Scavs are the same wager placed on somebody else's.

sun.name: Arasaka · Militech
sun.base:
[[The Figure]] Sunday is held by the two corporations that fought the Fourth Corporate War over the top of every faction below, and the argument is about what authority is for rather than about good against evil. Arasaka holds the bright face: a security house grown into a bank, old enough to have outlived the states it operates inside, whose own claim is that it supplies order where nothing else will. Militech holds the dark one: an arms manufacturer of comparable size that has never claimed to be anything but an instrument, and whose power runs entirely through the government it serves. Neither is a villain in its own account; they are one authority read from inside and from outside.

[[On the Dial]] The centre holds no arm and no hour. White-gold is the sum of every hue the wheel can mix, and the six seats around it are that light taken apart — a night watch, a fire, a secret, a market, a family, a discipline. Arasaka is what the source looks like when nothing has yet been subtracted from it: the only party in the city that owns a piece of all six.

[[The Lesson]] The bundle gives the ruler face Justice against Pride and the servant face Humility against Servility. Arasaka's justice is the kind that arrives with a private army — order supplied as a product, which works until the supplier is also the only appeal. Its Pride is architectural: the tower was destroyed in 2023 and rebuilt on the same ground, taller. Militech's humility is structural rather than moral, since it does not pretend to be sovereign; its Servility is the same fact seen from below, an arms house whose largest customer is also its only regulator. Nothing sits opposite the centre, so the two check each other and nobody else does.

[[The Hour]] *"Put not your trust in princes, nor in the son of man, in whom there is no help"* (Psalm 146:3). Sixty years of war between these two produced a balance rather than a winner, and the city has been living inside the balance ever since.

faces.ruler:
Arasaka is Sunday's bright face, and the argument for the seat is that it is the only body in this cast that behaves like a throne rather than like a business. Founded on security and grown into banking, it supplies the one commodity Night City cannot produce for itself — enforceable order — and sells it to everyone, the state included.

Its virtue is Justice in the oldest and least comfortable sense: a rule that is actually applied. Arasaka contracts are honoured and Arasaka debts are collected, and the only difference between that and law is that nobody voted for it. The vice that stalks it is Pride, and here it is written in the skyline: the tower was destroyed by a nuclear device in 2023 and rebuilt on the same ground, taller, which is a statement rather than a plan. Its mood is Glory, noon's own triumph — the corporation that lost the Fourth Corporate War on paper and holds the city's horizon anyway.
faces.servant:
Militech is Sunday's dark face — a power in its own right, seated here as the Servant because its whole standing runs through somebody else's sovereignty.

Its virtue is Humility, and the argument is structural rather than flattering: Militech has never claimed to be a government. It builds the weapons and leaves the New United States to decide what they are for, which is the only form of restraint this cast contains. The vice that stalks it is Servility — an arms house whose largest customer is also its regulator has no independent position left to take, and its own former executives keep reappearing on the customer's side of the table. Its mood is Awe: it wears the same glyph as the Throne and holds everything it has by permission.

variants.hexa_primary: On the painter's wheel the pair keeps the centre of the dial, white-gold, belonging to no hour: the six arms around it are that light decomposed, one virtue to each spoke. This is the home reading — the source rather than a spoke, an authority that precedes every office it hands out.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism changes every arm around the pair and cannot change the centre: white remains the sum of all wavelengths. It is the same fact from the other side — a corporation of this size is not a seventh faction on the board, it is the condition the other six are operating inside.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the pair steps onto the noon arm in royal gold (#F0C420), the estate of the King, the Crown for its object — the plainest seat in the set and the only one this cast fills with something that was never elected. Both hold the prerogatives of a state and neither carries the obligations of one.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the noon arm is Youth, the zenith of a life, and the pair wears sun-yellow (#FFE800) — apt for two houses that have already had their war and behave as though the next one is still ahead of them. The seat holds a career's summit and its aftermath under one hue.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross the Sunday pair holds 12h on the Summer arm, yellow, aimed at the summer solstice — shared with Thursday. The corporation beside the district its money keeps lit: the year's brightest spoke held by the two things in this cast that never close.
variants.trio: On the Trinity the seat keeps the centre and the cast around it narrows to three arms — Faith yellow, Love red, Hope blue. The geometry is indifferent to who holds it, which is exactly the warning this dual exists to make: the same centre seats the house that sells order and the house that sells the means to break it.

moon.name: Viktor Vektor
moon.base:
[[The Figure]] Viktor Vektor is Monday's figure because he is the only fixed point in a cast that is otherwise entirely in motion. A former boxer turned ripperdoc, he runs a basement clinic in Watson, installs the chrome the rest of this cast fights with, and carries the bills of people who cannot pay him — including the one patient whose account is the whole story. Serenity on this arm is not a disposition; it is what a steady hand looks like from the outside.

[[On the Dial]] His home is the 04h arm in deep blue (#002FFF), the hour the canon names Calm — the emptiest interval of the night, which in this cast is also the hour people arrive bleeding. The clinic is the one room in the setting where nobody raises their voice, and every other seat here has been through it.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Serenity and the vice is Fear, and Viktor's career is a running argument that composure is a professional obligation rather than a temperament. He gives V the diagnosis nobody else will give, plainly, without softening it, which is the seat's own definition of calm: telling the truth at the speed the patient can take it. Across the dial at 16h Tuesday's Courage is the named cure, and it runs both ways — his hands are steady because somebody else's are not.

[[The Hour]] *"They that be whole need not a physician, but they that are sick"* (Matthew 9:12). Every figure in this cast is on the second list, and Monday is the seat of the man who never once asked which.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 04h arm in deep blue (#002FFF), the Calm of the hour before dawn — the base reading, composure practised as a trade.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism keeps him at 04h and sharpens the blue to #0040FF — pigment's muted night becomes light's electric one. The hour and its Calm do not move; the same steadiness simply reads colder, which is what a patient sees of a doctor who has already decided not to lie.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Viktor takes the deep-night arm in lamplit ink blue (#1F5FA8), the estate of the Scholar, the Book for its object — earned rather than borrowed. A ripperdoc without a licence is a man who has read everything and been examined by nobody, and the only certification he carries is the number of people still walking around.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that deep-night arm is the Unborn, and he turns moonlight silver (#C8D7F0) — the seat reserved for the not-yet-living, held by the one figure in this cast whose entire output is more time for somebody else. Everything anybody here does afterwards is on his account.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Viktor moves to the 06h arm — Spring, green, aimed at the vernal equinox — and shares it with Saturday. The season of return held by this cast's two menders, one of bodies and one of memories, both of whom work slowly and neither of whom is ever in the room when it matters.
variants.trio: The Trinity keeps him at 04h and renames the watch: the blue arm now means Hope, guarding the morning from 0h to 8h beside Wednesday's fixers. The pairing is exact and unkind — one extends credit against a future the patient may not have, and the other never extends anything without security.

mars.name: Jackie · Panam · River
mars.base:
[[The Figure]] Tuesday holds courage in three registers. Jackie Welles is the reckless one: a Heywood kid who wanted the Afterlife's wall and went at the biggest job in the city to get it, and did not come back from it. Panam Palmer is the disciplined one: a nomad who left the Aldecaldos over a decision she thought was cowardly and returned to put the family back together on her own terms. River Ward is the slow one: an NCPD detective who kept working a case the department had closed and lost his standing for it. Appetite, resolve and refusal — the same arm three times.

[[On the Dial]] Their home is the 16h arm in ember orange (#DC9600), the Zeal of the working afternoon — the hour at which a fire is being used rather than admired. Every member of this rotation is defined by an action taken before the odds were known, which is the arm's own definition of its virtue.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Courage and the vice is Wrath, and the rotation is a graded scale between them. Jackie's version is the youngest — courage that has not yet learned to wait, and the cost lands on him inside a single night. Panam's is the hottest and the most governed at once: she is the only one who turns anger into a plan. River's is the least visible, because refusing to drop something is courage that looks like stubbornness until it is proved right. Across the dial at 04h Monday's Serenity is the named cure, and each of the three has needed it at a different hour.

[[The Hour]] *"Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed"* (Joshua 1:9). The two clauses are not the same instruction, and this seat holds three people who each got one of them right.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 16h arm in ember orange (#DC9600), the Zeal of the working afternoon — the base reading, heat kept at a working temperature rather than spent all at once.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism keeps the seat at 16h and burns the ember up to pure yellow (#FFFF00) — red and green fused. Light gives the same nerve a hotter hue without giving it an object; the hour and its Zeal are unchanged, and the difference between these three is entirely what each aimed it at.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the seat takes the 15h afternoon in copper (#C87533), the estate of the Merchant, the Coin for its object — stranger than the Soldier's and truer. All three trade in the same currency and price it differently: Jackie spends everything on one job, Panam refuses a price she considers dishonest, and River pays for a case out of his own career.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that afternoon arm is Maturity, and the seat wears amber (#FFB400). The wheel's own definition is the age at which strength stops being about the person holding it — Panam reaches it when she takes the clan back for the clan, River when he keeps working a case that can no longer help him, and Jackie is the one who dies just short of it.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross the seat takes the 18h arm — Autumn, red, aimed at the equinox — sharing the spoke with Friday. The season of reckoning holds this cast's loudest and most public seats: the ones whose deeds are known by name, and counted afterwards.
variants.trio: The Trinity moves the seat to 20h, onto Love's red arm beside Friday, guarding the evening from 16h to 24h. The reading is exact — not one of these three ever acted for a cause. Jackie went for a friend, Panam for a family, River for a nephew, and courage aimed at a person is what this arm is called.

mercury.name: Wakako · Padre
mercury.base:
[[The Figure]] Wednesday holds the two fixers of this cast, and a fixer is the seat's own profession: somebody who knows who needs what and sells the knowing. Wakako Okada runs Westbrook from a pachinko parlour and has been in the business long enough that her ties reach into the gang that owns the district. Sebastian Ibarra, whom Heywood calls Padre, runs his half of the city out of a church and keeps the collar. Both trade in the same commodity and dress it in opposite institutions.

[[On the Dial]] Their home is the midnight arm at 0h in Tyrian purple (#542E85), the Sorrow of the closed ledger. Purple is the dye that cost more than the cloth it coloured, and a fixer's whole margin is the surcharge on knowing first.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Wisdom and the vice is Greed, and this seat is where the canon's web pulls tightest — wisdom is the only virtue that can be stockpiled, which is exactly what makes greed its shadow. Wakako's version is the colder: she sold out a client, and the argument for the seat is precisely that she is good at her job and that the job includes it. Padre's is warmer and no cleaner — a man who hears confessions and prices them is still the person who priced them. Across the dial at 12h Thursday's Generosity is the named cure, and neither of them has ever taken it.

[[The Hour]] *"Buy the truth, and sell it not; also wisdom, and instruction, and understanding"* (Proverbs 23:23). The instruction has two halves, and Wednesday's seat is the trade that keeps the first and ignores the second.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the midnight arm at 0h in Tyrian purple (#542E85), the Sorrow of the closed ledger — the base reading, knowledge held as inventory.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns the purple to magenta (#BD00BD) — the one hue found in no rainbow, invented by the eye where the spectrum's two ends are made to meet. Apt for a trade that exists only in the gap between two people who have not been introduced.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the seat shifts to the 21h evening arm in stage-velvet violet (#7A2E8E), the estate of the Artist, the Mask for its object — the truest placement in this cast. A fixer is a face held steady while two parties who would never meet are told two different halves of one arrangement, and both of these wear an institution to do it: a parlour and a parish.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that evening arm is Old Age, and the seat wears dusk violet (#9C6BD4) — held as a fact rather than as a manner. Both members are the oldest working figures in this cast, and in a city with this life expectancy seniority is not a courtesy title, it is evidence.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross the seat keeps the bottom arm at 0h — Winter, blue, aimed at the winter solstice — and it alone shares that spoke with nobody. The year's midnight belongs to a single seat, and a fixer is the one figure here whose decisive acts are all performed alone, in a room, before anybody else knows there was a decision.
variants.trio: The Trinity lifts the seat off midnight to 04h, onto Hope's blue arm beside Monday, guarding the morning from 0h to 8h. The move is argued by what a fixer sells: every job is somebody's plan for a life they do not have yet, and this seat is the party that decides which of those plans get funded.

jupiter.name: Misty
jupiter.base:
[[The Figure]] Misty Olszewski is Thursday's figure because she is the only member of this cast who gives without invoicing. She keeps an esoterica shop above the ripperdoc clinic, reads tarot for people who cannot pay for it, and is the one person the rest of the circle goes to when there is nothing left to buy. Generosity here is not a mood; it is the one economy in Night City that runs on no return at all.

[[On the Dial]] Her home is the top arm at 12h in noon yellow (#F8E600), the Joy of the day's peak — the hour with more of everything than it needs. Thursday's plenty is the seat of what gets handed out rather than sold, and in this cast that is a single shop with a curtain in it.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Generosity and the vice is Excess. Misty's argument for the seat is not that she has much to give — she has the least of anybody here — but that what she gives she never withholds for advantage, which is the only definition of the virtue this dial accepts. Her own losses are the seat's cautionary half: she loses the man she loved, keeps the shop, and keeps giving. Across the dial at 0h Wednesday's Wisdom is the named cure, and the seat's own risk is exactly there — generosity without judgement funds the next disaster as readily as the next recovery.

[[The Hour]] *"Freely ye have received, freely give"* (Matthew 10:8). Thursday's whole instruction is a single sentence, and this is the one figure in the cast who never asked for the first clause to be settled before acting on the second.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the top arm at 12h in noon yellow (#F8E600), the Joy of the day's peak — the base reading, plenty measured by what leaves rather than by what arrives.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns her noon to green (#00DC00) — the wavelength at the summit of human sight. Fitting for a figure whose contribution is not an act but a continuity: the shop is open, and the number of people it has kept upright is measurable only over years.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Misty holds the 09h morning arm in alb ivory (#EDEDE0), the estate of the Priest, the Bell for its object — the one seat in this cast that needs no argument. She is the estate: the office of distributing something nobody privately owns, and the only figure here who performs a rite for anybody who walks in.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that morning arm is Childhood, and she wears spring green (#7CE577) — read as a disposition rather than as an age. Childhood's traits on this wheel are appetite, certainty and no memory of having been wrong, and hers is the third one inverted: she has every reason to have become cynical and has declined.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Misty holds 12h on the Summer arm, yellow, aimed at the solstice — sharing the spoke with Sunday. The year's brightest hour held by the cast's legend and by the one person who was kind to him: the two poles of what a reputation is worth.
variants.trio: On the Trinity Misty keeps the top arm at 12h, yellow, where the colour now means Faith, shared with Saturday as they guard the day's height from 8h to 16h. She is the least strained tenant this arm has ever had — hers is the only practice in the cast that does not work at all unless it is believed in first.

venus.name: Kerry · Lizzy Wizzy
venus.base:
[[The Figure]] Friday holds the two performers, and the seat is about what wanting does to a person who is already being looked at. Kerry Eurodyne played guitar in Samurai and outlived the band, the scene and the man it was built around, and spent the decades afterwards producing records he did not respect for money he did not need. Lizzy Wizzy is the pop idol who staged her own death on stage and had herself copied into a chrome body to finish the show. One cannot forgive his past; the other could not tolerate a limit.

[[On the Dial]] Their home is the 20h arm in deep red (#B60000), the Passion of the evening. Friday's red is the hour when the work is over and what is left is what a person actually wanted all day, and both members of this seat have made a career out of that hour.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Love and the vice is Jealousy, and this seat is the clearest demonstration on the dial that they are one motion at two distances. Kerry's jealousy is retrospective — of a dead friend, of a band that was never his, of a version of himself that was more admired than the one still working. Lizzy's is prospective and total: she wanted the audience so completely that she was willing to stop being the thing they were looking at. Across the dial at 08h Saturday's Patience is the named cure, and Kerry is the one who eventually takes it.

[[The Hour]] *"Vanity of vanities; all is vanity"* (Ecclesiastes 1:2). The word means vapour before it means conceit, and Friday's seat holds two people who built lives out of something with exactly that half-life.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 20h arm in deep red (#B60000), the Passion of the evening — the base reading, wanting treated as a career rather than as a feeling.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism keeps the seat at 20h and purifies the red to its light primary (#FF0000) — the reddest red there is, unmixed. In the light world Passion is a wavelength rather than a pigment, which suits two performers exactly: what they do is never blended, only aimed at a room.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the seat shifts to the 18h sunset arm in iron-blood crimson (#A02020), the estate of the Soldier, the Sword for its object — a placement neither would have chosen. Both spent decades in a fight nobody scored: one against a legend he could not outlive, the other against a body she could not keep, and each turned the weapon inward before anybody else got to.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that sunset arm belongs to the Elder, the harvest of a life, and the seat deepens to ember (#FF6A3C). The fit is chronological for one and ironic for the other: Kerry is genuinely old and still working, and Lizzy bought a body that will never be, which is the same harvest refused.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross the seat takes the 18h arm — Autumn, red, aimed at the autumnal equinox — sharing the spoke with Tuesday. Two seats that live entirely in public, on the season that counts what a year actually produced rather than what was announced.
variants.trio: The seat does not move: the Trinity's Love arm is its own 20h in its own red. Tuesday joins it, and the two guard the evening from 16h to 24h — the arm held by this cast's proof that being adored and being loved are different facts, and that only one of them survives the tour.

saturn.name: Judy
saturn.base:
[[The Figure]] Judy Alvarez is Saturday's figure because her whole trade is the unhurried assembly of something out of raw material. She is a braindance editor: she takes a recording of somebody else's minutes and cuts it until it can be lived through by a stranger, which is craft in the oldest sense and cannot be done at speed. Patience here is not endurance; it is the professional refusal to call a thing finished.

[[On the Dial]] Her home is the 08h arm in field green (#007E00), the Renewal of the morning. Saturday's green is the hour of slow repeated work with nothing visible to show for a day of it, and an editing timeline is the exact shape of that hour.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Patience and the vice is Envy. Judy's patience is real and her limit is the seat's own cautionary half — she leaves the Mox, leaves Clouds and in the end leaves the city, because patience with a craft is not the same capacity as patience with people who will not change. Across the dial at 20h Friday's Love is the named cure, and the argument is structural: she is the one member of the cast who consistently attaches herself to what she is working on, which is why the work is good and why the leaving costs her.

[[The Hour]] *"In your patience possess ye your souls"* (Luke 21:19). Saturday reads the verb literally — patience on this arm is ownership rather than endurance, and she is the one figure here who is never at any point somebody else's instrument.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 08h arm in field green (#007E00), the Renewal of the morning — the base reading, craft practised as a profession rather than displayed as a gift.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns her morning green to cyan (#00DDDD) — the colour of the clear early sky rather than of the ground under it. Renewal keeps the hour; light names what an edited memory is for instead of the labour of cutting it.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Judy takes the dawn arm, 06h, in field green (#3E8914), the estate of the Farmer, the Plough for its object — the one estate whose method is actually hers. A farmer's authority comes from having been present for every stage of the same ground, and an editor's from having been present for every second of somebody else's hour.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the dawn arm is Birth, and she wears predawn mist (#8FA8C8) — earned rather than assigned. A braindance does not exist until it is cut; the raw recording is material, and she is the one figure in the cast whose output is a thing that was not there before.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Judy moves to 06h — Spring, green, aimed at the vernal equinox — sharing the spoke with Monday. The season of return held by this cast's two menders: one repairs the body, the other repairs what the body remembers.
variants.trio: The Trinity promotes her from the morning to the crown: the 12h Faith arm, yellow, shared with Thursday, guarding the day's height from 8h to 16h. The reading is exact — an editor works for weeks on the assumption that a stranger will eventually feel something, and there is no way to verify that in advance.

sun.name: Johnny Silverhand · Rogue
sun.base:
[[The Figure]] Sunday's seat is held by two people who ran the same city from opposite sides of the same bar, and the argument is about what a legend is for rather than about good against evil. Johnny Silverhand holds the bright face: the rockerboy who fronted Samurai, made his politics into a stage act and then into an attack on Arasaka Tower in 2023, and did not survive it in any form that has a body. Rogue Amendiares holds the dark one: the solo who ran the same jobs, refused the same last one, and spent the next fifty years turning the Afterlife into the institution that decides who counts.

[[On the Dial]] The centre holds no arm and no hour. White-gold is the sum of every hue the wheel can mix, and the six seats around it are that light taken apart — a clinic, a charge, a deal, a gift, a stage, a craft. Johnny is what the source looks like before anything has been subtracted: the one figure here whose name is a measurement other people are held against.

[[The Lesson]] The bundle gives the ruler face Justice against Pride and the servant face Humility against Servility. Johnny's justice is the kind that will not accept a settlement — a permanent refusal to concede that the arrangement is the only arrangement — and his Pride is the same reflex with nobody left to spend it on but the people who follow him. Rogue's humility is the harder kind: she stayed, ran a business, and never once claimed the job she did was the same size as the one he did. Her Servility is the corresponding failure — an institution that lives on other people's risk eventually starts pricing it. Nothing sits opposite the centre, so the two correct each other and nobody else.

[[The Hour]] *"For what shall it profit a man, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul?"* (Mark 8:36). This cast is the one in which the question is not rhetorical, and Sunday holds the two people who each answered it in a different direction.

faces.ruler:
Johnny Silverhand is Sunday's bright face, and the argument for the seat is that nobody else in this cast is a unit of measurement. He fronted Samurai, turned a band into a political position, and in 2023 walked into Arasaka Tower with a nuclear device and a small crew, which is either the most serious act in the setting's history or the most theatrical, and is generally both at once.

His virtue is Justice, understood as the refusal to accept that the present arrangement is the only one available. He is the only figure in the cast who attacks a structure rather than a person, and the whole later history of Night City is written against what he did. The vice that stalks it is Pride, and it is inseparable from the virtue: a man who cannot concede also cannot be argued with, and everybody who went into the tower with him is dead. His mood is Glory, noon's own triumph — a reputation so large that fifty years later it is still being used as a weapon by people who never met him.
faces.servant:
Rogue Amendiares is Sunday's dark face — a power in her own right, seated here as the Servant because her authority is built entirely out of other people's careers.

Her virtue is Humility, and the argument is the one she made herself: she refused the tower job, stayed alive, and never afterwards pretended that the choice was anything but a choice. Running the Afterlife means knowing exactly what everybody in the room is worth and never confusing it with what she is worth, which is a discipline the bright face never had to learn. The vice that stalks it is Servility — a fixer who lives on the risk other people take will eventually price that risk, and the bar's whole hierarchy is a list of the dead sorted by how much they were paid. Her mood is Awe: she has spent five decades keeping the memory of somebody she declined to follow, which is the same seat's other face.

variants.hexa_primary: On the painter's wheel the pair keeps the centre of the dial, white-gold, belonging to no hour: the six arms around them are that light decomposed, one virtue to each spoke. This is the home reading — the source rather than a spoke, a reputation that precedes every job it is spent on.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism changes every arm around them and cannot change the centre: white remains the sum of all wavelengths. It is the same fact from the other side — a legend is not a seventh member of the circle, it is the standard the other six are measured with.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the pair steps onto the noon arm in royal gold (#F0C420), the estate of the King, the Crown for its object — a crown nobody conferred. Neither of them was appointed to anything; one took the position by an act and the other by outlasting everybody who might have contested it.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the noon arm is Youth, the zenith of a life, and the pair wears sun-yellow (#FFE800) — apt for a seat that never ages in one direction and does nothing else in the other. He is fixed at the age he died; she is the only figure in the cast who has been visibly getting older on the same stool for fifty years.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross the Sunday pair holds 12h on the Summer arm, yellow, aimed at the summer solstice — shared with Thursday. The legend beside the one person who was kind to him without wanting anything: the year's brightest spoke holding the loudest thing in the cast and the quietest.
variants.trio: On the Trinity the seat keeps the centre and the cast narrows to three arms — Faith yellow, Love red, Hope blue. The geometry is indifferent to who holds it, which is the warning this dual exists to make: the same centre seats the man who went into the tower and the woman who did not, and it does not adjudicate between them.

moon.name: Songbird
moon.base:
[[The Figure]] Song So Mi holds Monday because she is the cast's clearest case of the arm's vice rather than its virtue. An FIA netrunner of exceptional range, she reached past the Blackwall to get capability nobody else has, and the capability is dismantling her from the inside; everything she does afterwards is organised around a cure. Fear on this arm is not cowardice — it is the accurate estimate of a deadline, acted on.

[[On the Dial]] Her home is the 04h arm in deep blue (#002FFF), the hour the canon names Calm — the emptiest interval of the night, and the one in which a person with a terminal diagnosis is most alone with it. The seat is the quiet one, and she is the figure who cannot get any.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Serenity and the vice is Fear, and the seat holds them at their tightest. Everything Songbird does is defensible in isolation and catastrophic in sequence, because a person running out of time makes each decision correctly and the whole series wrongly. She betrays the man who trained her, not out of malice, but because he is between her and the only cure she has been offered. Across the dial at 16h Tuesday's Courage is the named cure, and the seat's argument is that she has plenty of it and no serenity whatsoever, which is precisely why the arm carries both.

[[The Hour]] *"Fear hath torment"* (1 John 4:18). Three words, and Monday's shadow face is completely described by them.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 04h arm in deep blue (#002FFF), the Calm of the hour before dawn — the base reading, held by the one figure in the cast who never gets any.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism keeps her at 04h and sharpens the blue to #0040FF — pigment's muted night becomes light's electric one. The hour and its Calm do not move; the reading simply goes clinical, which is the temperature every room she is in eventually takes.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Songbird takes the deep-night arm in lamplit ink blue (#1F5FA8), the estate of the Scholar, the Book for its object — earned in the worst way. She is the only person in the setting who has read what is on the far side of the Blackwall and come back able to describe it, and the reading is what is killing her.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that deep-night arm is the Unborn, and she turns moonlight silver (#C8D7F0) — the seat the wheel reserves for the not-yet-living. It is exact: everything she does is spent on a version of herself that does not exist yet and may never, and she has nothing else to spend it on.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Songbird moves to the 06h arm — Spring, green, aimed at the vernal equinox — and shares it with Saturday. Two forms of waiting on the season of return: one waits for a cure and the other for a verdict, and neither arrives in time.
variants.trio: The Trinity keeps her at 04h and renames the watch: the blue arm now means Hope, guarding the morning from 0h to 8h beside Wednesday. The assignment is brutal and correct — a person with a terminal condition who keeps negotiating is practising hope as a method, and the arm does not ask whether the negotiation is honest.

mars.name: Adam Smasher
mars.base:
[[The Figure]] Adam Smasher is Tuesday's figure because he is the arm's vice with nothing left to dilute it. A full-conversion cyborg in Arasaka's employ, he has replaced so much of himself that the question of what remains is no longer biographical, and his standing in the setting rests on a single fact: he is the one who killed Johnny Silverhand in the tower in 2023. Wrath here is not temper. It is a function that has been separated from the person who used to perform it.

[[On the Dial]] His home is the 16h arm in ember orange (#DC9600), the Zeal of the working afternoon — the hour at which a fire is being used. Every other seat in this cast wields force through somebody: a contract, a handler, a chain of command. This is the arm where the instrument is the whole of the argument.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Courage and the vice is Wrath, and this seat is the canon's own demonstration that the pair is not symmetrical. Courage requires something at stake; a body that cannot be meaningfully hurt has removed the requirement, and what is left has the shape of courage and none of its content. Across the dial at 04h Monday's Serenity is the named cure, and it is unavailable to him by construction — serenity is a settlement made with fear, and he has no counterparty left.

[[The Hour]] *"For all they that take the sword shall perish with the sword"* (Matthew 26:52). He is the setting's clearest proof of the sentence and its longest delay: fifty years on the same instruction, and the account is settled in the end by somebody younger.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 16h arm in ember orange (#DC9600), the Zeal of the working afternoon — the base reading, force with the person subtracted out of it.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism keeps him at 16h and burns the ember up to pure yellow (#FFFF00) — red and green fused. Light gives the heat a brighter hue and still no object; the hour and its Zeal are unchanged, and this seat is the arm's warning about exactly that.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Smasher takes the 15h afternoon in copper (#C87533), the estate of the Merchant, the Coin for its object — the placement that indicts him. He is not a soldier; a soldier belongs to something. He is a purchase, renewed for decades by a corporation that has never once had to explain what it was buying.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that afternoon arm is Maturity, and he wears amber (#FFB400) — the wheel's own definition being the age at which strength stops being about the man holding it. He inverts it exactly: his strength stopped being about him because there is no longer a him for it to be about.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Smasher takes the 18h arm — Autumn, red, aimed at the equinox — sharing the spoke with Friday. The season of reckoning holds this cast's two bodies that were made into products, one by choice and one by other people, and neither of them survives it.
variants.trio: The Trinity moves him to 20h, onto Love's red arm beside Friday, guarding the evening from 16h to 24h. It is the most uncomfortable assignment in the cast and it is argued rather than ironic: half a century of unbroken service to one house is loyalty by any measure the dial recognises, and the arm does not require that the object be worth it.

mercury.name: Dexter DeShawn
mercury.base:
[[The Figure]] Dexter DeShawn is Wednesday's figure because he is the seat's virtue turned entirely on its owner. A fixer of real standing, he knows the city's network better than almost anybody in this cast — who is available, who is owed, what a job is actually worth — and he spends that knowledge on the biggest score in the setting and then on removing the only witnesses to it. Greed here is not appetite for money; it is expertise with no obligation attached.

[[On the Dial]] His home is the midnight arm at 0h in Tyrian purple (#542E85), the Sorrow of the closed ledger. The colour is the dye that cost more than the cloth, and the seat's own mood is what a ledger looks like when the last entry is a person.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Wisdom and the vice is Greed, and the pairing is the canon's argument that they share a mechanism: wisdom is the only virtue that can be accumulated, and an accumulation with no purpose outside itself is the vice by definition. Dexter's decision after the heist is not a loss of nerve; it is the correct move for a man who has priced his own crew. Across the dial at 12h Thursday's Generosity is the named cure — the one instinct that would have made the same knowledge worth something — and it is the exact instinct he does not have.

[[The Hour]] *"For the love of money is the root of all evil"* (1 Timothy 6:10). The verse is usually misquoted with the first three words dropped, and this seat is the reason they matter: the money is not the problem, the ordering of everything else behind it is.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the midnight arm at 0h in Tyrian purple (#542E85), the Sorrow of the closed ledger — the base reading, expertise with nothing owed to anybody.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns his purple to magenta (#BD00BD) — the one hue found in no rainbow, invented by the eye where the spectrum's two ends are made to meet. Apt for a fixer: everything he sells exists only in the space between two parties who have not been introduced, and he is the only one who sees both.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Dexter shifts to the 21h evening arm in stage-velvet violet (#7A2E8E), the estate of the Artist, the Mask for its object — a truer estate for him than the Merchant's. His actual trade is presentation: the size of the job, the calibre of the client, the certainty in the room, all of it staged and none of it checkable until afterwards.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that evening arm is Old Age, and he wears dusk violet (#9C6BD4) — read as a career's late stage rather than a man's. He is a fixer with one score left in him and no succession of any kind, and the whole plan is an attempt to convert a reputation into an exit.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Dexter keeps the bottom arm at 0h — Winter, blue, aimed at the winter solstice — and he alone shares it with no one. The year's midnight belongs to a single figure, and this cast has exactly one whose decisive act was committed alone, in a car, with no witness he intended to leave.
variants.trio: The Trinity lifts him off midnight to 04h, onto Hope's blue arm beside Monday, guarding the morning from 0h to 8h. The move is argued by the job itself: the Konpeki score was a bet that one operation could put a man permanently beyond the reach of the city, which is hope with a crew staked on it.

jupiter.name: Solomon Reed
jupiter.base:
[[The Figure]] Solomon Reed holds Thursday because his entire professional output is given away. An FIA agent of long service, he trained the netrunner who sits on Monday, and everything she is capable of she is capable of because he handed it to her. Generosity in an intelligence service is a strange virtue and a real one: tradecraft is the only asset a handler owns, and teaching it is the one act that permanently reduces his own advantage.

[[On the Dial]] His home is the top arm at 12h in noon yellow (#F8E600), the Joy of the day's peak — the hour with more than it needs. Thursday's plenty is what a generation hands to the next one, and this cast's only teacher sits on it.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Generosity and the vice is Excess, and the seat's shadow is the quantity rather than the act. A handler spends assets; the arithmetic of the profession is that people are expended and the operation continues, and a career of it accumulates into something no single decision accounts for. Across the dial at 0h Wednesday's Wisdom is the named cure, and it is the exact deficiency — he gives everything away and never asks what it will be used for, which is how the student ends up pointed at the teacher.

[[The Hour]] *"For unto whomsoever much is given, of him shall be much required"* (Luke 12:48). The seat is usually read from the giver's side; this figure is the one who finds out what the second clause costs when the receiving end declines it.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the top arm at 12h in noon yellow (#F8E600), the Joy of the day's peak — the base reading, an asset that only exists once it has been handed over.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns his noon to green (#00DC00) — the wavelength at the summit of human sight. Fitting for a teacher rather than an operator: what he made goes on working after he stops, and it is measured by whether it still functions once he is no longer in the room.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Reed holds the 09h morning arm in alb ivory (#EDEDE0), the estate of the Priest, the Bell for its object — the placement this cast least expects and most deserves. A priest's office is the distribution of something nobody privately owns, and a handler's craft is exactly that: a body of practice with no author, passed to whoever is next.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that morning arm is Childhood, and he wears spring green (#7CE577) — read as the age of what he made rather than of the man. Everything his student does she does in the first generation of her own capability, with all of childhood's traits: appetite, certainty, and no memory of ever having been wrong.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Reed holds 12h on the Summer arm, yellow, aimed at the solstice — sharing the spoke with Sunday. The teacher beside the throne: the year's brightest spoke held by the two things in this cast that outlive the people occupying them, an office and a curriculum.
variants.trio: On the Trinity Reed keeps the top arm at 12h, yellow, where the colour now means Faith, shared with Saturday as they guard the day's height from 8h to 16h. The two loyalists of the cast hold one arm — one to a service and one to a house — and both discover the same thing, that the institution does not return the sentiment.

venus.name: Evelyn Parker
venus.base:
[[The Figure]] Evelyn Parker holds Friday because she is the one figure in this cast who tried to take her own life out of somebody else's hands and was destroyed for it. A doll by trade, she assembles the plan that drives the whole story and attempts to cut the fixer out of it, on the entirely reasonable ground that she is the one supplying the information. What follows is the seat's shadow rather than her failing: the city's appetite for what she is, applied without limit.

[[On the Dial]] Her home is the 20h arm in deep red (#B60000), the Passion of the evening. Friday's red is the hour of what a person actually wants once the working day is over, and hers is the smallest want in the cast — a life she owns — and the one the setting refuses most completely.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Love and the vice is Jealousy, and this seat reads the pair from the object's side rather than the subject's. Her own want is modest and clear-eyed; the jealousy on this arm belongs to everyone around her, and it is the ordinary commercial kind — the wish to have exclusive use of a person. Across the dial at 08h Saturday's Patience is the named cure, and she is the one figure here who was given no time at all: from the plan to the end is a matter of weeks.

[[The Hour]] *"For man looketh on the outward appearance, but the LORD looketh on the heart"* (1 Samuel 16:7). The whole of this seat is the first clause, applied by everybody in the cast except her.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 20h arm in deep red (#B60000), the Passion of the evening — the base reading, a want that was modest, specific and refused.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism keeps her at 20h and purifies the red to its light primary (#FF0000) — the reddest red there is, unmixed. In the light world Passion is a wavelength rather than a pigment, and hers is the only one in the cast aimed at a single outcome and nothing else.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Evelyn shifts to the 18h sunset arm in iron-blood crimson (#A02020), the estate of the Soldier, the Sword for its object — a seat she never wanted and is nevertheless owed. She is the only member of this cast who moved first against a fixer, a corporation and a club at once, with no organisation to back her and no way out if it failed.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that sunset arm belongs to the Elder, the harvest of a life, and she deepens to ember (#FF6A3C). The fit is bitter and exact: she is among the youngest figures on the dial and the harvest is taken from her in full, by people who had no part in growing it.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Evelyn takes the 18h arm — Autumn, red, aimed at the autumnal equinox — sharing the spoke with Tuesday. Two bodies made into instruments on the season of reckoning: one was bought by a corporation and consented, the other was taken and did not.
variants.trio: The seat does not move: the Trinity's Love arm is her own 20h in her own red. Tuesday joins her, and the two guard the evening from 16h to 24h — the arm held by this cast's two proofs that the same word covers a person's whole plan for herself and a corporation's line item.

saturn.name: Takemura
saturn.base:
[[The Figure]] Goro Takemura is Saturday's figure because his contribution is a wager settled slowly and never paid out. Saburo Arasaka's bodyguard for decades, he survives the murder of the man he served and spends everything afterwards on a single objective: assembling proof of who did it, to a standard an institution would accept, from outside that institution and with no authority whatsoever. Patience on this arm is not endurance; it is the willingness to keep building a case nobody has asked for.

[[On the Dial]] His home is the 08h arm in field green (#007E00), the Renewal of the morning — the hour of slow, repeated work with nothing to show for a day of it. He is the only figure in this cast whose method is accumulation rather than leverage.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Patience and the vice is Envy, and Takemura's position is the seat's own cautionary half. Loyalty extended past the point where it can be returned turns into a claim on people who never made him a promise, and his last demand is on somebody with no obligation to him at all. Across the dial at 20h Friday's Love is the named cure, and the argument is precise: a want with another person still inside it is only dissolved by love, and what he actually loved was an office rather than a man.

[[The Hour]] *"Better is the end of a thing than the beginning thereof: and the patient in spirit is better than the proud in spirit"* (Ecclesiastes 7:8). Saturday's seat is the one member of this cast who chooses the second clause, and it does not save him.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 08h arm in field green (#007E00), the Renewal of the morning — the base reading, a case assembled slowly by somebody with no standing to file it.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns his morning green to cyan (#00DDDD) — the colour of the clear early sky rather than of the ground under it. Renewal keeps the hour; light names the restoration he is actually working toward instead of the daily labour of it.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Takemura takes the dawn arm, 06h, in field green (#3E8914), the estate of the Farmer, the Plough for its object — an odd estate for a bodyguard and the right one. A farmer's authority is having been present for every season of the same ground, and he is the only person left who was present for all of Arasaka's.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the dawn arm is Birth, and he wears predawn mist (#8FA8C8). The reading is about what he is trying to produce rather than what he has done: an Arasaka restored to what it was before the murder, a thing that does not exist and never did in the form he remembers.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Takemura moves to 06h — Spring, green, aimed at the vernal equinox — sharing the spoke with Monday. The season of return held by this cast's two figures who are working toward a restoration: one of a body, one of a house, and neither gets it.
