variants.trio: The Trinity promotes him from the morning to the crown: the 12h Faith arm, yellow, shared with Thursday, guarding the day's height from 8h to 16h. The reading is uncomfortable and correct — decades of service on the assumption that the house is worth serving is faith, and only the outcome decides whether it was also judgement.

sun.name: Saburo Arasaka · Yorinobu
sun.base:
[[The Figure]] Sunday's seat is held by a father and the son who killed him, and it rotates in lockstep with a second pair who hold the same offices in a different empire. Saburo Arasaka holds the bright face: the founder, past a hundred and fifty years old, who built a corporation that outlives states and intended to outlive his own body as well. Yorinobu holds the dark one: the heir who spent his adult life posturing against everything the house is, strangled his father in a hotel suite, and then took the chair. The roster's other pair argues the same seat from the other side of the war — Rosalind Myers, who governs the New United States, and Colonel Kurt Hansen, who carved a private state out of a district and runs it as one.

[[On the Dial]] The centre holds no arm and no hour. White-gold is the sum of every hue the wheel can mix, and the six seats around it are that light taken apart — a diagnosis, an instrument, a deal, a lesson, a want, a vigil. The throne is what the source looks like before anything is subtracted: the only position in this cast that does not have to explain itself to anybody.

[[The Lesson]] The bundle gives the ruler face Justice against Pride and the servant face Humility against Servility. The Ruler's justice is the founder's kind — a rule actually applied, consistently, for longer than any living witness — and its Pride is the refusal of the one limit nobody negotiates, which is why an engram exists at all. The Servant's humility is the honest recognition that the house is monstrous; his Servility is that he takes it anyway, which is the seat's whole indictment. Nothing sits opposite the centre, so the two correct each other and nobody else does.

[[The Hour]] *"He that troubleth his own house shall inherit the wind"* (Proverbs 11:29). Sunday holds the two men the proverb is about, in the order it names them, and the inheritance in this cast is literal.

faces.ruler:
Saburo Arasaka is Sunday's bright face, and the argument for the seat is that he is the only figure in this cast who built the thing everybody else is standing inside. A corporation founded on security and grown into a power that treats governments as counterparties, held for over a century by one man who never delegated the direction of it.

His virtue is Justice in its coldest and most defensible sense: a rule that is applied without exception, including to his own family, which is precisely what makes him unsurvivable to be related to. The vice that stalks it is Pride, and here it is metaphysical rather than architectural — the one limit that applies to every person alive is the one he arranged not to accept, and the technology that makes that possible is this cast's own title. His mood is Glory, noon's own triumph: he is killed in a hotel room by his own son and is nevertheless the most powerful entity in the setting six months later.

The seat's rotating partner argues it from the other empire. Rosalind Myers holds the same stillness with no corporate tower to stand on at all — a president who came out of the arms industry and governs a state that has never been able to tell the two apart.
faces.servant:
Yorinobu Arasaka is Sunday's dark face — a man with every qualification for the throne, seated here as the Servant because his entire biography is a service he spent decades denying and then performed.

His virtue is Humility, and it is real before it collapses: he is the only person in the setting born to that name who has ever said out loud that the house should not exist, and he spent years outside it making the point. The vice that stalks it is Servility, and the collapse is the seat's whole argument — a man who kills his father over what the corporation is, and then runs the corporation, has not escaped the office, he has confirmed it. His mood is Awe: he carries a second presence he did not choose and cannot dismiss, and Glory is the same seat's other face.

The rotating partner holds the same position without the surname. Colonel Kurt Hansen deserted one empire's army and built his own out of the pieces, which is the same act performed by somebody with nothing to inherit.

variants.hexa_primary: On the painter's wheel the pair keeps the centre of the dial, white-gold, belonging to no hour: the six arms around them are that light decomposed, one virtue to each spoke. This is the home reading — the source rather than a spoke, an authority that precedes every office it hands out.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism changes every arm around them and cannot change the centre: white remains the sum of all wavelengths. It is the same fact from the other side — the throne is not a seventh power in this cast, it is the condition the other six are operating inside, and killing the man in it did not alter the geometry.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the pair steps onto the noon arm in royal gold (#F0C420), the estate of the King, the Crown for its object — the plainest seat in the set and the only one this cast fills twice over. One built the crown and refused to take it off; the other took it off a corpse and put it on.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the noon arm is Youth, the zenith of a life, and the pair wears sun-yellow (#FFE800). The hue is an accusation rather than a compliment: the father arranged never to leave the zenith, and the son arrived at it by the one route that guarantees nobody will ever believe he earned it.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross the Sunday pair holds 12h on the Summer arm, yellow, aimed at the summer solstice — shared with Thursday. The throne beside the teacher: the year's brightest spoke held by this cast's two institutions, one that transmits and one that only accumulates.
variants.trio: On the Trinity the seat keeps the centre and the cast around it narrows to three arms — Faith yellow, Love red, Hope blue. The geometry is indifferent to who holds it, which is the warning the dual exists to make: the same centre seats the man who would not die and the man who killed him, and the rotation seats two more who are doing the identical thing under another flag.

moon.name: Obi-Wan Kenobi
moon.base:
[[The Figure]] Obi-Wan Kenobi holds Monday because he is the one figure in this cast whose defining act is nineteen years of not acting. When the order he belonged to was destroyed by his own student, he took the surviving child to the least valuable planet in the galaxy and kept watch without intervening once — not because there was nothing to fear, but because everything he feared would have been triggered by any move he made. Serenity on this arm has never meant the absence of fear; it means an accurate fear held still.

[[On the Dial]] His home is the 04h arm in deep blue (#002FFF), the hour the canon names Calm — the emptiest interval of the night, and the only hour of the day whose whole content is waiting. The seat asks for a figure who can hold a position without a task, and this cast has exactly one.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Serenity and the vice is Fear, and the seat holds them at the tightest distance in the whole cast. Everything Kenobi knows argues for panic: the man he trained hunts the child he is guarding, and the child's only defence is that nobody knows where he is. Across the dial at 16h Tuesday's Courage is the named cure for Fear, and the pairing is exact — he does not lack courage, he declines to spend it, because courage spent early would have cost him the whole nineteen years. Serenity is the discipline that makes the delay survivable.

[[The Hour]] *"To every thing there is a season... a time to keep silence, and a time to speak"* (Ecclesiastes 3:1,7). Monday's virtue is knowing which of the two the hour is asking for, and no seat in this cast paid more for the answer.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 04h arm in deep blue (#002FFF), the Calm of the hour before dawn — the base reading, and the only seat in this cast whose whole assignment is to stay put.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism keeps him at 04h and sharpens the blue to #0040FF — pigment's muted night becomes light's electric one. The hour and its Calm do not move; the same stillness simply reads as vigilance rather than as rest, which is what it always was.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Kenobi takes the deep-night arm in lamplit ink blue (#1F5FA8), the estate of the Scholar, the Book for its object. He is the cast's keeper of a record nobody else has: an order's whole practice held in one memory, with no library left and no student to hand it to for two decades.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that deep-night arm is the Unborn, and he turns moonlight silver (#C8D7F0) — the seat the wheel reserves for the not-yet-living. It is exact rather than poetic: his entire nineteen years are spent on a person who does not yet exist in any sense that matters, and he has nothing else to spend them on.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Kenobi moves to the 06h arm — Spring, green, aimed at the vernal equinox — and shares it with Saturday. The season of return holds this cast's two long waiters, and neither of them is waiting for himself.
variants.trio: The Trinity keeps him at 04h and renames the watch: the blue arm now means Hope, guarding the morning from 0h to 8h beside Wednesday. The assignment is the plainest on the wheel — a man who guards a child on the theory that the child will one day be enough is practising hope as an occupation, and it is the only thing he does.

mars.name: General Leia Organa
mars.base:
[[The Figure]] Leia Organa holds Tuesday because her courage is the disciplined kind the arm actually asks for — not a temperament but an office. At nineteen she was interrogated by the commander whose fleet then destroyed her home world while she watched, and she gave up nothing true; thirty years later she held a command structure together after the state that authorised it had ceased to exist. Both are the same act performed at two ranks: refusing to let the loss decide what she does next.

[[On the Dial]] Her home is the 16h arm in ember orange (#DC9600), the Zeal of the working afternoon — heat kept at a working temperature rather than spent all at once. The seat is the Soldier's, and this cast seats it with the only member who commands rather than fights.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Courage and the vice is Wrath, and she is the cast's demonstration that the two are separated by aim rather than by intensity. She has every ground for wrath that any figure here has, and the record shows it converted into logistics every time. Across the dial at 04h Monday's Serenity is the named cure for Wrath, and the two seats hold the same discipline from opposite ends — one waits because moving would cost too much, the other moves because waiting would.

[[The Hour]] *"Courage is a mean with respect to fear and confidence"* (Aristotle, Nicomachean Ethics III). The mean is the whole seat: a general is not the bravest person in the room, she is the one who keeps the room's bravery inside a plan.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 16h arm in ember orange (#DC9600), the Zeal of the working afternoon — the base reading, courage held at the temperature an organisation can actually run on.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism keeps her at 16h and burns the ember up to pure yellow (#FFFF00) — red and green fused. Light gives the same nerve a hotter hue without changing what it is aimed at; the hour and its Zeal are unchanged, and so is the fact that nothing she does is spent on herself.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Leia takes the 15h afternoon in copper (#C87533), the estate of the Merchant, the Coin for its object — a placement that reads wrong until the office is understood. A rebellion has no treasury and no draft; everything it fields was negotiated out of somebody, and she is the one who did the negotiating for forty years.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that afternoon arm is Maturity, and she wears amber (#FFB400). The wheel's own definition is the age at which strength stops being about the person holding it, and hers is the cleanest case in the cast: she is a princess at the start of the story and a general at the end, and the title she loses is the personal one.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Leia takes the 18h arm — Autumn, red, aimed at the autumnal equinox — sharing the spoke with Friday. The season of reckoning holds this cast's two senators, mother and daughter, and the account it settles is the same one twice.
variants.trio: The Trinity moves her to 20h, onto Love's red arm beside Friday, guarding the evening from 16h to 24h. The reading is exact: she never once acted for a doctrine. Every command she gave was aimed at particular people, and the last one was aimed at her son.

mercury.name: Han Solo
mercury.base:
[[The Figure]] Han Solo holds Wednesday because he begins on the arm's vice and is argued onto its virtue, in public, once. He is introduced pricing a rescue, takes the payment, and leaves — and then returns, unpaid and unasked, at the only moment when returning is worth nothing to him. Wisdom on this arm is the merchant's kind, the knowledge of what a thing actually costs, and his whole life is that knowledge applied correctly to everything except the one decision that mattered.

[[On the Dial]] His home is the midnight arm at 0h in Tyrian purple (#542E85), the Sorrow of the closed ledger — the hour at which accounts are settled and nothing further can be added to them. The seat belongs to the Merchant, and this cast fills it with a man whose profession is moving other people's goods past other people's laws.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Wisdom and the vice is Greed, and the seat's argument is that greed is not the love of money but the belief that everything has a price. Across the dial at 12h Thursday's Generosity is the named cure for Greed, and this cast makes the cure literal: the Thursday seat gives away its standing for a stranger, and the Wednesday seat spends one night learning to do the same thing badly. Wisdom curbs Excess on the same axis, which is why the smuggler and the maverick master correct each other rather than agree.

[[The Hour]] *"For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also"* (Matthew 6:21). The seat is held by the one figure in this cast whose treasure demonstrably moves.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the midnight arm at 0h in Tyrian purple (#542E85), the Sorrow of the closed ledger — the base reading, everything valued and nothing yet given away.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns the purple to magenta (#BD00BD) — the one hue found in no rainbow, invented by the eye where the spectrum's two ends are made to meet. Apt for a trade that exists only in the gap between two jurisdictions, and for a man whose entire standing is that he knows where that gap is.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Han shifts to the 21h evening arm in stage-velvet violet (#7A2E8E), the estate of the Artist, the Mask for its object. The placement is not flattery: a smuggler's working capital is a face held steady while two parties are told two different halves of the same arrangement, and he is beaten at it exactly once, by a friend.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that evening arm is Old Age, and he wears dusk violet (#9C6BD4) — held as a fact rather than as a manner. He is one of the few members of this cast the story lets grow old, and what the years actually buy him is the understanding that the ship was never the asset.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Han keeps the bottom arm at 0h — Winter, blue, aimed at the winter solstice — and shares that spoke with nobody. The year's midnight belongs to a single seat, which suits the only figure here who works for himself and makes his decisive choice with no one watching.
variants.trio: The Trinity lifts him off midnight to 04h, onto Hope's blue arm beside Monday, guarding the morning from 0h to 8h. The move is argued by what a smuggler sells: every run is somebody's plan for a life they do not have yet, and this seat is the party that decides which of those plans get carried.

jupiter.name: Qui-Gon Jinn
jupiter.base:
[[The Figure]] Qui-Gon Jinn holds Thursday because his generosity is the kind that costs the giver his standing rather than his surplus. He found a slave child, staked his freedom on a wager he had no authority to make, and pressed the boy's training on a council that had refused it — and when the refusal held, he announced that he would train the boy anyway. Nothing in that sequence is charity. It is a senior man spending the only thing he cannot get back, which is the confidence of his own institution.

[[On the Dial]] His home is the top arm at 12h in noon yellow (#F8E600), the Joy of the day's peak — plenty measured by what leaves rather than by what arrives. The seat is the Priest's and the Teacher's, and this cast gives it to the one master who taught against the school.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Generosity and the vice is Excess, and the seat's honesty is that in this figure they are the same act seen from the two sides of a table. Across the dial at 0h Wednesday's Wisdom curbs Excess, and the pairing is this cast's sharpest: the smuggler who prices everything and the master who prices nothing are each other's only correction. His giving is vindicated by the seat he cannot see — the whole line of the story runs through the child — and indicted by the same one, because so does everything that goes wrong.

[[The Hour]] *"Freely ye have received, freely give"* (Matthew 10:8). Thursday's virtue is stated there without a condition attached, and this seat is what it looks like when somebody takes the sentence literally.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the top arm at 12h in noon yellow (#F8E600), the Joy of the day's peak — the base reading, plenty measured by what leaves rather than by what arrives.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns his noon to green (#00DC00) — the wavelength at the summit of human sight. Fitting for a figure whose contribution is not a victory but a continuation: he wins nothing and hands on everything, and the whole later story is the receipt.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Qui-Gon holds the 09h morning arm in alb ivory (#EDEDE0), the estate of the Priest, the Bell for its object — the one seat in this cast that needs no argument. He is the estate: an office whose whole authority comes from administering something nobody privately owns, held by the only member who ever used it against his own order.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that morning arm is Childhood, and he wears spring green (#7CE577) — read as a disposition rather than as an age. Childhood's traits on this wheel are appetite, certainty and no memory of having been wrong, and his are all three, which is simultaneously why he saw the boy and why he could not see the risk.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Qui-Gon holds 12h on the Summer arm, yellow, aimed at the solstice — sharing the spoke with Sunday. The year's brightest hour holds the teacher and the pupil's pupil: the man who insisted on the training and the hero it eventually produced, two generations apart on one spoke.
variants.trio: On the Trinity Qui-Gon keeps the top arm at 12h, yellow, where the colour now means Faith, shared with Saturday as they guard the day's height from 8h to 16h. He is the least strained tenant this arm has ever had: his position was a conviction with no evidence, argued against every superior he had, and it turned out to be right.

venus.name: Padmé Amidala
venus.base:
[[The Figure]] Padmé Amidala holds Friday because the whole catastrophe this cast is about begins in a love and not in a fall. Elected at fourteen, a senator by twenty-four, she is the figure who keeps arguing for the republic in the chamber that votes it away — and the marriage she holds in secret alongside that office — secret because HIS order forbids attachment, not because hers forbids marriage — is not a lapse in the record, it is the seat. What is seated here is Love; the arm's vice belongs to the man across the table from her, and it is what kills her.

[[On the Dial]] Her home is the 20h arm in deep red (#B60000), the Passion of the evening — the hour at which what a person wants stops being private. The seat is the Artist's, and this cast fills it with a politician, which is the correct joke: her medium is a public performance of a self, sustained for a decade, with one true thing kept out of it.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Love and the vice is Jealousy, and this seat is the dial's proof that they are not two feelings but one arm read from its two ends. Across the dial at 08h Saturday's Patience is the named cure for Jealousy, and the cure is exactly what her husband does not have: the whole ruin proceeds from an unwillingness to wait for a loss that has not happened. She loves a man who cannot bear the arithmetic of loving her, and the seat's honesty is that she is not thereby made a victim of the arm — she is its clearest holder.

[[The Hour]] *"Love is strong as death; jealousy is cruel as the grave"* (Song of Solomon 8:6). The verse names both ends of the arm in one line, and this seat is where the franchise puts them in the same marriage.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 20h arm in deep red (#B60000), the Passion of the evening — the base reading, the seat where the cast's whole chain of consequence actually starts.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism keeps her at 20h and purifies the red to its light primary (#FF0000) — the reddest red there is, unmixed. In the light world Passion is a wavelength rather than a pigment, which suits a figure who is never once ambivalent about anything she wants.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Padmé shifts to the 18h sunset arm in iron-blood crimson (#A02020), the estate of the Soldier, the Sword for its object — a placement she would have rejected and earned anyway. She commanded an invaded planet's recapture at fourteen and spent the rest of her life in the only fight this cast never wins, which is the one conducted in a chamber.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that sunset arm belongs to the Elder, the harvest of a life, and she deepens to ember (#FF6A3C). The fit is ironic and precise: she is among the shortest-lived figures in the cast and the one whose harvest is entirely posthumous, since everything she produced arrives after she is gone and under other names.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Padmé takes the 18h arm — Autumn, red, aimed at the autumnal equinox — sharing the spoke with Tuesday. Two seats that live entirely in public, held here by a mother and a daughter who never meet, on the season that counts what a life actually produced.
variants.trio: The seat does not move: the Trinity's Love arm is its own 20h in its own red. Tuesday joins it, and the two guard the evening from 16h to 24h — the arm held by this cast's proof that being loved and being possessed are different facts, and that only one of them is survivable.

saturn.name: Chewbacca
saturn.base:
[[The Figure]] Chewbacca holds Saturday because he is the longest continuous act of patience in the cast and its least acknowledged. He is roughly two centuries old, bound by a life debt to a man a small fraction of his age, and the arrangement runs for the whole of the story without renegotiation. Patience on this arm is duration rather than tolerance: not the capacity to endure an irritation, but the capacity to keep a commitment past the point where anyone is still counting it.

[[On the Dial]] His home is the 08h arm in field green (#007E00), the Renewal of the morning — the hour of work resumed rather than begun. The seat is the Farmer's, and it goes here to the only member of the cast whose actual daily occupation is keeping a machine running so that other people can make history in it.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Patience and the vice is Envy, and the seat is argued by the most famous omission in the franchise: at the ceremony where the survivors are decorated, he is the one who is not. Across the dial at 20h Friday's Love dissolves Envy, and the cure is what he actually runs on — the debt is owed to a person, not to a cause, which is why the absence of a medal never once alters his conduct. A figure with the strongest grievance in the cast and no trace of the vice is the cleanest possible tenant of an arm that names both.

[[The Hour]] *"Let patience have her perfect work"* (James 1:4). The perfect work of this seat is measured in decades and is never once described as a sacrifice by the one making it.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 08h arm in field green (#007E00), the Renewal of the morning — the base reading, loyalty practised as a trade rather than announced as a virtue.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns his morning green to cyan (#00DDDD) — the colour of the clear early sky rather than of the ground under it. Renewal keeps the hour; light names what the repeated repair is for instead of the labour of making it.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Chewbacca takes the dawn arm, 06h, in field green (#3E8914), the estate of the Farmer, the Plough for its object — the one estate whose method is literally his. A farmer's authority comes from having been present for every stage of the same ground, and no other figure here has been present for every stage of anything.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the dawn arm is Birth, and he wears predawn mist (#8FA8C8) — earned rather than assigned. He is the seat that makes the others possible: nothing this cast achieves happens without a ship that keeps starting, and the ship keeps starting because of one member.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Chewbacca moves to 06h — Spring, green, aimed at the vernal equinox — sharing the spoke with Monday. The season of return held by this cast's two long waiters: one guards a child for nineteen years, the other keeps a promise for two hundred, and neither is ever thanked in the same room.
variants.trio: The Trinity promotes him from the morning to the crown: the 12h Faith arm, yellow, shared with Thursday, guarding the day's height from 8h to 16h. The reading is exact — a life debt is a position held on no evidence for two centuries, which is the arm's definition with the theology removed.

sun.name: Young Luke · Vader
sun.base:
[[The Figure]] Sunday's seat is a father and the son who refused to kill him, which is the only version of this dual in the whole instrument where the two faces are the same body twice. Luke Skywalker holds the bright face: a farm boy with no training, no lineage he is aware of, and a moral certainty he has never had occasion to test. Anakin Skywalker holds the dark one under the name Vader — the same seat's earlier occupant, twenty years into a service he entered voluntarily and has not been able to leave.

[[On the Dial]] The centre holds no arm and no hour. White-gold is the sum of every hue the wheel can mix, and the six seats around it are that light taken apart — a vigil, a command, a bargain, a gift, a marriage, a debt. The throne is what the source looks like before anything is subtracted, and in this cast it is held by the least experienced person in it, which is the argument rather than an accident.

[[The Lesson]] The bundle gives the ruler face Justice against Pride and the servant face Humility against Servility. The Ruler's justice is the rarest kind on this dial: at the decisive moment he declines to execute, and the refusal is not mercy toward an enemy but a verdict on what winning by that route would make him. His Pride is the untested certainty that walks into an obvious trap on the strength of a feeling. The Servant's servility is total and self-inflicted; his humility arrives once and is decisive, which is exactly the claim this seat makes about the shadow face everywhere it appears — the servant is not the evil half, he is the half that obeys.

[[The Hour]] *"Honour thy father and thy mother"* (Exodus 20:12). The commandment is given no exemption for what the father has become, and this seat is the franchise's own answer to the question that raises.

faces.ruler:
Luke Skywalker is Sunday's bright face, and the argument for the seat is that he holds the throne with none of the qualifications the other casts require of it. No rank, no office, no inheritance he knows about — the centre is given to the one member of this cast who has not yet done anything and is nevertheless the source the other six are read against.

His virtue is Justice, and his version of it is a refusal: offered a victory that requires an execution, he throws the weapon away, and the dial's whole reading of the seat turns on that being the strongest available move rather than the gentlest. The vice that stalks it is Pride, and in this figure it is conviction rather than vanity — an untested certainty that abandons an unfinished training on an intuition and walks into a trap prepared for exactly that trait. His mood is Glory, noon's own triumph, and it is earned in the one scene where he does nothing at all.

The seat's shadow face is not an enemy from another house. It is the same office, held first, by the person he is most closely related to.
faces.servant:
Vader is Sunday's dark face — the Father, and the servant of the seat in the strictest sense the canon allows: a man of enormous capability whose entire twenty-year record consists of executing another man's decisions.

His virtue is Humility, and it exists as a single act rather than as a disposition: at the end he moves against the master he has obeyed since the day he was maimed, and does it for one person rather than for a cause. The vice that stalks it is Servility, and the seat's indictment is that the service was chosen. He is not conscripted, blackmailed or deceived about the nature of the arrangement; he takes it to prevent a loss and is thereby made the instrument of every loss that follows. His mood is Awe — the servant's own reading of the throne, a presence acknowledged rather than enjoyed.

Opposition is not evil on this dial, and this face is why the rule is worth stating: the shadow half of a throne is the half that obeys, and the whole tragedy is that it obeyed the wrong throne for two decades and the right one for four minutes.

variants.hexa_primary: On the painter's wheel the pair keeps the centre of the dial, white-gold, belonging to no hour: the six arms around them are that light decomposed, one virtue to each spoke. This is the home reading — the source rather than a spoke, and in this cast the source is a family.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism changes every arm around them and cannot change the centre: white remains the sum of all wavelengths. It is the same fact from the other side — the father and the son are not two positions on this wheel, they are one position occupied twice, which is the reason the reveal works at all.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the pair steps onto the noon arm in royal gold (#F0C420), the estate of the King, the Crown for its object — a crown neither of them accepts. One is offered an empire and refuses it in the same room where the other was offered it and did not.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the noon arm is Youth, the zenith of a life, and the pair wears sun-yellow (#FFE800) — a seat this dual holds twice over. The son is at his literal zenith; the father is a man whose youth was ended by the bargain that made him, and the wheel puts them on the same arm to say so.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross the Sunday pair holds 12h on the Summer arm, yellow, aimed at the summer solstice — shared with Thursday. The year's brightest spoke holds the throne and the master who insisted on training the man who would fill its shadow half: the cause and the consequence on one line.
variants.trio: On the Trinity the seat keeps the centre and the cast narrows to three arms — Faith yellow, Love red, Hope blue. The geometry is indifferent to who holds it, which is the warning this dual exists to make: the same centre seats the man who threw the weapon away and the man who did not, and it does not adjudicate between them.

moon.name: Grand Moff Tarkin
moon.base:
[[The Figure]] Tarkin holds Monday because he is the only figure in the franchise who states the arm's vice as a governing doctrine and signs his name to it. Fear, in his formulation, is not an effect of power but its delivery mechanism: dissolve the representative bodies, hold the regions in line by terror of the battle station, and the administration of an empire becomes an engineering problem. He is a bureaucrat rather than a warlord, and the seat takes him for that reason.

[[On the Dial]] His home is the 04h arm in deep blue (#002FFF), the hour the canon names Calm — the emptiest interval of the night. Nothing on the dial is colder than a seat whose virtue is composure held by a man whose composure is total and whose output is the destruction of a populated world without a raised voice.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Serenity and the vice is Fear, and this seat is the instrument's demonstration that a vice can be administered rather than suffered. Everyone else on this arm across the whole dial is afraid; he is the one who issues it. Across the dial at 16h Tuesday's Courage is the named cure, and the cure fails here for a structural reason — courage answers fear in the person feeling it, and this figure has arranged to be permanently on the other end. His own serenity is real and is the worst thing about him: a man who cannot be provoked is a man no argument reaches.

[[The Hour]] *"The fear of man bringeth a snare"* (Proverbs 29:25). The proverb warns the frightened; this seat is held by the one who sets it.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 04h arm in deep blue (#002FFF), the Calm of the hour before dawn — the base reading, and the coldest tenancy this arm has: composure with nothing behind it that an argument could reach.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism keeps him at 04h and sharpens the blue to #0040FF — pigment's muted night becomes light's electric one. The hour and its Calm do not move; the reading simply goes clinical, which is the temperature of every order this seat ever gave.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Tarkin takes the deep-night arm in lamplit ink blue (#1F5FA8), the estate of the Scholar, the Book for its object — the estate at its most dangerous. He is the cast's theorist: the doctrine that organises the whole Empire's behaviour was written by him, and every uniform below him is executing a paper.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that deep-night arm is the Unborn, and he turns moonlight silver (#C8D7F0) — the seat the wheel reserves for the not-yet-living. The fit is exact and unpleasant: his whole programme is aimed at a permanent order that does not exist yet, and the populations he spends on it are treated as an input to it.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Tarkin moves to the 06h arm — Spring, green, aimed at the vernal equinox — and shares it with Saturday. The season of return holds this cast's two professionals: one waits for a target and the other waits for compliance, and both are paid by the hour.
variants.trio: The Trinity keeps him at 04h and renames the watch: the blue arm now means Hope, guarding the morning from 0h to 8h beside Wednesday. The arm has never held a harder tenant — his doctrine is a hope, in the technical sense, that terror is cheaper than consent, and the story exists to test it.

mars.name: General Grievous
mars.base:
[[The Figure]] Grievous holds Tuesday because he is the cleanest separation of the arm's virtue from the arm's vice anywhere on the dial. He is the Separatist armies' supreme commander, rebuilt into a machine to fight better, and he collects the weapons of the Jedi he kills. He is also, without exception, the figure who withdraws the moment a fight turns against him. Ferocity and courage are different faculties, and this seat is the proof.

[[On the Dial]] His home is the 16h arm in ember orange (#DC9600), the Zeal of the working afternoon — heat at a working temperature. The seat belongs to the Soldier, and this cast gives it to a general whose troops are manufactured and whose own body has been replaced by degrees, which is the arm's question asked at its harshest: what is left of a soldier when everything but the appetite has been swapped out.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Courage and the vice is Wrath, and the trophies settle it. A collection of the weapons of the dead is wrath converted into an inventory — an appetite that has outlived every cause it was hired to serve. Across the dial at 04h Monday's Serenity quells Wrath, and in this cast the Monday seat is the man who commands him and does it by never raising his voice; the two are on the same axis for a reason. The seat's verdict is that a fighter who flees whenever the odds turn was never on the virtue's half of this arm at all.

[[The Hour]] *"He that is slow to anger is better than the mighty; and he that ruleth his spirit than he that taketh a city"* (Proverbs 16:32). Tuesday's whole distinction is in that sentence, and this seat sits on the wrong side of it deliberately.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 16h arm in ember orange (#DC9600), the Zeal of the working afternoon — the base reading, appetite kept at a working temperature by a body built to hold it.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism keeps him at 16h and burns the ember up to pure yellow (#FFFF00) — red and green fused. Light gives the same nerve a hotter hue without giving it an object, which is the whole diagnosis: the hour and its Zeal are unchanged and there is nothing underneath them.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Grievous takes the 15h afternoon in copper (#C87533), the estate of the Merchant, the Coin for its object — stranger than the Soldier's and truer. He trades in the only currency this cast respects: he is bought, he is upgraded, and his trophies are an account book kept in the one denomination that could not be spent.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that afternoon arm is Maturity, and he wears amber (#FFB400). The wheel's definition is the age at which strength stops being about the person holding it, and this seat is the inversion: everything he acquired was acquired to make the holder larger, and there is finally no holder left to be larger.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Grievous takes the 18h arm — Autumn, red, aimed at the equinox — sharing the spoke with Friday. The season of reckoning holds this cast's two collectors: one keeps the weapons of the dead and the other keeps a grudge, and both are counted at the same harvest.
variants.trio: The Trinity moves him to 20h, onto Love's red arm beside Friday, guarding the evening from 16h to 24h. The placement is the wheel's harshest joke and it is argued: courage aimed at a person is what this arm is called, and he is the one figure here who has never aimed anything at a person — only at a category.

mercury.name: Jabba the Hutt
mercury.base:
[[The Figure]] Jabba holds Wednesday because his power is entirely a ledger. He commands no army and holds no office; what he holds is debt, and the whole desert operates on the assumption that his accounts are collectible. Wisdom on this arm is the merchant's kind — knowing what a thing actually costs — and he has that faculty in full and nothing else beside it, which is precisely why the seat's vice is where he lives.

[[On the Dial]] His home is the midnight arm at 0h in Tyrian purple (#542E85), the Sorrow of the closed ledger. The hour is the one at which nothing further can be added to an account, and this seat is held by a creature who keeps a settled debt displayed on his wall rather than written off — greed that has stopped even pretending to be commerce.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Wisdom and the vice is Greed, and the distinction the seat draws is that greed is not the accumulation of money but the conviction that everything is priced. Across the dial at 12h Thursday's Generosity cures Greed; nothing in this figure's record is given, and the one thing he refuses to sell is the one thing he was offered a fair price for. A debtor kept as an ornament is the exact moment a trade becomes an appetite, and this cast's Wednesday is where the instrument puts it.

[[The Hour]] *"He that loveth silver shall not be satisfied with silver"* (Ecclesiastes 5:10). The verse is a description of a mechanism rather than a moral, and this seat is the mechanism running unopposed.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the midnight arm at 0h in Tyrian purple (#542E85), the Sorrow of the closed ledger — the base reading, an account that is never written off and never spent.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns the purple to magenta (#BD00BD) — the one hue found in no rainbow, invented by the eye where the spectrum's two ends are made to meet. Apt for a power that exists only in the gap between what is legal and what is enforced, and holds that gap as a territory.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Jabba shifts to the 21h evening arm in stage-velvet violet (#7A2E8E), the estate of the Artist, the Mask for its object — the estate inverted. His court is a permanent performance staged for an audience of debtors, and the only function of the spectacle is to make the size of the account visible to everybody who owes on it.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that evening arm is Old Age, and he wears dusk violet (#9C6BD4) — held as an institution rather than as a manner. Hutt seniority is measured in centuries and converted directly into leverage, which is what makes this seat's version of the age the least sympathetic on the wheel: nothing about it has been learned.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Jabba keeps the bottom arm at 0h — Winter, blue, aimed at the winter solstice — and shares that spoke with nobody. The year's midnight belongs to a single seat, and a creditor is the one figure here whose decisive acts are all performed by declining to move.
variants.trio: The Trinity lifts him off midnight to 04h, onto Hope's blue arm beside Monday, guarding the morning from 0h to 8h. The move is argued by what a debt actually is: a claim on a future that has not happened, held by the party least interested in whether it arrives.

jupiter.name: Count Dooku
jupiter.base:
[[The Figure]] Dooku holds Thursday because he is the cast's teacher, and every gift he makes is an instrument. He was a Jedi master of the first rank, trained the Jedi cast's own Thursday, and left the order over a diagnosis that was substantially correct: the Republic was corrupt and the order had made itself its enforcement arm. What he built on that correct diagnosis was a war designed by the man he served, and the truth he hands to a prisoner is handed at the moment it can do no good.

[[On the Dial]] His home is the top arm at 12h in noon yellow (#F8E600), the Joy of the day's peak — plenty measured by what leaves. The seat is the Priest's and the Teacher's, held here by an aristocrat who left an order, took a title, and spent the remainder distributing convictions he no longer had.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Generosity and the vice is Excess, and this seat is where the instrument shows the counterfeit. Generosity gives without a return; what this figure distributes — a truth, an army, an apprenticeship — always returns to the giver at a profit. Across the dial at 0h Wednesday's Wisdom curbs Excess, and the cure is unavailable to him because he has the wisdom and uses it as the instrument of the excess. The seat is also this cast's exact mirror of the Jedi Thursday: the same office and the same lineage, one master spending his standing for a stranger and the other spending a stranger for his standing.

[[The Hour]] *"Beware of false prophets, which come to you in sheep's clothing"* (Matthew 7:15). The warning is specifically about a teacher, which is the only reason it fits this arm.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the top arm at 12h in noon yellow (#F8E600), the Joy of the day's peak — the base reading, generosity's own hour held by the seat that counterfeits it.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns his noon to green (#00DC00) — the wavelength at the summit of human sight. Fitting for a figure whose public argument is the most persuasive in the cast and whose private position is a subordinate one: the brightest thing on the wheel is not the thing at the top of it.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Dooku holds the 09h morning arm in alb ivory (#EDEDE0), the estate of the Priest, the Bell for its object. He is the only member of this cast who ever held the estate legitimately and resigned it, and everything he does afterwards is the office performed without the ordination — a doctrine preached by a man who has stopped believing the part that would bind him.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that morning arm is Childhood, and he wears spring green (#7CE577) — read as a disposition rather than as an age. Childhood's traits on this wheel are appetite, certainty and no memory of having been wrong, and the most cultivated figure in the cast has all three, which is the seat's real indictment of him.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Dooku holds 12h on the Summer arm, yellow, aimed at the solstice — sharing the spoke with Sunday. The year's brightest hour holds the master and the master's master: the whole lineage of the Rule of Two standing on one spoke, each member having replaced the one above him.
variants.trio: On the Trinity he keeps the top arm at 12h, yellow, where the colour now means Faith, shared with Saturday as they guard the day's height from 8h to 16h. The strain is the point — this arm asks for a position held without evidence, and he is the figure who held one, lost it, and kept preaching the sentences.

venus.name: Maul
venus.base:
[[The Figure]] Maul holds Friday because he is jealousy in its long form: an attachment to one man, sustained for decades past the body it was formed in, with the affection removed and the intensity kept. He was raised as an instrument, discarded the first time he failed, survived that too, and spent the remainder of his life organising everything he could reach around a single person who had stopped thinking about him. The arm's vice is rarely this legible.

[[On the Dial]] His home is the 20h arm in deep red (#B60000), the Passion of the evening — the hour at which what a person wants stops being private. The seat is the Artist's, and this cast fills it with the figure whose entire output is one sustained work on a single subject.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Love and the vice is Jealousy, and the seat's claim is that they are one arm read from two ends. He has exactly one attachment in the record — a brother — and loses it, and everything afterwards is that capacity aimed backwards. Across the dial at 08h Saturday's Patience is the named cure for Jealousy, and he has an inhuman quantity of the wrong kind: he waits decades, and the waiting does not heal the wound, it preserves it. Patience without an object is simply a longer grudge, which is why the cure has to come from the arm across and not from the same one.

[[The Hour]] *"For jealousy is the rage of a man: therefore he will not spare in the day of vengeance"* (Proverbs 6:34). The verse describes a duration rather than an outburst, which is exactly what this seat holds.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 20h arm in deep red (#B60000), the Passion of the evening — the base reading, one attachment aimed backwards and kept at full temperature for decades.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism keeps him at 20h and purifies the red to its light primary (#FF0000) — the reddest red there is, unmixed. In the light world Passion is a wavelength rather than a pigment, and unmixed is the correct description: nothing else was ever added to this seat's motive.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Maul shifts to the 18h sunset arm in iron-blood crimson (#A02020), the estate of the Soldier, the Sword for its object — the estate held by a man who was manufactured for it. He is the cast's only figure raised from childhood to be a weapon and never given a war of his own, which is why the weapon eventually points at a person.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that sunset arm belongs to the Elder, the harvest of a life, and he deepens to ember (#FF6A3C). The harvest is the seat's whole verdict: he outlives his master, his order, his war and his own body, and at the end of the accumulation there is one name and nothing else in the ledger.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Maul takes the 18h arm — Autumn, red, aimed at the autumnal equinox — sharing the spoke with Tuesday. The season of reckoning holds this cast's two collectors, and the difference between them is that one kept trophies and the other kept only the grievance.
variants.trio: The seat does not move: the Trinity's Love arm is its own 20h in its own red. Tuesday joins it, and the two guard the evening from 16h to 24h — the arm held here by the cast's proof that the faculty this colour names is indifferent to its object, and will run for fifty years on a hatred as readily as on anything else.

saturn.name: Boba Fett
saturn.base:
[[The Figure]] Boba Fett holds Saturday because waiting is his entire professional method and he is famous for almost nothing else. A bounty hunter is a man paid to be slower than his target: he does not intercept, he arrives afterwards, and the one contract everybody remembers is won by hiding among garbage and following. Patience on this arm is duration applied as a technique, and no other figure in this cast has one.

[[On the Dial]] His home is the 08h arm in field green (#007E00), the Renewal of the morning — the hour of work resumed. The seat is the Farmer's, which is the correct estate for a trade whose whole economics are seasonal: a hunter is idle for long stretches and paid for the one week the work is possible.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Patience and the vice is Envy, and the seat holds them in an unusually literal arrangement. He is a clone of his father, raised as the one copy that was not produced for the army — an identity defined against thousands of men with the same face, which is envy's own founding condition. Across the dial at 20h Friday's Love dissolves Envy, and the record gives him one attachment and takes it away early. What remains is the virtue practised without any of the qualities that usually accompany it: a man who waits perfectly, for money.

[[The Hour]] *"The patient in spirit is better than the proud in spirit"* (Ecclesiastes 7:8). The verse ranks the two without requiring the patient man to be good, which is why it fits this seat exactly.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 08h arm in field green (#007E00), the Renewal of the morning — the base reading, patience practised as a paid technique rather than as a temperament.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns his morning green to cyan (#00DDDD) — the colour of the clear early sky rather than of the ground under it. Renewal keeps the hour; light names what the waiting is for instead of the labour of doing it, and in this seat what it is for is a fee.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Boba Fett takes the dawn arm, 06h, in field green (#3E8914), the estate of the Farmer, the Plough for its object — an estate whose method is genuinely his. A farmer's authority comes from having been present for every stage of the same ground; a hunter's comes from having been present for every stage of the same man's movements.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the dawn arm is Birth, and he wears predawn mist (#8FA8C8) — assigned with a bitter accuracy. He is the only figure in this cast whose birth is a manufacturing decision, requested as a payment and delivered unaltered, and the wheel's youngest seat is where the instrument puts that fact.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross he moves to 06h — Spring, green, aimed at the vernal equinox — sharing the spoke with Monday. The season of return held by this cast's two professionals: the one who writes the doctrine and the one who is hired under it, neither of whom has ever done anything out of conviction.
variants.trio: The Trinity promotes him from the morning to the crown: the 12h Faith arm, yellow, shared with Thursday, guarding the day's height from 8h to 16h. The reading is exact and cold — a contract is a position held for weeks on the assumption that a stranger will pay at the end of it, and there is no way to verify that in advance.

sun.name: Palpatine · Anakin
sun.base:
[[The Figure]] Sunday's seat is a master and the apprentice he assembled, and it is the only throne in this instrument whose holder wins outright. Palpatine holds the bright face: a senator, then a chancellor, then an emperor, each promotion granted to him by the body he was dismantling. Anakin Skywalker holds the dark one: recruited at nine, cultivated for over a decade by a man who was simultaneously his mentor and the author of every emergency he was mentored through.

[[On the Dial]] The centre holds no arm and no hour. White-gold is the sum of every hue the wheel can mix, and the six seats around it are that light taken apart — a doctrine, an appetite, a ledger, a lesson, a grudge, a contract. The throne is what the source looks like before anything is subtracted, and in this cast the source is a procedure rather than a person: two chairs, one occupied and one being prepared.

[[The Lesson]] The bundle gives the ruler face Justice against Pride and the servant face Humility against Servility. The Ruler's justice is the counterfeit at its most complete: every step of the seizure is lawful, voted, and applauded, and the seat's whole argument is that legality and justice are separable and this figure is the demonstration. His Pride is the declaration that he is the institution. The Servant's servility is the seat's indictment — a man of the largest capability in the cast who spends it entirely on obedience — and his humility is the single act that ends the arrangement. Nothing sits opposite the centre, so the two correct each other and nobody else does; here the correction takes twenty years.

[[The Hour]] *"And ye shall cry out in that day because of your king which ye shall have chosen"* (1 Samuel 8:18). The verse is about a people who ask for the throne and are warned about the bill, which is the exact sequence this seat records.

faces.ruler:
Palpatine is Sunday's bright face, and the argument for the seat is that no other figure in the franchise ever held the throne legitimately. Every office he occupies is conferred: elected senator, elected chancellor, granted emergency powers by acclamation, and finally handed an empire by a chamber that voted for it.

His virtue is Justice, and the seat takes him precisely because his version is procedurally impeccable and substantively void — an order that is regular, enforced and predictable, which is what the word means to a legalist and not what it means here. The vice that stalks it is Pride, and his is the most literal on the dial: he identifies himself with the institution out loud, which is the moment a ruler stops being a holder of an office and becomes its replacement. His mood is Glory, noon's own triumph, and he is the only figure in these three casts who actually gets it.

The seat's shadow face is not his enemy. It is the instrument he built to hold the office's other half, and it is the only thing that ever removes him.
faces.servant:
Anakin Skywalker is Sunday's dark face — the servant of this seat in the strictest sense the canon allows, and the reason the dual is an argument rather than a moral.

His virtue is Humility, and it exists here as a capacity rather than a practice: he is the only figure in the cast who was ever owned, freed, and then chose a second master, and a man who knows what service is has the knowledge the virtue is built from. The vice that stalks it is Servility, and it is the seat's whole indictment — the service was chosen, entered to prevent one loss, and it produced every loss that followed including the one it was entered to prevent. His mood is Awe: the servant's own reading of the throne, a presence acknowledged rather than enjoyed, and in this cast the presence was manufacturing the emergencies that produced the awe.

The same man sits again in the Jedi cast's own Mirror, twenty years later and under another name, and the two articles argue different deeds: this one argues the recruitment, that one argues the reversal.

variants.hexa_primary: On the painter's wheel the pair keeps the centre of the dial, white-gold, belonging to no hour: the six arms around them are that light decomposed, one virtue to each spoke. This is the home reading — the source rather than a spoke, and this cast's source is an office with two chairs in it.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism changes every arm around them and cannot change the centre: white remains the sum of all wavelengths. It is the same fact from the other side — the Rule this lineage runs on says there are always exactly two, and the geometry of a centre and its shadow says the same thing without needing the doctrine.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the pair steps onto the noon arm in royal gold (#F0C420), the estate of the King, the Crown for its object — the only crown in these three casts that is actually worn. One of them is given it by a vote and the other is given the second chair, and the difference between the two is the whole of the servant's biography.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the noon arm is Youth, the zenith of a life, and the pair wears sun-yellow (#FFE800). The fit is the seat's cruellest: the master's zenith arrives at the end of a long career and lasts two decades, and the apprentice's is spent before he is twenty-five, sold in advance to buy the master's.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross the Sunday pair holds 12h on the Summer arm, yellow, aimed at the summer solstice — shared with Thursday. The year's brightest spoke holds the lineage: the master, the apprentice, and the aristocrat who occupied the second chair between them, each having replaced the one before him.
variants.trio: On the Trinity the seat keeps the centre and the cast narrows to three arms — Faith yellow, Love red, Hope blue. The geometry is indifferent to who holds it, which is the warning this dual exists to make: the same centre seats the man who arranged the fall and the man who executed it, and it does not distinguish between them by position alone.

moon.name: Rose Tico
moon.base:
[[The Figure]] Rose Tico holds Monday because her serenity is built out of care rather than out of the absence of fear, and the seat has no other tenant in these three casts who arrives at it that way. She is a maintenance engineer, not a pilot or a commander; her sister dies in the opening hours of the story; and on the same night she stops a man from spending his life on a gesture. Both halves of that are the arm: a person who has just lost everything and whose first act is to prevent a loss.

[[On the Dial]] Her home is the 04h arm in deep blue (#002FFF), the hour the canon names Calm — the emptiest interval of the night, and the one in which grief has nothing to do but sit still. The seat is the Physician's, and this cast fills it with somebody who repairs machines, which is the same office performed on the other kind of body.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Serenity and the vice is Fear, and her position on the arm is stated by her own formulation: that the war is won by saving what one loves rather than by destroying what one hates. Read as symbolism rather than as sentiment, it is a claim about which of two motives survives contact with exhaustion. Across the dial at 16h Tuesday's Courage is the named cure for Fear, and this seat's argument is that the cure is not always the right prescription — the Tuesday seat of this cast is held by two people who ran, one away from an institution and one at a target, and the Monday seat is the one who asks what the running is for.

[[The Hour]] *"There is no fear in love; but perfect love casteth out fear"* (1 John 4:18). The verse states the arm's cure as a mechanism rather than as an encouragement, and this seat is where the cast puts it.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 04h arm in deep blue (#002FFF), the Calm of the hour before dawn — the base reading, composure assembled out of care by the one figure here with the least reason to have any.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism keeps her at 04h and sharpens the blue to #0040FF — pigment's muted night becomes light's electric one. The hour and its Calm do not move; the reading simply goes practical, which is what a mechanic's version of this virtue looks like from outside.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Rose takes the deep-night arm in lamplit ink blue (#1F5FA8), the estate of the Scholar, the Book for its object — earned by competence rather than by study. She is the only member of this cast who knows how the machinery everybody else is riding actually works, and the whole plan of that night depends on her knowing it.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that deep-night arm is the Unborn, and she turns moonlight silver (#C8D7F0) — the seat the wheel reserves for the not-yet-living. It is exact: her whole position is that a war is fought for people who are not in the room, and she is the one who says so out loud.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Rose moves to the 06h arm — Spring, green, aimed at the vernal equinox — and shares it with Saturday. The season of return holds this cast's two subordinates: one repairs what the command wrecks and the other resents having to, and only one of them is any use.
variants.trio: The Trinity keeps her at 04h and renames the watch: the blue arm now means Hope, guarding the morning from 0h to 8h beside Wednesday. The assignment is the plainest in the cast — she is the figure whose stated position is about what the fighting is for, and the arm is named after exactly that question.

mars.name: Finn · Phasma
mars.base:
[[The Figure]] Tuesday is held by two soldiers produced by the same institution, and the seat rotates between them because the arm's question has two complete answers. Finn was taken as an infant, conditioned to be interchangeable, and refused an order to fire on civilians in the first hour he was given one. Phasma commanded that institution's troopers and never once chose against it — and when a weapon was held to her own head she lowered her base's shields rather than die for it, which is obedience revealed as self-preservation.

[[On the Dial]] The seat's home is the 16h arm in ember orange (#DC9600), the Zeal of the working afternoon. It belongs to the Soldier, and this cast fills it with two of them: the deserter and the officer, which is the only pairing on the whole dial where both members wear the identical uniform.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Courage and the vice is Wrath, and the argument is that courage is not the willingness to fight — both these figures fight competently — but the willingness to bear the cost of a decision. One of them makes exactly one decision and pays for it for the rest of the story. The other never makes one at all: she executes flawlessly until the moment execution would cost her personally, and then complies with whoever is holding the weapon. Across the dial at 04h Monday's Serenity quells Wrath, and this cast's Monday seat is the person who talks the deserter out of the wrath he eventually acquires.

[[The Hour]] *"The wicked flee when no man pursueth: but the righteous are bold as a lion"* (Proverbs 28:1). The seat is the verse read carefully: one of these two ran first and stopped running, and the other never ran and never once chose anything.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 16h arm in ember orange (#DC9600), the Zeal of the working afternoon — the base reading, held by two products of one training programme and separated only by what each did with it.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism keeps the seat at 16h and burns the ember up to pure yellow (#FFFF00) — red and green fused. Light gives the same nerve a hotter hue without giving it an object; the hour and its Zeal are unchanged, and the difference between these two is entirely what each aimed it at.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the seat takes the 15h afternoon in copper (#C87533), the estate of the Merchant, the Coin for its object — a placement neither would claim and both earn. Both were bought: one conscripted as an infant and one promoted into a chain of command, and each is priced by the same institution in the same currency.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that afternoon arm is Maturity, and the seat wears amber (#FFB400). The wheel's definition is the age at which strength stops being about the person holding it — the deserter reaches it the moment he goes back for somebody, and the captain never reaches it at all, because her strength was never once hers to spend.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross the seat takes the 18h arm — Autumn, red, aimed at the equinox — sharing the spoke with Friday. The season of reckoning holds this cast's two returns: a man who comes back for a friend and a father who walks toward a son, and both are counted at the same harvest.
variants.trio: The Trinity moves the seat to 20h, onto Love's red arm beside Friday, guarding the evening from 16h to 24h. The reading separates the two members cleanly — the deserter's every act after the first is aimed at named people, and the captain's are aimed at an order, which is the whole distinction this arm exists to draw.

mercury.name: Maz Kanata · DJ
mercury.base:
[[The Figure]] Wednesday is held by two dealers in the same commodity, and the seat rotates because the arm's virtue and its vice are the identical trade at two prices. Maz Kanata has run a waystation for something over a thousand years, has watched every side of the same war pass through it, and keeps what matters rather than selling it. DJ is a codebreaker who takes a commission, delivers it, and then sells the same information to the other party in the same night.

[[On the Dial]] The seat's home is the midnight arm at 0h in Tyrian purple (#542E85), the Sorrow of the closed ledger — the hour at which accounts settle. It belongs to the Merchant, and this cast fills it with two merchants of information rather than of goods, which is the only commodity that can be sold twice without being moved.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Wisdom and the vice is Greed, and the seat's argument is that the difference is not in what a person knows but in what a person will attach a price to. A thousand years of accumulated understanding, given away free at the moment it is needed; a single night's technical skill, sold to both sides because both were buying. Across the dial at 12h Thursday's Generosity cures Greed, and this cast's Thursday is the seat that gives away command — the same medicine at a much higher dose.

[[The Hour]] *"Buy the truth, and sell it not"* (Proverbs 23:23). Both members of this seat bought it. Only one of them obeyed the second half.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the midnight arm at 0h in Tyrian purple (#542E85), the Sorrow of the closed ledger — the base reading, one commodity held by two people who price it differently.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns the purple to magenta (#BD00BD) — the one hue found in no rainbow, invented by the eye where the spectrum's two ends are made to meet. Apt for a trade that exists only in the gap between two parties who have not been introduced, and that both members of this seat live in.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the seat shifts to the 21h evening arm in stage-velvet violet (#7A2E8E), the estate of the Artist, the Mask for its object — the truest placement in this cast. A waystation keeper and a codebreaker both work by holding one face steady while two parties are told two different halves of an arrangement; the difference is that one of them does it to keep the peace and the other to raise the fee.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that evening arm is Old Age, and the seat wears dusk violet (#9C6BD4) — held as a fact by one member and refused by the other. A thousand years is not a courtesy title, it is evidence; and the seat's other tenant behaves as though nothing before tonight has any bearing on tonight, which is the same age inverted.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross the seat keeps the bottom arm at 0h — Winter, blue, aimed at the winter solstice — and it alone shares that spoke with nobody. The year's midnight belongs to a single seat, and a dealer in information is the one figure here whose decisive acts are all performed alone, before any other party knows a decision was available.
variants.trio: The Trinity lifts the seat off midnight to 04h, onto Hope's blue arm beside Monday, guarding the morning from 0h to 8h. The move is argued by what this trade actually sells: every transaction is somebody's plan for a night they have not survived yet, and this seat decides which of those plans get the information they need.

jupiter.name: Old Leia
jupiter.base:
[[The Figure]] Leia Organa holds Thursday in this cast, thirty years after the seat she holds in the Jedi one, and the deed argued here is a different deed. What the older woman does is hand things over: a command she built, a training she never completed and gives to somebody else, and finally her own life, spent in a single act aimed at a son who is already most of the way gone. Generosity on this arm is the surrender of something that cannot be got back, and by this age she has nothing left that is merely surplus.

[[On the Dial]] Her home here is the top arm at 12h in noon yellow (#F8E600), the Joy of the day's peak — plenty measured by what leaves rather than by what arrives. The instrument's rule is that a figure keeps its colour wherever it reappears when that is possible; here it is not, because the seat is chosen by the deed and this deed is not the interrogation that seats her younger self on the orange arm.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Generosity and the vice is Excess, and the seat's honesty is that she commits both. The training she abandoned and the command she would not put down are the same trait at two settings, and the story is explicit that the son was lost inside the gap between them. Across the dial at 0h Wednesday's Wisdom curbs Excess, and this cast's Wednesday is the seat that knows exactly what everything costs — the correction is available and this figure does not take it until the last hour.

[[The Hour]] *"It is more blessed to give than to receive"* (Acts 20:35). The saying is usually quoted about property. This seat is what it looks like when the thing given away is authority, and then a life.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the top arm at 12h in noon yellow (#F8E600), the Joy of the day's peak — the base reading, and a deliberate move off the orange arm her younger self holds in the Jedi cast: same person, different age, different deed.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns her noon to green (#00DC00) — the wavelength at the summit of human sight. Fitting for a figure whose last contribution is not an act but a continuation: she trains a successor she will not see finish, and the whole later story is the receipt.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Leia holds the 09h morning arm in alb ivory (#EDEDE0), the estate of the Priest, the Bell for its object. By this age she is the estate rather than an officer of it: the office of holding a cause that nobody privately owns, kept open by one person for decades after the institution that chartered it has gone.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that morning arm is Childhood, and she wears spring green (#7CE577) — read as a disposition rather than as an age, and here read against her. Childhood's traits on this wheel are appetite, certainty and no memory of having been wrong, and the certainty is precisely what cost her the son.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Leia holds 12h on the Summer arm, yellow, aimed at the solstice — sharing the spoke with Sunday. The year's brightest hour holds the mother and the two who inherit what she was fighting about: the last general of one war and the first pair of the next one.
variants.trio: On the Trinity she keeps the top arm at 12h, yellow, where the colour now means Faith, shared with Saturday as they guard the day's height from 8h to 16h. The reading is exact and expensive — she continues to act on the assumption that her son is recoverable for thirty years against all available evidence, and she is eventually right.

venus.name: Old Han
venus.base:
[[The Figure]] Han Solo holds Friday in this cast, thirty years after the seat he holds in the Jedi one, and the deed argued here is the bridge. A man who has spent his whole life pricing risk walks out into the open toward a son who has already murdered on his master's instruction, with nothing drawn and no plan beyond the distance itself. There is no calculation in it. The seat takes him because that is the arm's virtue in its exact sense: the willingness to be within reach of the person who may destroy you.

[[On the Dial]] His home here is the 20h arm in deep red (#B60000), the Passion of the evening — the hour at which what a person wants stops being private. The seat is the Artist's, and the move off his younger self's midnight purple is the whole argument: the smuggler who priced everything is not the same seat as the father who declines to.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Love and the vice is Jealousy, and his failure is the ordinary form the arm takes in a family. He left. The marriage ended after the son was lost and each parent went back to what they were good at, which is a real failure of this arm and is not softened by the ending. Across the dial at 08h Saturday's Patience heals Jealousy, and he never had any: his whole life is the refusal to wait, and the one time it is the right instrument is the last time he uses it.

[[The Hour]] *"Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends"* (John 15:13). The verse specifies friends. This seat is the case where the person is a son and has already decided.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 20h arm in deep red (#B60000), the Passion of the evening — the base reading, and a deliberate move off the midnight purple his younger self holds in the Jedi cast: same man, different age, different deed.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism keeps him at 20h and purifies the red to its light primary (#FF0000) — the reddest red there is, unmixed. In the light world Passion is a wavelength rather than a pigment, which suits the one act in his record that has nothing else mixed into it.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Han shifts to the 18h sunset arm in iron-blood crimson (#A02020), the estate of the Soldier, the Sword for its object — an estate he spent forty years avoiding. He is the cast's proof that the Soldier's seat is about exposure rather than about arms: he walks onto the bridge without reaching for anything, which is the most military act in the whole cast.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel that sunset arm belongs to the Elder, the harvest of a life, and he deepens to ember (#FF6A3C). The harvest is honest rather than flattering: the ship, the debts and the same trade he started in, plus one grown child he has not spoken to in a decade, and he goes to collect the only item on the list that is still open.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross Han takes the 18h arm — Autumn, red, aimed at the autumnal equinox — sharing the spoke with Tuesday. The season of reckoning holds this cast's two returns: one man goes back for a friend and one for a son, and only one of them is expected.
variants.trio: The seat does not move: the Trinity's Love arm is its own 20h in its own red. Tuesday joins it, and the two guard the evening from 16h to 24h — the arm held here by the cast's proof that this colour is not about being loved back, since in this case it demonstrably is not.

saturn.name: General Hux
saturn.base:
[[The Figure]] Hux holds Saturday because he is envy in its purest institutional form. He is a competent staff officer of genuine ability who cannot stop measuring himself against a colleague promoted past him on a basis he considers illegitimate, and who eventually informs on his own side for no strategic gain whatever — his stated reason is that he wants the other man to lose. The seat has never had a tenant who named the vice so precisely without noticing that he was doing it.

[[On the Dial]] His home is the 08h arm in field green (#007E00), the Renewal of the morning — the hour of work resumed. The seat is the Farmer's: the estate of long labour toward a harvest, and this cast fills it with a man who does the labour, builds the weapon, and watches the harvest handed to somebody with no rank in the organisation at all.

[[The Lesson]] The virtue is Patience and the vice is Envy, and he is the demonstration that the counterfeit of the first is indistinguishable from it until the moment of payment. He waits for years, correctly, in a chain of command that rewards waiting — and then spends the accumulated position on a private grievance. Across the dial at 20h Friday's Love dissolves Envy, and this cast's Friday is the seat that walks unarmed toward somebody who may kill him; the contrast is the instrument's own argument, since both men are acting on the same colleague and only one of them is aiming at a person rather than at a ranking.

[[The Hour]] *"A sound heart is the life of the flesh: but envy the rottenness of the bones"* (Proverbs 14:30). The verse makes envy structural rather than emotional, which is what a career built entirely on it eventually proves.

variants.hexa_primary: Home position: the 08h arm in field green (#007E00), the Renewal of the morning — the base reading, a long patient labour whose entire yield is eventually spent on a grievance.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism turns his morning green to cyan (#00DDDD) — the colour of the clear early sky rather than of the ground under it. Renewal keeps the hour; light names what the waiting was for instead of the work of doing it, and in this seat what it was for is a promotion that never came.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass Hux takes the dawn arm, 06h, in field green (#3E8914), the estate of the Farmer, the Plough for its object — the estate held by its least contented member. A farmer's authority comes from having been present for every stage of the same ground, and he was: he built the weapon from the ground up and was not the man it was given to.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the dawn arm is Birth, and he wears predawn mist (#8FA8C8) — assigned rather than earned. He is the cast's one figure whose entire identity is inherited from a father in the same service, and the wheel's youngest seat is where the instrument records that nothing after that was ever chosen.
