variants.cross: On the seasons cross Hux moves to 06h — Spring, green, aimed at the vernal equinox — sharing the spoke with Monday. The season of return held by this cast's two subordinates: one keeps the machinery running for people she will never command, the other keeps it running for a command he believes should be his.
variants.trio: The Trinity promotes him from the morning to the crown: the 12h Faith arm, yellow, shared with Thursday, guarding the day's height from 8h to 16h. The arm asks for a position held on no evidence, and his is precisely that: a settled conviction that merit will eventually be recognised by an institution that has never once done so.

sun.name: Rey · Kylo Ren
sun.base:
[[The Figure]] Sunday's seat is two people the story calls a dyad — its own term for a bond that makes them one power held in two bodies — and it is the only throne in these three casts whose two faces are not related by blood or by rank. Rey holds the bright face: a scavenger with no name, no family and no training, who takes a name at the end rather than discovering one. Kylo Ren holds the dark one: a man with every inheritance the story has to give, who destroys each of them in order and is still, at every point, serving somebody.

[[On the Dial]] The centre holds no arm and no hour. White-gold is the sum of every hue the wheel can mix, and the six seats around it are that light taken apart — a repair, a desertion, a bargain, a surrender, a bridge, a grudge. The throne is what the source looks like before anything is subtracted, and this cast is the one where the source is explicitly shared between two people who are on opposite sides of the war.

[[The Lesson]] The bundle gives the ruler face Justice against Pride and the servant face Humility against Servility. The Ruler's justice is the plainest version on this dial: she repeatedly goes back for people who cannot help her, including the one who is trying to kill her, and her Pride is the insistence on being nobody's — a refusal of inheritance held so hard that it becomes its own claim. The Servant's servility is the seat's indictment: he kills a master to be free of him and immediately takes the vacant chair, then kills the next one and takes that. His humility arrives once and is decisive, and it is the identical act his grandfather performed, which is the instrument's point about this whole family.

[[The Hour]] *"For whosoever will save his life shall lose it: and whosoever will lose his life for my sake shall find it"* (Matthew 16:25). Both faces of this seat perform the second half of that sentence, in the same hour, for each other.

faces.ruler:
Rey is Sunday's bright face, and the argument for the seat is that she holds the throne with less inheritance than any other occupant of it in these three casts. No rank, no house, no completed training and, for most of the story, no surname — and the instrument gives her the centre anyway, because the centre is the source the six arms are read against rather than the highest office among them.

Her virtue is Justice, and her version is the most literal: she goes back. For a droid, for a stranger, for a friend she has known for a day, and finally for the man on the other half of this seat, who has spent the story trying to recruit or kill her. The vice that stalks it is Pride, and hers is unusual — not vanity but a refusal, held to the point of obstinacy, to be anybody's property or anybody's continuation. The seat's resolution is that she takes a name at the end and it is a chosen one. Her mood is Glory, noon's own triumph, and it is the quietest instance of it on the dial.

The seat's shadow face is not her opposite. The story's own word for the two of them is a bond, and the instrument seats them accordingly: one throne, two faces, and neither of them complete alone.
faces.servant:
Kylo Ren is Sunday's dark face — the servant of this seat in the strictest sense the canon allows, and the most thoroughly documented case of it in these three casts.

His virtue is Humility, and like his grandfather's it exists as a single act rather than as a disposition: at the end he abandons the name, the office and the weapon, and spends what is left on one person. The vice that stalks it is Servility, and the seat's indictment is the pattern. He kills the master he served and takes the vacant chair, and within the year is taking orders from an older one who had been behind the first all along — at every moment executing somebody else's programme while insisting that he is letting the past die. A man who kills a master and is never once his own is the arm's definition. His mood is Awe: the servant's reading of the throne, a presence acknowledged rather than enjoyed.

Opposition is not evil on this dial, and this seat is where the rule is easiest to see — the two faces of this dual spend the story reaching for each other, and the story's own term for what they are is a single thing in two places.

variants.hexa_primary: On the painter's wheel the pair keeps the centre of the dial, white-gold, belonging to no hour: the six arms around them are that light decomposed, one virtue to each spoke. This is the home reading — the source rather than a spoke, and this cast is the one whose source is explicitly shared.
variants.hexa_secondary: The prism changes every arm around them and cannot change the centre: white remains the sum of all wavelengths. It is the same fact from the other side — a bond that the story calls one power in two bodies is a centre, not a pair of spokes, and no decomposition of the wheel separates it.
variants.octa_primary: On the Compass the pair steps onto the noon arm in royal gold (#F0C420), the estate of the King, the Crown for its object — a crown one of them is offered twice and refuses, and the other takes twice and cannot hold. Between them they exhaust every way of failing at an inheritance.
variants.octa_secondary: In the Ages wheel the noon arm is Youth, the zenith of a life, and the pair wears sun-yellow (#FFE800). The fit is exact and short: these are the only two figures in these three casts whose entire story happens at their zenith, and both spend it on the same question about where they came from.
variants.cross: On the seasons cross the Sunday pair holds 12h on the Summer arm, yellow, aimed at the summer solstice — shared with Thursday. The year's brightest spoke holds the son and the mother who never stopped expecting him back, on the one arm of the year where the light is longest.
variants.trio: On the Trinity the seat keeps the centre and the cast narrows to three arms — Faith yellow, Love red, Hope blue. The geometry is indifferent to who holds it, which in this dual is not a warning but the argument: the same centre seats the scavenger and the heir, and declines to rank the inheritance above the choice.

Aries.base:
[[The Sky]] Aries opens the zodiac at the point astronomers still call the First Point of Aries, the spring equinox. On the year wheel it begins at 270 degrees, the left side of the dial, the year's own six in the morning, and guards 21 March to 19 April, when everything begins again.

[[On the Dial]] It rides the green arm of Renewal, Saturday's arm borrowed from Saturn, where the virtue is Patience and the shadow is Envy: a hard school for a headlong ram whose ruler Mars burns far away on the orange arm of Tuesday. Its arm-mate Taurus walks the same green path at a slower, steadier pace.

variants.primary: In the paint world Aries wears deep pigment green, the painter's mixture of yellow and blue. It is the green of first grass and wet spring earth, a color made of matter, and it grounds the ram: fire held inside growing things, impatience buried in a seed that must wait for its season.
variants.secondary: In the light world the spring arm glows cyan, green and blue light added together on the screen. The ram turns electric and cool, dawn air instead of soil, and its charge is no longer buried in earth but broadcast as pure signal, renewal read as energy rather than matter.
variants.primary_south: South of the equator the wheel turns and the ram leaps out of spring's green into the evening arm at 20h, wearing deep pigment red (#B60000), the hour whose mood is Passion. This is Venus's own arm, and the old story tells itself again in color: Mars's headlong sign lodged in the rooms of his mythic lover, Ares caught in Aphrodite's evening. The southern ram keeps its fire but points it at the heart instead of the season — impatience ripened into ardor, the charge of first grass become the charge of first love — and its shadow shifts with it, no longer Envy but that vice's hotter cousin Jealousy, passion that has begun to grip what it should only warm.
variants.secondary_south: In the southern light palette the ram's evening arm burns pure red (#FF0000), the first primary of the additive world. The cool cyan dawn of its northern reading is gone; what was buried charge is now emitted flame, the ram as beacon rather than seed. Courage broadcast as desire, at full brightness, in Venus's own hour — a signal that does not wait for its season but announces it.

Taurus.base:
[[The Sky]] Taurus is the bull of the oldest sky, remembered as the white shape Zeus wore to carry Europa across the sea. It guards 20 April to 20 May, the arc from 300 to 330 degrees, the heart of spring when the year climbs steadily toward its summit at the top of the dial.

[[On the Dial]] It stands on the green arm of Renewal, Saturday's arm under Saturn, teaching Patience against the vice of Envy, and no sign wears that lesson more naturally than the unhurried bull. Its ruler Venus keeps house on the red arm of Friday, and its arm-mate Aries supplies the spark that Taurus turns into steady ground.

variants.primary: In pigment Taurus wears deep green, yellow and blue ground together into the color of pasture and leaf. The subtractive world of matter is the bull's own element: color you can till, weigh and hold, renewal as something grown slowly out of soil rather than switched on.
variants.secondary: In the prism world the bull's arm shines cyan, blue and green light summed on the screen. The pasture becomes clear water and cold sky, and Taurus grows lighter than itself: the same patience, but read as a calm transparent frequency instead of heavy fertile earth.
variants.primary_south: South of the equator the wheel turns and the bull comes home: the mirrored year seats Taurus on the evening arm of Passion, Venus's own house, in pigment red (#B60000), an ox-blood crimson as heavy with earth as its northern green was with grass. The myth shifts weight along with the hue, for the shape Zeus wore to carry Europa was always a passion story, and the unhurried grazer becomes the steadfast lover: the same patience re-voiced as devotion, the old envy warming into the arm's own shadow, jealousy, love that holds on the way a bull holds ground.
variants.secondary_south: In the southern light palette the bull's evening arm blazes pure red (#FF0000), the additive primary, and the reading sharpens: no longer pasture or wine-dark clay but signal, desire announced at full brightness. Venus's homecoming beast keeps its slowness, but a slow fire is the longest-burning kind — passion as steady emission, devotion broadcast rather than buried in the field.

Gemini.base:
[[The Story]] Gemini is Castor and Pollux, one twin mortal and one divine, and the myth turns on a gift: Pollux split his immortality so neither brother would be lost alone. The sky keeps them as two parallel chains of stars, two figures standing side by side.

[[On the Dial]] Gemini guards 21 May to 20 June, the arc from 330 degrees to the very top of the dial, spring ripening into summer. It sits on the yellow arm of Joy, Thursday's arm under Jupiter, whose virtue is Generosity and whose vice is Excess, the exact moral of its own myth. Cancer shares that arm just across the solstice, and Gemini's ruler Mercury lives on the purple arm of Wednesday.

variants.primary: In the paint world Gemini wears pure pigment yellow, a painter's primary that no mixing can produce. That suits the twins: something first-hand and unmixed, the brightest matter on the palette, joy laid on thick before any other color has touched it.
variants.secondary: In the light world the noon arm turns pure green, a primary of the prism as yellow is of the palette. Gemini keeps its rank but changes its voice: primary in both worlds, now glowing at the eye's most sensitive wavelength, quick conversation carried as living signal.
variants.primary_south: South of the equator the wheel turns and Gemini drops to the midnight arm, and the fall is a homecoming: the bottom of the dial is Wednesday's post, the house of its own ruler Mercury. Wearing purple (#542E85), red and blue pigment folded into the dye of mourning and of kings, the twins show the other face of their myth — Pollux's gift was also a grief, half of all their days spent below — and noon's quick talk deepens into the mood of Sorrow, wisdom traded in low voices, conversation kept like a vigil through the dark.
variants.secondary_south: In the light palette the southern midnight arm glows magenta (#BD00BD), red and blue light added into a color no single wavelength can carry. Nothing suits the twins better: two lights joined into one impossible hue, Castor and Pollux as pure signal, sorrow emitted rather than worn — the vigil turned luminous, midnight answering itself in light.

Cancer.base:
[[The Sky]] Cancer begins exactly at the top of the dial: its first point is the summer solstice, the anchor on which DOMY's whole year wheel is pinned, and the Tropic of Cancer still carries its name. It guards 21 June to 22 July, the first arc of high summer, 0 to 30 degrees.

[[On the Dial]] The crab is Hera's small and stubborn agent, sent to pinch Heracles and crushed underfoot for it, set among the faintest stars of the zodiac — a dim slender Y in the sky. It sits on the yellow arm of Joy, Thursday's arm under Jupiter, learning Generosity and shadowed by Excess, with Gemini as its neighbor on the same arm across the solstice. Its ruler is the Moon, at home on the blue arm of Monday: a child of night standing guard at the year's brightest gate.

variants.primary: In pigment Cancer wears primary yellow, the brightest matter a brush can carry. There is a tenderness in giving the Moon's shy creature the sunniest paint on the wheel: the crab keeps its shell, but Thursday's yellow warms it into open-handed, generous gold.
variants.secondary: In the light world Cancer's arm shines pure green light at the top of the star. The moonchild trades gold for the prism's own primary, and its softness turns luminous: not the glare of noon but the green of things that grow through it, joy as emitted light.
variants.primary_south: South of the equator the wheel turns and Cancer's solstice gate opens onto midwinter: the crab crosses to the bottom midnight arm and wears purple (#542E85), red and blue pigment folded into Mercury's dye of Sorrow. Thursday's open-handed gold is gone; here the Moon's shy creature learns the dark arm's curriculum, wisdom shadowed by greed, and its shell turns from ornament to shelter. It is the same stubborn guard Hera once sent, but re-tempered — pincers closed around what little warmth the long night allows, patient as tidewater, generous only after it has endured.
variants.secondary_south: In the southern light palette Cancer's midnight arm glows magenta (#BD00BD), the one hue no rainbow contains, conjured by the eye where the spectrum's far ends meet. Nothing suits the Moon's child better: moonlight too is borrowed radiance, and the crab becomes the lantern of the year's darkest gate, sorrow emitted rather than absorbed — a faint, invented shining that the sky cannot make and the mind refuses to put out.

Leo.base:
[[The Sky]] Leo is the Nemean lion, the first labor of Heracles, whose hide no weapon could pierce, set into the sky with Regulus, the little king, burning at its heart. It guards 23 July to 22 August, the arc from 30 to 60 degrees, the furnace weeks just past the solstice.

[[On the Dial]] It burns on the orange arm of Zeal, Tuesday's arm under Mars, where the virtue is Courage and the vice is Wrath, the lion's two temperatures. Virgo shares that arm as its quieter half. And Leo's ruler is unique: the Sun does not live on any arm but at the very center of the dial, the white light of Sunday from which all six arm colors are decomposed. The lion answers to the source itself.

variants.primary: In pigment Leo wears burnt orange, red and yellow milled together into the color of embers and late July. It is a mixed color for a proud sign, and that is its lesson: even the lion's fire is composed, courage blended from passion and joy, matter warmed rather than burning.
variants.secondary: In the light world Leo's arm blazes pure yellow, red and green light added until they sum toward the Sun's own brightness. Nothing is milled or muted here; the lion becomes a lamp, zeal as radiation, the closest of the six lights to the white center it answers to.
variants.primary_south: South of the equator the wheel turns and the lion crosses to the pre-dawn arm, trading its embers for blue (#002FFF), the deep worked pigment of the hour called Calm under the Moon. The hide no weapon could pierce becomes a night watchman's patience: Regulus, the little king, keeps the throne while its ruler the Sun is still below the horizon, courage cooled into composure, wrath banked to a guarded stillness, and the arm's own shadow, fear, faced down simply by staying.
variants.secondary_south: In the light palette the southern lion glows blue (#0040FF), the beam instead of the pigment. Regulus turns pilot light: the king's furnace reduced to one steady signal in the dark before dawn, zeal refined into vigil, a small unwavering lamp that answers fear with the promise of the Sun's return.

Virgo.base:
[[The Sky]] Virgo is the star-maiden, Astraea who left the earth last of the immortals, or Demeter of the grain; either way the sky agrees, giving her Spica, the ear of wheat, for her brightest star. She guards 23 August to 22 September, from 60 degrees down to the autumn equinox at 90, closing the summer at the dial's right side, the year's dusk.

[[On the Dial]] She takes, surprisingly, the orange arm of Zeal, Tuesday's arm under Mars, beside Leo, her louder arm-mate. The pairing is the lesson: the arm's virtue is Courage and its vice is Wrath, and Virgo argues courage in its harvest form, exact, patient and unarmed. Her ruler Mercury keeps its home on the purple arm of Wednesday.

variants.primary: In pigment Virgo wears harvest orange, red and yellow mixed into terracotta and ripe grain. The subtractive world suits her: a color of clay, bread and September fields, zeal made useful, the soldier's hue mellowed into everything the soldier fights to protect.
variants.secondary: In the light world her arm turns pure yellow, red and green light summed brighter than either. The gleaner becomes lucid: precision as illumination, the lamp on the desk rather than the fire in the field, her quiet zeal emitted steadily at the screen's warmest primary.
variants.primary_south: South of the equator the wheel turns and the maiden crosses to the Moon's pre-dawn arm, trading the soldier's orange for blue (#002FFF), the weighed-out lapis of the old workshops. The hour is Calm, and it reads her differently: zeal cools into serenity, her famous worry stands named at last as the arm's vice, Fear, and Mercury's lists are kept the water-bearer's way, a measured, quiet pouring in the dark. Astraea, last of the immortals to leave the earth, now holds the last watch before sunrise, Spica the one grain still bright at four o'clock.
variants.secondary_south: In the southern light palette her arm glows blue (#0040FF), a primary of both worlds, but here it is beam rather than pigment. The gleaner becomes the night's last lamp: precision as vigil, worry burned down to watchfulness, her exactness emitted steadily into the hour before dawn, serene because everything has already been counted.

Libra.base:
[[The Sky]] Libra is the only sign that is an object rather than a creature: a balance. It opens on 23 September at the autumn equinox, when day and night stand exactly equal and the year performs its own act of weighing, and it holds the wheel from 90 to 120 degrees, easing the light down into October. Its glyph draws a sun resting on the horizon line, neither risen nor set — the year's own act of weighing, made into a mark.

[[On the Dial]] It rides the red Friday arm of Venus, whose mood is Passion, whose virtue is Love and whose vice is Jealousy. Scorpio shares the arm with it, two schools of the same fire, one weighing passion and one plunging into it.

[[The Lesson]] Its classical ruler is Venus herself, and Venus lives on this very arm. Libra is thus the rare sign seated in its ruler's own house: love judged in the home of love.

variants.primary: In the paint world Libra's arm wears the deep pigment red of #B60000, a crimson with the weight of earth in it, the painter's primary. Passion becomes material: a weight set in the pan, love measured the way goods are weighed at a Friday market, heavy, warm and real.
variants.secondary: In the light palette the arm burns pure additive red, #FF0000. Red is a primary of light just as it was of paint, so Libra keeps its color across both worlds; only its substance changes. Screen red is not a pigment but a signal, passion as flame rather than clay, and the balance is held in a beam.
variants.primary_south: South of the equator the wheel turns and the balance changes houses: Libra leaves Venus' red evening for Saturn's morning arm, wearing green (#007E00), the pigment of dew and first grass, in the hour called Renewal. Its own equinox flips with it — 23 September opens spring there, not autumn — so the glyph's sun on the horizon is at last rising. The weigher becomes a sower, leveling seed against soil instead of goods against coin, and the seat keeps the old axis' promise: Patience is the very virtue that heals Jealousy.
variants.secondary_south: In the southern light palette the arm cools to cyan (#00DDDD), the color of the clear sky just before sunrise. The scale's beam becomes a beam in earnest: day measured against night at the year's own dawn, and love judged as a guest in Saturn's house, where patience rather than passion holds the pans level.

Scorpio.base:
[[The Sky]] Scorpio guards the dying of the year, 23 October to 21 November, from 120 to 150 degrees, where autumn stops pretending and the wheel sinks toward the winter tip of the dial. Its stars are drawn as a long chain that fans open at the head and hooks upward at the sting.

[[On the Dial]] It sits on the red Friday arm of Venus, mood Passion, virtue Love, vice Jealousy, and no sign knows that vice more intimately, for jealousy is love that has armed itself. Libra shares the arm: what Libra weighs, Scorpio defends.

[[The Lesson]] Its classical ruler is Mars, who lives across the dial on the orange Tuesday arm. Scorpio is therefore war lodged in the house of love, passion with a soldier's memory.

variants.primary: In paint the arm is the dark pigment red of #B60000, closer to dried blood than to fire. It suits the scorpion: subtractive color works by absorbing light and giving little back, and Scorpio's passion is exactly that, taken in deeply, held, and revealed only when the tail decides.
variants.secondary: In the light palette the arm blazes as pure #FF0000, the first primary of the additive world. What was venom becomes voltage: passion emitted instead of absorbed, the warning coloration of the screen age, a red that does not wait in shadow but announces itself at full brightness.
variants.primary_south: South of the equator the wheel turns and Scorpio crosses its own healing axis: lifted from the red evening house of Venus, it lands on Saturn's morning arm, wearing green (#007E00) under the mood of Renewal. Its dates now open the spring instead of closing the autumn, and Patience, the star's prescribed cure for Jealousy, is here the arm's own virtue, so the southern scorpion sits inside its medicine. The animal molts as the year does, shedding its plated armor the way the field sheds winter; Mars' iron is beaten into Cronus' sickle, and the venom is held back like sap, war's memory turned to the slow work of growing things.
variants.secondary_south: In the southern light palette the same arm shines cyan (#00DDDD), the clear sky before sunrise. The scorpion's warning red is gone entirely: venom cools into dew, and what was a threat displayed becomes a signal of first light. Passion is not extinguished but timed, held to the patient frequency of dawn, so the southern Scorpio stings only as the morning does — sharp, cold and renewing.

Sagittarius.base:
[[The Sky]] Sagittarius takes the year's final descent, 22 November to 21 December, from 150 degrees to the bottom of the dial. Its far edge is the winter solstice: the archer walks the year into its midnight.

[[On the Dial]] It stands with Capricorn on the purple Wednesday arm of Mercury: mood Sorrow, virtue Wisdom, vice Greed. Two climbers of the dark season share that post, one aiming beyond it and one enduring through it.

[[The Lesson]] Its ruler Jupiter lives on the yellow Thursday arm at the top of the dial, directly opposite, and by the star's law the opposite virtue heals the vice: Generosity is the cure for Greed. Like its glyph, the archer aims straight up at its ruler's noon.

variants.primary: In paint the arm wears purple, #542E85, red and blue pigment folded together into the dye of mourning and of kings. Sorrow becomes a worn material, and the archer's wisdom reads like Tyrian cloth: costly, dark, earned a drop at a time from the world itself.
variants.secondary: In the light palette the purple becomes magenta, #BD00BD, the one hue no rainbow contains, invented by the eye where the spectrum's far ends meet. A fitting midnight for an archer: he aims at a point that exists only because the mind insists on joining what nature keeps apart.
variants.primary_south: South of the equator the wheel turns and the archer lands where its aim always pointed: the noon arm of Jupiter, home at last on its own ruler's post, with Joy for its hour instead of Sorrow. In paint the arm wears yellow (#F8E600), the palette's unmixed primary, and the wisdom the north earned drop by drop is here spent freely: the arrow becomes a gift, generosity a form of marksmanship, and the sign's one shadow is Excess, the bow drawn a breath too far.
variants.secondary_south: In the light palette the southern noon glows green (#00DC00), the prism's own primary at the eye's keenest wavelength. The archer's hour turns from Sorrow to Joy and its aim sharpens: no shot now at an invented midnight color but a level arrow through living light, and only its old seat of Wisdom, straight across the dial, holds the draw short of Excess.

Capricorn.base:
[[The Sky]] Capricorn opens at the exact bottom of the dial. Its first point is the winter solstice, 22 December, the year's midnight beneath the silver tip, and from there to 19 January, 180 to 210 degrees, it does the hardest work on the wheel: turning descent into climb.

[[On the Dial]] It shares the purple Wednesday arm of Mercury with Sagittarius: mood Sorrow, virtue Wisdom, vice Greed. Where the archer aims out of the dark, the goat simply keeps walking through it.

[[The Lesson]] Its ruler is Saturn, keeper of limits and of time, at home on the green Saturday arm whose virtue is Patience. That placement is Capricorn's whole doctrine: the summit is never taken, it is outlasted. The sea-goat's hybrid nature is exactly this patience argued twice over: half the sign is the climb, and half is the memory of the deep it rose from.

variants.primary: In paint the arm holds pigment purple, #542E85, red and blue ground into the color of winter dusk and old authority. It fits the goat well: sorrow worn as a working coat, wisdom built up in layers like slow glaze, matte, dark and utterly permanent.
variants.secondary: The light palette turns the arm magenta, #BD00BD, the impossible color the eye conjures where red and blue light meet. The climber's midnight goes electric, sorrow with a neon edge, and the stubborn ascent is lit like a summit beacon no rainbow ever includes.
variants.primary_south: South of the equator the wheel turns and the sea-goat opens at the very top of the dial: its solstice is midsummer there, the year's midnight become its noon. The climber wakes on Jupiter's Thursday arm wearing primary yellow (#F8E600), joy laid on as thick as unmixed paint, and the old doctrine shifts a degree: the summit is no longer outlasted but inhabited, Saturn's hard-won thrift schooled into Generosity, the hoard of the whole climb spent open-handed on the view, wary now only of Excess, the one vice a goat that finally owns the height must learn to fear.
variants.secondary_south: In the light palette the southern noon glows pure green (#00DC00), the prism's primary at the eye's keenest wavelength, and the same green Saturn's own Saturday arm wears in paint, so the goat at last climbs under its ruler's color. Joy sharpens into growth: not the glare of the summit but the grass that takes it, patience finally in flower, gladness emitted as living signal.

Aquarius.base:
[[The Sky]] Aquarius holds deep winter, 20 January to 18 February, the arc from 210 to 240 degrees on the dial's lower left: the small hours of the year, past midnight and leaning toward dawn, when the light grows even as the cold deepens.

[[On the Dial]] It rests on the blue Monday arm of the Moon: mood Calm, virtue Serenity, vice Fear. Pisces shares the arm, the pourer and the swimmers, the vessel and what lives in the stream.

[[The Lesson]] Its classical ruler is Saturn, at home on the green Saturday arm of Patience. That is the water-bearer's secret: the pouring looks like abandon but is discipline, a measured emptying, serenity practiced until it becomes a public work. Aquarius is nominally an air sign, yet everything it owns it pours away as water — discipline is exactly that paradox held steady.

variants.primary: In paint the arm is primary blue, #002FFF, the lapis and indigo of the old workshops, once weighed out like treasure. Calm becomes a substance: the water-bearer pours a color painters ground by hand, and serenity settles onto the year like pigment into cloth.
variants.secondary: In light the arm keeps its name, for blue is a primary of both worlds, but #0040FF glows instead of covering. The poured water becomes a stream of screen-light, the beam rather than the pigment, and the bearer's calm turns luminous, a steady lamp in the dial's dark quarter.
variants.primary_south: South of the equator the wheel turns, and the water-bearer takes high summer, on the 16h arm of Mars, wearing ember orange (#DC9600), the milled pigment of the working afternoon. Deep winter's calm is left in the north; here the jar is carried to the fire, and Saturn's measured emptying becomes the quenching stroke — water poured with a soldier's timing, Zeal in the form of a steady hand, dousing Wrath before the furnace weeks can spill it.
variants.secondary_south: In the light palette the southern arm burns pure yellow (#FFFF00), red and green summed toward the Sun's own brightness. The poured stream goes incandescent: not the cool Monday beam of the north but water made lamplight, the bearer's discipline emitted as zeal, a working flame that pours without ever burning dry.

Pisces.base:
[[The Sky]] Pisces is the zodiac's closing word, 19 February to 20 March, from 240 to 270 degrees. Its far edge lands exactly on the spring equinox, at the dial's dawn side; there the old year dissolves and hands the wheel on.

[[On the Dial]] It lies with Aquarius on the blue Monday arm of the Moon: mood Calm, virtue Serenity, vice Fear. The bearer pours the stream; the fish are what it carries.

[[The Lesson]] Its classical ruler is Jupiter, resident of the yellow Thursday arm of Joy and Generosity. The dial gives the dreamer a benefactor: the sign that ends the year in blue calm is governed from the arm of gladness, so every ending is financed by joy.

variants.primary: Paint gives the arm true pigment blue, #002FFF, the deep working blue of water painted rather than water seen. The two fish swim in a material sea, calm laid on in slow opaque strokes, and even their fear sinks quietly into the same jar of color.
variants.secondary: In the light palette the arm stays blue, a primary in both worlds, but sharpens into the glowing #0040FF of a screen's own depth. The ring of fish becomes a circuit, two currents of light chasing each other, and the Moon's painted water is remade as pure signal.
variants.primary_south: South of the equator the wheel turns and the fish surface at 16h, on the ember orange (#DC9600) arm of Mars where the maiden gleans in the north. The working afternoon puts the dreamers to work: the closed ring turns like a mill-wheel now, the current drives it instead of carrying it, and Jupiter's generosity is paid out as the sea's own harvest, the netted catch beside the standing grain. Calm warms into Zeal here, and even the old fear is spent as fuel — the swimmer keeps stroke because stopping is the one thing it dreads.
variants.secondary_south: In the southern light palette the same seat flares to pure yellow (#FFFF00), red and green light summed, the prism's reading of the ember. The ring of fish becomes a wheel of signal, two currents driving each other like a turbine, and the sign that closes the year in northern calm here powers it home — zeal emitted rather than burned.

zodiac_articles_note: zodiac_articles[SignName] = {base, variants}: base = 3-4 left-aligned paragraphs weaving the sign's myth, the owner's art, its season arc on the year wheel, the hexa arm it sits on (color, mood, virtue, vice), its arm partner and its classical ruler's place on the dial; variants = one paragraph each for the paint and light palettes (signs live on the hexa pointer only). Display location TBD by the owner.

Faith.base:
[[The Figure]] Faith is the vertical line of the three: not a feeling but a direction, the part of a person that points upward the way the M points from the top of this ring. Paul named it first of the trio that remains when everything else passes - faith, hope and love - and the dial gives it the highest arm.

[[On the Dial]] It wears yellow, the noon color, and guards the day's height from 8 to 16 - the working hours, which is the quiet joke of its placement: faith is not kept at midnight vigils but in the plain middle of the day, where work either honors what one believes or betrays it.

[[The Lesson]] Two days carry it together. Jupiter's Thursday brings the Priest - faith professed, taught, celebrated - and Saturn's Saturday brings the Farmer's patience: faith TESTED, the kind that sows and waits without proof. Between them the pair warns of its own shadows, Excess and Envy: belief turned loud, or turned sour at a neighbor's harvest.

Hope.base:
[[The Figure]] Hope is the horizon line: it looks not up but FORWARD, at what is coming and cannot yet be seen. The dial seats it on the blue arm at 4h - the hour before dawn, the coldest and darkest stretch of the night, which is exactly where hope does its work.

[[On the Dial]] It guards the morning third, 0 to 8: the hours when the day exists only as a promise. Its blue is the pre-dawn sky one shade before it lightens - Calm, the mood of that hour, because hope is not excitement but a steady expectation.

[[The Lesson]] The Moon's Monday and Mercury's Wednesday share the arm: the Moon lends Serenity, the lamp that holds through the night, and Mercury - the morning star, the herald - lends the message that the light is already on its way. Their shadows are Fear and Greed: the Moon's darkness read as threat instead of promise, and the Merchant's grasping at what the morning has not yet delivered. Hope answers both - it waits, and it waits open-handed.

Love.base:
[[The Figure]] Love is the horizontal line, the one that runs from person to person - and Paul's verdict stands over the whole trio: the greatest of these is love. The dial gives it the red arm at 20h, where Y closes the ring's word, and the evening third from 16 to midnight: the hours people finally turn toward each other.

[[On the Dial]] Its red is Passion, the mood of the evening - the color Venus has always worn, the first star lit in the darkening sky. Love guards the night not as danger but as intimacy: the third of the day that belongs to closeness, tables, beds and long talks.

[[The Lesson]] Venus' Friday and Mars' Tuesday share the arm - the oldest pairing there is, love and courage, the lover and the defender; Babylon knew them as one goddess. Their shadows are Jealousy and Wrath, love's two failures, and the canon sends their cures from across the dial: Patience quells Jealousy, Serenity quells Wrath.

trio_articles_note: trio_articles[virtue] = {base}: one left-aligned multi-paragraph article per Trinity arm (Faith 12h yellow, Hope 4h blue, Love 20h red), shown under the trio arm hover header. The trio has a single palette, so there are no per-style variants.

Rat.base: [[The Figure]] First of the twelve — the Rat won the Great Race by riding the Ox's head across the river and leaping ashore at the last moment. Its years reward what the story praises: wit, thrift, quickness, the talent of arriving first with the least force. A Rat year returns every twelve; each return wears a new element of the five, so the same year comes back only once in sixty.

Ox.base: [[The Figure]] The Ox carried the Rat across the river and came second — the zodiac's patron of patient strength, of work done slowly and completely. Ox years favor endurance, honesty and the long furrow over the quick harvest. Each twelve-year return arrives in a new element; the same Ox comes back once in sixty years.

Tiger.base: [[The Figure]] The Tiger is the zodiac's raw courage — the mountain king whose years are said to bring boldness, upheaval and protection all at once; children born under it were dressed in tiger caps against evil spirits. A Tiger year returns every twelve, each time in a new element of the five; the same Tiger, sixty years apart, is said to be a different beast.

Rabbit.base: [[The Figure]] The Rabbit is the zodiac's gentleness and diplomacy — in the old tale it crossed the river hopping stone to stone and on a drifting log, arriving fourth on grace alone. Its years favor tact, mercy and quiet luck; the Chinese see a rabbit, not a man, in the face of the full Moon, pounding the elixir of life. Each twelve-year return comes in a new element; one full circle of the same Rabbit takes sixty years.

Dragon.base: [[The Figure]] The Dragon is the only creature of the twelve that does not walk the earth — the emperor's own sign, bringer of rain, the year in which births were always said to multiply. Dragon years promise ambition, luck and weather in every sense. Every twelfth year it returns in a new element; the same Dragon flies once in sixty.

Snake.base: [[The Figure]] The Snake is the zodiac's wisdom in its stillest form — the small dragon, as the Chinese call it, whose years favor insight, elegance and holding one's counsel. It came sixth by hiding on the Horse's hoof and slipping ahead at the line. Each return wears a new element, and no Snake repeats inside sixty years.

Horse.base: [[The Figure]] The Horse is the zodiac's free runner — years of motion, independence and open roads. The old books warn and promise the same thing: nothing holds a Horse year still — and each return wears a different element, so no two Horse years run alike. Twelve years bring the next Horse; sixty bring back the same one.

Goat.base: [[The Figure]] The Goat (or Sheep) is the zodiac's peace — years of art, kindness and community, the flock over the race. Eighth of the twelve, and eight is the luckiest of Chinese numbers; a Goat year is said to soften whatever it touches. Each twelve-year return arrives in a new element; the same Goat returns once in sixty years.

Monkey.base: [[The Figure]] The Monkey is the zodiac's cleverness unchained — the sign of invention, mischief and escape from every trap, with Sun Wukong, the Monkey King who out-tricked heaven itself, as its eternal patron. Monkey years favor wit over strength and improvisation over plans. Every twelfth year it returns in a new element; one full Monkey circle takes sixty years.

Rooster.base: [[The Figure]] The Rooster is the zodiac's herald — the one animal whose job is the DAWN, which suits a clock better than any other sign. Its years favor candor, punctuality and hard-earned show: the rooster struts because it works before everyone wakes. A Rooster year returns every twelve, each time in one of the five elements — the same Rooster crows once in sixty years.

Dog.base: [[The Figure]] The Dog is the zodiac's loyalty — years of justice, honesty and guarding what one loves. Eleventh in the race only because it stopped to play in the river, which the tale counts in its favor: faithfulness never hurries. Each twelve-year return comes in a new element; the same Dog keeps its watch once in every sixty years.

Pig.base: [[The Figure]] The Pig closes the twelve — the zodiac's sincerity and abundance, the sign of enjoying what the other eleven chased. Last in the Great Race because it stopped to eat and sleep, and unashamed of either; Pig years favor generosity, comfort and honest pleasure. Every twelfth year in a new element, the feast comes back once in sixty years.

chinese_articles_note: chinese_articles[Animal] = {base}: two left-aligned paragraphs per animal, written from the owner's bronze medallions (Greek-key borders — the same frame family as the ring letters), shown under the octa chinese-slot hover with the medallion on top.

Wood.base: [[The Figure]] Wood is the element of spring and the east — growth, flexibility, the green force that splits stone by patience alone. A Wood year bends rather than breaks and builds upward like a tree ring by ring; in the cycle of the five, Wood feeds Fire — what grows becomes fuel for what burns.

Fire.base: [[The Figure]] Fire is the element of summer and the south — passion, visibility, transformation. A Fire year burns brighter and faster than the same animal in any other coat: it warms, illuminates and consumes, and asks only whether the flame is a hearth or a wildfire. In the cycle Fire leaves ash — and ash becomes Earth.

Earth.base: [[The Figure]] Earth is the element of the center and the turning of the seasons — stability, nurture, the ground every other element returns to. An Earth year steadies its animal: harvests are gathered, houses are built, promises are kept. In the cycle Earth bears Metal, the way ore waits inside the mountain.

Metal.base: [[The Figure]] Metal is the element of autumn and the west — precision, rigor, the blade and the bell. A Metal year cuts away what is unnecessary and keeps what rings true: harvest, judgment, craft. In the cycle Metal collects Water, as dew gathers on a cold blade at dawn.

Water.base: [[The Figure]] Water is the element of winter and the north — depth, wisdom, the strength of yielding. A Water year flows around what it cannot move and wears it away all the same; it favors listening, memory and the long view. In the cycle Water feeds Wood, and the wheel of the five begins again.

chinese_elements_note: chinese_elements[Element] = {base}: one paragraph per Wu Xing element, shown under the animal article in the chinese-slot hover (the element qualifies THIS return of the animal; 12 animals x 5 elements = the sexagenary 60).
